Why the Cardinals' Future Is Brighter Than You Think
full_text:
It is safe to say that 2026 will not be a season Arizona Cardinals fans will have many great memories associated with.
However, despite the tough season, there's still plenty of optimism around what the future holds in the desert. And with it being Thanksgiving, the organization still has plenty to be thankful for despite another poor year.
Four reasons why Cardinals fans should be hopeful for the future:
With the Cardinals tallying a lot of losses this season, it might seem like that could lead to a grim future. However, that is quite the opposite. Arizona will likely pick anywhere from No. 3-7 in the upcoming NFL draft, which looks to be filled with future Pro Bowlers and All-Pros on both sides of the ball.
On defense, either edge rusher Colin Simmons from Texas or Dylan Stewart from South Carolina could be a keystone player on the Cardinals' defensive line. Going to the secondary, cornerback Leonard Moore from LSU could develop into one of the NFL's best corners.
On offense, there is the acclaimed wideout Jeremiah Smith from Ohio State. Unless Arizona picks number one, they probably won't be able to get him. There are still other amazing wide receiver talents such as Charlie Beck and Nick Marsh from Indiana, or Cam Coleman from Texas, all of whom could be a great one-two punch with wideout Michael Wilson .
On the topic of offense, Arizona has one of the best offensive players: tight end Trey McBride . After years of having a consistent yet dynamic threat in wideout Larry Fitzgerald, Cardinal fans didn't have to wait long before McBride took up that mantle.
Despite bumpy quarterback play, McBride has had a great 2026 season, putting up big numbers and making awesome plays. His best game of the season so far was against the Denver Broncos — where he gathered 111 yards on 10 catches.
While there were slight trade rumors about McBride getting shipped off at this year's deadline, the spectacular tight end is still in the desert. He is also only 27 years old, which is young for the tight end position. Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce and San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle are 37 and 33, respectively, and are still performing at a high level.
Whatever direction Arizona takes, McBride will be a player that fans can rely on for years to come.
The past two Super Bowl champions, the Seattle Seahawks and Philadelphia Eagles, have taught the league one thing: having a great offensive line matters. Whether it's buying the quarterback extra time in the pocket or blocking for running backs, an offensive line is non-negotiable for success.
Thankfully, Arizona has two players fans can count on in the coming seasons. One is tackle Paris Johnson Jr., who, despite tearing his left bicep in week four against the New York Giants, has been a good player so far when healthy. While Johnson Jr. isn't an elite yet, the potential is still certainly there.
There is also guard Chase Bisontis, who despite not playing this season still has a lot of promise despite a preseason MCL injury. Bisontis was one of my favorite players coming out of the draft. While every draft take doesn't age well, Bisontis looked good in the preseason. Hopefully he can translate that to 2027.
It is no secret the NFC West is a gauntlet as the 49ers, Los Angels Rams and Seattle Seahawks could all make deep playoff runs. Each of these teams have had the Cardinals' number in the past couple of seasons at one point or another.
The time for Arizona could be coming in the next couple of years. While San Francisco quarterback Brock Purdy is going to be great for years to come, a lot of their players, such as wideouts Mike Evans/Keenan Allen, running back Christian McCaffrey and left tackle Trent Williams are not exactly spring chickens.
This is even more true for the Rams, as quarterback Matthew Stafford, wide receiver Davante Adams, and defensive tackle Aaron Donald could all retire this coming offseason.
The Cardinals could take a page out of the Seahawks' playbook. Before winning the Super Bowl last season, Seattle built its team with a great young roster and key veteran players. Sure, the Seahawks were mediocre for a couple of years, but it was worth it when they took home the Lombardi Trophy.
Overall, the future is bright in Arizona if they play their cards right.

title: Cardinals Hint at Jeremiyah Love Return
full_text:
ARIZONA — The return of Arizona Cardinals rookie running back Jeremiyah Love appears to be approaching.
Love, who is nearing the end of his stint on injured reserve due to an ankle injury, will be eligible to have his practice window opened after Arizona's Week 12 matchup against the Washington Commanders.
The 3-8 Cardinals are close to being pushed out of the playoffs, mathematically speaking. They're the only team who can be eliminated this weekend.
Arizona — and their fans — still would like to see Love's return to action before the end of 2026, however.
How's the third overall pick doing? Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur gave an update:
“Yes, he's doing well," LaFleur said of Love this week.
"Again, for him, he's still in his four-week window there on IR (injured reserve), but we'll know more each day and then kind of figure it out on Monday to see what it looks like for Philly, or if we need the extra week for the bye week.”
Love suffered a high ankle sprain, the third ankle injury of his rookie season after picking up one in preseason and another during the early stages of the regular season.
The Notre Dame product had shown flashes of what made him a top pick in this year's draft, though he's played just six games this season while managing injury through others.
"Really the whole season, I haven't been able to feel like myself," Love said back on Oct. 30. "I haven't felt like Jeremiyah Love that the people see. I couldn't do what I wanted to do. You ain't see me hurdle anybody, any (expletive) spin move, none of that stuff."
Love has rushed for 268 yards on 76 attempts (3.5 yards per carry) and one touchdown while adding 11 receptions for 36 yards and one receiving touchdown as well.
The Cardinals could exercise a bit of caution when it comes to Love, as his first opportunity to return (against Philadelphia) comes one week before their bye in Week 14.
With their week off so close in proximity, Arizona could play it safe and wait until after they return to activate Love — which would give them four remaining games on the schedule against the New York Jets, New Orleans Saints, Las Vegas Raiders and San Francisco 49ers. All but New Orleans are at home in Glendale.

title: 3 Things the Cardinals Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
Happy Thanksgiving, everyone!
The Arizona Cardinals have just six games left on the season. 2026 by no means has gone according to plan, though a brighter future is (hopefully) on the way.
They always say showing gratitude is the best way to receive more blessings — here's three things the Cardinals should be thankful for this year.
This is the obvious one, right?
McBride, alongside being one of the best at his position, is one of the league's top players. Unfortunately, 2026 has been a "down" season due to injuries and circumstances around him. Still, 87 receptions for 689 yards and five touchdowns is a strong output regardless.
The Cardinals don't have much going for them, but an all-world talent like McBride in Arizona gives the team at least a glimmer of hope on a weekly basis alongside giving fans something to watch.
“The tide’s gonna turn,” McBride told reporters earlier this season. “And it’s fun because I want to be part of the dog days. I want to be part of the times where we weren’t good, and then, it’s like, we turned it around, and we’re good now."
Not much has gone right for Arizona this season. McBride is one of few pillars they can lean on in tough times like these.
2027's offseason has potential to be game-changing for the Cardinals.
According to OverTheCap, Arizona has the second-most cap space available in 2027 at $72.4 million in effective cap. They're only behind the Atlanta Falcons' $80 million figure with no significant players to re-sign from their projected free agent class.
The Cardinals will have ample opportunity to fill massive gaps in their roster, potentially at key spots such as offensive line or edge rusher.
A few months later in April will be the NFL Draft, where Arizona has assembled eight total picks — six of which come in the first four rounds. The Cardinals have multiple second and fourth-round picks thanks to prior trades.
Their first-round selection is currently sitting in the sixth spot with opportunity to move up.
The Cardinals have plenty of ammo to make some noise next offseason and seriously improve their team.
3-8 isn't exactly a glaring sign of confidence in a head coach, and being transparent, LaFleur's had his issues in his first season. As expected.
For as much hype as he received in the hiring process due to ties with Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay, we haven't exactly gotten extensive looks of that offense.
Yet for as sideways as this season has gone, LaFleur's managed to hold himself together as a rookie.
Injuries have plagued his offense, though the once-healthy iteration of his attack did show promise. Seeing him pull everyone on the sideline in the midst of a blowout weeks ago, when the season was already lost, at least showed he truly cared about the product on the field. He's been fairly open and transparent in regards to injuries with media, which wasn't always the case in the past.
The desire to make impactful changes while staying patient has been evident with LaFleur. There's still genuine hope LaFleur can turn 2026's lemons into lemonade in the future.

title: Cardinals-Commanders Injury Report: Latest on Carson Beck, Jayden Daniels
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals and Washington Commanders have revealed their first Week 12 injury report.
20 names litter the list between the two sides, ranging from Jayden Daniels to Budda Baker and notable faces between.
The Commanders, thanks to their participation on Monday Night Football, only held a walk-through on Wednesday — so their side of the report is only an estimation.
Quick breakdowns for the Cardinals and Commanders from Wednesday:
The biggest concern here is Beck, who didn't exactly get a glowing injury update from Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur today.
“Better than yesterday, hopefully better tomorrow. Obviously [he is] DNP for a reason but we'll take it one day at a time," he told reporters.
Daniels' presence isn't quite a surprise on this report, as he's consistently been listed on Washington's prior reports with his left elbow injury — though the hand is a new sprinkle.
“Yes, he's a stud. He's a good football player. I don't think people have forgotten that," LaFleur said of Daniels when speaking with reporters today.
"I think he's shown that this year, particularly over the last few weeks. I don't think their record is exactly a great indicator for how talented this team is, and how talented of a quarterback he is. So big win for them. We know we have our hands full. I think their defense had some challenges, I would say up front, early on in terms of some injuries, but they've seemed to build a good continuity amongst themselves for the last month. So, they're playing really good football right now and I think that was a great indicator on Monday for them.”
The Cardinals and Commanders will each practice twice more this week before revealing final game statuses such as out, questionable or doubtful. Final inactives will be revealed 90 minutes prior to kickoff at State Farm Stadium on Sunday.

title: Cardinals Claim Ravens QB — And It Makes Too Much Sense
full_text:
The Arizona Cardinals are officially set to welcome back a familiar face.
Former Baltimore Ravens quarterback Kedon Slovis was waived by the organization earlier this week before being claimed off waivers from the Cardinals today. Slovis, for fans who recall, spent all of 2025 and the 2026 offseason with Arizona before he was cut before this regular season.
The Cardinals, 3-8 this season, are on their fourth starting quarterback in 40-year-old Josh Johnson. Carson Beck is dealing with a back injury while Arizona has Joey Aguilar on the active roster as well.
As the Cardinals scramble for solutions in their quarterback room, Slovis makes the most sense out of anybody besides Beck — whenever he does get fully healthy.
Slovis spent the entire offseason digesting first-year head coach Mike LaFleur's offense in the desert, running it through OTAs, training camp and preseason.
At this point in the season, the top trait a backup quarterback could have is familiarity of the offense he'll be running. While LaFleur's directly influenced from others such as Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay, Slovis was the literal lone quarterback currently available who ran LaFleur's Cardinals-specific offense.
Slovis performed quite well through camp and preseason, which led to the Green Bay Packers (with big brother and head coach Matt LaFleur likely getting good word from Mike on Slovis) picking him up before the Ravens brought him on just days before trading for Jacoby Brissett.
Slovis' experience in the desert was so valuable, he initially was believed to be a potential trade piece in the Ravens' deal for Brissett before the trade was actually finalized.
The move for Slovis makes too much sense for Arizona.
"Slovis (6-2, 223) returns to the Cardinals after playing two games last season and spending the preseason with Arizona. A Scottsdale, AZ native, Slovis originally joined the Cardinals practice squad in 2025 before being added to Arizona’s active roster. After being released by the Cardinals, Slovis was on the Packers practice squad prior to signing to Baltimore’s active roster where he spent the past three weeks.
"He went to Desert Mountain High School prior to playing collegiately at BYU (2023), Pittsburgh (2022) and USC (2019-21). Slovis spent his rookie season in 2024 on the Texans practice squad after entering the league with Indianapolis as an undrafted rookie free agent."

title: Cardinals' Carson Beck Faces Growing Concern After Latest Injury Update
full_text:
ARIZONA — Arizona Cardinals QB Carson Beck will not practice today as the team builds up to their Week 12 outing against the Washington Commanders.
Beck, dealing with a back injury, is doing a bit better according to head coach Mike LaFleur.
“Better than yesterday, hopefully better tomorrow. Obviously [he is] DNP for a reason but we'll take it one day at a time," he told reporters.
Beck had back spasms flare up last week, and in a sudden turn of events, Josh Johnson was propelled to starting duties after Beck made his first appearance in an NFL game.
Beck previously suffered from back spasms earlier this year — though he was Arizona's emergency/third quarterback, and not in a crucial starting/evaluation period like he is currently in.
“There’s always gonna be a concern with that, so you're just trying to figure out different ways to strengthen it, treat it. Pre-hab or whatever it is to try to limit this from happening again, particularly this year and then really attack it this offseason in terms of how we can prevent this," LaFleur continued on Beck's back injury.
The Cardinals, with just six games left in the regular season, were hoping to see Beck take every rep for the remaining stretch of 2026.
Now, that's a massive question.
Arizona's going to have ample opportunity to address their quarterback situation next offseason. The Cardinals, according to OverTheCap, have $95.1 million in projected cap space — the second-most of any NFL team. Arizona also has six draft picks in the first four rounds of the 2027 draft, with their first-round pick currently in the sixth spot.
Beck, by all accounts, had to audition above average in this final stretch of games for the Cardinals to feel confident in bypassing opportunities to add to the quarterback room. Injuries — whether it be the multiple back setbacks or the ribs injury suffered in preseason that kept him out multiple weeks — put a damper on that.
Perhaps most disappointing is when Beck has been on the field, he's looked great. The Hall of Fame Game was a nice introduction under a national spotlight while his NFL debut drove rave reviews despite the overall team's loss against the Los Angeles Rams.
Perhaps Beck's back improves over the next few days. Perhaps he's able to overcome injuries and display the football so many in the desert want him to.
However, the clock is ticking on Beck's time on stage to convince the Cardinals not to pursue another quarterback elsewhere.

title: Cardinals' Most Overlooked Defender Deserves Extension
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals have a handful of players set to hit free agency next offseason.
While the Cardinals, projected with the second-most cap space in 2027, are sure to be big players, there's a few names Arizona should retain moving into the second year of Mike LaFleur's tenure in the desert.
Dante Stills needs to be at the top of the list.
Stills, a defensive lineman, isn't the biggest name in Arizona's trench play. He's not making highlight-reel plays left and right, and he's often overlooked.
However, where limelight is absent, steady play is — and that's exactly what makes him a perfect extension candidate in a Cardinals defense that needs precisely that moving into the future.
ESPN's Josh Weinfuss agreed this week, sprinkling in his section of NFL power rankings:
"In a dismal season, Stills has been a consistent bright spot for the Cardinals' defense. The 2023 sixth-round pick has started 32 games in his 59-game career, including all 11 this season. He has been consistent when given the opportunity, and he's on pace for a career-high 52 tackles. In his career, Stills has nine sacks and 157 tackles."
That's been Stills' underlying superpower since arriving to Arizona as an overlooked player — stability. In a Cardinals' defensive line group that has been anything but in recent memory, Stills is at minimum a floor-raiser for one of the most important groups on the field.
Consistency first starts with health, which has been there for Stills. He's played at least 15 games in each of his first three years in the league while featuring in every single matchup thus far. While larger names such as Darius Robinson and Walter Nolen III have more glaring profiles and expectations, the same can't be said for them in terms of health and availability.
Stills will be 28 next season, which still offers a few years left in his prime while his status as a rotational player would save the Cardinals plenty of dough in comparison to other large defensive line contracts.
This wouldn't be a move that rattles the NFL world or creates shockwaves through Arizona. Cardinals fans won't be planning Super Bowl parades or anything else of that nature — though keeping a guy like Stills in your defensive line room would be a sneaky good way to continue raising its floor while potentially allowing other budding stars in the room to blossom.

title: Deep Dive: Nick Rallis Firing is Only The Beginning for Cardinals
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' dismissal of defensive coordinator Nick Rallis has been official for just over 24 hours, and as the team looks forward to its final six games of the regular season, analysis of the move from all angles is underway.
We've done our own, ranging from our brutally honest thoughts to candidates to watch in his replacement.
That train continues with evaluating... where do the Cardinals go from here?
Austin, a long-time NFL defensive coordinator, was brought on staff this past offseason as a senior analyst and soundboard for Rallis. The Cardinals did well to have a veteran voice on staff in the emergency of needing an interim defensive coordinator, which is now the case.
Austin has six games to practically audition for a full-time role in the desert.
"You start building these foundations when guys get back in phase one and even before that, as you're getting it with your coaches. He's a smart guy," Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said of Austin this week. "There are no other changes that we're making on the defensive staff, so he'll lean (on) those guys, and I'll help out where I can. We have to get some stuff going on offense too.”
LaFleur was also adamant that the roster evaluation to finish the season would be imperative for who stays and goes moving forward. Just because the Cardinals are out of the playoff fight and a new DC is in place, that doesn't mean these remaining games don't count for anything.
"I see it as an incredible challenge. We're not going to win a Super Bowl this year. We're not going to the playoffs. We know that, but what a freaking opportunity to see what some of these guys can do and how they're going to be a part of the solution moving forward and who's going to be a part of this thing moving forward," said LaFleur.
It will be interesting to see what changes with Austin this week, and if success comes, perhaps Arizona keeps him around on a permanent basis. That goes the same with many players who are getting opportunities they typically wouldn't get.
LaFleur, one of the last head coaches to be hired in a loaded 2026 coaching cycle, didn't get his pick of DC. Arizona tried to interview other candidates before eventually turning back to Rallis, who still had one year left on his contract entering this season.
“I'll be honest with you, when it is a little bit later there's been some hires and stuff like that—with that said, like I've told you guys (I've) gone against Nick quite often and it wasn't fun," said LaFleur when asked about the process of trying to find a defensive coordinator after landing in the desert.
Even if Austin does a strong job, the Cardinals would be wise to interview more candidates in hopes of finding the right fit. With LaFleur's strong connections to Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay, it wouldn't be a shock to see multiple familiar faces from those trees land interviews with Arizona this offseason.
Personnel for the defense won't just possibly change on the coaching staff, too.
General manager Monti Ossenfort is on the hot seat, as his fourth season running the show in the desert has considerably been underwhelming. Outside factors such as injuries have been prevalent, but it feels as if his time has simply run out.
With the second-most projected cap space in the 2027 offseason and six picks in the first four rounds of the draft, Arizona holds major potential to make upgrades across the board alongside deciding the fate of stars such as Budda Baker and Josh Sweat.
Will Ossenfort still be in charge to upgrade a clearly deficient defense?
Arizona's general manager spot will surely be decided on before a new defensive coordinator is hired and changes are made to the personnel.
This next defensive coordinator hire has to hit.
LaFleur is patient. He was on Shanahan's staff in San Francisco their first season where they won just one of their first nine games. The 49ers' foundation was built through those dark days, and LaFleur's hoping that same success can be replicated here in the desert.
However, there's a few big dominoes the Cardinals need: A strong general manager and a defensive coordinator that can bring sustainable success to their side of the ball.
LaFleur, admittedly so, is a bit held back by the Cardinals' notorious lack of spending on coaching staffs. Arizona typically has been shy on shelling out big bucks to land top coaches, and with that line of thought, perhaps the Cardinals will be forced to bank on a young, up-and-coming name.
Regardless of who it is or what their resume looks like, Arizona needs improvement on that side of the ball. The excitement with LaFleur resides in his potential of what his offense will look like down the road — not in Week 11 of his first season.
However, the Cardinals cannot make the strides they so covet without at least an average defense. Arizona's not banking on finding the next Brian Flores or Mike Macdonald — they simply need somebody who can develop talent and get the Cardinals to play average NFL ball.
If that happens, and LaFleur's offense takes off sooner rather than later, there's no telling what can come in the desert.

title: Cardinals Should Think Twice About Brandon Aiyuk After Insider's Comments
full_text:
ARIZONA – The Arizona Cardinals appear to make sense for one of the NFL's biggest swings at the plate.
Brandon Aiyuk is no longer with the San Francisco 49ers, ending a long feud between the two sides as the player hasn't played in an NFL game since October of 2024 due to a severe knee injury that was followed by a series of off-field issues and drama between player and organization that finally comes to a close.
The Cardinals, at least according to ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter, make sense to land the new free agent wideout.
"If you look at the landscape and think about where he could make sense, where did he play college football? [Arizona State]. Does Arizona need any wide receivers right now? Does Arizona need any young infusion of talent on the offensive side of the ball right now? Would it make sense for him to go back there and head to Arizona as a potential option? I'm not telling you it's going to happen, I'm just telling you is that going to be an option? Yes."
Could Brandon Aiyuk land with the Cardinals? “Would it not make sense for him to go back there and head to Arizona?” Adam Schefter on his podcast says the Cards are “certainly” a potential option for the former 49ers WR. pic.twitter.com/Pt1IRBHoa2
That's a risk that just might be too rich for the Cardinals, even with how low the organization feels at the moment.
First, Aiyuk is a massively talented player. The former ASU product, when healthy, is a dynamic presence in any wide receiver's room. 4,305 yards and 25 touchdowns on 294 catches is nothing to shake a stick at, and for a Cardinals team that's devoid of a deep threat, Aiyuk could be just that in the desert.
It's also notable Aiyuk, a 2020 first-round pick, spent his entire career under Kyle Shanahan in San Francisco — a place and coach that helped shape Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur in the build-up to him eventually landing in Arizona.
That could be the precise factor in why the Cardinals don't pursue Aiyuk.
LaFleur and Shanahan are quite close thanks to their prior time together in Atlanta and San Francisco, meaning the first person LaFleur would call on a potential Aiyuk signing would be... Shanahan.
And those won't exactly be great reviews.
Aiyuk had been a massive headache the 49ers couldn't escape for multiple years, as the wideout spiraled out of control with off-field issues and disputes with the team and his rehab from the aforementioned knee injury — a situation so ugly the 49ers placed him on reserve/did not report list with his 2026 guaranteed money voided last year for failing to show up to his rehab.
It's a mess the Cardinals may have to keep cleaning if they sign him.
The NFL is the land of second chances. So long as you're talented and can overshadow any previous shortcomings.
Aiyuk certainly has the talent to do so, though off-field issues aside — he hasn't played in two calendar years. He'll be 29 next offseason.
Forget the off-field issues for a second: is he even the same player he once was?
There's layers to unravel in terms of Aiyuk as a player and person. Perhaps he's found his footing in a multitude of ways and just needs a fresh start. It's tough to deny the Cardinals need talent practically everywhere, and Aiyuk would be a plug-and-play fit thanks to talent alone and familiarity with LaFleur's offensive language thanks to the shared Shanahan connection.
However, it's tough to envision this panning out for the Cardinals. Numerous factors, both on and off the field, make this a hesitant call. Typically you can tolerate one or the other — though the massive unknown of both, with Arizona speaking often on wanting "the right guys" in their locker room, makes this a gamble that's not worth the risk.
Even for a roster that desperately needs talent like Aiyuk.

title: Cardinals' QB Crisis Suddenly Opens Door for Reunion
full_text:
ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals ' quarterback situation is, quite frankly, a mess at the moment.
Arizona's fresh off their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks following Josh Johnson handling duties in Week 11. Carson Beck remains a massive mystery thanks to his back injury while veteran Gardner Minshew is out for the season with a UCL injury and Jacoby Brissett is now on the Baltimore Ravens.
The 40-year-old Johnson and recently signed undrafted rookie Joey Aguilar are currently Arizona's top two options at the position. There's always the possibility of signing a player such as Daniel Jones , who just hit free agency.
However, things have gone so south in the desert that a reunion that once would have been an afterthought now presents itself as an enticing possibility.
According to NFL insider Mike Garafolo, the Baltimore Ravens are waiving former Cardinals quarterback Kedon Slovis. Arizona was specifically listed in his report as a team with current quarterback needs:
The #Ravens are waiving QB Kedon Slovis. They’d like to bring him back to the practice squad if he clears, though there are teams with QB needs, including his former team in the #AZCardinals .
A reunion, at this stage of the season, does make sense. Slovis had spent the entire 2025 season and 2026 offseason with Arizona before being released ahead of final roster cuts.
Slovis, since spending time with the Packers and Ravens, is one of few quarterbacks available that has direct experience working under Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur. He's practically the only available passer who exclusively has an understanding of LaFleur's specific system in Arizona, which was just beginning to be installed this past offseason.
Brissett, who was dealt to Baltimore, spoke on LaFleur earlier this season and his ability to tailor offenses to quarterbacks (while also name-dropping Slovis):
"I think the cool thing about it is he's done what fits the guys that's in. So, either way if I'm in, (QB) Gardner (Minshew II) is in, (Packers QB) Kedon (Slovis) was in, (QB) Carson (Beck) was in he's always kind of tailored around our skillset for that game or that practice or whatever the case may be.
"The flexibility to do a multitude of different things and while doing the same thing. I think that's the cool part about it. I've said a number of times, it's been so fun to work with him, and his energy is something that is hard to replicate."
When the Cardinals were engaging in trade talks with Baltimore surrounding Brissett, many believed Slovis could have been part of the package Arizona ultimately received back.
Slovis looked impressive in preseason action for Arizona. Across four games, he completed 39 of 61 attempts for 516 yards and two touchdowns to two interceptions.
The Cardinals have always talked highly of Slovis, and now with a slew of changes at Arizona's quarterback position, a reunion could very well be on the table.

title: Falcons Face a Different Kind of Kirk Cousins Problem Against Vikings
full_text:
Just two short years ago, Kirk Cousins had the City of Atlanta ‘Swag Surfin’ with him as he looked to be the quarterback to return the Falcons to prominence.
Everything went downhill from there, as his performance spiraled while the team plummeted in his two years on the roster.
It led to a messy breakup between the veteran quarterback and Atlanta, as the Falcons moved on to Michael Penix Jr. , whom they selected with the eighth overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, the same year Cousins inked a lucrative four-year, $180 million deal with the team. The Falcons are still paying the price for that deal today.
Fast forward to now: after a nine-game stint with the Las Vegas Raiders, the man who had initially looked to save the franchise is set to face them as the Minnesota Vikings quarterback following a trade-deadline deal.
Cousins spent two seasons in Atlanta, overlapping with many current Falcons players and, most importantly, defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich .
He knows the system; he knows the signals. And that could pose an issue for the Falcons come Sunday when they make the trip for the NFL Week 12 matchup.
“Sometimes it falls into the ‘They know that we know that they know’ category,” Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters on Tuesday. “I don’t think you overthink it. You change calls, you change signals, you try to do that to stay on top of it.”
Cousins has had an up-and-down return to Minnesota, the place he was selected to three Pro Bowls from 2018 to 2023 before a right Achilles tendon tear ended his run under center. Before leaving for the Cleveland Browns head coaching job in 2020, Stefanski was Minnesota’s offensive coordinator the previous two years , with Cousins running his offense.
In two games, he’s completed 47-of-69 passes for 442 passing yards, threw two touchdown passes, and tossed two interceptions.
The Vikings are 1-1 with Cousins back. They’re fresh off getting beleaguered by the San Francisco 49ers defense in a 35-10 loss. Cousins went 26-for-38 for 235 passing yards and an interception.
Stefanski sees “subtle differences” with Cousins’ addition, adding that the quarterback has been a “natural fit” in a system he once blossomed in.
“Looks like himself,” Stefanski evaluated Cousins. “Comfort level in that system, which should be no surprise because he’s been in that system with those coaches and a bunch of the players. Really looked seamless.”
Falcons (3-7) versus Vikings (7-3) kickoff is at 1 p.m. on Sunday at U.S. Bank Stadium. The game will be broadcast on FOX.

title: Booth or Sideline? Falcons’ Kevin Stefanski Settles Tommy Rees Question
full_text:
Kevin Stefanski is standing firm in his decision, which has raised questions throughout the bye week.
On Tuesday, the Atlanta Falcons head coach said that offensive coordinator Tommy Rees will continue to call plays from the sidelines during the NFL Week 12 road game against the Minnesota Vikings.
“He’ll be down on-field,” Stefanski told reporters.
Rees orchestrated the declining offense from the sidelines in Atlanta’s 35-13 home loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Nov. 15. Previously, he called plays from the coaches’ booth, even dating back to his first coordinator job at Notre Dame.
“He’s comfortable doing both,” Stefanski said. “He’s done both over the course of his career.”
Avid football fans remember the NBC cameras catching Rees screaming on the phone from the booth, telling former ND quarterback Drew Pyne, “Do your f—ing job” after a slow start.
When asked, Stefanski didn’t answer whether it was his or Rees’ idea to relocate, instead stating they “talk about a lot of things.”
“It’s just a matter [of finding] that consistency,” Stefanski said. “Just looking for different things that we can do differently.”
Calling plays from the sideline or the box has its advantages.
On the field, coordinators can get a face-to-face connection and manage needed adjustments more quickly. From up top, coordinators get a bird’s-eye view of the field, away from crowd noise, and can better maintain a play-calling rhythm.
There’s just a sample size of how the Falcons have performed with Rees on the field: their 13-point performance against Kansas City . They turned in 370 total yards (270 passing, 100 rushing), had 1-for-5 red zone efficiency, and two turnovers. While the yardage numbers look OK, 203 of those were in the fourth quarter, after the Chiefs built a 28-3 lead with 9:55 left in the game.
The Falcons had 167 yards of offense through the game's first 50 minutes.
From the first nine games, Atlanta averaged 20.9 points, 322.7 total yards (185.4 passing and 137.2 rushing). However, the offense has been quite mercurial outside of an early two-week surge from Week 3 to Week 4, averaging a league-high 40 points during that span.
Much of the blame has been placed on quarterback Michael Penix Jr. , and defenses have also begun stacking the box to stymie All-Pro running back Bijan Robinson and a rushing attack that was once No. 2 in the league.
“We just have not been consistent enough,” Stefanski said. “Is that true of players? Is that true of coaches? Yeah. That’s all of us.”
Atlanta (3-7) is set to travel to Minnesota to face the Vikings (7-3) at U.S. Bank Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. FOX will televise the game.
It’ll be a challenge for Rees and the Falcons offense, as defensive coordinator Brian Flores leads the highest-ranked blitz rate .

title: Kirk Cousins' Complicated Falcons Tenure Comes Full Circle Against Minnesota
full_text:
Kirk Cousins will take the field under the lights at the Vikings’ U.S. Bank Stadium for the third time since leaving his former home in 2023, but for the first time in Minnesota uniform. The last two trips came in different threads, ironically, for the team he will face on Sunday.
The quarterback left Minnesota and signed with the Atlanta Falcons as a free agent in 2024. He made one start against his former team that season, but he returned the following year to back up the now-starting Michael Penix Jr. The Falcons lost the first trip and won the second, and a lot happened in between, but Sunday will be a full-circle moment for the veteran.
His time in Atlanta was well documented, and the relationship was complicated.
After signing him to a lucrative free-agent contract, the Falcons drafted Penix No. 8 overall just a month later. Cousins started 14 games that year, leading Atlanta to a 6-3 start and to the cusp of snapping a then-six-year playoff drought, but a shoulder injury derailed their season.
He was benched after the Falcons lost four consecutive games, with Cousins throwing one touchdown and nine interceptions between Weeks 10 and 15. That stretch doomed their season, and they benched him for the rookie.
Penix started the 2025 season, but a knee injury ended his first full year as a starter. Cousins came on as a backup and went 5-2 as QB1, but the Falcons released him that offseason to pursue a starting role elsewhere, absorbing $35 million in dead cap to let him do it.
Despite how things ended, the veteran was gracious in his comments about facing the Falcons, now as the starter for his former-former team.
“I have a lot of respect for the guys in that locker room,” Cousins said. “I’m grateful for my two years there, and looking forward to getting back to US Bank and a chance to play there.”
Beyond his relationship with the organization and his old teammates, Cousins’ quarterback coach and offensive coordinator between 2017 and 2019 , Kevin Stefanski, is now the head coach of the Falcons. Cousins says those relationships, from the coach to the other parts of the organization, have helped him grow as a player in this league.
“I know Kevin Stefanski well,” Cousins said. “I had a good conversation with [Ian] Cunningham, the new GM [of the Falcons], and talked to Michael [Penix]. I just love those guys. Then that locker room – that is the unique part, as you play other places, you kind of get to see things from other perspectives and other places, how things are done. You get to know more guys, and I’m so grateful for those people I got to know there.”
But Sunday will be the first time the prodigal Vikings’ son will take the field in a purple jersey. He appreciates the venue and has a unique perspective on what the Falcons will face on Sunday.
“Playing as an opponent was when I was really able to fully appreciate how challenging it was to play there, and how great of an environment it is and just how unique of a stadium it is,” Cousins said about his impressions of the stadium as a visitor. “Having been in two other locker rooms since playing for the Vikings, I think it’s a pretty agreed-upon fact among players that US Bank is the number one place in the league in terms of just a stadium in terms of hitting a home run and making it a special place to play.”
Penix will need to bear the brunt of that experience , while shouldering the potential of another lost season in Atlanta. In Minnesota, Cousins hopes to bring the 7-3 Vikings back to the playoffs, while the Falcons may be wondering what might have been if the quarterback they're still paying for had worn their uniform.
On Sunday, they'll see what the quarterback they let go looks like in someone else's offense.

title: Falcons Injury Report: Six Players Miss Practice Ahead of Vikings Matchup
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons are dealing with several injury concerns as they begin preparations for their Week 12 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings , with six players missing Wednesday's practice.
Atlanta returned from its Week 11 bye hoping to get healthier before Sunday's road matchup. However, the team's first injury report of the week featured a lengthy list of players who were unable to participate, including several notable contributors on both sides of the football.
Starting left guard Matthew Bergeron headlines the list after missing practice with a back injury. Bergeron has started all 10 games for Atlanta this season, making his availability particularly important as the Falcons prepare to face Minnesota's defensive front. He's missed only two games (both last season) in his four-year Falcons career.
The offensive line could be without one of its most consistent pieces if Bergeron's injury lingers throughout the week.
The Falcons also had two wide receivers unavailable Wednesday. Jahan Dotson and rookie Zachariah Branch both missed practice with hamstring injuries.
Dotson's absence is another potential concern for an Atlanta offense looking to establish consistency through the passing game. Branch, meanwhile, has been working to carve out a role in the receiving corps and special teams. Branch injured his hamstring against Tampa Bay in Week 8, and he missed the following two games against the Bengals and Chiefs.
The defensive side of the football was not spared, either.
Safety DeMarcco Hellams missed Wednesday's practice with a foot injury. Hellams recently stepped into a starting role against the Kansas City Chiefs after Atlanta traded Jessie Bates III to the Jacksonville Jaguars. His potential absence would create another challenge for a secondary that has undergone significant changes.
Safety Jammie Robinson was signed to the 53-man roster on Monday in what may have been a signal about Hellams' availability.
Second-year defensive back Billy Bowman Jr. was also held out with a hamstring injury, leaving Atlanta with multiple questions in its defensive backfield heading into the weekend. Bowman has only played in five games this season, and only once since October 18th, against the Chicago Bears.
There was one additional absence that was not injury-related. Veteran defensive end Za'Darius Smith received a rest day and did not participate in Wednesday's practice.
Defensive end James Pearce Jr. was the only player listed as limited, working through a back injury. No Falcons players were listed as full participants on the initial report.
The number of players missing practice is something worth monitoring as the Falcons move through the remainder of the week. Five players are dealing with injuries, while Smith's absence was attributed to rest.
Atlanta has a significant challenge ahead against a Minnesota team that will be looking to defend its home field at U.S. Bank Stadium.
The Falcons will have two more scheduled practices to evaluate their injured players before Sunday's matchup. Bergeron, Hellams, Dotson, Branch and Bowman will be particularly important names to watch as Atlanta looks to get as many contributors back on the field as possible.
Kickoff between the Falcons and Vikings is scheduled for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

title: Rickea Jackson's Cryptic Message Puts Falcons James Pearce Jr. Back in Spotlight
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. is facing renewed off-field scrutiny after WNBA player Rickea Jackson shared new social media posts suggesting she is still experiencing harassment and unwanted contact from someone in her recent past.
Jackson, Pearce’s former girlfriend, recently took to Instagram to repost an image showing numerous incoming phone calls from a “No Caller ID” number. The post raised concerns about repeated attempts to contact her and suggested the situation remains ongoing.
Jackson addressed the calls in the comments, making it clear that the situation was something she was actively experiencing rather than an incident from the past. While she never mentioned Pearce by name, it was clear she was talking about Pearce.
“Yes still till this day!!! I would never repost something like this pertaining to something I’m not actively going through. This is ACTIVE!! I haven’t said anythinggg to or about this person in almost a year !!!! and after this I won’t say anything else ever again!!” Jackson wrote.
She also appeared to suggest that the person responsible would recognize themselves in her post, despite her not publicly identifying anyone.
“But obviously that person know what they know to know it’s that person.”
Jackson did not specifically name Pearce or directly accuse him of making the calls. However, given the former couple’s previous legal situation, the posts have brought renewed attention to the Falcons edge rusher.
The situation reached Atlanta’s coaching staff, with head coach Kevin Stefanski confirming Wednesday that the organization is aware of the latest social media allegations.
“I’m aware, we’ve spoken to James, but I don’t have much more other than that,” Stefanski said.
Stefanski declined to provide additional details about the conversation or discuss whether the Falcons anticipate taking further action. Pearce has not been made available to repeated media requests since rejoining the team after Week 8.
This is not the first time Pearce has faced scrutiny involving Jackson.
After their relationship ended, Jackson made allegations of stalking, harassment, and physical abuse. A February 2026 incident in Florida resulted in Pearce’s arrest and multiple charges, including aggravated stalking and aggravated battery.
The legal situation eventually resulted in an eight-game suspension from the NFL for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. Pearce served the suspension before being reinstated in November.
Now, the latest Instagram posts have brought the situation back into the public eye, raising questions about whether the Falcons or NFL could take another look at the circumstances.
It is important to note that Jackson has not specifically identified Pearce as the person behind the calls, and there is no independently established evidence connecting him to the latest allegations.
However, it was serious enough for the Falcons to check in with Pearce, even if they aren't commenting publicly.
For Atlanta, the latest developments create another off-field storyline involving one of its young defensive playmakers.
Pearce was a first-round investment for the Falcons in the 2025 NFL Draft and remains an important part of the organization’s plans for its pass rush.
For now, the Falcons have confirmed they have spoken with Pearce. Whether the latest allegations result in additional action from the organization or the NFL remains to be seen.

title: Falcons Prepare for Matchup from Hell in Vikings and Brian Flores
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons (3-7) head north to take on the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) on Sunday, and they're hoping they aren't serving quarterback Michael Penix Jr. up like a Thanksgiving turkey.
The Falcons have a glaring weakness on offense: their performance in the passing game when Penix is under pressure.
The Vikings have a mad scientist as a defensive coordinator who blitzes the opposition at nearly twice the rate of the next closest team in the NFL.
It's the matchup from hell for the Falcons, but it also presents an opportunity for offensive coordinator Tommy Rees, the offensive line, and Penix to quiet their critics.
Whether you're in the camp that blames one of, or some combination of, all three, the fact remains that defensive coordinators are exploiting the Falcons' inability to deal with pressure. The Kansas City Chiefs sent 6 players on the Falcons' first three plays last week, and they typically blitz less than half as often as the Vikings do.
Blitz Rates & Number of Blitzers Data: @FantasyPtsData pic.twitter.com/3UF61dNI4G
The chart above shows how far the Vikings lead the rest of the NFL in blitz rate. Pro Football Reference calculates the total numbers a little differently and have the Vikings at 67.4% with the Buccaneers still in second, but at 37.2%.
What's interesting about the Fantasy Points Data, is that it shows how often teams bring one extra man on a blitz, two, or three-plus. At 23.6%, the Vikings bring more than two players on a blitz more than four teams, including the Atlanta Falcons (22.3%), blitz at all.
Penix is the least accurate quarterback in the NFL when pressured, and by some distance.
NFL QB Ball Placement when Pressured 🟢 Highly Accurate 🟡 Poor Placement, but Catchable 🔴 Inaccurate & Uncatchable Data: @FantasyPtsData | throws with > 0 air yards | min. 30 qualifying attempts https://t.co/RCWEtBelba pic.twitter.com/pkX2Oqk1VO
Penix would need to increase his 33.3% on-target rate by nearly 13 points, or 38.7%, just to catch the next worst quarterback, Cam Ward of the Titans, at 46.2%.
The constant blitzing doesn't just affect Penix and the drop-back passing game; it's also an effective way to bottle up running back Bijan Robinson. For the most part, Penix is a stationary target behind center. If a defense swarms the target, they're also swarming the handoff to Robinson.
Two birds, one stone, so to speak.
Offensive lines weren't built to block five and six players consistently, and the Falcons haven't made defenses pay for playing what should be a high-risk style of defense. Defensive coordinators know that blitzing the Falcons has been a no-risk, high-reward strategy this season.
Even if six pass rushers are accounted for, it only takes one defensive player to win his rep to blow up an offensive play. Those are the kind of odds defensive coordinators live for.
Overwhelming the offensive line with numbers has worked well, and it's the entire philosophy behind Vikings DC Brian Flores' approach.
Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski alluded to the risk-reward of creating pressure with extra defenders this week.
"When teams pressure, it's our ability to have good answers for the quarterback. Having answers where it's then an opportunity for the offense to make a big play. And there's a risk-reward to pressuring. There's a risk-reward to every type of defense, but certainly as you pressure, you do have voids in coverage. So, taking advantage of those voids in a bunch of different ways is important for our offense and, obviously our quarterback," Stefanski said this week.
In their last game out, the Vikings were dismantled by the San Francisco 49ers and quarterback Brock Purdy. Did the Falcons see some things they can replicate on Sunday?
"You watch their tape and you understand what they're trying to accomplish," Stefanski said. "And it's a good scheme versus a good scheme. To say that they're going to do the exact same thing versus us is hard to say. So, you want to understand each play and understand the answers that the quarterback had on that play and then how that may factor into how you design a game plan.
"But certainly, there were some really good moments. I thought, some moments for our guys to learn from in that ballgame.
"I thought the quarterback played at a high level."
Purdy is third in the NFL in accuracy when under pressure. His 65.9% on-target rate is almost double Penix's 33.3%. Recognizing the blitz pre-snap and punishing the defense for vacating an area of coverage to send a blitz is what Stefanski means by having answers.
Penix and the Falcons can answer a lot of questions about their ability to beat pressure against the Vikings. Flores is going to blitz on virtually every down.
If the Falcons have no answers and crumble to pressure as they have in recent losses to the Chiefs and Bears, questions about the futures of Penix, Rees, and the offensive line are only going to grow louder.

title: Falcons Must Rediscover One Key Part of Their Identity to Save Season
full_text:
FLOWERY BRANCH – The Atlanta Falcons entered the bye week in a skid. The 3-7 squad has lost three straight games and five of their last six. The season isn’t completely lost yet , with the division still within reach, but the margin for error has nearly disappeared.
If the Falcons hope to reach their goals, it starts with getting back to what they do best: running the ball and stopping the run.
Head coach Kevin Stefanski spent his time away locked in his office, watching play after play and working to get his team’s season back on track. He said he identified some areas that they can improve and continue to address as a team.
From there, it’s a “big lift” for the position coaches to convey that information to the players in bite-sized form to avoid mental overload.
“All of our coaches have a specific area that they’re in charge of, quote unquote,” Stefanski said. “They do their self-scout in that area. Then, in our own ways, you go back, and you just watch games; and then you also go back, and you watch the run game, and then you cut it up; and you watch the wide zone and the duo and the perimeter run game, et cetera.”
After 10 weeks of games, the Falcons needed the reset, both offensively and defensively.
The Falcons are No. 23 in scoring offense (20.1 points per game), No. 18 in total offense (327.4 yards per game), and No. 27 in EPA per play (-0.16). They are No. 24 in scoring defense (25.8 points per game), No. 29 in total defense (358.2 yards per game), and No. 20 in EPA per play (-0.02).
There is plenty to improve, but fitting it all in a week away is a massive undertaking.
“I think it's the age-old as teachers and coaches, we should be able to handle a lot of that. And then what you give your students – what you give your players, maybe is not as much of that,” Stefanski said. “I often think about the playbook. The playbook's this big, but you don't need your players to know all of that. A lot of times that's for the coaches to go back and reference.
“We need our players to know the game plan… You definitely take the players through the key things and the bullet points, if you will. But as coaches, you do a deeper dive so that you have the whys and the what-fors behind all of it.”
The time away helped them identify their own trends, specifically what has been working against them on the ground.
Through the early weeks of the season, Atlanta was among the NFL’s best. They allowed 48.3 yards per game and piled on 181.0 yards of their own. Despite some starts from Cooper Rush that doomed the offense in two of those games, the Falcons rode the ground dominance to a .500 mark and 24.0 points per game.
Since then, the numbers have dwindled. The rushing offense has dropped to 101.8 yards, while the defense has plummeted to 166.3 yards allowed.
“It’s never one thing. If it was one thing, that’d be easy,” Stefanski said. “It'd be a short self-scout meeting. But it's never one thing.
“We're looking for a level of consistency that we haven't reached enough.”
Injuries have certainly played a role, with the Falcons missing key contributors in linebacker Divine Deablo and running back Brian Robinson. The week off should help both players get healthier, but their return will only be a small part of fixing a regressing facet of this team's self-proclaimed identity.
But focusing all of their attention on a single facet of their team would come at a cost.
“You have to make some decisions on what you want to do moving forward, because, like anything, it’s about what you want to attach your time to,” Stefanski said. “There’s a cost to everything. Every change you make or every investment in a scheme, there's a cost to it. And there's cost in terms of the meeting room and the practice field. So, I think a lot of the conversations with the coordinators, especially, are all these learnings: where do we want to streamline this so that we can maintain or find a level of consistency?”
That is what happens when a team loses its identity halfway through a season. With similar shortcomings in the passing offense and secondary, the Falcons have no time to lose if they want to snap out of this skid.
Stefanski didn't specify what he found, but his comments on streamlining suggest the Falcons will simplify what they ask of their run game and defense. That will be tested right out of the gate.
Three straight games against playoff-caliber opponents in the Vikings, Lions, and Browns await them after their time away, plus a trip to Washington and three division games to finish their season. How they manage these games will dictate how this season is remembered and whether this team can snap out of an eight-year playoff drought.
Garrett Chapman is a sports broadcaster, writer, and content creator based in Atlanta. He has several years of experience covering the Atlanta sports scene, college football, Georgia high school football, recruiting for 24/7 Sports, and the NFL. You can also hear him on Sports Radio 92.9 The Game.

title: Falcons Help Feed 1,000 Atlanta Families at 11th Annual Falcons Feast
full_text:
The Atlanta Falcons made an impact off the football field Tuesday, helping provide Thanksgiving meals to 1,000 Atlanta families during the 11th annual Falcons Feast
The event was presented by Publix in partnership with local nonprofit CHRIS 180.  It took place across three locations throughout Atlanta, bringing together current players, team legends, Atlanta Falcons Cheerleaders, Freddie Falcon, and team associates to distribute meals to families in need.
Each meal included a frozen turkey, green beans, corn, gravy, cranberry sauce, stuffing, and a Publix gift card. Families received meal vouchers ahead of the event, which were required to pick up their Thanksgiving meals.
For defensive tackle Brandon Dorlus, the opportunity to give back was about more than handing out food.
“People came up to me and said thank you for the turkeys. It means a lot to me that I can put a smile on someone’s face. I just want to help out and give where I can,” Dorlus said.
Dorlus also discussed how representing Atlanta comes with responsibilities beyond playing football.
“It’s part of our job to not just be football players but to be people too,” Dorlus said.
Chris Lindstrom shared a similar perspective, highlighting the relationship between Falcons players and the Atlanta community.
“Every interaction that you have could really uplift somebody’s day,” Lindstrom said.
“They give so much to us as players. Every time you give, you’re inherently receiving. You just feel great with that.”
The event also provided some lighter moments. Several fans shouted “Rise Up” while interacting with players, showing their appreciation and excitement for the organization.
Dorlus revealed that macaroni and cheese is his favorite Thanksgiving food, while collard greens are his least favorite. However, the defensive tackle and his teammates still had work to finish before heading home for the holiday.
Although the Falcons spent Tuesday giving back, the team also has its attention on Sunday’s Week 12 road matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.
Atlanta is coming off its Week 11 bye and will use the additional preparation time to get healthy, address areas that need improvement, and prepare for the final stretch of the regular season.
The Falcons are scheduled to practice on Thanksgiving Day before heading into their final preparations for Minnesota.
Dorlus is looking forward to getting that work in before enjoying the holiday with his family.
“I’m just happy that we’re practicing first, get the work in, and then I get to go home and stuff my belly up,” Dorlus said.
This shows the balance NFL players face during the holiday season, with Thanksgiving providing an opportunity to spend time with family while still maintaining the responsibilities that come with preparing for a game.
For Lindstrom, Dorlus and the rest of the Falcons, Tuesday was an opportunity to show appreciation for the community before shifting their focus toward Minnesota.
This continued tradition reminds Atlanta fans that the organization’s impact extends well beyond the football field.
Darius has a Master's in Communications from Georgia State and has previous experience covering the Atlanta Falcons with 3 Point Conversion and covering the NFL with On SI.

title: Kevin Stefanski Dishes on Minnesota Vikings Return and Kirk Cousins Reunion
full_text:
Much will be made of Atlanta Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski's return to Cleveland when the Falcons take on the Browns on December 13th, having coached them the previous six seasons.
But before we can get to that storyline, Stefanski and the Falcons travel to Minnesota to take on the Vikings on Sunday. Stefanski spent 14 seasons with the Vikings, including 2019, when he was the offensive coordinator for newly signed quarterback Kirk Cousins.
Stefanski helped Cousins to a Pro Bowl season, and Cousins helped Stefanski get his first head coaching job with the Cleveland Browns a year later.
More recently, Cousins spent two forgettable years in Atlanta before heading to Las Vegas as a free agent before the season, and Stefanski came to the Falcons as Cousins was headed out the door.
The Raiders traded Cousins to Minnesota mid-season, and now Stefanski and the Falcons will face a Vikings team that has more than a few familiar faces.
"I have, yeah. Obviously, I've followed," Stefanski said when asked about Cousins' journey since leaving Atlanta. " I've not talked to him. I can imagine he's inundated as we speak. But sure, it's a crazy league, and he's back out there in Minnesota.”
After six years in Cleveland, there's been plenty of time for Stefanski to distance himself from his days in Minnesota, but that doesn't mean he won't enjoy his visit to a city he called home for more than a decade.
“No, and I only say that - excited to see a bunch of people," Stefanski said of any emotions he might feel on his return. "A bunch of friends and that type of thing. But we went back when I was in Cleveland; we went back there, I believe, in '21. Kirk was quarterback there. So, got a lot of that out of the way.”
While the personal storylines surrounding Cousins and Stefanski will be unavoidable on Sunday, Stefanski knows it needs to be all business to try and get a win in a hostile environment.
“Sure, it's a very, very loud venue. I was there when it was the Metrodome, and that was very loud. Then you go to U.S. Bank Stadium, and you're wondering, is it going to be the same amount of decibels? Sure enough, it was.
"So, that's a great advantage that they have there that they've always taken advantage of, and it'll be an awesome experience for our players. We'll work very hard on the silent count like we've done, and make sure that we're doing our part to deal with those elements. We don't control those elements, but we have to deal with them.”
How the Falcons deal with the crowd noise and Brian Flores' blitz-happy defense will determine how close they're ultimately able to keep the game in trying to sneak back home with a win.

title: Falcons Undecided on Tommy Rees’ Playcalling Spot vs. Vikings
full_text:
Atlanta Falcons offensive coordinator Tommy Rees' play calling location remains uncertain heading into Sunday's matchup against the Minnesota Vikings , raising questions about whether he will return to the sideline or move back to the coaches' booth.
Rees spent the first nine weeks of the season calling plays from the coaches' booth before moving to the sideline for Atlanta's Week 10 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs. The change was intended to provide better communication between Rees and quarterback Michael Penix Jr., but the results did not immediately improve.
During Monday's press conference, head coach Kevin Stefanski was asked whether Rees would return to the sideline this week. Stefanski stopped short of providing a definitive answer.
"Going to work through it, yeah. Still something I want to think through," Stefanski said.
When asked whether the decision was 100% one way or the other, Stefanski confirmed that no final determination had been made.
"No, not yet," Stefanski added.
The decision is particularly interesting considering Atlanta's offensive production before and after Rees moved down to the sideline.
Through the first nine games, with Rees calling plays from the booth, Atlanta averaged 20.9 points and 322.7 total yards per game. The Falcons averaged 185.4 passing yards and 137.2 rushing yards during that stretch.
In Week 10 against Kansas City, with Rees operating from the sideline, Atlanta finished with 13 points and 370 total yards. The offense produced 270 passing yards and 100 rushing yards in the 35-13 loss.
While the Falcons generated more total yards and passing production against Kansas City, they scored nearly eight fewer points than their average through the first nine weeks. Of course, the Chiefs also have the No. 2 scoring defense in the NFL, so they might not have been the best litmus test.
The offensive struggles were especially noticeable early. Atlanta opened the game with four consecutive three-and-outs, marking the first time the franchise had done that since 2000. The Falcons entered halftime with just 117 net yards and four first downs, all on one drive.
The move to the sideline was also notable because Rees has become recognizable for his animated reactions in the coaches' booth, with some of his reactions during games going viral on social media.
However, the change was about more than appearances. Stefanski explained previously that the coaching staff was trying something different in hopes of improving communication between Rees and Penix.
Penix, however, downplayed the impact of the change following the Kansas City game, saying he did not notice much of a difference.
That raises an important question for Atlanta. Would returning Rees to the booth provide a better perspective for evaluating opposing defenses, or does keeping him on the sideline offer advantages in communicating with his quarterback?
There is already an established relationship between Rees and Penix that could help either arrangement.
Earlier in the season, Penix discussed the importance of his relationship with the offensive coordinator and how the two communicate throughout the week.
"We've been very close since he got here. It's always been, with the quarterback and offensive coordinator, y'all got to be hand in hand," Penix said.
Penix also explained that Rees encourages him to speak up about plays he does not like, allowing the coaching staff to adjust the game plan around his comfort level.
Rees has expressed a similar philosophy, emphasizing that he does not want to call a play his quarterback does not fully believe in.
"I never want to call a play that you don't have full belief or confidence in," Rees said.
That relationship could become increasingly important as Atlanta prepares for Minnesota and defensive coordinator Brian Flores. The Vikings present one of the league's more challenging defensive schemes, using pressure packages and disguised coverages to create problems for opposing quarterbacks.
With Penix needing to find consistency and the Falcons looking to turn around their season, having the right communication between the quarterback and offensive coordinator will be critical.
Rees' location might seem like a minor coaching decision, but it is another variable Stefanski is evaluating as Atlanta searches for answers offensively.
