title: 3 Changes Jesse Minter Must Make Immediately To Curb The Ravens' Six-Game Rot
full_text:
It would be nice if Jesse Minter could understand the situation he and the Ravens are in.
If he didn’t look glazed over and run over (by his players) on the sidelines every Sunday, that would be a nice start. If he found a way to win a football game and not allow most teams to hang 33-plus points on his defense, that would be fun for a change. If he found a voice and offered real accountability and didn’t come off as an overwhelmed functionary of the personnel department, that would be a welcomed wrinkle.
Any signs of growth, development and awareness from as an NFL head coach would be great. It might also, of course, force him into some tough conversations with failing general manager Eric DeCosta , who wanted him under his control but has undermined Minter, miserably, with this roster– both at the start of the season and by failing to get real at the trade deadline.
Minter’s job security must be in question and with this team likely to win no more than a game – two seems a stretch – from here on out, the rookie better find other ways to suggest and connote progress. The standings are not going to be his friend, and the people who hired him should have been fired years ago, but there is also mounting evidence to suggest this owner takes the easy way out and path of least work. In this case, that’s simply firing a coach and leaving the rest of his failing organization in place like this past January. Owner Steve Bisciotti has co-signed this aimless and feckless losing in a profound way.
"I'd probably keep a lot of the conversations between Steve and myself private,” Minter offered on Wednesday. “He's great. He's very supportive. Talk a lot; talk about a lot of different things. So I always appreciate our conversations. Leave it at that."
With the season running thin and nothing pointing in the right direction with this football team in any aspect, we have some suggestions for Minter on things to change ASAP, for this week at Houston, even before the looming bye:
If Adam Randall and Elijah Sarratt are not worthy of getting single snap, even on special teams, then it’s an indictment of everyone. The Ravens can’t beat anyone with their aging and bloated roster but also mastermind alleged-genius kid coordinator Declan Doyle can’t find any use for these players with an offense that is garbage as soon as he exhausts his early-game script?
There is no role in the screen game? Nothing? Team this bad doesn’t even need to get a look at a fourth-round pick or a fifth-round pick at the same time whatever is left of Mark Andrews continues to out-snap both rookie tight ends?
Doyle had the audacity to default to “player development” in taking vital blocking tight end Durham Smythe off the field in the home opener as Baltimore blew another big lead in defeat, and now the team is a laughingstock but the kids don’t need to be a point of emphasis? Make that make sense.
If you want to really have the bottom fall out as the weather turns and the stadium is about to be empty, mess around and become a joke stopping early down runs.
If you manage to run a defense that not only cannot stop the pass all season but then wilts in a massive way up front the first time you face volume on the ground, you are hastening your own demise. And, yeah, it’s going to mean you are slashing the role of some guys your bosses grossly misplayed but that’s coaching.
Trey Hendrickson on the field on early downs in divisional games against Pittsburgh and Cleveland will be brutal. Tampa will run all over him to. Houston will just throw the ball all over the place. But we know the hard-hat mentality that comes from December AFC North football and if Minter isn’t willing to adjust his run front and find ways to hold up without Tavius Robinson (IR) or the rest of the season and maybe without Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) for a while longer, it will definitely get uglier in Owings Mills.
He is utterly disconnected from this product and from reality up in the booth. He was supposedly gong to be willing to tinker and alter and be malleable as a first-time play caller. But the moment he looked good in the preseason opener that was enough to convince himself that being upstairs was the only way?
He seems to have little clue when his quarterbacks are being maimed up there. No idea how badly his offensive line is being whipped. He has the worst second half offense in the NFL by several metrics, and appears totally detached and says he wants to script the entire game.
Get him out of that comfort zone, get him interacting with players in the moment, on the sidelines, as humans – you know, looking in their eyes and all) – instead of cogs in part of his machine. Try something different to shake up how horrible your football team is after the half.
If this staff wants to curb the chatter about being one and done, and not answer questions about their job security and being on the hot seat down the stretch , then something new and different in their approach better show up, quickly.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The One Raven Truly Benefitting From Jesse Minter's Arrival
full_text:
The Ravens defense isn’t big on feel-good stories.
It isn’t big on anything good at all, at the core of the team’s six-game slide that is quite likely to run to seven against the potent Texans passing game on Sunday in Houston.
Head coach Jesse Minter has been totally overwhelmed to the point where his job security is being called into question and at the very least he should have divested himself of play calling duties (don’t worry, it’s coming) .
The highest-paid players have been failures by and large (especially alleged “closer” Trey Hendrickson) and now Kyle Hamilton is regressing, and Roquan Smith and Marlon Humphrey have been sunk costs for years. Oh, and the entire group of free agents brought into the $150M defense have been a collective and individual failure and the draft class hasn’t offered anything, either.
But there are strides made.
Linebacker Trenton Simpson has come along quite well and proven himself as an everyday player ( who needs a contract extension ) and perhaps could displace Smith next year. And one defender has made a true leap, threatening to thrust into a different stratosphere – 2025 second-round pick Mike Green. More than anyone else on this roster, he is making a significant breakthrough in his second season.
Green was asked to do way too much on early downs last season and was overextended as a raw rookie; exposed far too much against the run in a bad defense. Somehow, Minter’s defense is significantly worse than Zach Orr’s from 2025 despite all the resources poured into it. But Green is looking like the best young pass rusher the Ravens have produced since Terrell Suggs and certainly at least since Matt Judon.
He can’t anchor like Suggs and that isn’t a fair comparison, but Green has tapped into his strength and pliability and versatility this season, getting loose for inside pressures on twists and at times with pure tenacity. He has been focused and slippery and playing his best football now while so few around him seem to know what to do or where to be (especially in the second half).
Green is going to run away with the team lead in sacks and, with 7.5 already (no Raven had more than five last season), is on pace for a rare double-digit season in these parts. Since Suggs posed 11 sacks in 2017, Kyle Van Noy (12.5 in 2024) is the only edge defenders here to surpass 10.
“I'll say just first and foremost, just approaching every day with a clear mindset,” Green said Wednesday when asked what has helped him take the leap. “There's a lot going on for everybody in this building and what I try to do is to make sure that I'm just controlling what I can control and putting my best foot forward. So, just having that kind of mindset going into each day ended up helping me out a lot."
Green has more than twice as many sacks as anyone else on the team and has out-snapped Hendrickson the past two games, rightfully so. Green has more juice and energy and despite the proclamations about Hendrickson closing games he has no fourth-quarter sacks and just five pressures. Getting 50 snaps on Sunday was a nod to his development.
“It's been helping me out a lot,” Green said of the rising PT. “Even just from my first year, I think I played a good amount. I feel like once you get in a good rhythm and you get in a good flow of just how the game's going and the tendencies that your opponent typically does and things like that, it sets you up to play a little bit better. So, I think just overall just being able to go out there and play more snaps kind of gives you the confidence, and it gives you a little bit more time to be consistent."
Green registered two sacks against the Panthers on Sunday and had two less than a week prior, against the Chargers. Hendrickson has two in his Ravens career (he still trails Tavius Robinson, for second place, despite Robinson going on season-ending IR weeks ago).
Green ‘s average time to sack is extreme (4.16 seconds) and speaks to his motor and effort. He also has been fresher late in games. He leads the team with two fourth-quarter sacks and three QB hits in the final quarter.
He is far and away the most efficient edge player on the team. Green has those 7.5 sacks on just 23 pressures, an elite finishing rate (Hendrickson has two on 31 pressures. Green leads Baltimore with 13 QB hits; tackle Nnamdi Madubuike is second with nine.
He’s the rare positive this coaching staff can point to on any level, and he and Robinson should be the bookend starters next season despite Hendrickson’s bloated salary. Green is also one of the few players making defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver look sage. Weaver’s bold predictions about Humphrey and Smith from the spring are going to fall well short, but his prediction of 10-plus sacks for Green is looking pretty good.
“He shares his experience and what he thinks is going to work and things like that,” Green said of Weaver. “I like it a lot. He's played in the league. He's been to places that we're trying to go, and he knows a lot, especially on the defensive line. So, it's been great to have him around, and we appreciate him."
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Waive Struggling Return Specialist LaJohntay Wester After Final Straw
full_text:
The Baltimore Ravens announced a pair of roster transactions on Tuesday, and neither came as a surprise for different reasons.
The release of third-year quarterback Kedon Slovis, who had been serving as the emergency third quarterback for the past two weeks, might've resulted in him being re-signed to the practice squad had he not been claimed off waivers. The same can not be said for former starting return specialist LaJohntay Wester.
We have waived WR LaJohntay Wester and QB Kedon Slovis. https://t.co/cnZ4NuE7Sn
The Ravens parting ways with Wester comes off the heels of a disastrous outing by the second-year wide receiver in the team's 35-33 loss to the Carolina Panthers , in which his struggles fielding punts persisted in the worst way with two muffed attempts.
After the defense forced a three-and-out early in the second quarter, the first was recovered by the Panthers at the Baltimore 23-yard line, and it only took them three plays to get into the end zone for a go-ahead touchdown and then first of several lead changes in the back-and-forth affair.
It came as a huge surprise when the Ravens trotted Wester out for another opportunity later that same quarter, only to see him make the same mistake, but this time, he was fortunate that nickel cornerback Keyon Martin was able to fall on the ball at the Baltmore one-yard line before a Panther could recover it.
Those two colossal gaffes alone were at minimum a 10-point swing, and potentially a 14-point swing, in a game the Ravens lost by just two points. The Panthers scored as a result of the first, and the Ravens had to cover more ground on their final drive of the first half, which ended in a failed Hail Mary attempt from the Carolina 45-yard line, rather than a more manageable field goal or a closer shot at reaching the end zone.
Wester's short-lived tenure as a Raven began with a lot of promise after the 2025 sixth-rounder flashed explosive playmaking potential in his preseason debut as a rookie when he returned his second punt return for an 87-yard touchdown .
Through the first 10 games of his rookie campaign, he was still bringing the juice to the return game that Baltimore special teams has missed since the departure of All Pro return specialist Devin Duvernay. However, his decision-making and inconsistency when it comes to fielding punts have been a noticeable detriment to the team since he committed his second career muff in Week 11 of last year, which resulted in a lost fumble.
LaJohntay Wester 2025 Weeks 1-10 rookie season: 16.3 yard punt return average 1 fumble 0 fumbles lost Wester 2025 Week 11 - 2026 Week 11: 7.9 yard punt return average 5 fumbles 3 fumbles lost Wester never regained confidence after muffing a couple of punts at Cleveland. https://t.co/0Qmv3vyhRn
Wester was benched after the second muff, and the Ravens were bailed out from starting a later drive from inside their one-yard line a second time after second-year safety Malaki Starks failed to field a punt that rolled deep inside the 10-yard line and was downed by a gunner whose heel was luckily touching the goal line.
According to reports from the portion of Wednesday's practice that was open to the media, the Ravens had over half a dozen players fielding punts, and head coach Jesse Minter expressed confidence in their in-house options moving forward.
"I think we have a pretty good idea, but we'll kind of see how this week shakes out and see which direction we decide to go by the end of the week," Minter said. "It's always tough when stuff like that happens, but you just got to do what's best for the team."
Wester cleared waivers and officially ended his tenure with the Ravens after 28 career games in which he logged five receptions on six targets for 58 receiving yards as a pass catcher, 321 punt return yards and 625 kick return yards.
Moving on from him could open the door for fourth-round rookie Elijah Sarratt to finally be a regular active member of the roster on game days moving forward as both an option at punt returner, which he saw some preseason action at, and as a depth slot receiver option behind two-time Pro Bowler Zay Flowers.
In the same game in which multiple punt return gaffes cost them dearly, the Ravens got a much-needed boost from a different young receiver as a kick returner. Between Wester's muffs, underutilized third-year pro Devontez Walker took his third-career kickoff return opportunity 86 yards to the house for a go-ahead touchdown.
The incredibly clutch play accounted for over a third of Walker's 211 kick return yardage in the game and earned him the first AFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors of his career.
Touchdown Tez is the AFC Special Teams Player of the Week 🔥 @DevontezWalker pic.twitter.com/g9ZseaetE3
While that was the highlight of his performance against the Panthers, it wasn't the only impactful play of note. Walker added a 34-yard reception on his lone target of the game, giving him a career-high 245 all-purpose yards and making him the only player in the NFL to record 30-plus receiving yards and a kickoff return touchdown in a game this season, according to the Ravens communications department.
For inexplicable and blatantly inexcusable reasons, the 2024 fourth-rounder hasn't been regularly featured in the offensive game plan since entering the league, despite possessing game-breaking speed to take the top off of opposing defenses. Walker has shown explosive playmaking ability in limited opportunities with 12 catches on 21 targets for 22.2 yards per catch, five touchdowns and 266 receiving yards.
"When you get an opportunity, and you take advantage of it, there's definitely a path for more of that," Minter said.

He provides analysis, breakdowns, profiles, and reports on important news and transactions from and about the Ravens. His professional resume as a sports reporter includes covering local events, teams, and athletes in his hometown of Anchorage, Alaska for Anchorage Daily News. His coverage on the Ravens and other NFL teams has been featured on Heavy.com/sports, Maryland Sports Blog and most recently Baltimore Beatdown from 2021 until 2025.

title: Mark Andrews' Last 20 Games Have Been Nothing Short Of Disastrous For The Ravens
full_text:
In Week 10, with the Ravens playing on Monday night, out of nowhere during the broadcast came a report about Mark Andrews and a broken hand.
The tight end, who was leading all players at his position in false start penalties and had the highest drop rate as well, went on to have his first productive game, honestly, since September 2025, his first game over 50 yards receiving since then, and the hand, so the story went, has now good to go. Of course, Andrews has not shown up on an injury report and he hasn’t been wearing anything protective on his hand.
Maybe he was feeling better and maybe he wasn’t going to just go on being one of the most overpaid players in the NFL. Maybe, with each passing week, the ridiculous decision to extend his contract last December would look like an utterly foolish decision by a general manager, Eric DeCosta who has made such failures his brand .. Surely, Andrews was never going to look like half the player ex-Ravens tight end Isaiah Likely is week after week for the Giants, but at this point merely string together two 40-yard games would amount to significant progress.
… And nothing close to that came to pass..
Sunday’s debacle in Carolina was simply more of what ever week is for Andrews. A confounding display where he is asked do more than rookie tight ends Matthew Hibner and Josh Cuevas , and he offers precious little. It was another game where he simply did not show up in the passing game at all, he cannot do anything downfield, and he finished with two catches for two catches for 14 yards. The eight grabs for 82 yards vs the Chargers was the outlier, and it may prove to be for quite some time.
Andrews continues to exude rampant positivity in the face of a disaster season, but thinking he has the answers and can actually influence this offense would be silly at this point.
"I'm just fired up, man," he said after Sunday's setback." I am ready to go. I think for me, just playing with my heart, playing all I can and doing anything I can to help this team win is the main thing. And just being there for everybody. I just want to be able to do that."
This is no slump for Andrews; it’s the end of his tenure as a move tight end in the NFL. It’s been over and it is over, only the Ravens are going to be stuck paying him next year anyway with another $5M guaranteed on his deal (top seven at his position in average salary). He was paid like a top 10 tight end, but those days are long gone.
Andrews is going to end his career without every registering a playoff touchdown. Certainly his Ravens' career, with this team not sniffing the postseason anytime soon. And even with back-up quarterback Jacoby Brissett funneling the ball to tight ends, Andrews can’t do anything after the catch and he moves the chains on check downs and short passes and that’s about it.
Over his last 20 games, he's averaged three catches for 26 yards. Gulp.
He has just two touchdowns in his last 20 games.
He averages 2.1 yards after the catch in that span, and for the last two seasons , which is hard to fathom. He has caught just 63 of 91 targets in those games, despite his routes being pedestrian and high percentage by and large. He is averaging just 8.3 yards per reception.
He'll probably play more snaps and run more routes than anyone else at his position again Sunday. Nothing much ever changes in Owings Mills, and they refuse to get real about who they really are and how deep their personnel issues and coaching issues run.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Trey Hendrickson Isn't The Only Ravens Offseason Addition Failing To Deliver. He Has Company
full_text:
The Ravens are stuck with Trey Hendrickson.
They missed any chance to pawn him off before the trade deadline, and they will regret it , and they are stuck with another $30M fully guaranteed coming his way next season after getting nothing out of the $30M invested in him during this lost season. General manager Eric DeCosta has a failure offseason continuing a three-year debacle that should have cost him job in January when head coach John Harbaugh was fired.
He got nothing right, his offseason was doomed from the moment he pulled out of a Maxx Crosby trade and The Football Gods or karma have been kicking up every week since (or, well, it’s mostly just that he isn’t very good at this whole evaluating, negotiating, leadership thing). And no one, from an on-field standpoint, is going to embody this 2026 disaster as much as Hendrickson, who should honestly be doing far more standing on the sidelines as he gets attacked in the ground game with the weather turning.
They called him a $60M closer, and he hasn’t shown up in a fourth quarter all season and after six straight loses with rookie head coach looking overmatched all along, nothing Hendrickson does this season even really matters, now. Sad. But true.
With Hendrickson’s malaise getting more and more attention around the NFL, it’s as good a time as any to reflect on all the players brought in from outside the organization by DeCosta for this much-hyped defense and evaluate the evaluator. Hint: This ain’t pretty.
The defense is the biggest failure in the franchise and Minter can’t seem to do anything about it. His side of the ball was handed the preponderance of resources in free agency, and Minter is an alleged mastermind. so this should be keeping owner Steve Bisciotti up at night, and jobs should be on the line.
Key Stats : 2 sacks, 5 pressures in the fourth quarter, 12.7% pressure rate late five weeks
Verdict – F: He was supposed to be the guy who ended the fourth-quarter rot and turned this defense around and stopped all the blowing of fourth quarter leads. Doesn’t have a signature moment or game and has been increasingly invisible lately, except when getting exposed in the ground game. His "revenge" game vs. Bengals could not have been more of a dud.
Key Stats: 1 sack, 1 batted pass, 6 solo tackle, 28 snaps/game
Verdict – D: Hard to see him play out his age 40 season on a joke of a defense in a franchise hardwired to lose. Going to post close to 500 snaps if they keep this pace up, but with so few playmakers around him, the impact has been muted. He is an all-time great leader and exemplary human, but this DL has not been strong and now they are getting run on.
Key Stats : 6 GP, 1 Pressure, 16 tackles, 137.5 Passer Rating
Verdict – F: Will probably be out until the bye. Has not connected with any of the fellow safeties and communication issues are rampant. Showed up against the run and pass game with the Patriots but this has been brutal. Picked on when they do throw his way. Part of one of the worst secondaries in the NFL.
Key Stats: 103 Coverage Snaps. 97.9 Passer Rating
Verdict – D: Compared to last year, where he provided excellent bang for the buck, it’s an F. But, hey, he hasn’t been picked on as much as $19M corner Marlon Humphrey and he hasn’t needed Mayor Brandon Scott to rebuke him for offensive remarks about Baltimore, so we have to grade on a curve here. Even with Humphrey getting carved up, Minter hasn’t wanted to play him much and he’s fallen behind TJ Tampa now, too.
This was a total joke by the front office. Across the board. Every level. They got absolutely nothing out of the draft on defense – Zion Young (second round) has no pass rush and barely plays; Chandler Rivers hasn’t’ seen the field on defense in weeks – and you won’t find a bigger collective bust of new defensive coordinator plus lack of production from the players brought in during the offseason.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens' 5 Biggest Needs For 2027 (Excluding QB, Fingers Crossed)
full_text:
The Ravens refuse to acknowledge the depth of their problems.
Whether it’s failing general manager making silly buy-side trades at the deadline (and some that thankfully didn’t happen) and failing to unload contract of players who have no meaningful future here, or an overmatched rookie head coach dismissing calls to stop calling plays on defense in hopes he can grow into being an NFL head coach. Whether it’s refusing to bench underachieving veterans on bloated contracts who are hurting their product ($60M closer Trey Hendrickson, for instance) or choosing to make rookies healthy scratches every week despite the need to start seeing what they can.
It’s a woefully misguided organization and with six-straight losses and counting, it’s only getting worse. The biggest issue, of course, will be convincing two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson to stick around in 2027, and given what Lamar Jackson Entertainment has put on social media lately, that’s an uphill climb to say the least . It’s daunting all around, the head coach keeps talking and acting like someone who should be one-and-done, and this roster is in decay and needs an overhaul.
Even if you take quarterback out of the equation – which is impossible, but let’s do it anyway – there are glaring and massive needs facing this team in 2027. As it stands right now, here are their five biggest needs outside of QB, in reverse order:
Trading for Cam Jurgens was a failed stopgap measure . Thinking he is going to hold up for 2027 and play well while doing it would be based on pure folly; not game film here or in Philadelphia and not based on his medical history. Paying him $17M next year is a self-inflicted error but that’s GM Eric DeCosta’s brand, and this trade will haunt them.
They played a comp pick game picking up veteran center Ryan Neuzil, who has been riding the bench. Finding a long-term solution is vital; offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has been undermined by the rotating guards and shuffling offensive lines. Rookie guard Vega Ioane is still the best center on the roster, but they want him to focus on guard.
You can find plug-and-play starters on the second day of the draft.
Malaki Starks cannot handle deep duties in Minter’s defense and if he is married to split safety concepts , he better find a few guys who can do it. Free agent Jaylinn Hawkins has been a bust. Kyle Hamilton is a SAM linebacker.
It’s a pass-happy league and the Ravens have not been able to defend the middle of the field - short, intermediate or deep – since coordinator Mike Macdonald left after the 2023 season. This needs desperate attention and probably needs to be a proven veteran type if at all possible; this franchise stopped drafting or developing defensive backs with ball skills a long time ago.
Finally, Marlon Humphrey will be gone next season, along with a bunch of other cooked veterans on ridiculous contracts. But he’ll leave behind a $12M cap hit. Nate Wiggins has zero ball skills, Chidobe Awuzie won’t be back, and rookie slot corner Chandler Rivers never sees the field on defense despite Baltimore having the worst slot defense in the NFL … So yeah, this might be low because they need a handful.
Nice to see TJ Tampa finallly get to play and come up with their first pick by a corner all season, but this staff has shown no conviction in him.
This was allegedly a superpower for the Ravens and their wunderkind head coach . Oh well. More folly.
They tried to patch it up by keeping run-stuffer Broderick Washington around on a team-friendly deal and bringing back Calais Campbell for a second stint, despite being 40. They crossed their fingers that Nnamdi Madubuike would return to All Pro form after a neck injury negated almost all of his 2025 campaign.
And, worst of all, despite this being a lingering need DeCosta completely ignored it in any meaningful way in consecutive drafts that were loaded with DTs – one of which will go down as potentially generational. Madubuike as this point is a good player but might not be consistently great anymore, and he is only signed for one more year. Travis Jones is a nice rotational player but nothing more. This defense has lacked a spine for years, we already covered free safety, and Roquan Smith has been a marginal-at-best middle linebacker for years.
Better fortify the middle in a big way at the point of attack if this defense is ever not going to stink. (at least some youngsters are emerging on the edge).
Ronnie Stanley had a great career but he’s not going to be here by June 1 if this franchise has a clue. They should have drafted his successor by now and he is on borrowed time physically and is committing penalties in droves and the pass protection is going south. It’s time to move and this needs to a substantial commitment in terms of assets.
Not some hope-and-pray late round pick. If they don’t think enough of Carson Vinson to give him a run in a garbage season with journeyman Jacoby Brissett back there, don’t start selling parables about his potential and upside in the offseason. And the idea that Roger Rosengarten is a two-contract right tackle is in doubt; he can’t help on the blind side.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis: Biggest Winners, Losers and Role Changes From Week 11
full_text:
The Ravens results do not change.
They lose, week after week, as questions mount about just how overmatched this front office and coaching staff appear to be . It’s six straight games and counting and given the piercing issues in all three aspects of play there is no reason to expect that to change anytime soon. This franchise refuses to embrace its obvious rebuild and continues to keep players like Adam Randall and Elijah Sarratt inactive, while abstaining from letting youngsters like Carson Vinson and rookie tight ends Josh Cuevas or Matthew Hibner play as much as they should .
There were definitely some noteworthy trends with the snap counts however – that always tells the story of what coaches really think beyond what they say – and hopefully a thorough youth movement is unleashed amid this lost season in which the job simply appears too big for Jesse Minter; well, both jobs: head coach and defensive coordinator .
The questions are coming regularly now about Minter relinquishing play calling duties and, around the league, the chatter about him perhaps not being cut out to be a head coach is mounting. The Ravens faced some new personnel scenarios on defense with corner Marlon Humphrey suspended by the team for the game and top defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike out with injury.
TJ Tampa : Minter has been slow to embrace this former mid-round pick despite his body type seemingly a better fit in his zone-heavy schemes than other boundary options. Minter barely played him in the first half (six snaps), preferring veteran Chidobe Awuzie, but with the secondary starting to get lit up in the second quarter he made the switch to the youngster.
Tampa played 39 snaps on defense, by far his most under Minter and his most, period, since Week 5 of 2025. Tampa responded by getting into excellent train coverage on Tet McMillan and picking off a pass in the back of the endzone for the first interception by a Ravens corner all season. Even with Humphrey coming back, it would take a truly cowardly organization to sit him for Humphrey, but with Eric DeCosta in charge, well, don’t hold your breath .
“I thought T.J. took advantage of the opportunity to play more,” Minter said.” I thought, man, the play two plays before the interception, great play as well, particularly where they're at and just trying to throw like the run-pass option slant there. Great play by him there.”
Mike Green: The pass rusher is having a true breakthrough in Year Two, he’s headed for double-digit sacks, and he is out-performing $60M alleged “closer” Trey Hendrickson in a big way against the run and getting to the QB. Green out-snapped the big-ticket free agent again and v astly outperformed him.
Green played 50 snaps – tied for second-most of his career and most since Minter took over. He produced five tackles and two sacks and two QB hits and will continue to pace this edge group in snaps. He and Tavius Robinson should be the starters next season, but good luck dumping Hendrickson’s contract.
“He gives you everything he's got from a physical standpoint,” Minter said. “He strikes people in the run game. There are times where he's taking on a lot bigger bodies, and he's holding his own, and then he does things in the pass rush game where he works well with other guys. He works well within games.”
Ja’Kobi Lane: Receivers DeCosta drafts almost always stink, and the learning curves tend to be steep . The heady days of rookie offensive coordinator Declan Doyle being called a genius this summer and Lane being a preseason superstar seem long ago. After a very rough game against the Chargers Lane’s passing snaps were slashed from 36 to just 23 against the Panthers, he continues to struggle to find his way in this offense and we suspect the shift to more 12 and 13 personnel is on (more tight end emphasis). He did not have a target in the game.
Matthew Hibne r: The rookie tight end was the big beneficiary of Lane’s slashed role; but it didn’t turn into much. Hibner went from 22 snaps against the Chargers to 33 against the Panthers, but he isn’t really separating and the big-play potential hasn’t shown up since before Lamar Jackson got hurt in Week 4. He had two receptions for 12 yards and unlocking his YAC is a must. Jacoby Brissett loves throwing to TEs and the have to get this cooking.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Rookie Head Coach Jesse Minter Still Resisting Calls To Divest Play Calling Duties
full_text:
Ravens rookie head coach Jesse Minter, struggling mightily to manage games and on-field situations, while also suffering as a defensive play caller, nudged a bit on Monday when probed about his failures as a coordinator.
For the second time in his 12 regular-season weeks on the job Minter was asked at a Monday press conference about his willingness to relinquish play calling duties of what’s becoming one of the worst defenses in franchise history. And unlike the first time, he offered an actual response.
Two weeks ago, he blurted out, “No,” when the topic was first broached and now, with his team holding the worst second-half scoring differential in the NFL (-98) and his defense giving up 33 points or more in four of the last five games, Minter (4-7) deigned to show some understanding of why he was being questioned about Anthony Weaver potentially taking over play calling for him.
“Everything crosses my mind,” Minter said when asked about considering a change on the headset, “but I’m always going to try to do what I think is best for where we are right now.”
So, that was still a no, but not quite as resounding. And with a lot less sass.
And if the Texans smash Minter’s defense on Sunday for a seventh-straight loss – and there is every reason to expect that to be the case – he will invariably be asked about this again before Baltimore takes its Week 13 bye. His highest-paid players continue to fail at their jobs and players now speak openly about the lack of “trust” and “execution,” while Minter himself was already begging for “leaders” to emerge in his locker room by October.
Minter’s tone changed when asked about having arguably both the NFL’s worst second half offense and defense (30-year-old offensive coordinator Declan Doyle suffers mightily once off his early-game script). "clearly everything,” was his response in terms of what needs to change in that regard.
In general, Mnter has been short of specifics and devoid of corrections but heavy on trite colloquialisms about “sticking together” and everyone “in it together,” that are straight from the John Harbaugh/Jim Harbaugh playbook.
Now that teams aren’t just throwing the ball all over the field on an overmatched secondary that was supposed to be one of the best in the NFL, the run defense has become a significant issue. Minter’s alleged $60M “closer” Trey Hendrickson not only offers no late pass rush but is getting attacked in the ground game. Expect that to continue, with Minter unwilling to bench overpaid veterans to this point (struggling $19M corner Marlon Humphrey will return to practice to this week, Minter said, after being deactivated Sunday for disparaging remarks about Baltimore on his podcast).
The Ravens entered the season boasting about a defense that should be among the best in the NFL, propelling the team to its self-purported Super Bowl expectations, but the best Minter could muster Monday about where that standard is now was:
“We can be a serviceable, productive defense, but right now it’s too inconsistent." Good luck sending out those season-ticket renewals off that.
Minter did take blame, in a more straightforward sense, for botching a two-minute drill at the end of the game, keeping two timeouts in his pocket with back-up quarterback Jacoby Brissett under assault and wasting close to a minute of precious time.
In hindsight “banging” a timeout after a QB sneak would have been the better decision, Minter offered, as he weighed the need to save a timeout for a potential sack or negative play later in the drive. “You always want to try to keep one for that,” he explained.
The Ravens have lost seven straight games in a season just once before, 2007, when Super Bowl head coach Brian Billick was fired. Minter’s defense has a lot in common with that one , and he continued to carry the look of someone who might not be cut out for a second year on the job.
“We haven’t played the level of defense I think we’re capable of,” Minter said.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: The Ravens Created A $60M Problem With Trey Hendrickson They Won't Be Able To Fix
full_text:
The Ravens have a $60M problem on defense.
Well, in full candor, they have a $160M problem on defense.
Their team-record payroll on that side of the ball is producing almost no results – Sunday was another debacle – calling the job security of rookie head coach Jesse Minter already into question. They have no discernable strengths as a defense, getting gutted on the ground now that teams have finally started running the ball on them after being content to merely pick apart Minter’s dime coverages for most of the season .
Trey Hendrickson was the handpicked solution to years of defensive rot. Failing general manager Eric DeCosta – after bailing on an agreed to trade for Raiders elite run stuffer/pass rusher Maxx Crosby for alleged medical concerns  – then pretended he was planning to land Crosby and Hendrickson . In reality, he thought Hendrickson was a value-play, with his age, injury history and inability to stop the run leaving him with a shallow free-agent market.
And it turns out the market was right, and DeCosta was wrong (he has been consistently wrong for years on end in a way that should have had him fired when head coach John Harbaugh was let go ), And Hendrickson, about to turn 32, is a $60M (fully guaranteed) waste. He’s nothing close to the “closer” he was anointed to be by DeCosta and Minter. He has added nothing at all – no juice and no jam and damn sure no sacks – to their atrocious fourth-quarter defense and his ineffectiveness is a hallmark of their six-game losing streak.
Signed to put the team’s Super Bowl pursuits over the top, he is already a bust. These Ravens will "compete" to be possibly the worst defense in franchise history in 2026 , and won’t be contending for anything in 2027, either, with a rebuild imminent. This is a sunk cost, already. (Oh and the Bengals defense and pass rush is markedly better without him and hold-ins, as evidenced when they crushed the Ravens).
Literally nothing about how Hendrickson was billed has showed up. Thankfully, Mike Green is taking a leap in year two, but Hendrickson should be making way for him.
Hendrickson was somehow more effective while playing through a painful finger injury than he’s been since the surgery to repair it . He is the face of Minter’s shortcomings – nearly as much as Minter himself – and his recent suspect play would call for his benching if this was a meritocracy (but it’s a fiefdom for the front office where their litany of egregiously overpaid “stars” - Hendrickson, Roquan Smith, Marlon Humphrey, Mark Andrews – get unfettered opportunities to play because anything else would make an overmatched front office look even more so).
As bad as the Hendrickson signing has looked since around Week 3, it’s truly starting to tug at whatever fabric of this defense remains; opponents will be running 30 times or more on this failing front, and Hendrickson will be further exposed and the defense will suffer even more because of it.
“Going against him when he was with the Bengals I think he is a very good pass rusher, and that's it,” former Ravens coordinator Wink Martindale told me on “The Daily Flock Show” a few weeks back. “That's what he is. I think he's a third down, second-and-long type guy because he wants to get to the quarterback.
“The problem is … They're not getting leads where people have to throw the ball to get back in the game (with Lamar Jackson hurt). And when you get selfish, and you're rushing a passer on a run play, it exposes players. And that's what I'm seeing. That's what I'm seeing with him.”
Quite a rebuke, but a truthful one. And it’s really showing up now.
What Have You Done For Me Lately?
In the last five games, no longer wearing an apparatus and without his hand heavily bandaged in recent weeks, Hendrickson has three total pressures in the second half of games. That is a putrid 6.7% pressure rate for “the closer” who is being paid to be in the 18% and up stratosphere. Consider the following:
Last 5 Games (2nd Half): 3 Press/45 Rush (6.7% Pressure Rate)
Season (4th Quarter): 0 Sacks, 2 QBH, 3 Hurry, 6 Press (10.7% rate)
Since Surgery (6 Games): 1 Sack, 5 QBH, 11 Hurry (12.4%)
But that’s only half the problem.
Baltimore has allowed 300 yards rushing the last two weeks, and Minter has been unable to curb any issues thus far. With Hendrickson on the field the last two weeks, opponents have rushed 43 times for 234 yards and two TDs. He can’t set the edge; he is getting stiff-armed and cast aside and that 5.5 yards/carry average is going to go up. Watch.
On Sunday Baltimore had a pathetic 45.5% run defense success rate with Hendrickson on the field. He will be targeted on the ground - like Humphrey is through the air - by speed and power backs. And with Kyle Hamilton playing more deep safety (and struggling), he’s offering less thump around the line of scrimmage; Hamilton missed four tackles Sunday and Hendrickson will get picked on even more.
Baltimore’s best all-around edge – Tavius Robinson on a bargain-basement rookie deal – is on season-ending IR. Hendrickson not only isn’t a strength; he’s a liability. A franchise even somewhat serious about curbing its rot and beginning an obvious rebuild  would have peddled Hendrickson’s contract for anything possible at the deadline as we pointed out , but instead DeCosta bought older players and gutted future drafts .
More Zion Young – a second-round edge project DeCosta took over a bevy of starting center options – might help against the run, but he has limitations and he’s actually been playing less lately, despite facing run-heavy teams. Young shows up in short-yardage packages but it’s worth noting teams can pick on those personnel groups on the air, as a 128.4 opposing passer rating (vs. mostly weak QBs) with Young on the field speaks to. Jeepers.
Quite a quandary, and one this coaching staff and front office will be ill-equipped to solve. They create problems; they don’t fix them.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Ravens Unprecedented Second-Half Failures Call Jesse Miner's Job Security Into Question
full_text:
If only NFL games were a half-hour long, the Ravens’ novice coaching staff might have a fighting chance.
Of the many reasons why neophyte head coach Jesse Minter looks overwhelmed and overmatched every week – devoid of cogent defensive adjustments as a play caller let alone understanding game- management, timeouts, two-minute drills and obvious benchings/substitutions – the second-half failings stand tall. It’s part of why longtime Raiders team president and NFL analyst Amy Trask called for swift changes to the coaching staff – including potentially both coordinators  – and it’s a big reason why the Ravens have been so non-competitive for much of their six-game losing streak that should have Minter’s job security under immediate review .
The Ravens (4-7) are doing to finish with consecutive losing seasons for the first time since their first three years after moving from Cleveland and no team they ever hyped this much immediately fell flat on its face like this one. They are fallacy propped up only by Lamar Jackson’s singular brilliance, and Minter set about blowing 10-to-13-point leads with regularity even before Jackson got hurt the first time (they have taken a double-digit lead six times and handed it back five times and lost four of those games).
Minter’s defense is the biggest issue with the franchise ( historically bad ), despite a team-record $160M sunk into that side of the ball after the anointing of $60M “closer” Trey Hendrickson in March (two sacks) – even bigger than the loss of two-time MVP quarterback Lamar Jackson. Journeyman Jacoby Brissett has revived a moribund pass attack, but Minter got outclassed by the previously winless Chargers at home on a Monday night – by the worst offense in the NFL – and then gave up 35 points to the tepid Panthers despite being staked to a quick 12-point lead .
Choking leads is his brand, having no in-game solutions has defined Minter and 30-year-old offensive coordinator Delan Doyle (worst second-half offense in the NFL), and it’s all only getting worse with a schedule ahead in which even the Buccaneers are likely to be favored over the Ravens despite Baltimore being at home and coming off a bye before that Week 14 game.
They may not win another game, there should be sweeping changes from team president and general manager all the way down , and the inability to put out any fires through the course of a game means Minter likely does not merit another season at the helm for a team that crowed about “competing for championships” starting immediately upon hiring Minter according to team president Sashi Brown (who was arguably the worst GM in NFL history running the Cleveland Browns).
Minter not calling a timeout with Brissett under assault on a two-minute drill was bizarre – “Obviously, in hindsight, I could have banged a timeout there and calmed it down a little bit," he offered after the game. But his lack of defensive awareness and acumen is the biggest problem. As to blowing another late lead: “It was just a poor job by me, and that's what it was.”
Been that way all year, and the brutal second-half splits must make everyone question everything inside The Castle. That is why Minter is perceived by execs around the NFL as having to be on the hot seat. That is why his job security is already rightfully being questioned. This is a total mess, and the Ravens need a total rebuild, and Lamar quite reasonably may not want to stick around for it .
This staff can only show up for half a game, on both sides of the ball. That will get you exposed every week and will likely send the Ravens to the bye off seven straight losses (only happened once before here; 2007, which got Super Bowl winning head coach Brian Billick fired).
Here are the Ravens’ rankings in the second half:
169 Points Allowed : 2nd Most NFL (DAL)
71 Points Scored: 2nd Fewest NFL (PHI)
-98 Points Differential: Worst in NFL
Held 6 10+ Leads : Blow 5 (2-4)
The offense has plenty of excuses – no Jackson, a terrible offensive line that changes by the week, other injuries. Not the defense. All the major assets were put into that side of the ball – despite Minter (supposedly) being able to do more with less (he did with Chargers as simply a play caller under a strong-willed head coach with very streamlined duties).
Minter’s unit has been healthy, he proclaimed Hendrickson’s early-season finger surgery to be a springboard to dominance ( failing pressure rate since ) and he got elite defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike back for major neck surgery; turns out former DC Zach Orr did an infinitely better job with a lesser roster without Madubuike last season than Minter could dream of doing this season.
Here are the second -half defensive rankings:
Net Yards/Pass: 7.8/att. (28th)
Opposing Passer Rating : 112.9 (30th)
Completion %: 72.1% (31st)
Pass Yards: 1405 yds (30th)
Plays Allowed 20+ yds : 21 (25th)
Pressure Rate : 35.3% press (21st)
And in the last two weeks, with teams finally seeking volume on the ground against Minter’s defense, the Chargers and Panthers rolled up over 300 yards rushing. Expect more of the same as the weather turns and teams find more and more ways to exploit this coaching staff, and certainly not fewer.
Jason has covered sports professionally for newspapers, websites and broadcast networks since 1996 and have covered the NFL extensively for The Washington Post, CBS Sports and The NFL Network from 2004-2025.

title: Who is Halftime Performer for Bills vs. Chiefs Thanksgiving Day Game?
full_text:
Buffalo Bills fans should be spending the day stuffing their faces with turkey during Thanksgiving Day , but at night, they should all be glued to their televisions to watch as the Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs .
This will be the final game of a holiday triple-header, and will be the fourth time the Bills have been in action on Thanksgiving since 2019. While they're no strangers to playing on this holiday, this will be the first time that Buffalo will host a game.
The game itself is going to offer plenty of excitement with two of the best teams in the NFL squaring off. That said, Thanksgiving games are a major event which usually come with a big halftime show. That was the case for the Detroit Lions, who had the Wu-Tang Clan perform at their halftime show while hosting the Chicago Bears. The Dallas Cowboys, who usually offer great shows, had Miranda Lambert for their meeting with the Philadelphia Eagles.
So who is it that the Bills turned to for their show?
The performer for the Bills vs. Chiefs halftime show will be none other than The Goo Goo Dolls. Formed back in 1985 by lead vocalist and guitarist John Rzeznik and bassist Robby Takac, the Buffalo-based band rose to prominence in the 1990s and had songs like "I'm Awake Now" make it to the soundtrack of  "Fallin' Down" in 1991. They were also featured in the 1993 Pauly Shore film Son in Law soundtrack.
Their song "Name," which was from the album "A Boy Named Goo" led to their biggest mainstream success and led to a change in the band's tone as they leaned into a softer alternative sound. Arguably their biggest hit was the song Iris, which was released in 1998 and was featured in the City of Angels soundtrack. That song was also featured during a montage during the final game at the old Highmark Stadium.
The Goo Goo Dolls have remained tied to the city of Buffalo and performed during intermission of the Buffalo Sabres vs. New York Rangers Winter Classic at Citi Field on January 1, 2018. They also announced the Sabres' first-round draft pick during the 2025 NHL Draft.
Fans were hopeful the band would perform at their home opener during the second week of the 2026 season as they played their first home game at the New Highmark Stadium. That didn't happen, but this might be an even better option.

title: Bills' Thanksgiving Stat Predictions for James Cook, DJ Moore, Josh Allen vs. Chiefs
full_text:
It's the Buffalo Bills ' seemingly annual regular season showdown with the Kansas City Chiefs, and, this time, the AFC juggernauts take center stage on Thanksgiving night.
While poor weather, including potential heavy rain, is in the forecast , the Bills' offense should still be able to find a way to score close to their 31.3 points per game average.
Buffalo scored 39 points against the Cincinnati Bengals in the snow last December. In 2024, the Bills posted a 35-10 victory over the San Francisco 49ers in a snow-covered field.
While running back James Cook has shown the ability to cook in bad weather games, don't underestimate the Bills' passing attack in inclement weather. Quarterback Josh Allen threw multiple touchdown passes in each of those aforementioned snow games.
Some may say the predictions are a bit optimistic, but here are statistical achievements that Allen, Cook and DJ Moore should hit against the Chiefs on November 26.
Bills' head coach Joe Brady said that Allen's lack of rush attempts against the Dolphins had nothing to do with the team's Week 11 game plan. The Chiefs, however, weren't buying it , calling it more than an unplanned anomaly.
It's hard to imagine seeing anything other than a version of Allen Unleashed in a primetime game against a prime opponent with sky-high stakes . The ultimate dual threat quarterback should be expected to use his legs to move the chains whenever the situation presents itself on Thursday night in Orchard Park.
Allen has broken 40 yards rushing only twice this season, but both performances were against top-tier opponents. He rushed 14 times for 69 yards against the Detroit Lions in Week 2 and totaled 121 yards on 10 carries against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 5.
Including playoff meetings, Allen averages 50.6 rushing yards per game for his career against the Chiefs. He has four TD rushes over the last three  head-to-head regular season matchups with Kansas City.
The unprecedented streak continues, or so we think it will. Surpassing Hall-of-Famers John Riggins and LaDainian Tomlinson last week, Cook became the first player in NFL history to rush for 75+ yards and score a touchdown in nine consecutive games.
Although it may appear overly ambitious, especially considering the Chiefs will likely gear up to stop the run, Cook looks good to reach his weekly rushing average (106.0) on Thanksgiving. Going against Top 10 run defenses in the Los Angeles Rams and Minnesota Vikings, on the road nonetheless, Cook rushed for 111 and 107 yards respectively.
Look for the Bills to pound the rock early and often with Cook, attempting to set up the pass while wearing down the Chiefs' defense.
He's starting to heat up after his connection with Josh Allen was temporarily interrupted by injury . Moore has gained at least 90 yards receiving each of his past two games. He has a touchdown reception in three of four games coming out of the Week 7 bye.
Moore has played in eight games, leaving two of them early due to a shoulder injury. In five of the six games he's finished, he has gained at least 67 yards receiving. He's surpassed the 80-yard mark in four of those appearances.
The Bills have shown the ability to pass the effectively in poor weather before as Josh Allen's arm strength gives them an advantage over most opponents in such a setting. Furthermore, Moore has been good on screen plays, which could play more of a factor in wet, windy conditions. He has enough in his arsenal to carry him over his 58.3 yards per game season average.

title: Four Players Who Could Tilt Thanksgiving Matchup vs. Chiefs in Bills' Favor
full_text:
Thanksgiving is finally here , and the three “Fs”—family, food, and football—will take center stage within several households around the country today, particularly in and around Western New York.
Arguably the most highly-anticipated game on both teams’ remaining schedules this season, the upcoming matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park is certain to provide plenty of touchdowns and turkey legs throughout the evening.
But, will the Bills be able to walk away victorious in front of their home crowd in what is their first ever home game on this particular holiday?
Well, although it will be easier said than done, history does seem to be on the side of Buffalo’s quarterback Josh Allen when it pertains to playing Chiefs’ quarterback Patrick Mahomes in the regular season . . . it’s usually just the playoffs that have been the hangup.
So, with that in mind, it’ll be interesting to see if that history repeats itself or not when kickoff time comes around at 8:20 p.m. ET.
Here are four Bills’ players who can help Allen get the job done once again in primetime against Mahomes and Co.
All eyes will be on starting running back James Cook III at the beginning of the game—and for good reason considering his recent record-breaking streak of performances —but it could be another player in Buffalo’s backfield that plays a big role in deciding the outcome of the game against Kansas City.
And, veteran third-down specialist Ty Johnson just might be that other running back, especially considering he’s coming off one of his best performances of 2026 last week against the Miami Dolphins where he had a season-high seven receptions on eight targets for a total of 55 yards, which is his second-highest receiving output of the season.
Although Johnson has only nine carries all season long, he’s currently fifth on the team in receiving yards ( 269 yds ), total receptions ( 25 catches ), and total targets ( 26 targets ) despite only playing in eight games so far this fall, and he’s proven to be a reliable safety valve for former 2024 MVP gunslinger Josh Allen.
And, considering the weather is expected to be less than ideal under the primetime lights, Allen might not be able to push the ball down the field as much as he would like to against Kansas City, so Johnson could be in line for a large role on dump-offs and designed screens again this week.
If he’s able to turn supposed short gains into much larger ones, then it could provide the Bills’ offense with enough of a spark in the inclement weather, especially if it’s tough sledding to start.
For as much talk as there has been surrounding Chiefs’ veteran tight end Travis Kelce entering the Thanksgiving matchup tonight, there’s seemingly been the complete opposite amount of buzz around Bills’ tight end Dalton Kincaid heading into the game.
Whether it be because of his recent issues with thumb and ankle injuries—which caused him to miss last week’s game against Miami—or his inconsistent play as of late, Kincaid has definitely fallen off from the trajectory that he seemed to be on during the month of September when he tallied 263 of his 487 total yards this season in just the first three games alone.
And, with that said, the former 2023 first-round pick must get back on that track instead of continually sliding off the rails like he has at times this season.
Although listed as questionable entering the game , one would hope the playmaking tight end would be able to suit up for this pivotal AFC matchup .
If he does, then it’ll be imperative that he be more than just a glorified decoy. Buffalo’s offense is in desperate need of another top option in the passing game other than wide receiver D.J. Moore, and Kincaid has always been talked up as the player to do it.
Well, in spite of the lopsided loss last week, Arizona Cardinals’ star tight end Trey McBride hauled in nine receptions for 54 yards against Kansas City on Sunday, and Atlanta Falcons’ tight end Kyle Pitts ( 4 rec., 50 yds ) also reached the 50-yard mark the week before.
So, needless to say, there’s hope that Buffalo’s top tight end can do the same if healthy enough to be active.
Entering September, no player outside of veteran pass-rusher Gregory Rousseau received more buzz inside and outside of the Bills’ facility than second-year defensive lineman Deone Walker.
And, although his numbers in the box score might not totally show it, Walker has lived up to the hype so far this fall in terms of making his presence felt along Buffalo’s defensive front.
However, with a big game against Kansas City in primetime now on tap, the Bills surely could use a little more of his presence felt on the stat sheet, as well.
The 6-foot-7, 331-pound defensive lineman has just one sack on the season, which came way back in Week 1 against the Houston Texans, and he hasn’t recorded a tackle behind the line of scrimmage since before the bye week.
Buffalo is going to need Walker to feast in the backfield just a little bit more in the biggest of moments moving forward down the stretch, and there’s no better time to get started than tonight on Thanksgiving against Kansas City.
Sometimes, football is simply about being more physical than the opponent. And, other times it’s like a chess match.
Thursday night’s meeting between the Kansas City Chiefs’ potent offense—led by future Hall-of-Famers Andy Reid and Patrick Mahomes—and the Bills’ seemingly revived defense—guided by first-year NFL coordinator Jim Leonhard and defensive captain Terrel Bernard—is sure to be a mixture of both.
However, as has been stated since the bye week, there are some questions that remain in Western New York about the opposite side of the ball from quarterback Josh Allen.
Have Buffalo’s recent defensive performances been merely fool’s gold ? Or is it the start of something special ?
Well, Bills Mafia and the rest of the NFL world are about to find out a little bit more regarding that very topic, and the aforementioned Bernard will be in the center of it all from his inside linebacker position at Highmark Stadium.
Bills On SI already covered how Leonhard has fared against Mahomes during his time spent on the defensive staff of the Denver Broncos, so it’ll be interesting to see how well Bernard can orchestrate his plan of attack in primetime.
If Buffalo is able to keep Kansas City’s top-ranked offense (396.9 YPG) under control, then the veteran linebacker will deserve a lot of credit for getting his teammates lined up in the right spots more often than not.

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Kansas City Chiefs Week 12 Expert Pick Roundup
full_text:
History will be made this week as the Buffalo Bills will host the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.
While the Bills have played in 11 games on Thanksgiving Day , this is the first time they will be at home for the holiday.
The game itself will be full of intrigue as two of the top teams in the AFC will square off in a game that will have huge implications on the AFC playoffs seeding. Both teams come in on a winning streak, but the Bills' recent wins haven't inspired much confidence.
Buffalo has faced multiple backup quarterbacks, and while they did what good teams should do and won each time, they apparently didn't win convincingly enough. Over the past three weeks, the Bills defeated the Miami Dolphins 26-9, the New York Jets 31-12, and the Minnesota Vikings 23-6 and kept all from scoring touchdowns. Still, they enter this game with no shortage of doubters, which we see in our weekly NFL expert pick roundup.
Most of the experts are in agreement here, with the Chiefs holding a significant edge in the roundup.
While many experts seem to be swayed by Buffalo's soft schedule, they're overlooking the fact that Kansas City has had a favorable stretch lately as well. The Chiefs have beaten the Jets, Atlanta Falcons, and Arizona Cardinals over the past three weeks. Before that, however, they dropped consecutive games to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, which were the last two teams they faced with winning records. Those losses haven't drawn nearly as much scrutiny as Buffalo received for beating Miami by 17 points, which is odd.
That said, the Bills could have an edge in this one. The weather is going to be ugly and while Kansas City boasts a strong rushing attack, they will be without Kenneth Walker III . Buffalo is fully healthy at running back and James Cook is playing phenomenal football once again. Josh Allen will also be ready to use his legs after not rushing once in Week 11. The advantage on the ground should be enough for Buffalo to secure a narrow win.
Prediction : Bills 23, Chiefs 19

title: Four Things Other Than Josh Allen That Bills Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
Buffalo Bills ' fans have plenty to be thankful for on this Thanksgiving 2026.
Naturally, quarterback Josh Allen, a five-time NFL MVP finalist, is atop the list, but today we look beyond the Bills' elite field general.
As the Bills (9-1) prepare to entertain the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at 8:20 p.m. ET tonight in a NBC holiday special, here are four items the Mafia is thankful for this season.
It's easy to take James Cook for granted when the quarterback is Josh Allen, but the Bills' former second-round pick is arguably the premier running back in the NFL.
The reigning rushing champion, who needed only 10 games to break the 1,000-yard barrier (1,060), enters Week 12 with only 38 fewer yards than league leader Jahmyr Gibbs (1,098). Cook and Gibbs are the lone two running backs with 200+ carries thus far.
In the Week 11 win over the Miami Dolphins, Cook became the first running back in NFL history to produce 75+ rush yards and 1+ touchdown in nine consecutive games. He surpassed Hall-of-Famers John Riggins and LaDainian Tomlinson.
Having developed into a true bellcow, Cook brings a dynamic element to the Bills' offense. He's willing to pound the rock, and his explosive ability makes him a threat to score from anywhere on the field.
The Bills' defense was in desperate need of an overhaul this past offseason, and first-year head coach Joe Brady wisely gave the keys to former NFL safety Jim Leonhard .
Right off the bat, Leonhard brought a fresh new energy and philosophy. He changed the defense to a 3-4 base formation while making versatility a core component.
It wasn't pretty early on as Buffalo was gashed through the season's first six games heading into its Week 7 bye. Although they've faced lesser quarterbacks over the past four weeks, the Bills' defense has been practically impenetrable.
Opponents have failed to score a touchdown against the Bills in 43 consecutive possessions. Furthermore, they've held the opposition to under 130 net pass yards in three of the last four games.
Special teams are one-third of the game, and the Bills' units are operating at an elite level across the board.
While Buffalo was solid in this phase of the game last year, veteran coordinator Jeff Rodgers has essentially optimized the operations on specials. The Bills are second overall in the special teams DVOA metric, behind only the Minnesota Vikings.
Kicker Tyler Bass leads the NFL with 101 points scored buoyed by a 96 percent field goal conversion rate. Return specialist Greg Dortch has the fifth-most punt return yards (185) and ninth-most kick return yards (699).
In coverage, the Bills have allowed the fewer punt return yards (46) against in the NFL. They rank 10th in opponent's kick return average (26.6).
Special teams could prove to be the ultimate decider when the Chiefs visit on Thanksgiving night. Kansas City is 30th in special teams DVOA.
We all loved The Ralph for one reason or another, but the Bills' new stadium has been a blessing for Western New York and its beloved football team.
Highmark Stadium, which opened to heavy fanfare , has been just what Buffalo needs in terms of a home venue. The game day experience is a much more comfortable one for fans, and the grass field is stunning to see in person.
Sure the video boards are puny, and there are a couple areas that need some extra dressing, but, overall, Highmark Stadium is solid. Most importantly, it ensures the Bills will remain part of the community for generations to come.

title: Bills vs. Chiefs Weather Forecast Presents Major Concerns For Week 12 Game
full_text:
When the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills meet for the Week 12 game at Highmark Stadium on Thursday, they won't just be battling each other.
It's that time of the year again when weather is going to start being a bigger factor in games on a more regular basis, whether it's wind, precipitation, cold temperatures, or a combination of those factors.
Thanks to a storm rolling through Buffalo , the weather could be a major factor during a game in which the Bills are looking to keep their grasp on the No. 1 spot in the AFC while the Chiefs are looking to snatch it away with a win and Denver Broncos loss.
Here's what we know going into kickoff on Thursday night.
UPDATE: Here's the latest weather update from Meteorologist Kevin Roth of MySportsWeather.com with hours to go before kickoff.
"Worst of the weather in Buffalo looks like it comes between 5-8pm," he said. "Still likely pouring pretty good in the first half too. Could be much improved by the 2nd half."
According to MySportsWeather.com , the forecast calls for a 100% chance of rain and sustained wind of 13 MPH with gusts upwards of 35 MPH. Neither team will be getting a break with the temperature, which will be around 37 degrees.
Meteorologist Kevin Roth of MySportsWeather.com offered the following analysis of what to expect throughout the contest:
"The worst of the weather comes pregame, but the heavy rain likely continues into kickoff as well," Roth said. We could see a bit of clearing opening up during parts of the game, then more rain building in late. I'd say this looks like the best possible outcome here, and yet it's very wet."
"Temperatures are in the 30s all game as well, so it's a nasty cold rain (but not quite cold enough for snow)," Roth added. "Winds are ripping too, sustained 15-20mph with gusts at 35mph. The design of the new stadium, a partial roof which covers most of the seats but not the field, should help protect against some of the wind impact, but will do nothing to stop the rain."
As Roth notes, Highmark Stadium is specifically designed to help with windy conditions, but the key word here from Roth is the stadium will help with "some" of the wind, not all of it.
Let's start with the wind, which Roth estimates could sit around 15-20 MPH. Wind can start impacting the ball in the air in that range, and gusts upwards of 35 MPH would be a major issue.
As a result, quarterbacks Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes and their pass-catchers could all be negatively impacted, as could kickers Tyler Bass and Harrison Butker, both of whom may not receive as many field goal chances, and especially not long attempts.
Of course, rain is another issue that can impact the game.
Wet weather makes it harder to hold on to the football, which can lead to more drops, fumbles and botched snaps, and it obviously doesn't help footing, either, so players can't explode as much as they'd like and will fall more often while running.
All of this favors Bills and Chiefs running backs, including James Cook and Emmett Johnson, because teams tend to lean on the running game more in circumstances such as these.
If the weather ends up being as bad as it looks like it's going to be, there may not be a lot of scoring on Thursday night.

title: Bills' Final Week 12 Injury Report: Dalton Kincaid One of Four Starters Questionable vs. Chiefs
full_text:
The Buffalo Bills focused more on rest and recovery than actual physical practice reps during the short week leading into their highly-anticipated Thanksgiving night home game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
The Bills didn't hold a full practice, opting instead for only meetings on Monday and back-to-back walkthroughs on Tuesday and Wednesday. As a result all practice participation is estimated.
Buffalo started the week with 14 players officially dealing with injuries. Nine of those players, which include defensive lineman Ed Oliver and right tackle Spencer Brown, were tabbed as full participants on Wednesday and have been cleared for the 8:20 p.m. ET holiday kickoff .
Meanwhile, the remaining five injured players, four of whom are starters, are questionable to face the Chiefs on November 26.
On offense, it's tight end Dalton Kincaid and right guard O'Cyrus Torrence. On defense, there's uncertainty around the availability of cornerback Christian Benford, inside linebacker Dorian Williams and rotational lineman TJ Sanders.
Kincaid, Benford, Williams and Sanders all missed the November 22 game against the Miami Dolphins.
On a positive note, Brown, outside linebacker Greg Rousseau and backup safety Damar Hamlin all progressed from limited to full participation during the short week and are ready to go against Kansas City.
Kincaid saw only two more snaps after injuring his thumb against the New York Jets on November 15 when he got tangled up with linebacker Demario Davis on a third-quarter red zone play.
After not practicing in Week 11, the Bills ruled the tight end as doubtful to face the Dolphins. When asked if Kincaid was close to being available for the November 22 game, head coach Joe Brady said "yeah."
Kincaid also apparently told reporters on Tuesday that he should be out there come Thursday night.
Benford strained his groin in the second half against the Jets in Week 10. He left early and did not return.
After missing three consecutive practices in Week 11, Benford was ruled out for the Dolphins game . He kicked off the short week by logging a DNP before progressing to limited participation.
With wet conditions expected, and only 11 days since the injury, Benford may find himself scratched again this week. Returning in fewer than two weeks from a mild groin strain seems a bit overly ambitious.
Torrence came out of the November 22 win with an ankle injury, but it isn't apparent when, during the game, it occurred. He was estimated as limited all three days.
It's worth noting that the right guard has never missed a start since being drafted in 2023. Should he be unavailable, veteran Austin Corbett will presumably start in his place.

title: Sean McDermott Is Gone, And Two Bills' First-Round Pass Rushers Are Thriving
full_text:
Could it simply be a matter of coincidence?
There are plenty of arguments that suggest former Buffalo Bills ' head coach Sean McDermott, and his conservative nature, ultimately prevented quarterback Josh Allen from reaching his full potential , but what about the pair of first-round defensive studs drafted two years apart?
The Bills used the No. 9 overall selection on Houston defensive tackle Ed Oliver in 2019 and the No. 30 overall pick on Miami defensive end Greg Rousseau in 2021.
While Oliver and Rousseau were certainly not first-round busts, their production always seemed to come up a little shy of expectations based upon the raw talent they showed coming out of college.
Both men proved serviceable enough to warrant lucrative four-year contract extensions , but neither has even managed to sniff a Pro Bowl appearance.
This year, however, and particularly this month, Oliver and Rousseau are both on a tear operating in new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's 3-4 rooted scheme.
The former leads the NFL in raw pressures thus far for the month of November and the latter already activated a $500,000 incentive for total sacks by making two last time out against the Miami Dolphins.
"Now you're seeing teams really have to figure out what to do, right? When Greg's rushing the quarterback at the level he is, and now Ed's really picked it up," said Leonhard.
After a career-high 9.5 sacks in 2023, Oliver totaled only 3.0 sacks and 13 quarterback hits through 14 games in 2024.
Oliver's 2025 was spoiled by injuries. First, his ankle was stepped on during a September practice following the Week 1 win. Then, his regular season was ended by a biceps tear in his second game back from the ankle injury. He registered 1.0 sack in all three of his appearances.
While Oliver has fought through minor ailments this season, and has only one-half sack, he's managed 11 quarterback hits over seven games. Over three November games this fall, Oliver has generated a league-high 22 quarterback pressures ( per PFF ).
“I think he's playing aggressive," said Leonhard on Monday. "He's really forcing the issue with offensive linemen. We've been able to get him in some situations where he's had some one-on-ones, and I would say he's more decisive than he was earlier."
Rousseau, who reached his previous single-season high for sacks (8.0) in both 2022 and 2024, has shattered his career highs already through only 10 games this year.
In addition to recording 10.0 sacks , he has registered 29 quarterback hits. Rousseau's previous best was 24 quarterback hits over 16 starts two seasons ago.
Greg Rousseau is giving QBs nightmares pic.twitter.com/RjtdM7XIRo
"Feel like I got the same approach for the most part that I've had over the last few years," said Rousseau amidst preparations for the Thanksgiving night game against the Kansas City Chiefs. "I feel like stats don't always tell the full story. It's great to get the double digits, it's a shout out to the back end, shout out to the coaches, shout out to just the other three guys rushing with me on the field during those times."
While Oliver leads the NFL in pressures this month, Rousseau ranks fifth overall having generated 18 pressures.
