title: Five Key Things to Know About Chiefs vs. Bills in Week 12
full_text:
It’s been a bounce back season for a franchise that reached the Super Bowl five times in seven years from 2019-25. Much went wrong for the Kansas City Chiefs a year ago. The results were six straight losses to close the season and a 6-11 campaign. Andy Reid’s team missed the postseason for the first time since 2014, and quarterback Patrick Mahomes was not on a playoff team for the first time during his impressive career.
Meanwhile, the Buffalo Bills made their seventh straight postseason appearance in 2025—the longest active streak in the league. Once again, Josh Allen and company failed to reach the Super Bowl. Hence a head coaching change.
Joe Brady’s club enters this clash with a six-game winning streak and a 9-1 record—both marks tied for the best in the league. On the other hand, the 8-2 Chiefs have righted the ship after consecutive losses to the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos, and are on a three-game roll.
What a way to wrap up the Thanksgiving tripleheader !
Bills. Chiefs. 2021 Divisional Round. A forever legendary ending 🔥 pic.twitter.com/WKVXaiMAB5
Including four postseason battles, including a pair of AFC title clashes in 2020 and 2024, the Bills and Chiefs are meeting for the seventh consecutive season and the 11th time dating back to 2020. The clubs have split their previous 10 clashes, but there’s a catch. Buffalo’s five victories have all come in the regular season, the last two at Orchard Park, while four of Kansas City’s wins are of the playoff variety.
The most recent clash came last season at Buffalo in Week 9, which resulted in a 28-21 Bills’ victory.
The rookie Emmett Johnson has his fourth-straight game with a touchdown AZvsKC on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/KtsWXC5Q74
This offseason, Kansas City signed Super Bowl LX MVP Kenneth Walker III. The ex-Seahawk has excelled, but will miss his third straight game this week. Enter rookie Emmett Johnson , who’s rushed for 100-plus yards in two straight contests. The Chiefs are averaging 134.2 yards per game rushing (5th in the NFL).
Back in 2024, only two teams in the league came up with more takeaways than the Bills (32). A season ago, that number decreased as the club forced only 20 turnovers. However, 10 games into 2026, Buffalo has totaled 15 takeaways (8 interceptions, 7 fumble recoveries)—nine on those in their last four outings.
Josh Allen throws his second interception of the first half! Zayne Anderson comes up with the pick! pic.twitter.com/uxvDTJF9R0
Patrick Mahomes has thrown 13 touchdown passes and zero interceptions in the team’s last four games. This season, he’s totaled 22 scores through the air, lost only one fumble, and turned over the ball only five times in 10 contests. It’s hardly a surprise that the Chiefs lead the NFL in total yards per game (396.9).
Buffalo began the season by not committing a turnover in either of their first two games. Since then, the Bills have given up the football a combined 16 times in their last eight contests—giving up the pigskin at least twice in six of those games. Quarterback Josh Allen (9 picks, 1 lost fumble) has 10 of those miscues.

title: How Panthers Have Emulated 49ers’ Offense & Why It’s Hugely Important for the Future
full_text:
It's been an up-and-down season for the Carolina Panthers , who are 5-5 with clear holes on the roster, yet are in first place in the NFC South anyway. The defense is still a major work in progress, and the Panthers haven't won more than two games in a row, but one bright spot has emerged.
The offense has taken a step forward, now ranking 10th in the NFL at present, and showing growth from its biggest stars. Chuba Hubbard has been outstanding this season, having a career year thus far.
Through 10 games, Hubbard has eclipsed 1000 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. The only other Panther to do so is Christian McCaffrey, who's now on the 49ers.
McCaffrey has sustained his success from Carolina and brought his production to a real contender, linking up with one of the best play callers in all of football, Kyle Shanahan.
Under Shanahan, the 49ers have had one of the best offenses in the NFL, and that hasn't changed this year, as the 49ers are No. 1 in scoring offense. That offense shone against the NFL's best defense in the NFL, scoring 35 points against the Minnesota Vikings.
Carolina's offense seems to take influence from the 49ers, especially with assistant coach Darrell Bevell on staff, who was under Mike McDaniel, who is from the Shanahan tree.
That influence will be extremely important soon, as the Panthers play the Vikings in Week 13.
ESPN's Ben Solak dropped his seven things he thinks he knows entering Week 12. One of those seven things was that the 49ers exposed the formula for attacking the Vikings' defense.
Running condensed formations, using the RB in the passing game, and throwing quick passes between the numbers. All things that the 49ers excel in, that Carolina does as well.
Minnesota's defense is ultra-aggressive and will bring the blitz early and often, so quick throws and passes to the running back in the flat will be key to keeping Carolina on schedule and sustaining drives.
With Hubbard's success this season, the formula is certainly feasible. That doesn't mean Carolina will execute as well as San Francisco did; Carolina has the No. 10 offense in the league, compared to San Francisco's No. 1.
That said, it's still the only game plan thats dominated Brian Flores' defense this season, and Carolina has the pieces to be able to try to succeed in similar fashion.
The game will be ugly, just as Minnesota wants it to be, but now, after Week 11, we know that the Vikings' defense can be exploited. Now the only question is whether Carolina can execute for four quarters to do so.

title: Panthers Can Deliver Major Blow to Buccaneers' NFC South Hopes With One Win
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are in a good spot to win the NFC South title once again, but they can’t start planning their celebrations just yet.
Currently, Carolina is 5-5 and leads the division by two games. Last week, they defeated the Baltimore Ravens 35-33. Meanwhile, Tampa Bay and New Orleans both lost. Atlanta was on its bye.
With seven games remaining, they have ample opportunity to secure the division title. Monday’s game against Tampa Bay is critical to achieving that goal.
Winning divisional games is crucial, and Carolina can do that on Nov. 30 when they play the Buccaneers on Monday Night Football.
This is a game Carolina would especially like to win, given that earlier this season they were beaten by Tampa Bay 43-13. At the moment, Tampa Bay owns the head-to-head advantage over the Panthers, so a win by Carolina would even the season series and remove that advantage.
The Next Gen Stats model by NFL.com suggests that prior to Week 12, the Panthers had a 56% chance of winning the NFC South. With a win over Tampa Bay, that number increases to 80%. Conversely, with a loss, it decreases to 41%.
If Carolina wins, Tampa Bay would be three games back with six games remaining on the schedule. At that point, the Buccaneers would be under considerable pressure to make up ground during the final weeks of the regular season.
In addition to Tampa Bay, the other two NFC South teams Carolina still has left to play are New Orleans and Atlanta.
Carolina already won both of those games earlier in the season. The Panthers played New Orleans in Week 10 and won 20-17. They played Atlanta in Week 2 and won 34-3.
Should these final games decide the divisional tiebreaker, the current division records are important. Carolina is 2-1 against NFC South teams, Atlanta is 1-2, New Orleans is 0-2 and Tampa Bay is 2-0.
Carolina can’t take any of these divisional opponents for granted just because of their records. This late in the season, teams are looking to overtake each other in the division.
Carolina has four games outside the NFC South remaining as well. They play Minnesota on the road in Week 13, and then host Cincinnati in Week 15.
They will play in Pittsburgh against the Steelers in Week 16 and in Carolina against the Seahawks in Week 17. These games will be further tests for the Carolina team to see if they can win games that will, more likely than not, come down to the final play.
The Panthers have shown they can compete in difficult situations, particularly with Bryce Young leading the offense late in games. However, the defense will need to become more consistent, and Carolina cannot continue relying on late-game heroics to get through the schedule.
Carolina can't depend on Young to bail them out each game. The defense came up with a big play to end the game against the Ravens to secure the win, but they gave up 421 total yards in the process.
To further increase their lead on the other teams in the NFC South, Carolina will need to win on the road against Tampa Bay in the next game. Currently, Carolina has a two-game lead on the rest of the division and has three games left against NFC South opponents.
Winning on Monday night would provide some breathing room for the Panthers’ playoff hopes.
No divisional team is out of the playoff race yet, but Carolina can make things very difficult for the rest of the division over the next few weeks.

title: Bryce Young Just Landed Ahead of Patrick Mahomes in Surprising NFL Ranking
full_text:
Bryce Young may not be considered one of the top quarterbacks in the NFL, but a recent statistic should bring some comfort to Carolina Panthers fans.
Steven Patton, a football analyst, posted a leaderboard ranking quarterbacks by their expected points added (EPA) per completion. Young is currently ranked seventh with an EPA of +0.79. Others further down the list include Patrick Mahomes (+0.76), C.J. Stroud (+0.74) and Dak Prescott (+0.73).
Young's placement on this list may seem ironic, considering some of the media coverage and commentary directed at the quarterback since he was drafted in the first round by Carolina. However, this is more evidence of the positive progress Young has made this season. His development has been a recurring topic, including in a recent look at Young's regression and continued progress.
EPA per Completion Leaders: 1. Trevor Lawrence (+0.94) 2. Brock Purdy (+0.88) 3. Drake Maye (+0.83) 4. Josh Allen (+0.81) 5. Jordan Love (+0.80) 6. Jared Goff (+0.80) 7. Bryce Young (+0.79) 8. Patrick Mahomes (+0.76) 9. CJ Stroud (+0.74) 10. Dak Prescott (+0.73) pic.twitter.com/00FVfTJoDc
Some of the other players ranked on Patton’s leaderboard include Brock Purdy at second with an EPA of +0.88, Drake Maye at third with an EPA of +0.83, Josh Allen at fourth with +0.81, and Jordan Love and Jared Goff at fifth and sixth, respectively, with an EPA of +0.80 each.
Young being ranked seventh is extremely positive, considering some of the quarterbacks mentioned previously on the list are widely considered among the best in the NFL.
One statistic used to evaluate quarterback performance is expected points added (EPA). Rather than just looking at standard quarterback stats like completions and yards, this statistic analyzes how each play changes a team's expected scoring outlook.
It’s important to note that this ranking doesn’t measure EPA on each quarterback dropback, which includes pass attempts, sacks and scrambles. Patton’s ranking of Bryce Young is specifically for completions.
This is one advanced quarterback statistic in which Young ranks ahead of several of the best players in the NFL.
Through Week 11, Young was among the best in the league with 2,651 passing yards and 18 passing touchdowns. He also had the 32nd-best completion percentage at 61.1%.
Young’s EPA per play ranked 17th, while his QBR ranked 15th.
Though those numbers don’t seem very impressive on their own, they provide some additional context for Young's ranking on Patton’s list.
Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns in Carolina’s 35-33 win against the Baltimore Ravens.
That win helped the Panthers extend their win streak to two games and keep first place in the NFC South. Young has been clutch in the second half of games, making key plays that have helped the team win. More of those plays will be needed down the stretch. His ability to protect the football has also been a positive, as one recent statistical breakdown highlighted another encouraging part of his game.
In Young’s previous matchup against the Buccaneers, he was held to 163 passing yards, with one touchdown and two interceptions in a 43-13 loss.
This rematch provides the Panthers with an opportunity to extend their lead in the NFC South, and Young will need to improve on his previous performance to outduel Tampa Bay’s pass rush.
The EPA per completion ranking isn't the be-all and end-all of Young's standing among NFL quarterbacks. For now, though, being listed ahead of Patrick Mahomes, C.J. Stroud and Dak Prescott is a positive development Young can build on.
Young doesn’t need to outperform his opponents in every metric, but he must continue to make good decisions with the football and protect it while giving the team the big plays it needs on third and fourth down.
The Panthers' quarterback situation will likely be less of a liability moving forward if Young continues to play the way he has recently.

title: Have the Panthers Played on Thanksgiving? Full History and Potential Future
full_text:
On Thanksgiving, the NFL reigns supreme. It's been that way forever, and there are more games on the holiday than ever before. You can conceivably sit at the television and watch football the entire day, like it's a Sunday slate.
The Carolina Panthers aren't involved, though. They are going to play a rivalry game on Monday night rather than a holiday game on Thursday. So, Panthers fans will have to settle for the Lions, Cowboys, and other teams.
The Panthers have played on Thanksgiving once, and it was one of the most iconic games in their history. They dominated the Dallas Cowboys in 2015. The Cowboys, famously, play every Thanksgiving, so beating them on "their day," so to speak, was huge .
The undefeated Panthers won 33-14. Cam Newton threw for 183 yards and added 45 and a touchdown on the ground. The Panthers' defense picked off Tony Romo three times, and Kurt Coleman and Luke Kuechly each returned one for a score.
Perhaps that's why the Panthers haven't been on the holiday since. They crashed the party too hard. For now, that is the lone appearance on Thanksgiving, which is honestly pretty strange. Only the Jacksonville Jaguars (also a 1995 expansion team, weirdly) have never played. Otherwise, the Panthers have the least amount of Thanksgiving games.
Could they play on Thanksgiving again? Absolutely. Someday, they probably will. However, it is very strange that they haven't played on the holiday since 2015. In 11 seasons since then, they've faced the Cowboys six times, yet it never ends up on Thanksgiving.
The Panthers have faced the Lions six times as well, but it has never been on Thanksgiving. Carolina has also never gotten lucky with being picked as one of the non-guaranteed teams. The Lions and Cowboys play on the day every year, but other teams get picked by the NFL.
So, it stands to reason that one day, you'll be able to watch the Panthers on Thanksgiving. But it is odd that it has been so long since the last one and could be a while. The Panthers will play the NFC North sometimes and get the Lions added to the schedule some years. The same goes for the NFC East and the Cowboys.
So, when that happens, the Panthers might just get lucky and get to grace the Thanksgiving game for the second time in franchise history.

title: 7 Things the Panthers Should Be Thankful for in 2026
full_text:
It's Thanksgiving, an NFL holiday at this point. And while the Carolina Panthers don't have a game today, they do have plenty to be thankful for this time of year.
Maybe Bryce Young isn't the top-five QB he played like for the first quarter of the season and change, but he is still a good quarterback. The Panthers should be thankful he really blossomed and is having a career year, because it makes a difficult extension question a lot easier to answer.
The Panthers have had a gaping black hole at tight end for years. Darren Waller's late arrival really changed things. He allowed the Panthers to have a weapon at the position, which also opened things up for everyone else. Both Mitchell Evans and Tommy Tremble have been good, and Waller's late arrival to training camp is arguably the key to it all.
Where would this Panthers' defense be without Devin Lloyd? He has been a ridiculously good signing, and for less than expected, too. That aggression paid off, but it's not all. Cutting Trevin Wallace (a move we criticized at the time) was smart, and replacing him with Bobby Okereke was brilliant. Getting Tyrel Dodson on the practice squad was just the cherry on top.
Far be it from us to celebrate someone else's downfall, but this was a move the Panthers arguably needed to make long ago. We've heard the excuses plenty, but Evero just wasn't getting it done. We're confident he will bounce back elsewhere, but it wasn't working with the Panthers, and it was a needed firing.
It sounds crazy now, but plenty of folks (us included, at times) thought the Panthers should trade Chuba Hubbard and roll with Jonathon Brooks and Rico Dowdle. When it became clear they weren't going to trade him, people still wanted to keep Dowdle. Hubbard responded with a career year as the dominant RB1 while Brooks got hurt again.
Our money would've been on Sam Hecht being the surprisingly good late-round pick for the Panthers. Instead, Zakee Wheatley forced his way into the starting lineup and earned a PFF grade among the best rookies . Not just late-round picks or Panthers rookies, but all rookies. He's been excellent. A diamond in the rough.
Dave Canales and Bryce Young didn't mesh well. And while Canales still has his issues as a coach despite losing play-calling, the offensive execution is better than we could've expected. Idzik is very far from perfect, but he helped unlock this offense and Young, doing things Canales likely never would have done.

title: Panthers' Chuba Hubbard Reaches Christian McCaffrey Territory With Historic Season
full_text:
Chuba Hubbard is having a standout season and has recently been recognized for his accomplishments, with comparisons being made to one of the best running backs in Carolina Panthers history.
Hubbard reached a franchise milestone in the game against Baltimore on Nov. 22. With his performance, he became the second player ever, along with Christian McCaffrey, to record 1,000 yards from scrimmage and 10 touchdowns through the team's first 10 games of a season.
Novig on X also reported that Hubbard and McCaffrey are the only two players in franchise history to achieve these feats.
PANTHERS HISTORY! 🚨 The ONLY players in Carolina Panthers history to record the following through the team's first 10 games of a season: 1,000+ Scrimmage Yards 10+ Touchdowns Christian McCaffrey Chuba Hubbard pic.twitter.com/sNIs4ngGA4
Through the first 10 games, Hubbard has gained 831 yards rushing and 247 yards receiving, giving him a total of 1,078 yards from scrimmage and 11 total touchdowns, nine of which were rushing scores and two receiving scores.
Hubbard's last two games have been particularly impressive, with his performance against the Baltimore Ravens being his best of the season. That game also helped Carolina pull off a comeback win. Against the Ravens, Hubbard carried the ball 27 times and gained 120 yards and two scores. Against New Orleans the previous week, he rushed for 92 yards and added 80 receiving yards.
With Hubbard gaining 120 of the Panthers' 147 rushing yards against Baltimore, he gave the team a major boost in the running game and helped Carolina pull off the come-from-behind win.
Carolina has shown confidence in Hubbard's ability to lead the backfield, even with questions surrounding the team's running back depth, as discussed in this l ook at the Panthers' stance on Hubbard with Jonathon Brooks nearing a return.
It's a big deal that Hubbard's name is being mentioned in the same breath as McCaffrey's. During his time with the Panthers, McCaffrey was named a first-team All-Pro in 2019, and rightfully so. He was one of the best offensive players in the league that season and established himself as one of the NFL's most dangerous dual-threat running backs.
Like McCaffrey, Hubbard's success this season has earned him a spot in the team record books. McCaffrey was more productive overall during his time in Carolina, but Hubbard is now putting together a season of his own that deserves recognition.
The Panthers' decision to move forward with Hubbard also looks better considering why letting Rico Dowdle leave in free agency may have been the right move.
Hubbard has quickly become a focal point of the Panthers' offense this season, and his ability to run and catch the ball gives the team some stability amid inconsistent offensive play.
When the Panthers take on the Buccaneers on Nov. 30, Hubbard will have another opportunity to add to his season stats. With another strong performance, he has the potential to further help the Panthers' fight for the top spot in the NFC South division.

title: 3 Reasons the Panthers Won’t Be Embarrassed by Buccaneers Again
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers have their biggest game of the season on Monday. A primetime, divisional showdown on the road against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
This is the Panthers' final primetime game, completing the trifecta of playing on Thursday, Sunday, and now Monday Night Football on ESPN. Entering Week 12 at 5-5, the Panthers have a two-game lead atop the NFC South, with both Tampa Bay and the New Orleans Saints losing on Sunday.
Tampa Bay is widely regarded as the next-best team in the division, which isn't saying much. That said, being swept by the Buccaneers is a nightmare scenario for the Panthers and needs to be avoided at all costs.
Carolina has found life as of late, winning two straight and moving to 5-5 on the season. Now that momentum has to continue, and theres plenty of reason to believe it can continue against the Buccaneers on Monday. Here are three reasons why Carolina will remain competitive against Tampa Bay on the road.
Against the Ravens, Young was elite under pressure , completing 10-of-15 passes for 173 yards and 2 touchdowns. His passing yards under pressure are a career high for Young, and he'll need to maintain that type of accuracy against the Buccaneers.
Tampa Bay ranks No. 7 in the NFL in pass-rush win rate; they will be pressured early and often. Carolina will be better prepared after what should've been a wake-up call in Week 7.
The run defense isn't fixed, but in two of interim defensive coordinator Todd Wash's three games at the helm, it's been better.
Against the Denver Broncos and New Orleans Saints, Carolina allowed just 126 rushing yards total and gave up 2.6 yards per carry. It's just a two-game sample size, but that's a massive improvement and suggests the change in defensive coordinator has been the right move so far.
The most embarrassing part of Carolina's Week 7 loss to the Buccaneers was that the Panthers allowed 43 points, with Baker Mayfield completing just 7 passes for 64 yards and 1 touchdown.
It seems highly unlikely that Carolina is that inept at run defense again. That said, there will be crucial moments when Baker Mayfield has to beat Carolina with his arm, and so far this season, the Tampa Bay pass offense has been putrid.
The Buccaneers are the NFL's 32nd-ranked pass offense, which is dead last. Carolina recently got reinforcements back in the secondary, with Will Lee III and Mike Jackson back in the lineup. Those additions will be key to limiting a struggling passing game.

title: Dave Canales’ Jonathon Brooks Admission Raises Questions on Draft Pick and Future
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers are anticipating getting Jonathon Brooks back soon. The oft-injured running back had surgery earlier this season, and the Panthers opened the return window on November 11. They had three weeks from then to actually activate him.
In the past, that would have been considered a big boost. When Brooks finally got healthy enough to make his NFL debut in 2024, there was plenty of excitement. Then, when he was ready to go in Week 1 of this season, the hype was massive.
This time, though, Dave Canales had a strange admission about Brooks' role on this team and it raises plenty of questions.
Lost in the shuffle of a pretty exciting and crucial win on Sunday was the fact that Trevor Etienne had a really solid day as the backup running back. He had only a few touches, but he did well with them.
He's also been pretty great, excluding a bad choice to let the first punt of the game roll, on special teams all season. He and Tre Tyus, another running back, have been really good on returns this year.
That, according to Dave Canales, makes it very difficult to find a place for a healthy Jonathon Brooks. He has to be activated in about a week, but the Panthers don't seem to have a spot for him.
Dave Canales: Trevor Etienne’s production and Tre Tyus’s special teams value making it challenging to find a spot for Jonathon Brooks, whose return-from-IR window is open for another 8 days. pic.twitter.com/1qfOg7nXA8
Brooks is a talented player, but he doesn't fill a need right now. Etienne is both a return man and a receiving back out of the backfield. It would seem that, for now, Brooks lost his spot to Etienne.
This raises all sorts of questions. The simple fact that the head coach is wary about where to put him speaks volumes about his high draft selection and his future with the team. Brooks' contract ends after next season. Is there any world he gets extended?
Dan Morgan has generally drafted pretty well during his tenure, but he got off to an abysmal start. Just look at the 2024 draft class:
Is it crazy to say that Smith-Wade is the best player there? Legette is healthy but running zero routes. Brooks can't stay healthy and lost his position to a fourth-round running back. Sanders has been healthy scratched every week but one.
Brooks was arguably the high-profile addition. The ACL injury dropped him to the second round, but he was a first-round pick before that. The Panthers seemed to think they got a steal, but he has not been on the field much and hasn't made an impact.
It's troubling for a player the Panthers invested so much in, to say the least.

title: Baker Mayfield's New Contract Could Create a Major Offseason Dilemma for Panthers
full_text:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are in the NFC South division with the Carolina Panthers. The Bucs just signed quarterback Baker Mayfield to a three-year, $165 million contract.
The Buccaneers signed Mayfield to the extension on Tuesday, Sept. 8, averaging $55 million per year.
The Panthers are still considering their options with Young. He has played better than expected this season and has put himself in a good position to negotiate a contract with the team.
Mayfield's contract could serve as a comparison for future contract negotiations between the Panthers and Bryce Young.
Young completed 22 of 30 passes for 254 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday’s 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens. Young has thrown for 2,651 yards and 18 touchdowns with seven interceptions in 10 games this season.
Bryce Young, the fourth-year quarterback for the Carolina Panthers, had another great game Sunday. There are still many areas in which Young can improve, but the Panthers have seen enough to pick up the fifth-year option on his contract for the 2027 season.
The average annual value of Baker Mayfield’s new contract is $55 million. As long as Young continues to develop as Carolina believes he can, the Panthers could be looking at a similar commitment in the future.
The Panthers have some time to decide on an extension for the fourth-year quarterback, as they exercised his fifth-year option for the 2027 season earlier this year.
The Panthers don’t have to rush into signing Young to a long-term contract extension. He could become even more valuable to the team as the market for quarterbacks increases over time.
Young has shown improvement in several areas since late last season, and the Panthers believe he can be the franchise quarterback for several years to come. In addition, the price for a franchise quarterback could increase as the Panthers compete in the NFC South.
But I’m not saying that Young should make $55 million a year. All I’m saying is that Baker Mayfield’s contract with the Buccaneers can be used as a comparison in future contract negotiations with the Panthers.
After making so many investments to try to find a franchise quarterback, the Panthers must wait and see if Young can develop into that player and then make the right decision about his contract.

title: Panthers Catch Major Break After Jalen Coker Injury Scare Against Ravens
full_text:
The Carolina Panthers received some encouraging injury news on Monday f ollowing their 35-33 win over the Baltimore Ravens on Sunday. Wide receiver Jalen Coker was hit hard in the fourth quarter and was taken to the medical tent to be evaluated for a concussion.
Coach Dave Canales provided more good news on Monday, revealing that Coker had been cleared through concussion protocol. He will be available for the Panthers’ Week 12 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Monday night.
Dave Canales: Jalen Coker has been cleared, so he's not in the concussion protocol entering Week 12.
Coker was taken to the locker room for evaluation after getting hit by linebacker Roquan Smith late in the fourth quarter. He had just caught a 6-yard pass on Carolina’s go-ahead drive.
The Panthers were able to hold on to the lead and seal the win, but losing Coker for an extended period of time would create more issues for an offense that has struggled to be consistent in the passing game.
Coker had some big plays prior to his injury, including a 35-yard reception in the first quarter that set up Mitchell Evans’ touchdown on the next play. He finished the game with 4 catches for 47 yards.
The third-year wide receiver has been a steady contributor for the Panthers this season, catching 35 passes for 440 yards and 3 touchdowns in 11 games. Only rookie Tetairoa McMillan has more receptions than Coker for the Panthers this season.
This is great news for the Panthers, who are set to play the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Tampa on Monday night. This is also a divisional game, which the Panthers can use to increase their lead in the NFC South division as they look to secure a playoff spot in the latter part of the season.
The Panthers are currently two games ahead of the Buccaneers in the NFC South division standings. They can add to that lead in Week 12 when they play Tampa Bay on Monday night.
With Coker back in the fold, Carolina’s offense will have another weapon at its disposal and Young another quality target to throw to. The Panthers will look to build off of their impressive win against the Ravens on Sunday in order to carry that momentum into their next game against the Buccaneers on Monday night.
The Panthers are trying to maintain as many offensive players as possible for the remainder of the season, and keeping the wide receiver healthy is great news for Carolina.

title: Why Fumble in Bears-Lions Thanksgiving Game Was Ruled a Safety
full_text:
There was a wild play at the end of the first half of the Week 12 game between the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears.
With the Bears up against their own goal line with a little over one minute remaining, quarterback Caleb Williams fumbled the ball and it ended up going into the end zone.
In an attempt to prevent the Lions from recovering and scoring a touchdown, right tackle Darnell Wright smacked the ball out of the end zone and received a penalty as a result, which the Lions accepted, leading to a safety.
Here's why Wright was penalized and why the play was ruled a safety.
Even though the ball wasn't recovered in the end zone, it was still ruled a safety because Wright was flagged for illegal batting in the end zone.
Lions head coach Dan Campbell had the option to accept the penalty and take the safety, or he could have declined and gotten the ball at the 15-yard line.
"Oof. Caleb Williams coughs up the ball after a 3rd down pressure gets home while trying to avoid getting sacked for a second play in a row. Darnell Wright slaps the ball forward to get it out of the end zone. Lions recover at the 15-yard line and decline the spot and accept the safety. Smart play by Detroit given how far out the ball was," ESPN's Courtney Cronin wrote.
Campbell chose to take the safety in order to give his team a chance to score another three or seven points before halftime on top of the two points Detroit received for the safety.
And the decision by Campbell paid off, as the Lions drove down the field to cash in on their extra opportunity before the half to grab a 19-10 lead going into the second half.
The fumble was the second of the game for the Bears, who also lost the rock on their first offensive series when Colston Loveland lost the ball after it was punched out by Lions edge rusher Derrick Moore.
The nine points Detroit put on the board before the half was a big swing, as the Bears took back momentum after falling behind 10-0 and had a chance to double up with an end-of-half drive and the first possession in the second half.

title: Will Cole Kmet Return This Season? Colston Loveland Injury Puts Bears TEs Room in Peril
full_text:
The Chicago Bears' tight ends room is in serious trouble after the team lost Colston Loveland due to an injury in the first half of the Thanksgiving Day game against the Detroit Lions.
Loveland suffered a knee injury on the Bears' second drive of the game and after leaving the field, he was carted off the field and into the locker room.
Not long after that, Loveland was ruled out with his knee injury and it isn't looking good initially, as not only was he ruled out quickly, Loveland looked dejected while on the cart and was in tears, according to CBS' Tracy Wolfson.
With Loveland hurt, the Bears are seriously thin at tight end, but not only because of Loveland's injury, but because of the one to Cole Kmet, also.
Unfortunately, Bears tight end Cole Kmet is not expected to return this season after he suffered a knee injury in Week 7 .
After that game, head coach Ben Johnson confirmed Kmet will miss the remainder of the campaign.
"Bears TE Cole Kmet will miss the rest of the season with a knee injury," The Chicago Tribune's Sean Hammond relayed.
"He’s everything we want to be about here. He’s going to be sorely missed. He’s Chicago. He’s been here his whole life. He’s a big part of our heartbeat. It stinks. It does. I hate it for him," Johnson said of Kmet to reporters.
Loveland is a top-flight pass-catcher and Kmet is a strong pass-catcher and a great blocker, so losing them hurts the Bears' offense in multiple ways.
The Bears only have two healthy tight ends on their active roster in Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson, and one on the practice squad in Qadir Ismail, who will likely get promoted after Loveland's injury.
However, none of those guys can do what Kmet and Loveland can do on a football field, so there is no replacing either one.  Carlson and Ismail have very limited skill sets, and Roush has seen no shortage of struggles as a pass-catcher and blocker in 2026.
The Bears like to use a lot of 12- and 13-personnel, so Johnson might have to adjust things on offense if his remaining tight ends aren't effective enough when on the field.

title: Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Inactives: Who's in, Who's Out For Week 12
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions have released their list of inactives ahead of kickoff of the Thanksgiving Day contest.
For the Bears, we already knew three of the players who would be inactive, a list that includes cornerback Kyler Gordon, safety Elijah Hicks and running back Roschon Johnson, all of whom were ruled out on Wednesday.
The Bears had two players listed as questionable in cornerback Tyrique Stevenson and linebacker D'Marco Jackson. Both are active for Chicago.
As for the Lions, they ruled out cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. and defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard on Wednesday and Gill-Howard has since been placed on injured reserve with his season-ending knee injury.
The two Lions players listed as questionable, safety Chuck Clark and edge rusher DJ Wonnum, are both inactive. Wonnum is the Lions' sacks leader this season and Clark wears the green dot, so their absences are huge blows to Detroit's defense.
Now, a look at the full list of inactives for both teams.
Bears inactives: CB Kyler Gordon, S Elijah Hicks, RB Roschon Johnson, QB Case Keenum (emergency third QB), DL Jayden Loving, OL Jordan McFadden, CB Isaac Yiadom
Lions inactives: CB Ennis Rakestraw Jr., EDGE DJ Wonnum, S Chuck Clark, DB Keith Abney, EDGE Tyrus Wheat
The Bears have a few avenues to take here.
Chicago could opt to run it back with Clark Phillips, the defensive back who was acquired in the Gervon Dexter trade .
Phillips was sensational in the slot last week with four tackles (one for loss), one sack, one QB hit, two pressures and one pass break-up.
The other option is to deploy Malik Muhammad in the slot, but that would mean the Bears are more reliant on Stevenson, which is not the best approach.
Cam Lewis has also played in the slot in 2026, but with Hicks on the shelf for this game, the veteran defensive back is needed at safety with Chicago already being short-handed in the depth department.
With Johnson out, Salvon Ahmed will step into the RB3 role. Ahmed was one of the Bears' practice squad elevations on Wednesday.
At safety, rookie Skyler Thomas could be the next man up if the Bears need a safety off the bench. But Chicago will also need another punt protector because that's Hicks' role.
On that front, Thomas and Ahmed both played snaps there in the preseason, so they are options for the Bears in Week 12.

title: Stat Predictions for Bears vs Lions Includes a Breakout Game for Zavion Thomas
full_text:
The Chicago Bears are set to face their toughest test yet this Thanksgiving afternoon as they head to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions. Both teams are 8-2 on the season and will be playing for sole control of first place in the NFC North, and that has left the experts divided when picking the winner of this Week 12 clash .
The stakes could not be much higher in this one, especially for the Bears. For one thing, some of the players, and especially Caleb Williams, are doubtlessly hoping to exorcise those demons from their last Thanksgiving game against the Lions in 2024. Another win would also put them three full games ahead of the Packers in the NFC North standings after the Packers' woeful loss to the Rams on Wednesday night.
No matter who wins this one, I expect this to be an epic clash of NFC heavyweights. With that in mind, here are my stat predictions for this showdown.
Chicago's run game has struggled mightily of late, even with the return of Kyle Monangai to the lineup, and I don't expect that to change against an improving Lions defense. I said in my Week 12 keys to victory that the Bears are likely going to have to score at least 30 points to win this one, and that means Caleb Williams and the passing game will have to step up and show out.
Following his implosion in Week 9 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Williams played a so-so game against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday, but today will be the day he gets back into form. I expect him to complete over 70% of his pass attempts, cross the 300-yard mark for the third time this season, and take care of the ball.
After his big day against the Saints on Sunday, Zavion Thomas is sure to get more touches against the Lions. He proved his worth in clutch situations, and head coach Ben Johnson tends to reward players who step up in big moments with an increased role in his offense.
I predict that Thomas will finish the game with five receptions and 95 yards, both of which will be career highs by a mile, and his first NFL touchdown. Keep an eye on No. 13 while watching the game today, Bears fans. I expect to see some truly electric highlights.
The Lions' offensive line has played tremendous football so far this year, but they haven't faced a defensive line like Chicago's yet. Jeffery Simmons is a true force multiplier , and his presence has elevated the entire defense since his arrival last month. So while the Lions have done a good job protecting Jared Goff through 11 weeks, that's about to change.
I expect Goff, who isn't very eluse to begin with, to be under constant fire. Simmons will record another sack, his fourth consecutive game with at least one sack, and the rest of the defensive line will add three. Throw in a sack on a safety blitz, and that will be five for the Bears.

title: Fantasy Start or Sit Week 12: Monangai, Swift, Burden, Williams, Loveland, Odunze
full_text:
The Chicago Bears and Detroit Lions will square off in Week 12 on Thanksgiving in what could be the best game of the entire slate this week.
This matchup between Chicago and Detroit is a fantasy football dream, with both offenses ranking inside the top 10 in rushing yards and points, and inside the top 15 in passing yards.
As a result, we're expecting a lot of production from both teams in what could be an exciting contest that features a lot of points.
Now, a look at how we're handling the Bears' top offensive players in fantasy football, including Caleb Williams, Kyle Monangai, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden, D'Andre Swift and Colston Loveland.
Before his injury, Monangai was an every-week starter, ranking as RB13 overall over the first four weeks, according to Fantasy Pros .
But upon his return last week , Monangai only saw eight carries and turned them into just 18 scoreless yards. He also only saw one target that he failed to bring in.
While that kind of workload is a concern on the surface, he was also in his first game back and chances are the Bears were just easing him back in, especially with a quick turnaround for the following game this week.
We expect Monangai's workload to increase, and it could even be a bigger one than Swift, who isn't expected to be punished for his fumble last week but could still see a reduced workload in favor of Monangai getting more work since Monangai has been the more effective back when on the field this season.
Now, temper expectations here, because the Lions are giving up the fifth-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs, per CBS Sports .
But in a game that could be a shootout, there should be ample scoring opportunities for Monangai, which will offset what might be a lackluster yardage output in Week 12.
The last time Swift fumbled in a game before Week 12, which was Week 4, head coach Ben Johnson benched him for the entire second half of the game.
While there's a concern that Johnson might punish him again, the Bears head coach did say he doesn't plan on doing that , but that doesn't mean Swift won't see a reduced workload.
That said, we have to take Johnson's word for it right now, and that means our lineup decision is based on what Swift has done the entire season, and the matchup.
Entering Week 12, Swift ranks as RB12 overall, which puts him on the RB2 map and makes him a weekly starter in all formats. Again, the matchup isn't great here, but touchdown opportunities could be plentiful and that's enough to not be too scared about this matchup.
Burden has emerged as the Bears' best wide receiver this season and has already surpassed his production from his rookie year.
In terms of fantasy points, Burden ranks as WR15, which means he's a WR2 and no-brainer starter each and every week.
Adding to the optimism about starting Burden, the Lions are giving up the 11th-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers this season and there should be plenty of scoring on Thursday.
Burden has been a regular in your lineup all season long and that should not change in Week 12.
Williams hasn't been great in his last two games, but he still ranks as QB12 overall in fantasy points per game and this week is a fantastic get-right spot.
Only one team in the NFL is giving up more fantasy points per game to quarterbacks this season than the Lions, and we are expecting a shootout between two potent offenses.
Another avenue for points is Williams' legs. Not only is he a mobile quarterback, but the Lions are allowing the fourth-most rushing yards per contest to signal-callers.
Williams is an easy start this week.
Loveland's yardage production continues to be a disappointment, as we saw last week, but he has been finding pay dirt more often, with three touchdowns in his last five games.
Overall, Loveland ranks as TE10, and TE13 in fantasy points per game, which makes him an every-week starter in 12-team leagues.
As we've tirelessly noted throughout this article, the Lions-Bears contest has major shootout potential and that means plenty of slinging and scoring.
Detroit is also ceding the most fantasy points per contest to tight ends. You definitely can't sit Loveland this week.
Odunze was supposed to be the Bears' No. 1 wide receiver this year, but that title is now owned by Burden, as Odunze has taken a back seat to Chicago's clear top option.
As a result, Odunze ranks as WR44 overall in fantasy points per game, which makes him a matchup-based fantasy asset.
The matchup here is a good one, and for multiple reasons. Not only are we expecting plenty of points from both teams, but the Lions are permitting the 11th-most fantasy points per game to wideouts.
If there was ever a week that Odunze should be in your flex spot, this is the one.

title: Bold Predictions for Bears vs. Lions Week 12 Matchup
full_text:
The Chicago Bears will travel to Ford Field to take on the Detroit Lions on Thursday afternoon. Both teams are 8-2 and rolling (the Lions have won six straight and the Bears have won five straight) heading into the Week 12 clash.
The Bears are 2.5-point road favorites (according to DraftKings Sportsbook ), and the experts are split down the middle on their pick to come out with a win. The stakes really couldn't be any higher, as the winner will take sole possession of first place in the NFC North.
Bears head coach Ben Johnson will be eager to get his first win against his former team, as Chicago went 0-2 against their NFC North rivals last season.
We think a few key players should put up strong enough performances to help them in that endeavor.
The Bears have remained hot over the past month and a half, but quarterback Caleb Williams has unfortunately cooled off in recent weeks.
While his performance last week against New Orleans, an 181-yard, 2 TD, 1 INT showing, wasn't nearly as detrimental as his four-interception performance against Tampa Bay ahead of the Bye Week, it also wasn't a flashy performance by any means. He had no fewer than 247 yards over his previous four games since returning to the lineup.
The Lions have been strong against opposing passing games over the past month. They've given up an average of 163 passing yards per game over the past three games. That streak ends against Chicago.
Williams will eclipse that mark by halftime, and he'll reach 300 in the contest. He'll also bounce back in a big way with three passing touchdowns on top of it. They're much stronger against the run (they've given up the sixth-fewest rushing yards per game at 93.4 yards), and Williams will put the offense on his shoulders early and often.
Luther Burden III will be a major beneficiary of Williams' big game. Two receivers with similar skill sets to Chicago's star receiver, Chris Olave and Garrett Wilson, both enjoyed massive performances against Detroit. The former had 10 grabs for 182 yards, while the latter had 10 catches for 107 yards.
The Bears' crowded WR room will make it tough for Burden to match their catch total, but he should make a huge dent in the receiving category. We like his odds of reaching the 120-yard mark in a potential shootout.
Burden was on a tear before having a quiet performance against New Orleans. He'll get back on track with another strong performance against Detroit as the defense is forced to key in on their other pass-catchers ( including the recently integrated Zavion Thomas ).
There has been a ton of discourse surrounding Chicago's return to earth in the turnover differential department. They led the league in that department at +22 last year, and currently rank 25th at -4 over the first 11 weeks of this season.
They'll get a bit closer to the green later today, though. Lions quarterback Jared Goff has always struggled when he gets quick pressure in his face, and he's never faced Jeffery Simmons since he joined the Bears.
Simmons will force Goff into a few questionable decisions. They'll enjoy another two-takeaway performance on the defensive side of the ball.

title: 6 Things the Bears Should Be Thankful for This Thanksgiving, Including a Former Coach
full_text:
Thanksgiving Day is a holiday traditionally associated with thankfulness for what we have. For the Chicago Bears and their fans, the list of things to be thankful for is longer than it's been in a long time. Since winning the NFC North for the first time since 2018 last year, they've raced out to an 8-2 start and are tied with the Detroit Lions for first place in the division. Any fears that 2025 was a fluke season have been put to bed as fans and analysts come to grips with the fact that these Bears are built for sustained success.
So before we settle in for what should be an epic Bears vs Lions Thanksgiving showdown , let's think back to the people and events that got the Bears to where they are today and express our gratitude.
If ever the Bears' stadium saga comes to an end and the Bears actually build a new home, they might consider placing a Lovie Smith statue right outside the front gate. As the head coach of the Houston Texans, it was his decision to go for two and the win in the final minute of a meaningless Week 18 game that got the Bears the No. 1 overall pick in the 2023 NFL draft.
That pick was then traded to the Carolina Panthers for DJ Moore plus a 2024 first-round selection that became, once again, the No. 1 pick. This time, the Bears stuck with it and used that pick to select Caleb Williams, the long-awaited franchise quarterback. And even though Moore is already on a new team, he etched his name into franchise history with his overtime touchdown grab to seal the Bears' miracle comeback win over the Packers last December, an iconic victory that foreshadowed more to come in the postseason.
That catch from DJ Moore, the playoff win over Green Bay, hiring Ben Johnson, drafting Caleb Williams. None of it would have happened had Lovie Smith not called a two-point conversion as the head coach of a team that wasn't even in Chicago's conference. How's that for a butterfly effect?
Here's another butterfly effect for Bears fans to be thankful for today. After losing three straight games in November of 2024, one to each division rival, the Bears broke with 100 years of tradition and fired head coach Matt Eberflus midseason. It was a painful stretch of games for Bears fans, to be sure. They first lost to Green Bay, marking the team's 11th consecutive loss to their rival, on a blocked field goal. Then they forced overtime against the Vikings just to choke it away.
Finally, a late collapse against Detroit on Thanksgiving , a game in which time ran out on the offense despite Eberflus still holding on to a timeout, forced the McCaskey's to fire him. But from pain comes pleasure, as the saying goes. At the conclusion of a disastrous 2024 season, the Bears finally did the obvious thing and hired hotshot offensive coordinator Ben Johnson as their next head coach.
Since then, the Bears are 20-9, including the playoffs, Johnson's offense is the envy of the NFL, and the Bears are legit Super Bowl contenders for the first time in at least 15 years. And there's a strong likelihood that, had Eberflus just called timeout in his final game with Chicago, Johnson would never have darkened the doorway of Halas Hall.
This one is pretty simple. Trading for superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons has revolutionized Chicago's defense and raised the unit's ceiling from pretty good to Super Bowl-caliber. The Bears paid a hefty price (two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick), but Simmons has already proven to be worth the investment, especially after his three-sack game against the New Orleans Saints.
If the Bears do go on to reach the Super Bowl, the trade for Simmons will be a big reason why.
Ryan Poles has made his fair share of bad picks in the NFL draft. Thankfully, none of those bad picks came with his first-round selections. Darnell Wright, selected at No. 10 overall in 2023, was Poles' first first-round selection, and he signed a record-setting contract extension this offseason. Next came Caleb Williams, the Bears' first franchise quarterback since Jim McMahon, and Rome Odunze, who has been making some tough catches of late.
Colston Loveland was an unpopular pick at first, but he showcased his potential to be an elite playmaker. Finally, we have Dillon Thieneman, who is putting together a strong rookie season. Bears fans may criticize Poles' overall draft record, and rightfully so, but they should at least acknowledge and be thankful for the picks he's made in the first round.
The San Francisco 49ers have been like the Bears' big brother in recent years, beating up the rest of the NFC North and stopping the Packers from winning at least one more Super Bowl with Aaron Rodgers. They ended Green Bay's season in the 2019 NFC Championship game, and then again in the 2021 Divisional round. Last Sunday, they stomped out the Vikings to send them tumbling down to third place in the division.
Plus, 49ers tight end George Kittle is himself a Bears fan, and Bears legend Robbie Gould was their kicker for the final six seasons of his career. If there's any other NFC team that Bears fans should root for and be thankful for, it's the crimson and gold.
To use the parlance of the kids these days, the NFL schedule-makers cooked when they put together this Thanksgiving Day slate of games. As you relax with your family and friends, awaiting the feast to come, you'll get to watch a titanic clash of NFC North heavyweights as the Bears take on the Lions. Then you can enjoy a good dinner as the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys fight to stay alive in the NFC East. Finally, a Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs showdown closes out the night.
Plus, the schedule leading up to this game has been favorable for the Bears. They got a Week 10 bye to rest up and get healthy, followed by a tune-up game at home against the 3-6 Saints. They're simultaneously well-rested and ready for their biggest test yet, and that could be the difference between victory and defeat.

title: Bears' Final Week 12 Injury Report: 3 Ruled Out & Another New Addition Among 2 Questionable
full_text:
The Chicago Bears have released their final injury report on the day before the Week 12 game against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving.
As they did the previous two days , the Bears held a walk-through once again, so the injury report is an estimation for the third consecutive day.
The final injury report includes a new addition for the second straight day, and that player, along with another, is listed as questionable.
As for players ruled out, there are three in total. We'll go over all of that and much more after checking out the injury report for Wednesday.
Cornerback Tyrique Stevenson is a new addition to the injury report with a groin injury and, along with linebacker D'Marco Jackson, he is questionable to play on Thursday.
Assuming he didn't somehow injure himself during the walk-through, the fact that Stevenson was listed as limited gives Chicago's cornerback a chance to suit up.
As for Jackson, three full practices suggests he will go.
As expected, defensive back Kyler Gordon, safety Elijah Hicks and running back Roschon Johnson have been ruled out.
The writing was on the wall with both Gordon and Johnson after they were estimated non-participants on Monday and Tuesday.
Gordon got hurt before the bye, and Johnson was carted off with his injury during the Week 11 game against the New Orleans Saints. This is now two missed games in a row for Gordon.
Hicks popped up on the injury report on Tuesday and was ruled out immediately by head coach Ben Johnson due to his concussion.
That situation is a little strange because Hicks was not reported to have a concussion during or after last week's game and Chicago didn't hold a full practice this week.
That said, sometimes players don't start getting symptoms until a day or two after a game, so that's probably the case here.
The Bears have a few options to replace Gordon, assuming Stevenson overcomes the questionable tag.
One of them is to put Malik Muhammad in the slot and have Stevenson on the outside. Muhammad played very good football in the slot earlier in the season while Gordon was out with a calf issue.
The other option is to run it back with Clark Phillips, who played in the slot against the Saints and had himself a great game .
There would be a third option in Cam Lewis, but with Hicks ruled out, the Bears need Lewis at safety next to Dillon Thieneman.
Rookie Skyler Thomas is in line to be the primary backup at safety with Hicks sidelined, but the Bears also need a new punt protector, which was Hicks' other job. Thomas, Salvon Ahmed and Marlew Sewell, who was re-signed to the practice squad this week, all received looks in that role during the preseason.
Speaking of Ahmed, he will be Chicago's RB3 with Johnson out.

title: Bengals Legend Voices Frustrations After Team's Disappointing Loss vs. Commanders
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals allowed a golden opportunity to slip through their fingers with their 22-20 loss to the Washington Commanders on Monday night.
In a week that saw the Pittsburgh Steelers and Baltimore Ravens both lose, the Bengals had a chance to extend their lead in the AFC North. Instead, the Bengals watched a three win team earn their fourth victory of the season on a last-second field goal.
It's going to be a long week for this team and the fan base. Not only that, but former players are even frustrated with how things played out on Monday night.
Bengals legend T.J. Houshmandzadeh shared his feelings on the team's final defensive drive during a recent episode of 'Speakeasy'.
"There's just no way on God's green earth they go down the field in two plays with no timeouts," Houshmandzadeh exclaimed . "Nobody's doing that on Madden to me, let alone in real life."
The final drive of the game was a backbreaker for the Bengals. In just two plays, the Commanders were in chip-shot territory for kicker Drew Stevens. As Houshmandzadeh said, it almost felt like it wasn't possible for this Commanders team to get down the field this quick on the Bengals.
The Bengals legend also mentioned the team not having its best offensive performance of the season. In the Bengals' last two plays before Evan McPherson drilled a 56-yard field goal, quarterback Joe Burrow nearly threw an interception and took a terrible sack.
How did the Bengals offense get to that point? The answer could be found in the non-existent run game. The Bengals rushed for just 31 yards on Monday night. Sure, the weather was poor, but that didn't stop the Commanders from rushing for 150 yards.
Burrow is an elite quarterback, and it makes sense for him to have the ball in his hand during winning time. However, it couldn't hurt to also equip his offense with a running game that has a pulse.
It feels like the Bengals have been flying too close to the sun without a reliable run game.
Burrow has put the team on his back through the air, but since this offense seems to be so one-dimensional, it seems as though defenses are going to be able to make plays like the Commanders did on Monday to put the Bengals in more uncomfortable situations.

title: Joe Burrow Addresses Aaron Rodgers' Release, Chasing Drew Brees' Record and Giving Thanks
full_text:
Joe Burrow has always spoken fondly and with a lot of reverence for Aaron Rodgers in the past, but the Cincinnati Bengals quarterback didn’t want to say too much about the ongoing dysfunction in Pittsburgh that led to the Steelers releasing the future Hall of Famer today.
“I don't know much about the situation,” Burrow said. “It's certainly surprising, but I don't know much.”
With the Steelers sitting just one game behind the Bengals in the AFC North standings, a quarterback switch in Week 12 isn’t ideal.
And it could be something that benefits the Bengals in their pursuit of a division championship for the first time since 2022.
One way Rodgers release does resonate with Burrow is that it’s a reminder of how fortunate he feels to be in the position he is.
“I'm always thankful to be to be playing and certainly don't take being a quarterback in the NFL for granted,” he said. “I've worked really hard for it, certainly. But it takes a lot of luck and being in the right place at the right time to be in this spot, and I've had a lot of people that have helped me get here, and I’m super, super grateful for all those people.”
Burrow enters Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints with a 74.2 completion percentage, which is just shy of the NFL record Drew Brees set while playing for the Saints.
Brees posted a 74.4 in 2018 and 74.3 in 2019.
“It's a huge, huge part of playing quarterback, is being accurate enough to let those guys go to work,” Burrow said. “It's something I take pride in.
“Certainly gotta keep improving and would love for my career at the end of it to look like his.”
Despite the admiration for Brees, Burrow said he doesn’t feel any extra oomph in facing a Saints team that Brees led for 15 seasons.
“I think it would mean a little more if we were playing down there,” Burrow said.
Burrow still has a lot of fans in the Louisiana region after leading LSU to the national title and winning the Heisman trophy there in 2019.
He admitted it’s meaningful to have that support from so far away.
“People in Louisiana love their culture, they love their football, and they love their people, and I became that,” he said. “Certainly it doesn't surprise me in Louisiana, but when we played in Houston this year, I always forget how many people relocated after Katrina to Houston. I saw a lot  of No. 9 jerseys in the stands that day – purple ones – and a lot of people saying, ‘Go Tigers.’ I always forget about that, but that was a pleasant surprise.”

title: Bengals Injury Report: Initial Saints Practice Status Revealed For Dalton Risner And More
full_text:
The Bengals dropped their opening injury report for Saints week on Wednesday.
All eyes are on Dalton Risner's knee injuries over the next few days as things got off to a poor start projecting his return on Sunday. He is listed as a DNP on the projected Wednesday report after Cincinnati just went through a walkthrough after playing so recently on Monday night.
Zac Taylor did say earlier today to not read into Risner's status until later in the week.
Stars like Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins know one loss isn't the end of the world for Cincinnati.
The Bengals are still heavy favorites to win the AFC North. ESPN's Football Power Index gives them a 91.2% chance to win the division.
"I mean, we started off playing in the rain. I'm not going to make an excuse; you know what I'm saying? But I think that's a different start for us trying to find rhythm. But once we got going, we just got to make those great decisions. Get the right looks, read the right coverages, and you know, execute it," Chase said to the media on Monday. "One loss doesn't determine anything. It's the NFL. You got a loss, you learn from it. We learn from our mistakes. That's what we're going to do. We're going to watch the film, we're going to correct it and move on."
Higgins echoed a similar sentiment as the Commanders found a way to slow him and Chase down in the 22-20 loss during Monday Night Football.
"I mean, no, but, yeah, they were doing a lot of doubles and things like that, a lot of stick strong and stuff like that, especially to [WR] Ja'Marr [Chase]. But we were able to figure it out, there in the second half. We made some plays, but just not enough," Higgins said. "When you win some, you lose some; you just gotta live to see the next day. Go back to practice, correct what we did wrong, and be ready for next Sunday."
Cincinnati is widely expected to bounce back with a home win over the Saints on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET inside Paycor Stadium.

title: 'It Depends' - Joe Burrow Dives Into Bengals Run Game Struggles as Cincinnati Prepares For New Orleans
full_text:
Joe Burrow is the heavy engine of Cincinnati's offense, but he's willing to let off the passing gas to help spark the Bengals' run game back up after a brutal showing against the Commanders (14 carries for 31 yards).
He gave his view on the ground attack, which now ranks 19th in EPA/rush and 16th in success rate, noting they "just gotta execute." They didnt do that enough in Monday's 22-20 loss.
"It depends," Burrow said about the Bengals needing to run the ball more. Or just more effectively. "Obviously, you'd love to be super explosive in both, but we'll play the game however we need to play to win it, and I'm certainly prepared for either one. I'm prepared to throw it no times. I'm prepared to throw it 70 times. Whatever it takes to win."
Cincinnati has the best pure passer in the NFL and almost all of its offensive money in the passing game, but it sputtered in the rain to start against Washington. One possession (and one more score) was the difference between a real shot at AFC's No. 1 seed and the longshot reality now.
The Bengals are battling a New Orleans defense playing solid football of late, ranking 14th in EPA/play allowed and 11th in success rate allowed since Week 6.
Burrow has full respect for another NFC opponent.
"Yeah, their linebackers are good at blitzing," Burrow said about the Saints. "Their front is explosive, and they're good rushers. When you put those two things in combination, it makes it hard."
The Bengals are at the top of the AFC North and still riding great team chemistry, while the second-place Browns own a -32 point differential this season and the fellow 6- 4 Steelers deal with crazy locker room turmoil.
Aaron Rodgers got released today, and Cincinnati can now take full control of the division; Burrow is just focusing on getting to 8-3.
"Just worried about trying to win this week," Burrow said. "Landscape will play out the way it plays out, and we just got to keep winning."

title: Bengals Coaches Taylor, Golden Weigh In on Why Shemar Stewart Can't See the Field
full_text:
The Cincinnati Bengals have been down an edge rusher since rookie Cashius Howell went on Injured Reserve with a broken wrist Nov. 3.
And yet 2025 first-round pick Shemar Stewart still can’t find his way onto the field.
Monday night in the 22-20 loss at Washington, Stewart was active but didn’t play a single snap on defense.
Stewart, who suffered a knee hyperextension in the first practice of training camp and didn’t return until just before the season opener, has been active for seven of the team’s 10 games this  year.
Monday marked the second time he failed to play in a game when he dressed, and in four of the others, his snap counts were in the single digits.
Bengals head coach Zac Taylor and defensive coordinator Al Golden both continued to throw their support behind Stewart on Wednesday.
Taylor said Stewart’s inability to get off the sideline was more a product of how the game played out.
“The first half was very unique in that I think they had a five- or six-play drive to start and then three and out, three and out, three and out, and then they finished with a six-play drive that scored,” he said. “So those (defensive linemen) felt really good because they were on the sideline quite a bit. I think in the second half they felt pretty good, too.
“With that being said, you've got to find some opportunities for Shemar and Cedric (Johnson) to get in there and mix in,” Taylor added. “It was just a strange first half the way it played. In the second half, those guys felt really good. But we'll rotate those guys a little more than we have.”
Taylor has spoken positively about Stewart all season, and he said the lost time in training camp is no longer affecting the decisions to not play him.
“I've been pleased with Shemar,” he said. “  know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here and then he doesn't take any snaps. I get that. But he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a positive spot right now for us.
“We'll provide him with some opportunity to go make some plays for us,” he continued. “I like where he's at. Just the way it unfolded last week wasn't any sort of indictment on him.”
Golden said it’s on him, not Stewart, to make sure the young edge rusher sees action.
And Golden expects that Stewart will as the season moves into December and January.
“He will (play),” Golden said. “We're gonna need him. I keep saying it. This is a long stretch we have in front of us, and whatever I have to do to help him and to get him into the game and impact the game, I am committed to doing that. I have to do a better job with that.”
The next opportunity comes Sunday against the Saints.
Stewart played 280 snaps in eight games as a rookie. He’s logged just 52 in seven games this season.

title: Zac Taylor Updates Dalton Risner's Health, Shemar Stewart's Lacking Impact Entering Saints Week
full_text:
Zac Taylor returned to the podium on Wednesday for the first time since the Bengals' five-game win streak ended against the Commanders.
The 22-20 loss featured one of the worst rushing performances in team history (14 carries for 31 yards), and Jalen Rivers' 58 snaps at right guard had something to do with it.
The backup right guard filled in for Dalton Risner (knees) and only notched a 55.3 Pro Football Focus grade (50.5 run-block grade). Getting Risner back to complete the offensive line continuity this week would be massive.
Taylor updated his status.
"He'll be day to day, so we'll see," Taylor said about Risner. "Just talked to him this morning, and we'll just take it day to day and see where he ends up on Sunday. Today's a walkthrough-only day, so I wouldn't read too much into how that goes today."
Bryan Cook suffered an injury in the first half of the game but ended up playing 64 snaps and should be good to go this week. Taylor said he is just "sore" after the recent loss. Meanwhile, Cincinnati desperately needs help at defensive end amidst Shemar Stewart's shutout from the lineup.
He didn't play a snap Monday, and the week prior, he didn't enter the game until the Bengals were up 31-3. The three weeks prior to that, he played five, six, and zero total snaps.
"I've been pleased with Shemar," Taylor said, noting the game flow led to no snaps for Stewart because Boye Mafe and Myles Murphy didn't play a lot in the first half. "I know I sound a little bit like a broken record up here, and then he doesn't take a snap, so I get that. But he's controlling everything he needs to control. He's in a positive spot right now for us. We'll provide him some opportunity to go make some plays for us, and I like where he's at. So just the way it unfolded last week wasn't any sort of indictment on it."
We will see if the Bengals put weight behind Taylor's words by actually playing Stewart a significant snap diet this week.
All in all, Cincinnati is pretty healthy entering Week 12 as they get their first normal game week in nearly a month to enjoy at home.

title: Referee Report: Bengals, Saints Should Expect Lots of Flags in Sunday's Game
full_text:
Not only are the Cincinnati Bengals wearing the same uniform combo they wore when they blew a 15-point lead against the New York Jets last year, they’ll also have the same referee they had that day.
Scott Novak will be on the call for Sunday’s game against the New Orleans Saints at Paycor Stadium, marking his first Bengals game since the team’s infamous 39-38 loss in Week 8 last year.
Novak has been a head referee since 2019 and has been an NFL official since 2014.
The Bengals are 3-5 with Novak. The Saints also are 3-5 with him.
Novak and his crew are averaging 17.4 accepted penalties per game, which is a close second to Craig Wrolstad (17.44) for second most in the league.
Last year Novak ranked 11th (11.82), and in 2023 he was 10th (12.24).
Novak and his crew have called 46 offensive holding penalties this year, most in the league. The next highest number is 37 by Alex Moore, who has only worked nine games this season to Novak’s 10.
The next highest number for a referee that has worked 10 games is 32 by Shawn Smith.
Novak and his crew also lead the league with 13 unnecessary roughness penalties, which is almost 50 percent more than the next highest total, which is nine by Shawn Hochuli.
In Week 4, Novak’s crew had 30 accepted penalties for 280 yards.
The penalties are the most this season, and the yards are second most behind 289 in a Week 2 overtime game between the Packers and Jets, which Novak also worked.
Novak has one career playoff assignment, which was an NFC Wild-Card game between the Buccaneers and Commanders way back in 2020.
Here is the full list of eight Bengals games Novak has worked:
Week 8, 2025: Jets 39, Bengals 38
Bengals 2-15; Cowboys 4-25
Week 14, 2024: Bengals 27, Cowboys 20
Bengals 10-77; Cowboys 4-36
Week 8, 2024: Eagles 37, Bengals 17
Week 14, 2023: Bengals 34, Jaguars 31
Bengals 6-35; Jaguars 7-55
Week 5, 2022: Ravens 19, Bengals 17
Week 9, 2021: Browns 41, Bengals 16
Bengals 4-31; Browns 10-84
Week 8, 2020: Bengals 31, Titans 20
Week 10, 2019: Ravens 49, Bengals 13

title: This Week's Cincinnati Bengals Uniform Combination Will Send Shivers Through Fan Base
full_text:
If you tie memories to Cincinnati Bengals uniform combinations, prepare to be uncomfortable.
The Bengals will wear black jerseys, orange pants with black stripes and black socks Sunday afternoon at Paycor Stadium against the New Orleans Saints.
They’ve only worn the combination three other times, and two of them were losses that stuck with fans long after the clock hit 0:00.
The uniform combination debut came in Week 5 of 2024 against the Baltimore Ravens. The Bengals blew up a 10-point fourth-quarter lead to go to overtime, where holder Ryan Rehkow dropped the snap on what would have been a 53-yard field goal attempt to win the game.
One play later, Derrick Henry ripped off a 51-yard run, followed seconds later by Justin Tucker’s 24-yard field goal for a 41-38 victory that dropped the Bengals to 1-4.
Later that season, with the Bengals riding a two-game winning streak, they wore it again for a home game against the Cleveland Browns, and the Bengals won easily, 24-6.
But last year in Week 8, the uniform combination returned for one of the games that encapsulated the disaster the 2025 Cincinnati defense was – a 39-38 loss to the New York Jets.
The Bengals led that game by 14 twice in the second quarter and took a 15-point lead into the four quarter, only to watch the Jets outscore them 23-7 over the final 14 minutes to pull off a stunning win.
It also was Trey Hendrickson’s final game with the team as he asked off the field due to an injury in the second quarter.
The following week, the Bengals blew another late lead against the Chicago Bears.
Breaking down the individual elements of the uniform combination, Cincinnati is just 3-7 while wearing orange pants, although they snapped a three-game losing streak in the britches a few weeks ago in Madrid with a 34-17 win against the Atlanta Falcons.
Conversely, the black socks had been lucky. The Bengals had won five in a row with them and 9 of 11 before losing Monday night at Washington.

title: Shemar Stewart Off to a Historically Bad Start in His Young Career
full_text:
There's always a game every fan base would like to have back at the end of a season. For Cincinnati Bengals fans, that game happened on Monday night.
The Bengals had a chance to take care of business on the road in a Monday night showdown with the Washington Commanders. Instead, the rest of the week is being spent wondering how the Bengals allowed the Commanders to grab the 22-20 win.
The offense was a shell of itself for most of the first half, while the defense crumbled during crunch time. The pass rush was solid in the first half, earning three sacks, but looked a little gassed in the second half, resulting in zero sacks. Which begs the question: where is Shemar Stewart?
The Bengals' 2025 first round pick has been non-existent for the franchise this season. On Monday night, Stewart didn't even play a snap. Looking at his performance this season, Stewart has only played 52 snaps for the Bengals.
A team that is looking for help in the pass rush is not getting it from a player who was selected in a premium spot just two drafts ago. To make matters worse, Stewart is on a path to being one of the worst pass rushers to be selected in the first round in the last twenty drafts.
According to Gridiron Grading , Stewart is off to the slowest start of any edge rusher drafted in the first round in the last 20 years. This chart was created using each player's Pro Football Focus grades.
Sure, Stewart should take some blame for not being able to translate his game at the NFL level. However, the Bengals front office had to know this pick could have always been a high-risk, high-reward situation.
Stewart was not known as a player to rack up sacks during his college career. In three seasons with the Texas A&M Aggies, Stewart had just 4.5 sacks.
The current pass rush situation also can go back to the team not making any moves prior to the trade deadline. Well, they made one move, then decided it wasn't the right move, but let's just leave that in the past.
Now, the Bengals are hoping for edge depth and a running back who can show any life in the backfield as they quickly approach the end of the season. The only problem is that the team will have to make do with what they currently have.

full_text:
