title: The Browns’ Biggest Underperformer Has a Lot to Prove During the Final Seven Games
full_text:
With the Browns sitting at 6-4 and awaiting a home date with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday Night Football, there is not much to be wary of if you are a Cleveland fan.
Deshaun Watson has now thrown for 300+ yards in three straight games, something he hadn’t done once since joining the Browns in 2022.
The rookies at receiver are as advertised: Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion are first and third among receiving yards by a rookie this season; both have added a couple of touchdowns as well. Second-year Ohio product Harold Fannin Jr. has blossomed into a top-five tight end in the league, continuing to show reliable hands and an unstoppable motor.
Another 2025 draftee has struggled to find his groove in the past couple of games: running back Quinshon Judkins.
After rushing for 96 yards and two touchdowns against the Titans a month ago, Judkins has rushed for 106 yards on 36 carries (2.9 per attempt) and the game-winning score vs. Houston in Week 10.
Cleveland’s run game has been subpar this season, averaging just 97.5 yards per game (24th in the NFL) and 3.8 yards per attempt (25th in the NFL).
The Browns run the ball on 41.2% of their plays, putting them in the lower half of the league. Another stat that puts them down is that they average just 0.94 yards before being contacted per rush, bringing their success rate to 35.5% on runs, which is 26th in the NFL.
Judkins currently has the fourth-worst success rate among qualified rushers this season at 30.2% and the second-worst rushing EPA at -35.7.
These final seven games for the Browns will give Judkins plenty of opportunities to show his worth, as the Raiders give up the second-most rushing yards per game. Cincinnati (which Cleveland plays twice) allows the ninth-most rushing yards per game; Atlanta and New York aren’t exactly world beaters when it comes to defending the run.
Baltimore is solid at stopping it, but Indianapolis is right up there with the Raiders as one of the worst run defenses in the league.
Again, though, Judkins is only in his second season in the NFL, and while we have seen other young Browns players break out almost immediately, there could be some growing pains with Judkins.
He is just 23 years old and has dealt with some injuries early in his career, but if there was any time to break out, now is the time.
Hi, I’m Paul, I’m from Northeast Ohio, and a recent graduate of Kent State University. As an Ohio native, I’m a huge fan of the Browns, Guardians, and Cavaliers. Just don’t ask me about my favorite college team, though.

title: Predicting the Browns’ Quarterback Room for the 2027 Season
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have a ton to be thankful for this season by starting 6-4 and putting themselves in a position to make the playoffs. Todd Monken was a questionable hire at the time, but he has the team bought in and is pressing all the right buttons.
Deshaun Watson has had his best season in Cleveland after a contentious preseason. The young players have stepped up , showing a bright future.
On the other hand, the Browns have put themselves in a pickle going into 2027. They have won too many games to pick a top quarterback in the draft. Watson’s contract expires after the season, and although he has played well, he has not been consistent enough to sign to a long-term deal.
The quarterback room is up in the air for next season, with no real viable answer. The room could stay the same, or a big addition may be made for the future.
The #Browns have no interest in signing QB Daniel Jones, who cleared waivers today after being released by the #Colts .
Watson should be extended on a short-term contract as a bridge quarterback. He has improved every week he has played under Todd Monken and has had three straight 300-yard games. The team believes in him to win games, and he has developed chemistry with the young receivers.
He would have another offseason with Monken. The talent around him would get more time to develop with him, rather than trying to learn a new quarterback's tendencies. The roster will be ready to win next season, and handing the reins to a rookie drafted low in the first round would be a risk for a regression.
The University of Oregon product had an injury-plagued 2026 season. He has not played since early in the season, but in 2025 he was considered the second-best quarterback in his class. Moore chose to stay in college for another year, which hurt his draft stock. Moore took over for Dillon Gabriel at the University of Oregon, and they were teammates in 2024.
The Browns have two first-round picks in the 2027 draft , both of which may be in the back half. They have reloaded their roster in the last two drafts and brought in players at every level of the offense and defense.
Rookies no longer have to come in and start on day one.
Andrew Berry can use the higher first-round pick on a starter, but the second one can be used to take a risk and draft a prospect. Moore would have time to sit behind Watson and learn Monken’s offense while serving as the backup. He has a big upside, but his floor is now lower than it was last year.
Gabriel has been praised for his understanding of the offense. However, his physical tools limit his potential. He can serve as an emergency quarterback, and he is beneficial to have in the quarterback room.
The Browns had the chance to cut Gabriel when he came off the injured reserve list, but chose to keep him on the roster.
The physical tools are off the charts with Green, but he has struggled with accuracy. He did not get a lot of reps as the fourth quarterback, but after another offseason, he may challenge Gabriel for the emergency quarterback position. The Browns should hold onto him and find a way to utilize his skills for niche plays.
The obvious omission from the list is Shedeur Sanders. Monken had a chance to start Sanders at the beginning of the season, but chose Watson.
He made the same decision after Sanders’ lone start when Watson was injured. Sanders has shown that he has a chance to be an NFL quarterback, and there will be a team that would be willing to trade for him and give him a chance .
There are a lot of options out there to play quarterback for the Browns in 2027, but none of them are a no-brainer. Moore may be the future, but for next season, Watson could be the easiest answer to start at quarterback.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: How This Running Back's Return From Injury Strengthens Browns' Offense
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' running game will have a chance to bounce back for the back half of the 2026 season.
Through the first 10 games of the year, Cleveland sits with a nice 6-4 overall record and the top spot in the AFC North still within reach.
However, such success has not been thanks to the running game. The unit has posted a measly 975 total yards, averaging fewer than 100 yards per game, numbers that rank the Browns 24th in the league. In rushing yards per carry, they are 25th, and in total touchdowns, they sit right in the middle of the pack.
Fortunately, the Browns did get a positive update on a player who could help the rushing attack regain its form.
On Tuesday, Nov. 24, running back Raheim Sanders was activated off the injured list after missing the last few weeks due to a hip injury he suffered in a Week 5 loss to the New York Jets. In his place, the Browns have leaned on the likes of Audric Estime, who is no longer with the team, and Jaleel McLaughlin to fill his spot on the depth chart.
The #Browns have designated RB Raheim Sanders for return from injured reserve. He is eligible to practice today.
Now that he is back, though, the running back room will likely see Sanders return to the No. 3 spot behind Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson, with McLaughlin sliding to fourth.
Before being injured, Sanders had played in five games, rushing nine times for 43 yards and one first down . He has not yet scored this season. In the passing game, he complemented the unit nicely, hauling in 11 receptions on 12 targets for 74 yards.
With both Judkins and Sampson struggling to find consistency, Sanders will look to take some of the dirty reps away from them and give them more time to get quality reps. In his role, the 24-year-old will likely be the fill-in back when substitutions are needed.
A look at #Browns RB Raheim Sanders at practice today, who was designated to return from IR after being placed there Week 5 with a hip injury. pic.twitter.com/NuzCpsuXkK
After all, a deeper running back room gives the offense more comfort in giving guys like Judkins and Sampson longer drives, knowing that if a break is needed, they can turn to Sanders. On the counter, they can also spread out drives more, giving each back a chance to shine, saving a player like go-to back Judkins' energy for later in a game.
No matter how the coaching staff decides to use Sanders post-injury, the rushing game simply needs to be better, especially if the Browns want to make a late-season push for a playoff spot.
Sanders' first chance to return to the gridiron will be on Sunday, Nov. 29, when the Browns take on the Las Vegas Raiders from Huntington Bank Field at 8:20 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns Get Unexpected Help In AFC North Race As Steelers, Bengals Stumble
full_text:
Over the past week, the AFC North had a lot of big events take place to determine its winner in 2026.
For the Cleveland Browns, they got help from all of the other teams losing while they had their bye week . On top of the losses, the Steelers just had some major drama go down within their organization
Let's take a look at all three of the Browns' rivals to see if Cleveland can get their first division win since 1989.
After losing to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11, the Steelers swapped places with the Browns in both divisional and playoff standings. Pittsburgh now sits in 3rd in the North and 7th in the Playoffs.
However, that was just the tip of the iceberg.
As the Browns were closely competing with Pittsburgh, drama broke out within the organization between quarterback Aaron Rodgers and head coach Mike McCarthy.
Steelers releasing QB Aaron Rodgers. (via @RapSheet , @AdamSchefter ) pic.twitter.com/x4UVthdEoI
After a sequence of events where both parties did not see eye to eye, along with a historical Pat McAfee show appearance from Rodgers, the Steelers have decided to part ways with the 42-year-old.
This is huge for the Browns. While Mason Rudolph is still a solid QB, he is no Aaron Rodgers, who had over 2,200 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions on the season.
Especially looking at standings, this disaster should help the Browns focus on one team in particular for the title of AFC North Champs.
Cincinnati has been on fire this season, with Joe Burrow looking like an MVP-caliber quarterback. Despite this, the Bengals still lost to the 3-5-1 Washington Commanders on Monday Night Football.
Looking at the standings following that one, the Browns sit one game back at 6-4 compared to the Bengals, who lead with a record of 7-3.
The big news? Cleveland has yet to face off against Cincinnati this season.
In fact, two of the last six games will be against the Bengals, with the first matchup in Cleveland in week 13, and the finale on the road in Cincinnati in week 18.
Realistically, that game could be one of the biggest this season in the entire NFL. For years, the league sets kickoff as "TBD" due to the potential nature of the game we seem to have each year.
Unless the Bengals run away with the division and are able to rest their starters that game, expect that Week 18 matchup to be intense, and maybe even get flexed into yet another prime time game.
The story of the 2026 Baltimore Ravens is quite sad. Lots of injuries, which is hard to deal with while having a first-year head coach, Jesse Minter.
With Lamar Jackson sidelined for potentially the rest of the season, Cleveland needs to capitalize on the opportunity to get a win in Baltimore when it comes time in week 16.
While the Ravens aren't competing for the AFC North title, the divisional record plays a big role in deciding the champs.
For Cleveland, they must win against the injured Ravens roster.
As fun as it is to finally see Pittsburgh go through a similar situation to the Browns with Aaron Rodgers, work still needs to be done.
Cincinnati is a legitimate championship-caliber team, and beating them is going to be a battle for the Browns.
All focus should be on winning games, especially now that the window has opened up just a bit more.
Louis Timura is a student sports broadcaster and content creator. He currently attends Ashland University while pursuing a degree in Digital Media Production.

title: How the Benching of Aaron Rodgers Benefits the Browns
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns are used to bringing dysfunction to the AFC North with their actions both on and off the field.
However, there has not been a peep heard from Berea, and they sit second in the division at 6-4. The stalwart of the division, historically, has been the Pittsburgh Steelers until this season.
The Steelers and coach Mike Tomlin parted ways at the end of last season after 19 years with zero losing seasons. Now the story has changed, as new coach Mike McCarthy benched Aaron Rodgers overnight in favor of Mason Rudolph.
Rodgers has had his lowest completion percentage of his career, but he should still give the Steelers the best chance to win. They are on a two-game losing streak after getting blown out by the Cincinnati Bengals and then dropping a close game against the two-win Philadelphia Eagles.
No matter how Rudolph performs, it looks as though Rodgers is finished in Pittsburgh. He did not show up to the team meeting Wednesday morning, which could signal his end.
Rodgers and McCarthy had a contentious relationship prior to his benching, and the relationship seems to be unsalvageable.
The Steelers’ first team meeting today was scheduled for 8 am, and Aaron Rodgers was not at the team’s training facility at that time. pic.twitter.com/yIYmWfrXKf
The path to the playoffs has now changed for the Browns, as they are the sixth seed in the AFC, one spot ahead of the Steelers.
Both teams are tied, but the Browns have the tiebreaker as of now due to their record within the division.
The Steelers should be underdogs in their next three games, and they play the Baltimore Ravens twice in the last four weeks. The Ravens are having a down year, but the offense has turned around under Jacoby Brissett, and their matchups are always physical. The Browns have the easier schedule for the rest of the season.
The other teams trailing the Browns are the New England Patriots, who lost Drake Maye. Behind them are the Houston Texans at 4-6, and the Browns already beat them head-to-head to win the tiebreaker. The Las Vegas Raiders raced off to a 3-0 start, but have fallen to 4-7. If the Browns can beat them Sunday night, then they will be all but finished .
There is blood in the water for the last wild-card spot, but it’s not the Browns’.
Not only do the benching and fallout with Rodgers benefit the Browns’ playoff hopes, but it also shows the turnaround and shift in the division.
The Browns were on a two-game losing streak, falling to 5-4 and out of a playoff position. Todd Monken did not panic and stuck with Deshaun Watson after missing a week with a concussion.
They fell down 17-0 against the Texans, and fans were ready for Shedeur Sanders to come out and spark the offense. The belief Monken had in Watson paid off as he had his best three-quarters of the season to lead the Browns to a victory and back into the playoff race.
The move to bench Rodgers and his reaction is a typical move the Browns would make in years past, but now the shoe is on the other foot, and the Browns are the ones making responsible decisions. As a result, they are poised to finish ahead of the Steelers in the division. The Browns sit only one game out of the Cincinnati Bengals, and they play each other two times in the last seven games.
The Browns’ roster is so young, and they do not care about the past. Monken has everyone in the organization on the same page, and there has been no discontent .
Rodgers' benching is an alarm that change is coming in the AFC North.
And fortunately, the Browns aren't at the center of negative attention for once.
Graduated from Bowling Green State University with a Journalism degree. Written and contributed to numerous media outlets. Cleveland sports victim.

title: Jared Verse Believes He's Improving, But One Thing Is Still Missing
full_text:
When the Cleveland Browns traded away future Hall of Fame defensive end Myles Garrett, all eyes were on who his replacement would be.
Fortunately, young edge rusher Jared Verse, who was acquired in the trade, quickly emerged during the offseason. He worked with players outside of practice hours, maintained a vocal and standout presence in the media spotlight and seemed poised for a big 2026 season for the Browns' defense.
But through the first 10 games of the year, Verse has struggled . That role he was expected to fill may have been too much pressure for him to handle.
Multiple times now, his public comments have been used as motivation and a competitive edge for opposing teams, all while he has yet to record a sack and is posting career-low numbers across the board in other areas.
Despite the lack of production in the box score, Verse believes his performance against the Houston Texans in Week 10 was a step in the right direction.
On Wednesday, Nov. 25, Verse spoke to the media ahead of the Browns' primetime Week 12 meeting with the Las Vegas Raiders. He was asked how he felt he played against the Texans, whom the Browns beat to improve to 6-4 on the season.
“I think I was my best self that game," he said. "I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to [CJ] Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting in his face, hitting him.
"I won most of my rushes, so I feel like I impacted the game in the aspect I need to.”
Browns DE Jared Verse on his performance against the Texans: “I think I was my best self that game. I did exactly what I had to do. I closed the B gap with the tackle, I was able to set the edge, I was able to get to Stroud a couple times. Didn’t end up getting a sack but getting… https://t.co/pAyktiUzBv
And while it would have been nice to see a sack recorded, the 26-year-old is right; it probably was his best game this year. He registered season-best marks in pressures with five and total pressure rate with 17.9%, routinely getting into the backfield to disrupt the Texans' passing game.
But there is still work to be done, especially as he searches for his first sack of the season.
In the win over the Texans, after allowing 17 quick points, the entire defensive unit anchored down, allowing just seven points across the next 41 minutes of the game . CJ Stroud, surprisingly, was sacked just once, though.
Browns DE Jared Verse registered season-high marks in pressures (5) and pressure rate (17.9%) against the Texans.
Verse has certainly slowly but surely gotten better since the first few weeks of the season, but that ability to get in the backfield and register sacks is something he needs to start doing, not just for the team's ability to shut down opposing offenses, but for his own confidence.
Prior to the Texans game, he revealed that in order to break out of the slump he's in and regain that mindset he once had, he had been seeing team psychiatrist Dr. Mayur Pandya.
“I’m upset with the way I’ve been playing," Verse said back on Nov. 12. "I don’t think it’s physical; there’s nothing wrong with my body. I think it was the mental aspect of the game and I’ve attacked that very well these past couple weeks. But I think this past week is a key thing that I’ve done. I’m very excited for next week."
Coming out of a Week 11 bye , Verse has all the opportunities in front of him to go out there and break his sack-less streak against a rookie quarterback-led Raiders offense.
The Browns and Raiders will meet from Huntington Bank Field on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST.
Cade Cracas is a sports media professional with experience in play-by-play, broadcasting and digital storytelling. He is a recent graduate of Ashland University with degrees in digital media production and journalism.

title: Browns QB Shedeur Sanders Gives Cleveland Shoppers a Thanksgiving Surprise
full_text:
Pilar Sanders was looking for her son in the aisles of Dave’s Market.
“It’s a pop-up surprise,” she told her Instagram followers as she tried to catch up with him. Two days before Thanksgiving, Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders stopped at the East 61st Street store in Cleveland after practice to pay for shoppers’ groceries.
His mom was there to share the moment.
“And it’s more than just a Thanksgiving dinner, too...So many people are being blessed today. It's so much fun!” Pilar said in her Instagram video .
Thanksgiving can bring the joy of getting everyone around the same table and the worry of figuring out how to pay for what goes on it. For the shoppers Sanders sent to the checkout, one of those worries was taken care of.
In footage from News 5 Cleveland , Sanders told one shopper to get in the middle line, where he’d heard they were giving away free groceries.
“Oh, okay. I need that,” the shopper replied.
“You're ahead of the game now,” Sanders said as he showed the customer where to go.
Kandis Maxwell was among the shoppers Sanders invited to the checkout. She told News 5 Cleveland she had kids and that Sanders was her favorite Browns quarterback. Meeting him was a surprise in itself. Having him pay for her groceries meant something more.
“It just came at a good time and it was unexpected,” Maxwell said. “I’m just thankful.”
Asked what Cleveland had come to mean to him, Sanders talked about the respect people showed one another and how the city had supported the entire team.
“I think that’s just we’re all trending in the right direction here in Cleveland. I’m excited,” he told News 5 Cleveland.
There was still time for a little football talk. When a shopper asked if Sanders would start Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, the quarterback pointed to how the Browns were playing .
“You got to think we are winning and we are doing what we got to do,” he told the fan. “Of course I want to play. I’m going to be aggressive when I get out there.”
Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns in his first start of the season, an overtime loss to New Orleans on Nov. 8. Deshaun Watson returned the following week as Cleveland beat Houston. The Browns come out of their bye at 6–4 and host Las Vegas on Sunday night .
Sanders said he picked this day because he knew plenty of people would be shopping. He also talked about the times someone had shown him an unexpected kindness and how even a few words could change his outlook.
At Dave’s Market, he had a chance to do something for the people right in front of him.
“You don’t know how long you may be alive,” Sanders said. “So you might as well do it while you can.”

title: Todd Monken Warns Browns About Challenge of Facing Raiders' TE Brock Bowers
full_text:
Browns Head coach Todd Monken is a vocal leader. The kind of guy that players love to have in their corner.
All season long, he has shown not only a deep desire to win and succeed on Sundays, but also a commitment to helping both new and veteran players keep improving. Even now, as the head coach of the Cleveland Browns, he is quick to recognize and praise opposing competitors, even those who could stand in the Browns' way of coming away with a win.
On Tuesday, Nov. 24, Monken took time during his media availability to praise Las Vegas Raiders tight end and former Georgia Bulldog Brock Bowers. The Browns are taking on Bowers and the Raiders this coming Sunday, Nov. 29, at 8:20 p.m. EST in a primetime showdown from Huntington Bank Field.
"He's just wired the right way, man. He's unique," Monken said. "He's rare. From the moment he got to Georgia, I always tell the story: we used to mess with him and call him Buddy the Ole' Lab. You could play ball all day, and his tongue would be hanging out, and he never wanted to come out. He would just want to keep playing..."
Monken, the Bulldogs' offensive coordinator from 2020 through 2022, coached Bowers during his freshman and sophomore seasons. He said that from the moment Bowers came into the program, he excelled.
"He got to Georgia, and we were in the stadium. Winter conditioning," Monken continued. "You are doing the old-school run: run the long, walk the short around the football field... You had to run as a group... So, there were groups together, and I will never forget this... On his first day there, they had to meet a certain time; they start running, and he is 10 yards in front of all of them. Now, I could never have done that.
"Here, you are first day; you are going to run with the pack; everyone is going to say you're showboating, you are trying to impress the coaches; that is all he knows. All he knows is one speed and work..."
During Monken's span coaching Bowers, the Bulldogs won back-to-back national championships and Bowers was one of the offensive catalysts, hauling in 119 receptions for 1,824 yards and 20 touchdowns . He also rushed 13 times for 165 yards and four scores.
Browns HC Todd Monken talks about #Raiders TE Brock Bowers who he coached at Georgia pic.twitter.com/oImPaEcus0
Monken went on to joke that he hopes Bowers is still hurt this weekend, which would give the Browns an advantage this weekend in defending the passing attack. Obviously, he doesn't actually mean it, though.
"And uh, hopefully, he is still hurt," he said with a grin.
Bowers has been dealing with both ankle and quadriceps injuries that kept him out of the Raiders' Week 11 loss to the Denver Broncos . Without him in the game, the passing attack leaned more towards Ashton Jeanty and Jack Bech, with the tight end targets going to Ian Thomas and Michael Mayer.
While Bowers is a really important piece to the Raiders' offense, rookie Fernando Mendoza, being so fresh and impressionable, has allowed him to adjust to whoever he ends up getting on the field with.
But as Monken alluded to, if the Browns can match up with the Raiders on Sunday without Bowers on the field, they will be in a much better position to lock down the former No. 1 overall pick.

title: Browns Could Be One Defensive Addition Away From Becoming a Championship Threat
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns’ 2026 season is shaping up to be a memorable one, with the team firmly engaged in the race for the playoffs despite below-average quarterback play and a running game that scares no one.
Coordinator Mike Rutenberg’s defensive unit has been a big factor in the Browns’ surprising season, managing to keep most games close enough for quarterback Deshaun Watson to turn it on late and lead a number of fourth-quarter comebacks.
Cleveland’s defense features several big-time names, including cornerback Denzel Ward, who’s playing the best ball of his life at 29 years old , and second-year wonder Carson Schwesinger , who’s already earned a spot among the league’s top linebackers. Standout rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren has also been making noise despite starting just four games this year. And they’ve managed all this despite trading away all-World defensive end Myles Garrett during the offseason.
The Browns are currently ranked fifth-best in passing defense (2,011 yards), second-best in passing completion percentage allowed (58.8), second-best in tackles for a loss (64), and seventh-best in yards allowed after the catch (980) after 10 games.
However solid this group looks week after week, it’s still not part of the truly elite echelon in the league--not by a long shot.
The Browns aren’t so bright in many other aspects of defensive play, including 10th-worst in rushing defense (1,263), 10th-worst in rushing yards per game (126.3), sixth-worst in rushing yards per attempt (4.6), and 10th-worst in quarterback hurry percentage.
And the team is downright mediocre in other spots as well, such as points allowed per game (22.0, tied 14th), takeaways (13, tied 14th), and sacks (27, tied 11th).
Personnel-wise, Cleveland is still waiting for Jared Verse’s breakout game after recording zero sacks, zero passes defended, zero forced fumbles, zero fumbles recovered, and just four tackles for a loss after the first 10 games in a Browns uniform.
Mason Graham started the season on fire, but has since slowed down statistically after knee and ankle injuries forced him to miss two games in October, while Derek Barnett --a late offseason addition to the defensive line-- is also sackless and has one forced fumble and one tackle for a loss in 10 appearances for the club.
Yes, but it won’t be easy. Over the past 15 months, NFL teams have traded away generational talents in their prime, such as Micah Parsons, Jeffery Simmons, and, of course, Garrett.
The Browns own two first-rounders and three fourth-rounders in 2027, two second-rounders in 2028, and two third-rounders in 2029, so there are ample resources to work with if another marquee name should come up available during the next offseason.
A couple of big names to watch in case a trade market materializes are the Niners’ Nick Bosa and the Raiders’ Maxx Crosby.
Bosa is tricky. He hasn’t recorded a sack in five appearances this year, and injuries are clearly piling up. He hasn’t compiled double-digit sacks since 2023, and at 29 years of age, it’s hard to expect him to get substantially better than what we’re seeing right now.
But those numbers, coupled with two remaining years on his deal with no guaranteed money, mean he could be available, with the acquiring team signing an extension to lower projected cap hits of around $33 million and $34 million for 2027 and 2028, respectively. San Francisco would also need to agree to take on a dead cap charge of $49 million by letting him walk, which isn’t impossible.
A Crosby trade had already been agreed upon during this past offseason for two Ravens’ first-rounders, before Baltimore backed out of the deal . Unlike Bosa, it doesn’t seem like Crosby has lost a step, so that figure might still be the going rate for his services, along with about $85 million for the three remaining years on his deal, which only includes about $29 million guaranteed for 2027. That sounds enticing. But if Crosby were put on the trading block again, expect him to have multiple suitors.
A talent like Crosby, coupled with Verse's expected breakthrough, should instantly change the dynamics up front for the Browns, for the better.
A couple of non-elite but still very interesting names to keep tabs on would include the Steelers’ Alex Highsmith and the Eagles’ Nolan Smith. If we’re talking about help on the inside, the Eagles’ Jalen Carter instantly becomes the biggest name out there.
Potential free agent alternatives at edge rusher include the Bills’ Greg Rousseau, Chargers’ Tuli Tuipulotu, and Rams’ Byron Young. While these names would save the team valuable draft capital, the financial burden of an open-market free agent contract could become unbearable in the medium term.
Other names to watch in free agency include Bucs’ YaYa Diaby, Titans’ Jermaine Johnson II, and Giants Kayvon Thibodeaux, with all those names likely commanding deals worth around $20 million and upwards per year. Rams’ Kobie Turner would surely draw a similar figure at the tackle position.
Regardless, expect the Browns to add more bodies to the defensive line via the draft, with a high chance of a top-round pick, depending on what the team decides to do at the quarterback position.
Outside of Crosby, it's hard to find one name that could change it all for Cleveland. Therefore, a multiple-reinforcement strategy looks like the safest bet. Nonetheless, the defensive line should be the top priority on defense.
Rafael brings more than two decades worth of experience writing all things football.

title: Todd Monken Gets Honest About Browns' Week 11 Bye
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns' 2026 bye couldn't have come at a better time.
Following a Week 10 win over the Houston Texans at home, 27-24 , the Browns marched right into a Week 11 bye, giving themselves time to reset and regroup ahead of the back half of the regular season.
Fortunately, while they didn't suit up this past weekend, they got plenty of wins as the Baltimore Ravens, Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals all lost. Not only does that give the Browns a big opportunity to take the No. 1 spot in the AFC North , but they also now sit in sixth in the playoff bracket.
Head coach Todd Monken spoke to the media on Tuesday, Nov. 24, shedding light on how this bye week couldn't have come at a better time.
"... I told the team this morning. I hope they enjoyed their time away. They earned that," Monken said. "...And we have earned the right to be where we are at, and that same old saying: 'so what, now what.' All we can control is having the best Tuesday that we can today. That's all we can do.
"...All that matters is the day we have today and getting ourselves ready to fight like hell to seven [wins]."
With the entire AFC North losing this weekend, the bye week couldn’t have gone better for Todd Monken and #Browns . pic.twitter.com/KHPvmgarpN
The Browns, unlike many teams this Thanksgiving week, won't have to suit up for a mid-week affair.
The Green Bay Packers play on Wednesday night against the Los Angeles Rams, and the Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions, Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys, Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills all play on Thursday for Thanksgiving.
Monken went on to say that it was nice that the Browns didn't have to change their practice schedule around, especially coming out of the bye.
"It worked out great for us," he said. "In my opinion, having the bye last week, to bring them back today, have today be like a normal Wednesday practice, tomorrow be like a normal Thursday, then Thursday morning we have the ability to basically get ahead of redzone, walk on Thursday... and then really recap what we have installed the first two days and then get the guys out of here.
"Like I said before, it is a unique opportunity here. Because normally you are scrambling to install on Thursday and let the guys have time with their family and friends... Because all have a lot to be thankful for..."
Todd Monken is thankful the #Browns bye week came right before Thanksgiving pic.twitter.com/5ob08fUGS3
While Monken's comments sure are correct, the only hope now is that the players didn't waste the bye week and added free time to their schedules, but instead used it to get ready for a critical stretch of the season.

title: Dallas Cowboys' Thanksgiving Press Box Meal Is An Epic Feast For Game Day vs Eagles
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys take their fair share of criticism thanks to Jerry Jones' love of creating a 24/7 soap opera , but when you're America's Team, you have to get some things right.
For Dallas, that moment comes each and every year on Thanksgiving Day. For the 2026 season, that means welcoming the NFC East rival Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium as the team looks to win its fifth consecutive Thanksgiving Day game and put together its first winning streak of the season.
The Cowboys' Thanksgiving traditions begin with the Red Kettle Kickoff partnership with The Salvation Army, extend to the annual Thanksgiving Day game, and include an epic feast for media members at AT&T Stadium.
We always get a sneak peek at the Thanksgiving spread for media members on social media, and this year, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram blessed the timeline with a look at today's meal
The Cowboys always make sure Thanksgiving at AT&T Stadium is a treat pic.twitter.com/uHDLz6g0N3
Let's hope the Cowboys' offense and defense can eat as well as the media members did before the game, because Dallas needs a big win to keep their postseason dreams within reach.
Last week, despite a big win over the Tennessee Titans, the Cowboys' playoff chances took a big hit thanks to the Giants' upset win over the Jacksonville Jaguars.
But back to the Cowboys' most important Thanksgiving tradition, the Red Kettle Kickoff partnership with The Salvation Army, the Gene and Jerry Jones Family made a $30 million donation to The Salvation Army of North Texas' One Army, Many Fronts Campaign, which is the largest gift to the campaign to date.
"Thirty years ago, we began a partnership with The Salvation Army that has grown into something far greater than we could have ever imagined," said Cowboys owner/General Manager Jerry Jones in a statement. "What makes this 30th anniversary especially meaningful is now being able to have four generations of our family come together around something that means so much to us .
"We wanted to honor this incredible milestone with a special gift that reflects how much this partnership means to our family and our commitment to the important work The Salvation Army does every day. It's a tradition that has become part of the fabric of our lives and one we hope will continue for generations to come."

title: Dak Prescott Has Shot at Breaking Historic Tom Brady Record on Thanksgiving
full_text:
Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott already made history earlier this season when he passed Tony Romo to become the franchise's all-time leader in career passing touchdowns.
Now, he's on the brink of more history ahead of Thursday's Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.
Though it's less significant than becoming the all-time passing touchdowns leader for one of the most historical franchise in sports, it's hard to ignore a record potentially being broken when it's attached to Tom Brady's name.
As pointed out by RJ Ochoa of SB Nation, Prescott has won 20 straight home games against divisional opponents as a starting quarterback, which is tied with Brady for the longest streak of its kind since the NFL merger.
A win on Thursday against the Eagles would move Prescott past Brady for a record that could remain untouched for the remainder of our lifetimes. Prescott has not lost a divisional home game in which he started since 2017. That's almost unheard of.
In that time, the Cowboys have lost three NFC East games at home, but Prescott was not active for any of them due to injury.
Sure, it's somewhat of a cherry-picked stat with very specific criteria but breaking a record like that proves impressive longevity and consistency as a quarterback. It's no surprise that Brady held it for so long.
It hasn't quite been the MVP-worthy season he had in 2023 but Prescott is still on pace to come close to those numbers. In a year where the Cowboys might not even made the playoffs, Dallas' high-volume passing offense has allowed Prescott's numbers to thrive.
Headed into Thursday's game against the Eagles, Prescott is 276 of 420 passing for 3,049 yards, 25 touchdowns and six interceptions.
After having four interceptions combined in back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Green Bay Packers earlier this season, Prescott has had 17 total touchdowns and just one pick in the five games since then.
But it doesn't seem like it's ever enough to the rest of the world.
It seems that many Cowboys fans still take his greatness for granted at this point. He has gotten some unfair criticism from both the fans and media at times this season despite being one of the best quarterbacks in the NFL once again.
Prescott hasn't been perfect but if the rest of the team can't improve, he just might need to be in order to give the Cowboys a shot at winning the NFC East.

title: Dallas Cowboys vs. Philadelphia Eagles Predictions: NFL Expert Picks For Week 12 Game
full_text:
For the second and final time this season, the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles will square off in Week 12 at AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving Day.
The first battle between the NFC East foes took place in Week 7, when Dallas handled its business against an ailing Eagles team that didn't have Jalen Hurts and other starters.
Philly is even more depleted since then after the team traded away defensive lineman Jordan Davis at the deadline. And, instead of Tanner McKee starting, the Eagles will deploy Joe Milton .
In what is a crucial game for the Cowboys , who are clinging to their playoff hopes, let's see what experts think will happen in the Week 12 contest between Dallas and Philadelphia on Thursday.
It's a clean sweep for the Cowboys in our expert picks round-up, and that's not at all surprising given the current state of the Eagles.
I'm going to make it 34-0, and not because this is some major vote of confidence in the Cowboys, but rather skepticism that Philly is capable of keeping up with the Cowboys' offense.
Philly's defense has played better of late , but this is still the same unit that gave up 38 to Dallas' offense back in Week 7 and there's no reason to suspect things will be different this week, especially with Dak Prescott playing some of the best football of his career lately.
While the Eagles will have a different quarterback this time around in our old friend Joe Milton, the third-year signal-caller has not looked good in two starts.
Of course, this Cowboys defense is very beatable and I would never put it past any signal-caller to have a good game against Dallas' unit, but we did see a slight improvement on defense in Mike Pettine's first game as the play-caller .
The keys to success are very simple: limit Saquon Barkley and Milton on the ground and force the Tennessee product to win through the air while the Dallas offense takes care of the rest.
Do that and it should be a fun Thanksgiving for the Cowboys.

title: 3 Things Dallas Cowboys Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
It's been an up-and-down season for the Dallas Cowboys, but today is a day to recognize the positive moments. After weeks of waxing poetic about how terrible the defense is and how it may be time to move on from head coach Brian Schottenheimer , let's look at things through a more optimistic lens in the spirit of the holiday.
Dallas welcomes the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium on Thursday evening, and if the oddsmakers at DraftKings Sportsbook are to be believed, we could have something to be thankful for by the end of the day.
The Cowboys enter the game as 8.5-point favorites at home, so as long as the team takes care of business like it did a week ago and for the past four Thanksgivings, we can end the day on a high note.
But while we wait for today's result, let's take a look at three things Cowboys Nation should be thankful for this Thanksgiving.
Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER .
Sure, the NFL didn't anticipate the Cowboys and Eagles sitting where they currently are when the season began, but after picking up a win over the Tennessee Titans in Week 11 , the Cowboys have an opportunity to end the month on a winning streak for the first time this year.
The Eagles have been awful, and while they are coming off a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, the Cowboys should have the upper hand. And who wants to sit around on the holiday watching their favorite team lose? The NFL is giving Dallas a chance to keep the vibes high.
After how poorly the Cowboys started the regular season, the team has no business being in the playoff mix. The defense has been putrid, and the offense has had its share of stumbles. But because of the chaos in the division, the Cowboys still have a chance .
The New York Giants and Eagles are both down their starting quarterbacks, while Washington Commanders star Jayden Daniels also missed some time with a dislocated elbow. That has kept the division race tight, so as long as Dallas can do its job, the NFC East title is within reach.
There is still a chance to turn things around, but it all starts on Thanksgiving Day.
Speaking of chaos, thank you to the Pittsburgh Steelers. If it weren't for the organization, the Cowboys wouldn't be without two of their best players on the roster. Last year, the Cowboys traded for star wide receiver George Pickens , and he's helped to open up the offense. This year, an even bigger addition was made.
Yes, it's nice to have a flashy offense, but the reason the Cowboys haven't been able to accomplish anything in recent years is because of the defensive struggles. The team went out and acquired cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from Pittsburgh , and he's been the definition of a shutdown corner.
In his six games since joining the Cowboys, Porter has allowed only five catches on 15 targets for 35 yards and no touchdowns allowed. Porter has added five pass breakups, and he's done all of this while dealing with a nagging foot injury. He is the type of superstar you can build your defense around.
Both players have contract situations that will need to be addressed in the offseason, but that isn't today. Today, we can just be thankful that they have the star on their helmets and can help lift the team to victory over the visiting Eagles.

title: Dallas Cowboys Sign Promising RB For Thanksgiving Game After Flashing Signs of Brilliance

The Dallas Cowboys running back room has been bruised and battered throughout the 2026-27 NFL campaign, with a revolving door behind bell-cow back Javonte Williams.

title: Former Cowboys QB Defends Mike McCarthy After Aaron Rodgers' Tirade
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys have somehow gotten sucked into the drama that's currently infecting the Pittsburgh Steelers locker room ahead of Week 12 in the NFL.
Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy was the subject of some heavy criticism on The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday by quarterback Aaron Rogers, who accused McCarthy of laziness, falling asleep during meetings and eating an unnecessary amount of ice cream sandwiches.
The Steelers released Rodgers shortly after.
Rodgers said that McCarthy's alleged issues were prevalent when he was head coach in Dallas from 2020-24. However, one former Cowboys quarterback is sharing his side of the story and defending McCarthy in the process.
Former Cowboys quarterback Ben DiNucci, who is now a studio analyst for CBS Sports, took to social media on Wednesday to defend McCarthy.
DiNucci was a seventh-round pick by the Cowboys in the 2020 NFL Draft ahead of McCarthy's first season as head coach. Dallas parted ways with DiNucci for good ahead of the 2022 season, but during that span, he got to work with McCarthy closely.
DiNucci wrote on X that he never saw McCarthy falling asleep during quarterback meetings and that he made an effort to get to know everyone "from what he could tell."
No mention of ice cream sandwiches here.
"I was a rookie/young guy so I wasn’t really paying attention to what the head coach was doing. Had other things to worry about," DiNucci wrote on X. "Aaron obviously has a different relationship with him but that’s my two cents."
I was in Dallas with Mike for 2.5 years - never witnessed him doze off or fall asleep, he was part of the qb meetings daily - he didn’t call plays , Kellen Moore did - from what I could tell he made an effort to get to know guys I was a rookie / young guy so I wasn’t…
DiNucci played in three games for the Cowboys as a rookie, which included the only start of his NFL career in Week 8 against the Philadelphia Eagles that season. He finished that year 23 of 43 passing for 219 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions along with six carries for 22 yards.
DiNucci got thrown into the fire after Dak Prescott suffered a season-ending leg injury while backup Andy Dalton missed time due to a concussion and COVID protocols.
McCarthy's first season in Dallas was filled with adversity. DiNucci was right in the middle of it and likely got to see the best and worst of McCarthy.
His opinion of the former Cowboys head coach holds weight, but it's also been a few years. It's anyone's guess what McCarthy has gone through in the time since then.

title: Dallas Cowboys Get Major Boost on Defense Before Eagles Game
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys started off the season with some major injury issues on defense. This certainly didn't help first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker get off on the right foot with a unit that was already going to struggle in the first place.
Though the defense still needs to show notable improvement if the Cowboys want to make the postseason, things could be trending up ever so slightly. Dallas has gotten healthier and Mike Pettine has taken over play-calling duties on defense, potentially giving the Cowboys a boost that they desperately need.
Now, Dallas is receiving more good news ahead of Thursday's matchup with the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day.
The Cowboys announced that they have elevated safety Jalen Thompson from injured reserve, paving the way for him to make his return following an eight-game absence due to a hamstring injury that he originally suffered in Week 3's loss to the Baltimore Ravens.
Thompson started the first three games of the season for Dallas while posting 17 total tackles (eight solo) and one quarterback hit on 167 defensive snaps.
Thompson's addition to the Dallas defense this past offseason was viewed as one of the more notable signings that the front office made. He was set to bring a veteran presence to the secondary as starter from Day 1, but his injury left the Cowboys with questions on defense.
Thompson's extended absence hasn't allowed him to show his worth quite yet. That could certainly change moving forward, especially since the Cowboys are still without veteran safety P.J. Locke III against the Eagles.
Along with activating Thompson from IR, the Cowboys are making an expected move to address their running back room before hosting the Eagles.
Dallas is elevating running back Jashaun Corbin from the practice squad, just like last week. Corbin will serve as the backup to Javonte Williams with Tyler Goodson still out after being placed on injured reserve.
Corbin had the best game of his career against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, finishing with five carries for 32 yards along with one catch for five. After primarily playing special teams and have a minimal role on offense to start his NFL career, Corbin could play a notable role for the Cowboys if Williams were to exit with an injury.

title: Mile High Roundtable: Broncos at Steelers Predictions on Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos got out to an 8-2 start for the second straight year. That's an exceedingly difficult feat to achieve.
It's especially impressive given the brutal schedule the Broncos faced in the first half of the season. In what remains of the schedule, the Broncos have just two opponents that are currently above .500, and the first one comes this week.
However, the 6-4 Pittsburgh Steelers seem to be reeling after benching quarterback Aaron Rodgers , who promptly went on the Pat McAfee Show the next day and slammed head coach Mike McCarthy for sleeping in meetings, being forgetful, skipping offensive meetings, neglecting the defense, and more. The Steelers released Rodgers on Wednesday.
And so Mason Rudolph will start for the Steelers. It's been a PR firestorm in the Steel City, and a massive distraction, so the Broncos will get the chance to exploit the situation.
Expect rain and wind on Friday, too. Sean Payton is planning on it being a "weather game." How will this one shake out?
Let's go around the table to see how the Mile High Huddle / Denver Broncos On SI staff envisions this one unfolding on Black Friday.
Keith Cummings ( @KeithC_NFL ) 8-2 : Even with the distinctly average Rudolph at the controls, the Broncos never seem to blow anyone out. Inclement weather might make Jonah Coleman the key player on Black Friday football, but Bo Nix's knack for protecting the ball will be massive. Denver's defense ultimately has too much for Rudolph to handle, forcing three turnovers in a crucial road victory.
Pick : Broncos 24, Steelers 14
Chad Jensen ( @ChadNJensen ) 8-2 : This game has Jonah Coleman written all over it. The Broncos faced their own PR controversy this week when Payton suspended running back J.K. Dobbins, but it paled in comparison to what the Steelers have been through. In Nix's first two career starts, he lost to the Seattle Seahawks and Steelers. Nix avenged the Seahawks loss, so now it's time to balance the scales with Pittsburgh. Look for Vance Joseph to be merciless in his pressure packages to force Rudolph into some bad decisions. And just as I predicted last week that Coleman would notch his first-ever 100-yard rushing day, the rookie has another big game on the ground with two touchdowns, though he comes up short of the century mark against Pittsburgh's third-ranked rushing defense.

Zack Kelberman ( @KelbermanNFL ) 8-2 : This feels more like a "trap game" than the Cardinals, Panthers, or Raiders contests did — a weird Friday afternoon game, on the road, against a team in total freefall. Add a little bad weather, and this has the makings of a low-scoring, ugly, run-oriented, defensive battle. But one from which the Broncos should be able to emerge victorious. Don't expect a ton of Nix wizardry; this has "Jonah Coleman statement" written all over it.

Nick Kendell ( @NickKendellMHH ) 8-2 : Current forecast, it’s gonna be an ugly weather game for the Broncos in Pittsburgh. The Steelers have invested heavily on both sides of the line of scrimmage, but are severely lacking on the perimeter, compared to the Broncos. Weather could nullify those advantages. Expect a heavy dosage of run game and reliance on Nix’s legs in an ugly one.
Pick : Broncos 17, Steelers 16
Bob Morris ( @BobMorrisSports ) 8-2 : While it's easy to think Rudolph starting means a blowout for the Broncos, the Steelers' defense is good against the run, and Jaylen Warren is a good running back . The weather could mean this will be an ugly game and a close one at that. Still, the Broncos can get it done, even if it doesn't look pretty.

Carl Dumler ( @CarlDumlerMHH ) 7-3 : The Steelers have been a different beast at home this year compared to on the road. This is looking like another close, down-to-the-wire game, with the Broncos relying on their defense to contain on an ugly day. title: Broncos' Black Friday Blueprint: 3 Keys to Beating the Steelers
full_text:
The 8-2 Denver Broncos have a legitimate shot at not only winning the AFC West title for the second straight season, but also the No. 1 seed in the conference again, too.
While the Broncos might be entering the easier part of their schedule, that doesn't mean they are facing pushovers. The Las Vegas Raiders were a challenge last week, and now the Broncos will take to the road to face a solid Pittsburgh Steelers team on Black Friday.
The Steelers are 6-4 for the season and are looking to make the playoffs again. And as much as a win would help the Broncos in their playoff hunt, the same could be said for the Steelers, who are currently the sixth seed and aren't yet out of the running for the AFC North title.
Even amid the PR upheaval in Pittsburgh this week, the Broncos will have to play a good game in all aspects — and they'll have to deal with inclement weather , with rain in the forecast that could potentially turn into sleet.
The weather will be a key factor in Friday's game, but it's not the only thing the Broncos need to worry about. Let's break down my three keys to a Broncos win on Friday.
The Broncos entered the week expecting to face the 43-year-old Aaron Rodgers, a future Hall of Famer. His numbers looked fine on paper — 60.9 completion percentage, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions — but he's taken 31 sacks despite being pressured on just 20.3% of his dropbacks.
Rodgers doesn’t have the ability to extend plays as he did in his prime. Perhaps that’s one reason he was benched in favor of Rudolph , who is at least younger.
However, that may not be saying much, because Rudolph has taken 35 sacks in 38 career games (19 starts) while being pressured on 20.3 % of his dropbacks. He might be able to extend plays more than Rodgers at this point, but Rudolph still takes too many sacks.
The Broncos' defense needs to turn up the pressure and go after Rudolph whenever he drops back to pass. If the Broncos can do that, they'll either force him into a mistake or sack him.
The Broncos will need to have good coverage as well, because the Steelers' offensive line does a good job with pass blocking. If the Broncos' pass rushers can’t get to Rudolph, they need to keep him in the pocket rather than giving him a chance to extend the play.
Rudolph is a backup, but he’s shown he can make plays when the opportunity is there — and furthermore, he has quality playmakers around him that the Broncos must watch.
Broncos fans know about DK Metcalf, a talented receiver who made headlines this past week after being ejected for poking Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye.
Metcalf is a good player, and he's not facing a suspension this week, but he's not necessarily the biggest worry for the Broncos. Patrick Surtain II will often draw him in coverage.
Metcalf is a threat, but he isn't having the same impact with the Steelers that he did with the Seattle Seahawks. However, Warren and Friermuth are different stories, particularly when it comes to the Broncos' weaknesses on defense.
Let's start with Warren, who has averaged 5.5 yards per carry this season, leading all NFL running backs in that stat. He's the guy who sets the table for the Steelers' offense, even if he hasn't produced many touchdowns (he has just two rushing scores this season).
But we've seen the Broncos have issues letting running backs make big plays, whether on the ground or in the passing game. Warren is a good receiver, as evidenced by his 32 receptions on 45 targets for 321 yards this season.
And then there's Friermuth, who doesn't enter the conversation when people talk about the best tight ends in the game, but he's proven he can get the job done. He leads the Steelers in receiving touchdowns with five and has caught 32 receptions on 43 targets.
Tight ends producing big numbers against the Broncos has become a theme. Friermuth is worth watching, as he could make a bigger difference for the Steelers than Metcalf, given the weaknesses of the Denver defense.
The Broncos can't ignore Pittsburgh's other weapons, but Warren and Friermuth have to top the list, particularly to limit the effectiveness of a good running back and a good tight end.
The weather forecast for Friday in Pittsburgh may indicate the Broncos are better off running the football, but that plays to the strengths of the Steelers' defense.
The Steelers have given up just 840 yards rushing to opponents thus far, limiting opposing running backs to just 3.6 yards per carry, and ranking third in the NFL against the run.
While Jonah Coleman is coming off a strong outing — and you can't take that away from him — it did come against a Raiders defense that ranks low against the run. The Steelers aren't soft up front, so Coleman can't be expected to put the offense on his shoulders.
That means Bo Nix has to come through — and it means his receivers need to do their jobs too. Nix had a good game against the Raiders, but it might have looked better had it not been for a number of accurate passes being dropped.
The Broncos do have to be mindful of the Steelers' pass rush, which features TJ Watt (7.5 sacks) and Alex Highsmith (5.5 sacks, though Highsmith is dealing with an ankle injury ), but if the pass protection holds up and Nix stands tall in the pocket, he has a chance to exploit this secondary.
The Steelers have given up 2,303 yards to opposing quarterbacks this season and 6.1 yards per passing attempt, and they rank 24th against the pass. They do have seven interceptions, but teams must execute well in the passing game to prevail against Pittsburgh.
While one shouldn't expect Nix to have 300 yards passing or any receiver to eclipse the century mark, given the weather forecast, they need to produce to take the load off Coleman and whoever spells him for some carries — possibly Tyler Badie, who is designated to return from injured reserve as J.K. Dobbins serves a one-game suspension imposed by Sean Payton.
Coleman deserves praise for his breakout performance against the Raiders , but he has a tougher task ahead. The Broncos need the passing game to come through to help him out.
The Broncos' second-half schedule might be easier than the first half of this season, but the Steelers won't be an easy team to beat. They have good playmakers on offense, despite the quarterback change, and a quality defense, so the Broncos will have their work cut out for them.
It may not be the most ideal weather conditions, but the Broncos will have to deal with it the best they can, work for every score they get, and be consistent on defense.
A win would do a lot to help the Broncos' playoff standing — especially with the Buffalo Bills and Kansas City Chiefs going at it on Thanksgiving. However, the Broncos have to remember they're facing an opponent that would be in the tournament if the playoffs started today.

title: Broncos Rule Out Two Players for Black Friday Game vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Denver Broncos have released their final injury report prior to Friday's road clash with the Aaron Rodgers-less Pittsburgh Steelers.
Denver announced Wednesday that defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones (hamstring) and safety Taylor Rapp (quadricep) are ruled out for the Week 12 contest. Jones failed to practice Tuesday or Wednesday, while Rapp was a limited participant both days.
Five other players — running back Tyler Badie (thumb), wide receiver Pat Bryant (ankle), safety Brandon Jones (hamstring), tight end Caleb Lohner (foot), and safety JL Skinner (shoulder) — were full participants and given no designation for the Black Friday tilt .
The Broncos are expected to leave for Pittsburgh on Wednesday evening, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.
“We were originally going Thursday and then last week [Assistant to the Head Coach] Paul [Kelly] put the schedule up and Thursday looked really noisy," Payton explained to reporters. "I turned to him and I said, ‘Hey, no one’s got the schedule yet, right?’ He said, ‘Nope.’ I said, ‘All right.’ So then I said, ‘Are you sure no one’s got it?’ You have to know Paul, he said, ‘Well, I kind of told [QB Jarrett] Stidham.’ (Laughs) I said, ‘So someone has it.’ But anyway, just relative to that Thursday, and there’s a setup there where we can get a walkthrough in, then guys will have extra time after the game.”
On the Steelers' side , Rodgers (who's since been cut), outside linebacker Alex Highsmith, wide receiver Ben Skowronek, and defensive lineman Cameron Heyward did not practice on Wednesday. Safety DeShon Elliott, outside linebacker Nick Herbig, and inside linebacker Cole Holcomb were limited.
Rapp has been a nice find for the Broncos, an experienced former starter who began on Denver's practice squad and filled in admirably following injuries to starting safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones.
Hufanga returned for last week's win over the Las Vegas Raiders and Jones is back this week to face the Steelers. And with JL Skinner joining Devon Key behind them on the depth chart, Rapp is needed much less than he was.
Jones has been a rotational contributor to Denver's defensive line in 2026, helping fill the shoes of John Franklin-Myers, whom the club lost in free agency this past spring.
To compensate for Jones' rule-out, the Broncos signed ex-Chiefs DL Khalen Saunders to the practice squad. It's also possible (if not probable) that third-round rookie Tyler Onyedim sees an increased snap count against the Steelers.

title: Broncos Sign Two-Time Super Bowl Champion Amid D-Line Injuries
full_text:
With injuries to the defensive line, the Denver Broncos added some veteran depth ahead of their Black Friday road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
On Wednesday, the Broncos signed eighth-year defensive lineman Khalen Saunders to the practice squad. The Broncos worked him and three other defensive trenchmen out on Tuesday, but they ultimately went with the 30-year-old Saunders.
Two weeks ago, the Broncos lost Eyioma Uwazurike to a shoulder injury. He's got a couple of games left until he could return from injured reserve.
In Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders, Broncos second-year defensive lineman Sai'vion Jones suffered a hamstring injury. Jones did not participate in Tuesday's practice, and the Saunders addition implies that Denver expects him to miss more time.
The Broncos' starting trio up front is Zach Allen, D.J. Jones, and Malcolm Roach, and with Jones out of commission, that leaves veteran Jordan Jackson and rookie third-rounder Tyler Onyedim as depth. The Broncos also have the 6-foot-3, 307-pound Jordan Miller on the practice squad, but he's relatively untested and is on the small side.
Saunders, 6-foot-0 and 324 pounds, was a Kansas City Chiefs third-round pick back in 2019. He appeared in 38 games with the Chiefs, with five starts. He contributed to two of Kansas City's World Championships.
In the spring of 2023, Saunders hit free agency, signing a three-year, $14.5 million deal with the New Orleans Saints. He started 30 games for the Saints over the next two years.
In August of last year, the Saints traded Saunders to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Alas, it didn't work out well in Jacksonville, and he was waived after appearing in just two games.
Saunders signed with the New York Jets a few days after being waived, and went on to appear in seven games last season. The Tennessee Titans signed him in early August, a little over a week into training camp, but he was waived in the final roster cutdowns later that month.
All in, Saunders has appeared in 77 NFL games with 32 starts, totaling 193 tackles (87 solo), 7.5 sacks, and one interception. His lone interception came as a Saint and was at the expense of Patrick Mahomes, his long-time teammate in Kansas City.
Saunders has played in some big games. That experience is important to a playoff-bound team like the Broncos.
Aside from his veteran experience, Saunders brings some mass and power to the Broncos' defensive line. The Broncos have prioritized athleticism up front, but opponents have been able to exploit the D-line's relative lack of size this season on the ground.
The Broncos enter Week 12's matchup with the Steelers ranked 22nd against the run, relinquishing 126.2 yards per game. I doubt we're going to see Saunders on a short week against the Steelers, but there's a chance he could be a practice squad elevation.
More likely, the elevation possibility comes after Black Friday's road game .
Saunders could be a short-term rental on the practice squad while Uwazurike is on IR and Jones is banged up. Then again, the Broncos could opt to hang onto Saunders down the stretch and into the playoffs, if he does well on the practice squad.
It's better to have and not need than to need and not have.

title: Broncos vs. Steelers: 2 Battles That Could Decide Black Friday
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are on a short-week turnaround as they prepare to take on the Pittsburgh Steelers in their house on Black Friday.
It's another trip to the East Coast, where the Broncos have historically struggled, but that was before Sean Payton came to Denver. There's been a lot of talk about how the Broncos got to 8-2, but the same is true of the 6-4 Steelers, a team with plenty of issues that has somehow managed to win.
The Steelers benched quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Tuesday, then released him, and head coach Mike McCarthy is under fire, but don't let that fool you; it's still going to be a tough game. Going into Pittsburgh is never easy, but winning these key matchups would go a long way toward the Broncos getting to 9-2 and beating one of the two plus-.500 opponents remaining on their schedule.
Let's break down the matchups.
Throughout the season, the Broncos' interior offensive line has had issues. Center Luke Wattenberg has been among the worst centers, left guard Ben Powers has played poorly enough to be replaced by Matt Peart, and even right guard Quinn Meinerz hasn't been the powerhouse blocker he usually is.
These issues led Payton to voice his dissatisfaction with the blocking up front during the bye, which prompted the aforementioned change at left guard, with Peart starting in place of Powers. Against the Steelers, though, this interior O-line is about to face a much bigger test.
The Steelers' defensive strength over the years has been their front seven, particularly their depth and consistency along the interior defensive line. Cameron Heyward leads the D-line, but Keeanu Benton, Derrick Harmon, and Yahya Black are all good players who can give the Broncos' interior blockers plenty of issues.
The Steelers are great against the run, with plenty of ability to generate pressure against any ground attack. Pittsburgh is currently the NFL's third-ranked rushing defense, and its 30 sacks rank sixth.
Heyward leads the group with 27 pressures, with the other three combining for 32, but Harmon has only played in six games this season. With the Broncos' interior issues, they have to be wary of this unit, especially in the running game, where they've struggled the most.
The Broncos can’t let the Steelers' defensive line control the trenches; otherwise, it could lead to a long day for Bo Nix and company, including Jonah Coleman, the AFC's reigning Offensive Player of the Week .
Flipping to the other side of the ball, it's another trench battle. The Steelers' offense goes through its ground game, and Frazier is a key part of the run blocking.
Frazier is technically sound on combo blocks, double teams, and climbing, so opponents have to account for him in the run game just to slow down the Steelers' rushing attack. That puts a lot of pressure on Jones, the Broncos' key run defender.
Jones is a solid run defender and a great one when he can force one-on-one blocks, but he struggles against double teams. He lacks the mass and length to hold up at the point of attack against double teams.
That means Jones must beat Frazier one-on-one and try to hold up against Pittsburgh's double teams. When Jones draws a double team, he just has to hold up long enough to keep those two blockers engaged, particularly Frazier, to prevent them from pulling off to the second level.
If Jones can hold the double teams, it'll give the Broncos another open man, running free to stop the run. This is one of the rare matchups where it's about a player doing his job in order to free up a teammate, rather than making a direct impact on the ball.
But if Jones can’t hold up against Frazier, individually and in a double team, it will likely allow Pittsburgh to control the trenches, which would be costly, given how badly the Broncos have struggled against the run at times, ranking 22nd in the NFL.

title: Broncos' Jonah Coleman Earns Major NFL Honor After Historic Day
full_text:
It's unfortunate what's happening with J.K. Dobbins and his suspension , but don't let it detract from the Denver Broncos' Jonah Coleman phenomenon.
Coleman rushed for 111 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries in the Broncos' Week 11 win over the Las Vegas Raiders . The fourth-round rookie running back has been named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his historic day against Denver's oldest division rival, as well as the FedEx Air and Ground Player of the Week.
🎩🎩🎩 RT to help us congratulate @jonahcoleman8 on being named AFC Offensive Player of the Week! 👏 pic.twitter.com/dLq30d8EaH
Coleman is the third Bronco to win conference honors this season, joining safety Talanoa Hufanga and linebacker Alex Singleton. Both of those players are veterans, though.
Against the Raiders, Coleman became the first Broncos rookie to rush for 100-plus yards and three touchdowns in a game since Clinton Portis in 2002. Coleman wasn't born until August of 2003, the next summer.
It's been a while since the Broncos have had a running as prolific as Coleman out of the gates. This team went 19 games without a 100-yard individual rusher, but he finally got that monkey off Denver's back.
The last Broncos' rookie running back to make this kind of noise was Phillip Lindsay in 2018, but he didn't have any three-touchdown displays. However, what made Lindsay's emergence so unique was that he was an undrafted rookie, and he'd go on to eclipse 1,000 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns from scrimmage.
Lindsay became the NFL's first undrafted rookie running back to ever be selected to the Pro Bowl. He's also the first undrafted running back to produce back-to-back 1,000-yard rushing seasons to start his career.
As the Offensive Player of the Week, Coleman became just the 12th Broncos running back to earn the award, joining Lindsay (2018), Ronnie Hillman (2015), C.J. Anderson (2014, '15), Knowshon Moreno (2012), Clinton Portis (2003), Mike Anderson (2000), Olandis Gary (1999), Terrell Davis (1996, '97, '98), Gaston Green (1991), Tony Dorsett (1988), and Joe Dudek (1987). The award has only existed since 1984, and a Broncos skill-position player has won it 67 times.
Coleman has a shot at a 1,000-yard rookie campaign, but he'll have to continue producing close to how he did against the Raiders. With 302 yards and six touchdowns thus far, he's got seven games left to try and reach the milestone, and it won't be easy.
In Lindsay's case, he had the entire season to reach 1,000 yards. Coleman started his rookie campaign healthy, but suffered an ankle sprain in Week 2, which landed him a four-week stay on injured reserve.
Since his return in Week 7, though, Coleman has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns. If the Broncos' offensive line can continue to block like it did against the Raiders, there's a solid chance the rookie can crack 1,000 yards.
Coleman already leads all rookies with his six rushing touchdowns this season, which is one more than the next-highest guy — Kansas City Chiefs running back Emmett Johnson. I have little doubt that Coleman will rush for double-digit touchdowns as a rookie, but there might not be enough runway left to get him over 1,000 yards, given the four games he missed.
Another one for the rook. RT to congratulate @JonahColeman8 on being named a @FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week! pic.twitter.com/uAovj84KFd
The Broncos are absolutely thrilled with Coleman. He may have gone in the fourth round, but he was one of the few complete backs in the 2026 draft class.
Teams saw a willing and able pass protector and a natural catcher of the football, to go along with Coleman's between-the-tackles vision, power, and burst. He's already caught 17 passes for 146 yards and six first downs, with a long of 51 yards.
Coleman may not have been the fastest running back in a straight line, but his burst is something special. And his jump-cut? Perhaps as potent as RJ Harvey's.
Suffice it to say, the Broncos got an enormous steal in Coleman. They're very fortunate he was still on the board at No. 108 overall. And he's just getting started.
Again, it's too bad that Dobbins is taking his diminished role poorly. But the Broncos aren't letting that get in the way of Coleman's continued rise.
The rookie will be put to the test this week with a Black Friday throwdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on deck, in their house. The Steelers currently have the NFL's third-ranked rushing defense, and the weather is expected to be cold and rainy.
It's likely to be a Jonah Coleman type of day.
