title: Broncos' Biggest Stars Weigh In on J.K. Dobbins Suspension
full_text:
Denver Broncos veteran running back J.K. Dobbins wasn't at practice on Tuesday .
We learned afterward from head coach Sean Payton that he had suspended Dobbins for one game due to "conduct detrimental" to the team. Shortly after Payton spoke, quarterback Bo Nix stepped up to the podium for his presser ahead of this Black Friday's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
Two questions in, Nix was asked what his reaction was to hearing of Dobbins's suspension.
'Well, obviously, I have nothing to do with it, and so we'll just keep finding our way to figure out how to win games," Nix said. "Unfortunately, it has nothing to do with me."
Nix likely knows what's going on behind closed doors, but he's not going to break ranks with Payton and spill any beans or be unprofessional by opining publicly on a very sensitive topic. But Nix has always said good things about Dobbins, and since arriving in June of 2025 as a free-agent signing, the veteran back has contributed to a lot of winning.
After Nix, it was Pro Bowl cornerback Patrick Surtain II's turn at the podium. After being asked about this Steelers matchup, the obligatory Dobbins question followed.
"I ain't got nothing much to say about it," Surtain said. "It's a coach's decision at the end of the day."
It was exactly that, according to Payton: a "coach's decision." Dobbins will serve his one-game suspension, during which, he'll be on a suspended/reserve list, opening up a temorary roster spot.
It would appear that spot will be filled by fellow running back Tyler Badie, whom the Broncos designated to return from injured reserve on Tuesday . Badie practiced in full and is poised to return to the field after suffering a thumb injury in the Broncos' Week 6 overtime win over the Seattle Seahawks.
We didn't learn anything from Payton, Nix, or Surtain about why Dobbins was suspended, but we can only assume that the running back's conduct has something to do with his dissatisfaction over his dwindling role on offense. Since rookie running back Jonah Coleman returned from IR in Week 7, Dobbins has set a new career low in snaps in each subsequent game, culminating in his one snap in Sunday's 38-24 win over the Las Vegas Raiders .
Payton will have to strive to ensure this doesn't become a distraction that unfocuses his team. The Steelers are no joke, sitting at 6-4 and coming off back-to-back losses.
At home in front of the Pittsburgh faithful, the Steelers will be hungry to hand Payton and Nix just their fifth regular-season loss since Week 1 of the 2024 season. Payton is a veteran who's been a head coach for two decades, and he's had to deal with some monumental off-the-field distractions over the years, so if anyone knows how to nip things in the bud, it's him.
But it's still a risk. Dobbins is well-regarded in the Broncos' locker room, and has been a vocal leader since arriving two summers ago, even if he's not a team captain.
Nix was taught by his Oregon head coach — Dan Lanning — the art of avoiding the off-field-distraction trap. Nix may be a team captain, but he's only one voice in Denver's locker room.
"Yeah, it's a part of playing long seasons," Nix said on Tuesday. "You have to limit the distractions, starve the distractions and feed your focus. That's something Coach Lanning taught me a long time ago at Oregon. So for us, it's just about the next game and how we can win it."
Nix's off-field distractions this season have been cacophanous at times. National media types have always loved to criticize him, but following his rough day at the office against the Seahawks, there were actually calls for the Broncos to bench him, including from portions of the fan base and local media.
The noise reached a fever pitch entering Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals, but it was in that road game that Nix seemed to turn a corner in his recovery from a broken ankle, as he busted off a 62-yard touchdown run and passed for 200-plus yards.
Nix's confidence seemed to come flooding back after that long run, and he's been on the rise in every game since, outdueling Patrick Mahomes in Week 8, Bryce Young in Week 9, and Fernando Mendoza in Week 11.
Do you know what else coincided with Nix's sudden return to pre-injury form? The return of Coleman, who has rushed for 263 yards and five touchdowns in the four games since then.
The momentum that Coleman has given this offense is not a train that Payton wants to stop any time soon. It's unfortunate that it's come at the expense of Dobbins's playing time, but he had six long weeks to help the Broncos produce an effective ground attack, and cement himself — an $8 million/year veteran — as the RB1.
Alas, Dobbins failed to do that, so Payton went looking for a spark from his rookie fourth-rounder. And Coleman has delivered that spark, oxygenating it to a point now where it's become a roaring blaze.
Here's to hoping the Broncos can avoid too many more questions on the Dobbins topic, so they can take care of business against one of the two plus-.500 opponents remaining on their schedule this season.

title: Steelers Make Sudden QB Change Ahead of Broncos Game
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers made a shocking move at quarterback in the lead-up to Friday's game against the Denver Broncos .
In a brief statement released late Tuesday night, the Steelers announced that QB Aaron Rodgers has been benched and longtime backup Mason Rudolph will start the Week 12 contest at Acrisure Stadium.
"The Pittsburgh Steelers have named Mason Rudolph the starting quarterback for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos. Aaron Rodgers will be inactive," the statement reads.
As of this writing, no reason has been given for Rodgers' benching, which may be related to his recent declining performance. Some have speculated this could be a precursor to Rodgers' release from Pittsburgh or even retirement from the NFL.
Already on record as playing his final season, Rodgers has completed 60.9% of his pass attempts across 10 starts, throwing for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions while leading the Steelers to a 6-4 record.
Rodgers, however, has looked every bit like a soon-to-be 43-year-old quarterback, completely immobile both inside and outside the pocket. He's taken 31 sacks thus far this year, including five amid last week's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
Nevertheless, Broncos head coach Sean Payton was anticipating another head-to-head against the future Canton-bound field general — something that occurred regularly during Payton's time in New Orleans.
"They kind of run together," Payton said Tuesday regarding his encounters with Rodgers. "He’s a first-ballot [Pro Football] Hall of Famer. He’s a first-ballot thrower. Just the arm angles, the rhythm, so many things that he’s exceptional at. It was Green Bay for a number of years. They kind of run together, like I said, but the ball comes out quick. He’s got a great throwing motion. There are just so many things that he’s accomplished in his career. Nothing but respect for his skill set and also his staying power. It’s not easy to do.”
For Pittsburgh, there's really nowhere to go but up for an offense that ranks 30th in total yards and 27th in scoring and passing yards per game. Rudolph's insertion could be a green flag for the team's primary pass-catchers, such as DK Metcalf, Roman Wilson, and Pat Freiermuth.
Rudolph, 31, is similar to Broncos backup QB Jarrett Stidham in that he provides a relatively safe floor, though not a particularly high ceiling. Across 38 career appearances, he's thrown for 4,927 yards, 30 touchdowns, and 22 interceptions. He has a career record of 9-9-1 in 19 starts.
Ultimately, Rudolph might not be a central focus of the gameplan in what could be a wet and windy affair in the Steel City. That honor would likely go to Steelers running back Jaylen Warren, who's set for a massive workload on Black Friday.
The Broncos — who executed their own controversial move, suspending RB J.K. Dobbins for the game — will be near full strength on the defensive side, with starting safety Brandon Jones likely to return following a two-week absence.

title: Broncos Dealing With New D-Line Injury Concern Ahead of Steelers Game
full_text:
The Denver Broncos were back at it on Tuesday, practicing for this Black Friday's road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers .
It's a short week, but the Broncos are battle-tested. We saw some new names pop up on the practice report, so let's take a look at where things stand for the Broncos on the injury front early in the week.
After Tuesday's practice, Sean Payton announced that Dobbins has been suspended , which explains why he didn't participate. Fortunately, Badie is eligible to return from injured reserve, and the Broncos designated him to return this week.
Because Dobbins is suspended, he'll go on a reserve list for this one game, which means the Broncos will be able to activate Badie without cutting another player to make room. That makes things a little more awkward, potentially, for Lohner, who is working his way back from the physically unable to perform (PUP) list.
The Broncos started Lohner's clock last week , giving the team 21 days to decide whether to activate him. He's got roughly two weeks of that clock left.
The new injuries to monitor are Bryant, Skinner, Rapp, and Sai'vion Jones. However, both Bryant and Skinner were a full go in practice, while Rapp was limited and Jones didn't participate.
The Broncos worked out four defensive linemen on Tuesday, perhaps anticipating that Jones may not have enough time to recover from his hamstring injury on a short week. Denver worked out Jalen Hunt, Derrick Nnadi, Khalen Saunders, and Ben Stille, but as of this article, none have been signed.
Besides suspending J.K. Dobbins and activating Tyler Badie's practice window from IR, the #Broncos worked out four defensive linemen today: • Jalen Hunt • Derrick Nnadi • Khalen Saunders • Ben Stille pic.twitter.com/x557EDmmow
The Broncos have rookie Tyler Onyedim and veteran Jordan Jackson on the 53-man roster, with nose tackle Jordan Miller on the practice squad, so they have options with Jones banged up and Eyioma Uwazurike on injured reserve.
Now, for some good news: Brandon Jones was a full go on Tuesday. That means, barring an unforeseen setback, he's going to play on Friday, after missing the last two games with a hamstring.
The Steelers are relatively healthy. However, Highsmith is a starter, so his status will be worth monitoring, while Skowronek is a backup.
Pittman hasn't played since October, as we works back from his injury, so the Steelers could activate him this week . Dunker is also working back from injured reserve. Pittman is the name to watch here, beyond Highsmith and Herbig.

title: Broncos Make Move to Maneuver Around J.K. Dobbins Suspension
full_text:
The Denver Broncos are losing a running back for Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers after suspending J.K. Dobbins for conduct detrimental to the team.
But they're also gaining a running back, as the Broncos designated backup Tyler Badie for return from short-term injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday .
Badie missed the mandatory minimum four games after suffering a broken thumb amid Denver's Week 6 victory over the Seattle Seahawks. He was officially listed as a full participant in Tuesday's practice.
The Broncos now have 21 days to activate Badie to the 53-man roster, which appears highly likely before the club departs for Pittsburgh.
Prior to going down, Badie recorded six carries for 22 yards and hauled in six of seven targets for 67 yards across 52 offensive snaps. He also pulled double duty as a special-teamer, returning four kickoffs for 105 yards.
“I think one of the strengths that he has is and this is a valuable trait, you know exactly what you’re going to get from the players," Broncos head coach Sean Payton said of Badie in October. "So you know what it is you might want to do with him, how he is in the protection special teams. It’s harder if you don’t, I think he’s very consistent and that allows us as game planners to know, hey, we’re going to ask him to do this and he’s going to do that very well. There are no surprises and that’s a really good trait.”
Badie was one of two Broncos RBs on injured reserve along with RJ Harvey, who'll be eligible to return for next week's home contest versus the Miami Dolphins.
Even if he weren't suspended this week, it's likely that Dobbins would be further phased out of the offensive game plan after handling only one touch in Week 11. This backfield belongs to rookie Jonah Coleman, and Denver has not exactly hidden that fact.
Combined with Harvey still being out, Badie should be activated and operate as the No. 2 behind Coleman against the Steelers, perhaps mixing in with recent practice squad callup Cody Schrader.
Badie's snaps will seem minuscule compared to Coleman's anticipated workload — especially with the forecast calling for some rain and possibly light snow — but he'll certainly see the field at Acrisure Stadium.
What happens next week ... is another story.

title: Lions Tate Ratledge Questionable to Return Against Bears
full_text:
Detroit Lions right guard Tate Ratledge suffered an injury on the team's first drive against the Chicago Bears and left the game.
He was replaced by Miles Frazier. Ratledge was officially diagnosed with ankle and knee injuries and ruled questionable to return.
Ratledge is in his second professional season after the Lions drafted him in the second-round of the 2025 NFL draft out of Georgia. He has not missed a game to this point in his career, starting all 28 possible games including Thursday's Thanksgiving matchup.
The second-year pro returned to the Lions' bench during their second offensive series and appeared to be preparing to re-enter the game. He would return to action for Detroit's third offensive series.
The Georgia product played over 1,000 snaps last year as a rookie, notching a 70.3 overall offensive grade via Pro Football Focus. He's one of three returning starters from last year, along with Penei Sewell and Christian Mahogany.
To help revamp their offensive line, the Lions brought in veterans Juice Scruggs and Cade Mays while drafting right tackle Blake Miller in the first-round of this year's draft. Scruggs has started nine games at center, while Miller has started all 10 of his appearances though he missed the Buffalo game with an injury.
The Lions have had some tough injury luck throughout the season. Defensive end Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season, while linebacker Jack Campbell is also on injured reserve with a neck injury. Detroit also lost rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard for the year to a knee injury suffered last week against the Buccaneers.
Frazier is also in his second NFL season, as the Lions drafted him in the fifth-round of the 2025 Draft out of LSU. He has made one start this season, that being at left guard when Christian Mahogany was benched for disciplinary reasons.
The LSU product appeared in five games as a rookie in 2025 after missing the start of the season with a lengthy bout of illness.
To make matters worse, the Lions were without defensive end D.J. Wonnum (back), safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) for Thursday's game.
Detroit lead Thursday's game early, 3-0, on a Jake Bates field goal on their first drive. The defense, though shorthanded, came up big when rookie defensive end Derrick Moore forced a fumble on Chicago's ensuing offensive drive.

title: Setting Lions Fans Expectations for Jared Goff Against Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are set to battle with the Chicago Bears with first-place in the NFC North on the line in front of a national audience.
Detroit has relied on its veteran quarterback Jared Goff to play at a high level each week, and he has done just that throughout the season. Through 10 games, Goff has thrown 20 touchdown passes against four interceptions.
Against the Bears and their high-powered offense, Goff may be lured into a shootout . Chicago's defense features a star on the interior line in Jeffery Simmons, who they acquired ahead of the trade deadline. Simmons has had five sacks since joining the Bears, including three last week against New Orleans.
As a result, Goff may have to air it out to give the Lions their best chance to win. He's facing off against his former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson on the other sideline, as Johnson is the Bears' head coach. Because of that, Goff will likely feel some added motivation to play well.
Sports Betting Dime's Drew Ellis believes a big day is in store for Goff, as he's predicting Goff to go over his projected over/under for passing yards in Thursday's game.
"I think these games with the Chicago Bears and Ben Johnson are a little more personal to Jared Goff than he lets on," Ellis told Lions OnSI. "His former OC has thrown some jabs at Goff since becoming Chicago’s head coach and Goff has responded with over 330 passing yards in both meetings with Johnson’s Bears. I expect Chicago to have more offensive success than Lions opponents have had over the last six games, so the Lions offense will have to produce a lot of points to win. That puts more on Goff to perform at a high level and I expect his yardage to pile up and reach at least 279 yards on Thursday."
Goff currently has a 1-4 record on Thanksgiving as a member of the Lions, with the lone win coming over the Bears in 2024. However, he has played well on the holiday with 1,202 passing yards, nine touchdown passes and zero interceptions in his appearances with the Lions on Thanksgiving.
Detroit went 2-0 against the Bears last season, and will be looking to extend their unbeaten streak against their former coordinator in what could be the biggest Thanksgiving matchup in franchise history.

title: Detroit Lions Week 12 Inactives List: Is DE Playing?
full_text:
The Detroit Lions have released their official list of players that will not suit up against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field.
Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw was previously ruled inactive, as he continues to work his way back from a shoulder injury.
D.J. Reed and Kerby Joseph did not appear on the injury report and are set to play against Ben Johnson's squad.

Safety Chuck Clark will also be inactive this week. Against the Buccaneers, the talented defender was the green dot captain, given his prior experience leading a defense and communicating defensive calls.

“It's definitely some extra preparation for sure. I have not done it in three seasons, since 2022. So, just talking to myself at the house, saying the calls, making sure I'm not stuttering or mumbling up my words or whatnot, talking to the guys in the huddle and just not overthinking it, trying to get them all back on one page," said Clark. "I mean, that's the biggest thing. I know when I'm back there and I don't have a green dot, 'Hey, what's the call? What's the call?' So, guys want that call quick, fast so they can think and process, see the formation and we can go out there and make plays.”
He expressed he was proud of the defense and how they executed last week, especially since the Buccaneers had the top rushing offense in the National Football League.
“It felt good for sure," said Clark. "I mean, but it's always room to improve and grow. I mean, that's the cliche answer. I mean, we definitely left some things out there in that aspect of the run game. But we just definitely want to grow and get better. But facing a duo with tandem like that, man, we know those guys can take to the house at any time. So, that was big just to have that put out against them.”

title: Expert Predictions For Detroit Lions Matchup With Chicago Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will look to secure their seventh straight win when they take on the Chicago Bears Thursday afternoon.
The Lions are coming off a 31-21 defeat of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11. Meanwhile, Chicago prevailed against the New Orleans Saints last week, 21-13.
Without further ado, here are the predictions from the Detroit Lions On SI staff for the Lions' Week 12 matchup with Chicago.
The Lions and Bears are meeting in what is the biggest Thanksgiving in recent memory for the franchise. The team that wins this game will step into the driver's seat for the NFC North with six games remaining and could put themselves in position to contend for the No. 1 seed.
As a result, I'm predicting that Dan Campbell will try to bring the fight to the Bears and be ultra-aggressive. With how explosive the Bears' offense can be, I expect Campbell to press the issue and go for it on multiple fourth-downs. This could turn into a shootout, but I think the Lions' ability to run the ball and manage the clock will be the difference-maker. After years of struggles on Thanksgiving, the Lions get over the hump and defeat the Bears in a barnburner.
If the Lions are going to notch their seventh straight victory Thursday, they're going to have to absolutely earn it.
They're set to face one of their stiffest tests of the season, going up against Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears.
Heading into the Week 12 affair, the Bears own both a top-10 offense and a top-10 defense. And just like the Lions, they can absolutely pound the rock.
So, I believe this clash between NFC North rivals will come down to who wins the battle in the trenches. While it won't be easy, I believe that Detroit will open up just enough holes for Jahmyr Gibbs to run through, enabling Dan Campbell's squad to secure the Thanksgiving Day victory.
The Lions now face their toughest test of the 2026 season.
Ben Johnson will have the Bears offense ready to take advantage of certain weaknesses in the Lions’ secondary.
While both teams will look to establish the run, Detroit’s offense will execute more consistently.
Caleb Williams is turning the football over too much and Kelvin Sheppard’s defense will capitalize.
This game could become very high scoring, which favors Detroit.
Thursday is a major test for the Lions, going up against Ben Johnson and the red-hot Chicago Bears. Additionally, this is the Lions’ third game in 11 days, including an overseas flight to Munich, Germany.
The Lions have the opportunity to prove that the defensive improvement is more than just a lack of competition. In recent weeks, the Lions have seen their defense shut down the passing game, but their best competition in those contests was against an already injured Baker Mayfield.
The Bears have a knack for explosive plays, but also do not grade out well in play action. With Jahmyr Gibbs as the bellcow back in Detroit, that is a mismatch offensive coordinator Drew Petzing can exploit.
That said, with the recent injuries to Aidan Hutchinson, Jack Campbell and now underrated pass-rushing defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard, I see the Lions unable to come out on top on Thanksgiving.

title: Lions Week 12 Depth Chart Against Bears
full_text:
The Lions’ defense will receive its biggest test in a while when it takes the field Thursday against Ben Johnson and the Chicago Bears.
The Bears enter the Thanksgiving Day tilt with the No. 8 offense in the NFL, averaging 26.2 points per game.
It furthers the significance of the return of D.J. Reed to the Lions’ starting lineup.
Reed, the No. 1 cornerback for defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit, has missed the last three games with a hip ailment. He'll provide a big boost to Detroit's secondary, curtailing the efforts of Chicago signal-caller Caleb Williams through the air.
Here's an updated look at the Lions' depth chart ahead of their Week 12 clash with the Bears.
Starter: Jared Goff. Backup: Joshua Dobbs.
Goff will make his 80th consecutive start when he takes the field Thursday against the Bears. He continues to be the straw that stirs the drink for the Lions, with 20 touchdowns and just four interceptions to his name thus far in 2026. Drew Petzing & Co. will be relying on him to play a clean game in the holiday clash.
Starter: Jahmyr Gibbs. Backup: Sione Vaki. Reserves: Jacob Saylors. Inactive: Isiah Pacheco (Injured reserve).
Gibbs took over in the second half again last week against the Buccaneers. The do-it-all back finished the Week 11 contest with 98 yards and two touchdowns on 23 carries.
Expect the Lions to ride him early and often once again Thursday vs. the Bears.
Starters: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jameson Williams, Isaac TeSlaa. Backups: Tay Martin, DeAndre Carter. Inactive: Kendrick Law (Injured reserve), Tom Kennedy (Injured reserve).
The Lions got a big game from Williams vs. Tampa Bay, with “Jamo” recording a game-high 93 yards and a score. Meanwhile, St. Brown amassed just 37 yards on five catches. I expect an uptick in production from the All-Pro receiver vs. the Bears.
Starter: Sam LaPorta. Backup: Brock Wright. Reserves: Tyler Conklin.
Starters: Penei Sewell (left), Blake Miller (right). Backup: Larry Borom. Inactive: Gio Manu (Non-Football Injury).
Sewell continues to be the very best tackle in all of football. He's logged 94.0 overall PFF grade through the season's first 11 weeks, including a 94.8 run-blocking mark (first among all OTs).
Starters: Christian Mahogany (left), Tate Ratledge (right). Backup: Miles Frazier. Inactive: Ben Bartch (Injured reserve).
Mahogany and Ratledge have been solid all season for Detroit. But, they certainly will face a stiff challenge Thursday against Bears interior defensive lineman Jeffery Simmons. Simmons is coming off a three-sack performance against the Saints in Week 11.
Starter: Juice Scruggs. Backup: Ratledge Reserve: Seth McLaughlin. Inactive: Cade Mays (Injured reserve).
Scruggs continues to log valuable reps in place of Mays, who has been placed on injured reserve for a second time this season. Scruggs, who owns an overall grade of 75.4 from Pro Football Focus, has been a godsend for Detroit, and has become arguably the best acquisition of GM Brad Holmes of the past offseason.
Starters: Alim McNeill, Tyleik Williams. Backups: Levi Onwuzurike. Reserve: Anthony Lucas (practice squad elevation), Mekhi Wingo. Inactive: Skyler Gill-Howard (Injured reserve)
Gill-Howard was placed on injured reserve after suffering a knee injury a week ago against the Buccaneers. It came on a goal-line play in which he was being used as an extra blocker. It's an unfortunate end to a solid rookie campaign for the sixth-round pick.
In his place, the Lions have called up defensive end Anthony Lucas from the practice squad. It marks the second time he's been elevated, as he also logged 12 defensive snaps against the Miami Dolphins in Week 9.
Starters: DJ Wonnum (Questionable; back), Derrick Moore. Backups: Tyler Lacy, Ahmed Hassanein. Reserves: Eric O'Neill, Tyrus Wheat. Inactive: Aidan Hutchinson (Injured reserve), Payton Turner (Injured reserve).
Wonnum is questionable for Detroit's holiday clash with Chicago with a back ailment. If he can't go, it makes it even more pivotal that Moore delivers a strong performance. Just last week against Tampa Bay, he generated five total pressures, including a sack of Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield.
Starters: Derrick Barnes, Malcolm Rodriguez. Backups: Trevor Nowaske, K.J. Britt, Owen Pappoe. Reserve: Joe Bachie, Amen Ogbongbemiga. Inactive: Jack Campbell (Injured reserve), Jimmy Rolder (Injured reserve), Damone Clark (Injured reserve), Devin White (Injured reserve).
Detroit's linebackers continue to step up in the absence of Jack Campbell. In the team's win over Tampa Bay last week, Rodriguez and Britt notably delivered strong efforts. The Lions certainly will need more of the same against Williams & Co. Thursday.
Starters: Roger McCreary, D.J. Reed. Backups: Rock Ya-Sin, Nick Whiteside Reserve: Khalil Dorsey. Inactive: Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder)
The cornerbacks room receives a big boost with D.J. Reed being active, after missing the last three weeks with a hip injury. The Lions No. 1 corner was on a heater prior to the ailment, receiving some of his very best coverage grades of the season from Pro Football Focus.
Reed and the Lions’ cornerbacks will have their hands full against Bears leading receiver Luther Burden III. Burden enters the Thanksgiving Day affair with 51 catches, 654 yards and four touchdowns on the season.
Starters: Brian Branch, Kerby Joseph. Backups: Chuck Clark (Questionable; hamstring), Andre Cisco Reserves: Christian Izien, Keith Abney. Inactive: Avonte Maddox (Injured reserve), Thomas Harper (Injured reserve).
Joseph did not have a hugely productive day in his season debut a week ago against the Bucs. However, he did stay on the field for the entirety of the game, a huge positive for Dan Campbell's squad.
Clark, who possessed the green dot for Sheppard's defense against Tampa Bay, is questionable this week with a hamstring injury. If he can't go against the Bears, it'd be a significant loss for the back-end of the defense.
Kicker: Jake Bates. Punter: Jack Fox. Long-snapper: Hogan Hatten. Kick returners: DeAndre Carter, Jacob Saylors Punt returner: Carter.
Bates missed one-of-two field-goal attempts against the Bucs last week. It came on a 53-yard attempt on Detroit's first offensive possession of the game.
The Lions definitely would like to see him go perfect Thursday, in what will likely be a close game against the divisional rival Bears.

title: 5 Things Detroit Lions Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Detroit Lions will be making their 87th appearance playing on Thanksgiving Thursday.
All-time, the Lions hold a 38-46-2 record, but have lost four of the five they've played under head coach Dan Campbell. However, they have an opportunity to change their fortunes in a big way as they're battling the Chicago Bears for first-place in the NFC North.
The organization has come a long way during the Campbell and Brad Holmes era, and as a result the organization and it's fan base have plenty to be thankful on this holiday.
Here are five things the Lions should be thankful for this Thanksgiving.
The Lions seem to have struck the right chords as of late, as they're one win away from four-straight winning seasons. Even last year, when the team finished in last-place in the NFC North, they had a 9-8 record and came up just shy of a postseason berth.
Under the leadership of Sheila Hamp, Brad Holmes and Dan Campbell, the Lions have been in one of the best stretches in franchise history. They enter Thursday's game with an opportunity to cement themselves as the NFC North leader ahead of the final six games, and could be in the No. 1 seed by the end of the week if the 49ers lose.
This run of sustained success is a welcome sight for an organization that has yet to as much as appear in a Super Bowl . Though they came up short in their trip to the NFC Championship game in the 2023 season, the sustained success of the organization has the fan base believing a trip to the big game is more of a reality than the illusion it was for so many years.
The Lions have been fortunate to have some excellent running backs in their history, and the latest in that lineage suits up as their bell-cow every Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs, who the team drafted to the surprise of many 12th overall in the 2023 Draft, has been playing like the league's most dynamic player in the league as of late.
Gibbs is already over 1,000 rushing yards for the third-straight year, and leads the league with 13 rushing touchdowns through 10 games. He's following in the footsteps of players like Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders, who electrified Lions fans throughout the 1990's.
Gibbs has already usurped Sanders in some record books for his performance in the first four years of his career, and after signing an extension will be looked to as a source of big plays for the foreseeable future.
The Lions have drafted exceptionally well under Brad Holmes, whose background as a draft scout has shone through early in his tenure. They've hit on many picks, both in early rounds and late, and those drafted players have been integral parts of their success.
First-round picks like Gibbs, Jack Campbell , Aidan Hutchinson, Jameson Williams and Penei Sewell have asserted themselves as leaders. Meanwhile, the team has struck gold with mid-round picks like Alim McNeill, Kerby Joseph and Amon-Ra St. Brown who have become team captains and annual Pro Bowl-caliber contributors.
Detroit's drafting record has given them plenty to be thankful for, as these drafted players have become key cogs in the machine that has allowed them to remain at the top of a competitive division and win two of the last three NFC North titles.
Another huge element of the Lions' ascent in recent years has been the resurgence of quarterback Jared Goff. Acquired as part of the blockbuster Matthew Stafford trade upon the hiring of Holmes and Campbell, Goff was viewed by many as a bridge quarterback to the future.
However, after a rough first season Goff has found his way back to performing at a high level and fueled the Lions' offense with his consistency. Goff has recorded four seasons in a row with at least 4,400 passing yards and made three Pro Bowls since coming to Detroit.
This year, he's thrown 20 touchdown passes against just four interceptions through 10 games, and his consistency has provided the offense with the ability to dominate against opposing defenses.
The Lions through four games had one of the NFL's worst defenses, and coordinator Kelvin Sheppard was viewed as a coach on the hot seat. Since then, though, the Lions have bounced back defensively and have had quiet the resurgence.
Even with the injuries to players like Aidan Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, the Lions have been able to right the ship amidst their six-game winning streak. Since the Week 5 bye week, the Lions rank second in the league in points allowed and yards allowed.
Thursday's game will be a statement opportunity for the defense, as their opponents have created some skepticism as to whether this success has longevity. If they can shut down Ben Johnson's group on Thursday, Detroit's defense will gain some serious credibility heading into the stretch run.

title: Spot the Ball: 10 Thoughts Ahead of Lions Thanksgiving Game Against Bears
full_text:
The Detroit Lions are set to battle for first-place in the NFC North in front of a national audience on Thanksgiving.
On Thursday, the Lions will take on the Chicago Bears. Both teams will enter Ford Field with identical 8-2 records, and the winner will take sole possession of first-place with six games to go.
These two teams will meet again in Week 17, so not all is lost for whichever team comes up short, but it presents an opportunity for a massive midseason win ahead of the stretch run.
Here are 10 thoughts surrounding Thursday's game between the Bears and Lions.
The Lions have had one of the best resurgences defensively in the league as of late, as coordinator Kelvin Sheppard has been able to get the unit back on the right track after some early struggles. One key part of that has been the performance of cornerback Roger McCreary.
A five-year veteran, McCreary has found a nice niche in Detroit. With the recent injury to D.J. Reed, McCreary has been a difference maker over the last three weeks in particular. He notched his first interception of the season in Munich in Week 10, and has started each of the team's last eight games.
Against a Chicago offense loaded with weapons, McCreary will need to be at his best in matchups with players such as Luther Burden and Rome Odunze. With Detroit's style, his performance in man-to-man coverage will likely have a big impact on the outcome.
The Lions have been in first-place on Thanksgiving just four times since 2000 according to Sumer Sports, most recently in 2024. In those four games where they've held the top spot, they are 3-1 including a 2016 win over the Minnesota Vikings in which the two teams entered the game tied for first.
Ironically, the last time the Lions played on Thanksgiving when in first-place in the NFC North came in 2024 when they hosted the Chicago Bears. That year, the Lions won 23-20, thanks in part to a late-game fiasco that ultimately cost Bears head coach Matt Eberflus his job.
With both the Lions and Bears sitting at 8-2 and firmly in the mix not only for the division crown but also the NFC's No. 1 seed, this may in fact be the team's biggest Thanksgiving game in recent history. Detroit is 1-4 in Thanksgiving games since 2000 where their opponent is in first-place, with the lone win being that over the Vikings in 2016.
The Lions and Bears have plenty of overlap , with the biggest being on the sidelines between head coaches Dan Campbell and Ben Johnson. The two worked together for several years, first in Miami as assistants and then in Detroit when Campbell was hired as head coach in 2021.
Johnson began his tenure with the Lions in an assistant role before being promoted to offensive coordinator in 2022, and held that role until departing for Chicago's head role after the 2024 season. In their two meetings last year, Campbell was 2-0 against his former apprentice, but Johnson ultimately led the Bears to the NFC North crown.
It's been intriguing to see Johnson's rise in just over 1.5 seasons in Chicago, as he finished fourth in AP Coach of the Year voting in his first year and has the Bears off to an 8-2 start this year. He's 19-8 as head coach, with Campbell looking to deal his former mentee his ninth loss on Thursday.
The Bears have lost just one of Caleb Williams' seven starts this season, as his year was interrupted by a hamstring injury that cost him three games earlier in the year. He presents a unique challenge for Detroit with his mobility and willingness to play off script and extend plays.
Of quarterbacks with 250 drop backs, Williams ranks fifth with a scramble rate of 7.9 percent according to Sumer Sports. The Lions will need to be firm setting the edge, as allowing him to escape the pocket could have dire consequences. This puts an emphasis on the performances of Derrick Moore, DJ Wonnum and Alim McNeill.
Williams also ranks first in the league in play-action percentage, and has a completion percentage of 65.4 percent on this type of play. As a result, the Lions will have to put an added emphasis on keeping the young passer in the pocket to limit the damage he can do with his legs.
Detroit's defensive line stepped up last week without Aidan Hutchinson, and appears deep enough to weather that storm. DJ Wonnum and Derrick Moore have been on hot streaks as of late, while Alim McNeill has been playing at a high level throughout the season.
However, the Lions will have to play without rookie defensive tackle Skyler Gill-Howard for the remainder of the year as he suffered a season-ending knee injury.
The Lions got Kerby Joseph back on Sunday, giving them another excellent option at the safety position. An All-Pro in 2024, Joseph was back in action for the first time in over 400 days and played 46 snaps in his return.
With Joseph back in the mix, the Lions went with some three-safety packages involving Joseph, Brian Branch and Chuck Clark. This could be something they look to utilize in future weeks, as it gives them the opportunities for multiple playmakers in the secondary.
The Lions will be squaring off against more than Johnson when it comes to their former teammates. Running back D'Andre Swift and wide receiver Kalif Raymond both play vital roles for Chicago after playing for the Lions earlier in their careers.
Swift was a Lion from 2020-22, and was traded during the 2023 Draft after the Lions drafted Jahmyr Gibbs. The move has turned out well for both parties, as Gibbs leads the league in rushing and has had three-straight 1,000-yard seasons, while Swift has 627 yards for the Bears and has had at least 900 in every year since leaving Detroit.
As for Raymond, the veteran is fourth on the Bears in receiving yards and handles punt returns. His 33 receptions are the most he's had in a season since the 2023 season when he had 35 for Detroit.
The Lions and Bears took vastly different approaches with their moves ahead of this year's trade deadline, and the outcomes could be massive either way. In Detroit's case, general manager Brad Holmes elected to maintain the future and trade a late-round pick in a future draft for safety depth in Andre Cisco.
Meanwhile, Chicago made a huge splash by dealing multiple first-round picks for Tennessee's Jeffery Simmons. So far, that deal looks to be a win for Chicago as Simmons has recorded five sacks and 12 pressures in three games for the Bears.
The splash deal could be difference-making for Chicago, as Simmons has elevated their defense. After a three-sack game against New Orleans last week, the veteran is looking to cause mayhem in Detroit.
The Lions had a lot of success against their former offensive coordinator, limiting the Bears to 37 total points in their two meetings last year. They won both games, including a 52-21 rout in Detroit in Week 2 last year.
If the Lions have it their way, it will be more of the same formula. Jared Goff is kept upright by a strong performance from the offensive line, and the threat posed by Chicago's defensive line to Detroit's run game is neutralized.
Goff and Jahmyr Gibbs both have big days, as both shine in front of the national audience. Chicago threatens early in the third quarter, but the offense keeps them at an arm's length and the defense creates multiple takeaways en route to a comfortable, tone-setting Thanksgiving win.
Ben Johnson will have a chip on his shoulder after his last return to Detroit resulted in a blowout loss. After going winless against his former team, the second-year head coach will likely have some unique looks in store for Kelvin Sheppard's defense.
Williams can do a lot of damage with his legs, and his ability to extend plays will force Detroit's secondary to cover longer. If he hits big completions early, it could be bad news for Detroit.
In the worst-case scenario, Williams dices the secondary with his arm and keeps drives alive with key conversions on the ground. Jeffery Simmons disrupts Detroit's run game, and Detroit can't keep up in a shootout loss.

title: Former Lions OL T.J. Lang Sounds Off on Aaron Rodgers: 'It's Despicable'
full_text:
Current Detroit Lions radio analyst T.J. Lang has a unique perspective on the prevailing story around the NFL on Wednesday.
Lang played 10 NFL seasons before transitioning to the radio, and the first eight years of his career were spent in Green Bay. During his time with the Packers, the quarterback he blocked for was future Hall of Famer Aaron Rodgers and his head coach was Mike McCarthy.
Rodgers and McCarthy have had their history, but on Wednesday things were taken up a notch. They reunited this offseason as McCarthy was hired as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers, where Rodgers is in his second season as quarterback.
Reports late Tuesday indicated that McCarthy had made the decision to bench Rodgers and replace him with Mason Rudolph. Rodgers didn't take the news lightly, as he appeared on 'The Pat McAfee Show' Wednesday and aired out his grievances with McCarthy.
His critiques of the head coach didn't stop at differences on the field, as he made allegations of the head coach sleeping in meetings and missing walkthroughs. Lang reacted to this news during an appearance on ' The Valenti Show With Rico ,' which is the Lions' flagship radio station's popular drivetime show.
Lang, who has a unique viewpoint due to his connection to both parties from their time together in Green Bay, lashed out regarding Rodgers' comments about McCarthy.
“I think it’s despicable. I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has b*****d about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media," Lang said. "He has blacklisted I don’t know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth."
Lang noted that the veteran quarterback has distanced himself from others who have handled situations similar to how he has handled this one. Ultimately, Rodgers was officially released by the Steelers after the interview with McAfee, and is free to play out the remainder of what he has stated will be his final NFL season elsewhere.
“Honestly, I don’t know if I want to watch the whole thing. It’s just unnecessary. It’s a victim mentality, it’s a ‘Poor me, woe is me, oh I thought this.’ I’m sick, man," Lang said. "I’ve been in a group chat with a whole lot of former teammates that feel the exact same way I do. I think it’s completely unnecessary, I think it’s victim mentality."
While Lang has noted that he hasn't kept up a relationship with Rodgers, he has maintained one with McCarthy as the two reportedly spoke earlier this week.
"If it was the Ravens or something, I’d be like, ‘This is awesome.’ Mike McCarthy was my head coach for eight years, and I love Mike McCarthy," Lang said. "I just talked to Mike McCarthy on Monday Night. Still have a great relationship with him. I haven’t talked to Aaron Rodgers in probably five years, I can’t remember the last time he returned a text. I don’t have a relationship with him. I think it’s absolutely despicable what he just did to big Mike. Truth or not, nobody knows. We’re not in those meetings, we don’t know that.”

title: Detroit Lions Place DT on IR, Elevate Defensive End
full_text:
The Detroit Lions announced a flurry of roster moves, one day ahead of their Week 12 NFC North showdown against the Chicago Bears.

title: Detroit Lions Rule Out CB, 2 Questionable Against Bears
full_text:

title: It’s Over: Three Overreactions After Packers Were Turned Into Turkeys by Rams
full_text:
GREEN BAY, Wis. – The Green Bay Packers had to beat the Los Angeles Rams. The NFC playoff standings demanded it. Moreover, they had to show they were capable of beating a premier team.
Instead, the Packers were mashed like potatoes on Thanksgiving Eve. They got the stuffing kicked out of them in the second half of a 26-13 loss. Not even grabbing the wishbone can save the Packers, which is reason to cry in the cranberries.
Here are our three big takeaways after the Packers looked like made-up contenders during the NFL’s made-up holiday.
The Packers had their chance to show the world they are contenders on Wednesday night. However, following a familiar pattern, they showed they weren’t ready for primetime.
In the Week 1 matchup at the Vikings, the Packers were pulverized in the second half and lost by 17. Riding a three-game winning streak into a Week 7 showdown at Detroit, the Packers went 5-of-15 on third down and 1-of-4 in the red zone, missed two field goals and lost by three.
Still, Green Bay was 6-3 when it got its big rematch against the Vikings. The Packers were at home. They would be better prepared for Brian Flores’ blitzes. The Vikings played without a couple of their top offensive weapons and their star linebacker. Instead of turning the tables, the Packers lost by 20.
That all set up what essentially was a last-stand game against the Rams, with the winner taking a huge step toward the playoffs and the loser taking a huge step toward irrelevancy. The Packers, essentially, were handed a 10th home game. Micah Parsons made his debut. The Rams lined up without their two elite receivers and two starters on the offensive line.
And the Packers lost by 13. It might as well have been 31. They were not the least bit competitive in the second half.
The Packers have played five games against teams with winning records. They are 1-4, with the lone win coming against the Bears, who played without Caleb Williams.
General manager Brian Gutekunst and coach Matt LaFleur were handed contract extensions. Some top players were given contract extensions. Instead, it’s the same old Packers.
Parsons was acquired in a blockbuster trade to help get the Packers back to the Super Bowl. Half of his contract is about to go down the drain. It’s an organizational failure. The general manager didn’t do a good job building the roster. The coach hasn’t done a good enough job utilizing the roster. And too many big-money players – the quarterback was among them on Wednesday night – haven’t played to their paychecks.
Micah Parsons made his long-awaited debut. In his first game in 346 days, nobody quite knew what to expect other than his presence would help everyone around him hit another level.
Parsons wasn’t at Superman-level dominance but he was really good. He had one sack and four pressures in his debut. The problem is nobody else hit another level.
Lukas Van Ness? Three assisted tackles and two pressures. Devonte Wyatt? Zero pressures. The Packers had only one sack (by Parsons) and three quarterback hits (two by Parsons, one by Isaiah McDuffie).
Maybe everyone was so excited to see Parsons rush the passer that they forgot to stop the run. The Rams embarrassed the Packers with a soul-crushing 241 rushing yards. It was the fourth-worst performance of the Matt LaFleur era.
“We talk about all the time, the game honors toughness. I think we’re playing tougher,” Rams coach Sean McVay said.
The Packers, obviously, aren’t tough enough, which led to this killer line by Parsons.
“We need to figure out who’s going to be a dog or not,” he told reporters after the game. “Like that’s just the reality of it. To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don’t have an answer for it … that’s accountability. That’s just how I really feel about it.
“I wasn’t able to get on the field because of it, because they didn’t want to waste my plays on first and second down. I think the whole thing is just bad and we’ve got to figure out who’s willing to play with us or who’s playing against us at this point because every quarter, every minute, every down matters and we’ve got to figure out who’s in this for the long haul and who’s in it for the ride.”
Meanwhile, on the other side of the ball, Jordan Love for the second consecutive week wasn’t up to the task. He has to be Superman because of an unreliable running game and offensive line. But these are the games that define great quarterbacks and Love wasn’t close to good enough.
Forget about playing like Superman. Or even Clark Kent. It was more like Jimmy Olson. He threw two interceptions and was fortunate it wasn’t four. Not for a moment during the second half did he play like a quarterback capable of winning the game.
Rams coach Sean McVay is a difference-maker.
Did the Packers have some injury issues, especially after losing Christian Watson to a concussion late in the first half? Of course. But the Rams lined up without Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and two starting linemen. Two more linemen went down during the game. And yet the Rams dominated most of the game.
“It was awesome,” McVay said. “You guys have heard me say it, and it's really been tested and on display. It's the greatest team sport that there is. There is a long way to go, so don't misunderstand me, but our group is just starting to build skills with mental, physical toughness, resilience, guys being able to step up.
“You never know when your opportunity is going to present itself, and that was on display defensively, offensively, and in the kicking game. I love this team, love the staff. I'm excited about what they've done and I'm excited about continuing to push the envelope and see how we can grow from here.”
That’s an unbelievable quote because of the state of the Packers with their 6-5 record.
Where was the mental toughness to turn the game around in the second half?
Where was the physical toughness with the Rams rushing for almost 200 yards in the second half?
Where was the resilience as the game got away from them in the second half?
In what phase did the Packers hold their own on offense, defense or the kicking game?
Packers coach Matt LaFleur can’t push the envelope when trying to prevent the envelope from going up in flames.
Team president and CEO Ed Policy saw the Packers lose their final five games of last season and decided to give contract extensions to LaFleur and general manager Brian Gutekunst. With a 6-5 record, a team built to win a Super Bowl seems to be headed for a cliff.
This is the time of year when teams should be making their move to the playoffs and beyond. The Packers, instead, just got clobbered by the Vikings and Rams. The offense ranks a woeful 20th in scoring, including just 15.2 points in five losses, due in large part to a poorly constructed and poorly coached line. The defense, in the words of Javon Bullard, got its “ass” kicked for a second consecutive game by a depleted offense.
The Packers are in deep trouble. Significant changes are needed for an organization headed in the wrong direction.

title: Packers Report Card: Bad Grades And Looking for Dogs After Loss to Rams
full_text:
The grades are in, and the Green Bay Packers’ season is starting to circle the drain. No, they are not simply going to give up, but perhaps Micah Parsons said it best before his debut on Wednesday.
Parsons said that every game was the “difference between the playoffs and Cancun.”
Well, through one game since that statement was made, the Packers are much closer to Cancun. Their defense was beaten bloody by Blake Corum and the Rams’ run game. Their offense could not find any semblance of a rhythm in the second half. As a result, a 13-13 tie at halftime turned into a 26-13 loss that conjured memories of Jim Mora’s infamous “Playoffs?!” rant .
“We need to figure out who’s going to be a dog or not. Like that’s just the reality of it,” Parsons said after the game. “To me, to be honest and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don’t have an answer for it … that’s accountability.”
Let’s jump into the grades, and they’re not going to be pretty.
It was a tough night for Jordan Love and the offense. At this point, the excuses wear pretty thin. The Rams’ Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford were able to cobble together enough offense with receivers that would not dream of starting in Green Bay.
Yes, they lost Christian Watson during the game, and that’s a big blow. That’s also part of the design of Green Bay’s offense. What happens when less is less instead of more, as was the narrative coming into the season?
Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with one touchdown pass and two interceptions. He was only sacked once. With only 44 passing yards in the second half, he played poorly, even if he was largely let down by those around him. Any conversation about the MVP effectively died on Wednesday night.
“Not good enough. Definitely not,” Love said. “We’ll see when we look at it but just not good, especially the second half. Yeah, nowhere where my play needs to be and, obviously, it starts with me. I’ve got to be a lot better.”
Green Bay’s top receiver tandem of Watson and Matthew Golden caught five passes for 104 yards, but 65 of those yards came on Watson’s four catches. Golden caught 1-of-5 targets. Tucker Kraft remains disappointing and fumbled early in the game to set up a Rams field goal.
Green Bay’s quarterback has been asked to carry the whole franchise this season. As it turns out, asking one man to be Superman is a bad strategy, because eventually Superman becomes Clark Kent.
In what was the most predictable outcome ever, the Packers’ run game found no traction against the Rams’ stingy run defense.
They ran the ball 14 carries for 52 yards. Kaleb Johnson got the start. With no blocking whatsoever, his first three carries resulted in a loss of 8 yards. They didn’t have the ball nearly enough thanks to some of their issues on defense with stopping the run, but the Packers’ run game is bad. It’s not getting better, with their 65.9 rushing yards per game on track to be the worst in NFL history .
Now, they’re getting to the point where their passing game is starting to wilt, and they don’t have any other answers when that happens.
The final numbers from Matthew Stafford weren’t gaudy, but they didn’t have to be. Stafford was 16-of-23 for 140 yards and one interception by Ty’Ron Hopper.
Keisean Nixon has had better days against much better receivers. PFF charged him with 5-of-6 passing for 46 yards. Brandon Cisse was flagged for interference on the opening possession. Aside from Hopper’s interception, there were no passes defensed.
Micah Parsons had one sack and four of the team’s 11 pressures in his return to the lineup. He was active whenever the Rams did drop back to pass. Those moments were few and far between because the Rams may have been able to move the ball without ever attempting a forward pass.
The interception could have changed the game in Green Bay’s favor, but Jordan Love and Matthew Golden were not on the same page a couple plays later, resulting in an interception that made Hopper’s big play a relative footnote.
The numbers weren’t gaudy for a long time. The Packers were holding Blake Corum and Kyren Williams in check and forcing Matthew Stafford to make plays in obvious passing situations.
Then the second half came. Corum and the Rams’ offensive line, which featured mostly backup players, started to lean on Green Bay’s defense. Carries that went for 2 yards in the first half started going for 4 yards, carries that were gaining 4 yards started going for 6, and so on.
It culminated with a 35-yard-burst from Corum to set up Brandon McManus’ field goal to give the Rams a 10-point lead.
The final numbers were 32 carries for 184 yards for Corum. Kyren Williams had 12 carries for 46 yards. The Rams piled up 241 rushing yards as a team. The Rams entered the game without their three most-explosive weapons in the passing game. Everyone knew the Rams were going to run the ball, but they ran for 195 yards in the second half, anyway.
The most telling number is the time of possession battle. The Rams held the ball for 40:40 compared to the Packers’ 19:20.
“Some things just need to stay in-house, and I plan on directly checking that as a unit when we get back from this break,” edge Micah Parsons said. “But we all saw that game and we saw where we got exploited at. It starts with us. It starts with up front. I think I’m at that point where we say it’s not pointing fingers at things, but when runs open up like the Red Sea, we got to look at ourselves in the mirror regardless of how that is. We have to do a better job collectively up front.”
This was a win by total knockout from the Rams.
The Rams have a kickoff specialist who essentially killed any chance of the Packers being able to mount anything resembling an explosive return.
Joshua Karty specializes for the Rams in dirty kicks. For some reason, the Packers do not employ that despite drafting a kicker. This is making a mountain out of a molehill. The Packers have much bigger problems, but it’s worth observing that Trey Smack has not attempted a dirty kick this season.
Outside of that observation, special teams gave up one explosive punt return, but the kicker made all of his kicks. Maybe that is something that will help the Packers as their season enters December.
The Packers’ coaching staff was beaten up by Sean McVay and the Rams.
Matt LaFleur did not have any answers as his personnel dwindled with the loss of Christian Watson. That excuse falls on deaf ears when McVay is working with journeymen receivers. The Rams held the ball for two-thirds of the game.
But this is about the bigger picture.
The Packers do not win games like the one they played on Wednesday night. If there is a game in which they play an NFC team on equal or greater footing, the Packers are likely going to lose.
That’s been true for each of the last three years for LaFleur’s Packers. That’s why they’re 6-5 after back-to-back blowout losses. All five of their losses are against NFC opponents, and their most recent loss against the Rams provided a devastating punch to their playoff hopes.
Then again, perhaps the Packers should have expected that with the mountain of evidence that was in front of them last January. Despite that, they signed up for more of it. They’re reaping the fruits of their labor.

title: Playoffs?!? Packers’ Woeful Loss to Rams Came With Perfectly Imperfect Timing
full_text:
During the second half of the Green Bay Packers’ loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night, Green Bay’s defense got run over and its offense got thrown into the ditch.
In what was a must-win game for both teams, the Packers were trounced 26-13.
In terms of the Packers’ playoff hopes, their miserable performance had impeccable timing.
On Nov. 25, 2001 – exactly 25 years ago – the Jim Mora-coached Colts lost 40-21 at home against the 49ers. It was their third consecutive loss and sent their record to 4-6. Mora was asked about the team’s playoff hopes following what he called a “disgraceful” performance.
“Playoffs? Don’t talk about – playoffs?! You kidding me? Playoffs?! I just hope we can win a game!”
There were no epic rants from coach Matt LaFleur after the game. Just a tip of the cap to the Rams and the acknowledgement that the Packers didn’t take care of the football or stop the run.
“That’s a recipe for disaster,” he said.
Not just for a game but an entire season.
The Packers opened the night with a 6-4 record, ahead of the Rams and Seahawks by tiebreakers and clinging to the final spot in the NFC playoff chase. Now, the Packers are 6-5 and essentially two games behind the Rams with six games to play.
Just how deep of a hole are the Packers staring at?
“To be real, you know that answer,” edge Micah Parsons said after his debut game . “This hole is massive. This hole is massive. We took a big swing and we missed ginormously. The only way to get out is we probably have to win out. That’s just the reality of this situation. I think the people know that. We know that. From player to coach, we have to play better. It’s not just the players. It’s coaches, the whole thing, we have to all be better. I definitely look at that.”
Playoffs? Are you kidding me? The Packers are in ninth place in the NFC, though they’d move up to eighth if Seattle loses to San Francisco on Sunday. Along with the head-to-head tiebreaker against the Rams, Green Bay’s 4-5 record in conference games is becoming increasingly problematic.
Here’s what the computers say about Green Bay’s playoff chances.
According to The Athletic’s Playoff Predictor had a 64 percent chance of qualifying for the playoffs before hosting Minnesota. Now, with back-to-back losses, that’s down to 25 percent.
At ESPN , the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs two weeks ago. Now, that’s tumbled all the way to 19 percent.
At NFL.com , the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs before the Minnesota game. Now, it’s 23 percent.
At Playoff Status , the Packers had a 66 percent chance of reaching the playoffs a couple weeks ago and would have been at 63 percent with a win over the Rams. Instead, their chances have been cut to 31 percent.
Using Stick to the Model ’s Playoff Machine, the Packers had a 62 percent chance of reaching the playoffs before the back-to-back blowout losses. Now, they have a 16 percent chance. If Green Bay can somehow win five of its final six games, it would have an 82 percent chance of reaching the postseason.
But, to quote Mora, the Packers just have to win a game.
“Yeah, it’s extremely disappointing,” LaFleur said. “And like I told the team, it’s always 1-0, but we’re in a one-game season from here on out. We’ve dug ourself a hole, and we’ve got to put in the work to put yourself in position to even win a football game. And it all starts in practice.”
What gives LaFleur the belief the team can grab a shovel and dig itself out of the hole instead of simply dropping it on its collective toes?
“Because we’re going to take it one day at a time,” LaFleur said. “I know for a fact this group cares. They care a lot, and they’ve been willing to work. Unfortunately, like you just mentioned, we’ve put ourselves behind the 8-ball.”
The Packers’ six remaining opponents have a combined .550 winning percentage. That’s the ninth-toughest remaining slate of games. Never mind the NFC North teams. Everyone in the division seems out of reach. Focusing on the Rams and Seahawks, here is how it shapes up.
Rams (7-4): home against Chiefs, at 49ers, home against Cowboys, at Seahawks and Buccaneers, home against Seahawks. Those six teams have a combined .607 winning percentage, second-toughest in the league.
Seahawks (6-4): at 49ers on Sunday, home against Cowboys and Giants, at Eagles, home against Rams, at Panthers, home against Rams. Those seven teams have a combined .582 winning percentage, fourth-toughest in the league.
Packers (6-5): at Saints, home against Bills and Dolphins, at Bears, home against Texans and Lions. After the New Orleans game, four of their final five games are at Lambeau.
“You never know how the schedule is going to go and who they may lose to and who we may win against,” nickel Javon Bullard said. “Really, you just got to take it one game at a time. Shit, if we win out, you never know where the chips are going to fall.”
The Packers finished the night with 244 yards and three turnovers. The Rams had 241 rushing yards, 374 total yards and a 2-to-1 edge in time of possession.
“We knew we needed to come in and win this game,” receiver Matthew Golden said. “We knew it was a must win. It hurts we lost, but now like every game matters from here on out. We’ve got to take it one game at a time, and we’ve got to go out there and dominate.”

title: Here’s Where Packers’ Micah Parsons Vows to Be Better After Loss to Rams
full_text:
Appropriately given what it took to make his season debut on Thanksgiving Eve, Green Bay Packers star Micah Parsons was thankful to be back on the field during Wednesday night’s loss to the Rams.
“Personally, I’m just happy I had a game where I walked off the field and I can take that as gratitude,” he said after the 26-13 loss. “I’m thankful that I was able to play again and be with my friends and my brothers as teammates. But as the competitor, I’m just highly, highly disappointed with how we performed collectively.”
The game was tied 13-13 at halftime, the Packers going toe to toe with the preseason Super Bowl favorites. The second half, though, the Packers were thoroughly dominated in every phase. They gave up 241 rushing yards.
“We just have to be better,” Parsons said. “We talk about championships and so many more things. That wasn’t a championship attitude, competitiveness, drive. That second half is just inexcusable. I would say that’s my whole take on that.”
Playing in his first game since suffering a torn ACL at Denver on Dec. 14, Parsons started and played the first three snaps. Would Parsons be Peak Parsons or Rusty Parsons?
Rams coach Sean McVay wasn’t about to find out.
On early runs, the ball went away from Parsons. On passes, the ball was out of Matthew Stafford’s hand in the blink of an eye.
That was the right plan of attack. With the game tied at 13, the Rams got the ball with 1:50 left in the half. So, a 2-minute opportunity for the reigning NFL MVP and a reason for McVay to be aggressive. On first down, Stafford dropped back to pass but was buried by Parsons, who blew past standout left tackle Alaric Jackson in the blink of an eye.
sheeeeeeeesh pic.twitter.com/GoF3dq0YrB
That was enough. McVay ran the ball on second down, threw a screen on third down and was happy to get to halftime with a tie.
On nine passing-game snaps in the first half, four of the passes were screens. On the other five, Parsons had one sack, one hit and one hurry. It was a remarkable performance after a 346-day layoff.
The Rams found the ultimate recipe in the second half. They just ran the ball. Again and again. And again. Los Angeles ran the ball 35 times for 195 yards in the second half alone. You have to earn the right to rush the passer, and the defense didn’t put Parsons in position to make any impact plays as the game got away from them in the second half.
So, Parsons ended the game exactly how he ended the first half: One sack, one tackle (the sack) and two quarterback hits.
“The first game was OK,” Parsons said. “It was OK. It just really sucks how the game played out. I take accountability. I obviously didn’t have our room prepared enough for what we were about to face. We knew it would be a run and screen dominant game because of who they were missing. We just didn’t play good enough as a front and I hold myself accountable in that process where we just have to be better. We can’t let teams dictate the game like that.”
Parsons played 27 snaps – 15 against the pass and 12 against the run. He finished with four pressures – nobody else had more than one and the team finished with 10.
There would be no finger-pointing, Parsons said, but the problem was obvious.
“When runs open up like the Red Sea, we got to look at ourselves in the mirror regardless of how that is. We have to do a better job collectively up front,” Parsons said.
He added: "We need to figure out who’s going to be a dog or not."
Parsons said he needs to be a better, more serious leader.
“You like to play, you like to have fun with your teammates, you like to be all joyful and smiling all the time,” he said. “But reality, everyone just can’t flip that switch. That’s where a teammate had told me I could do better in that, and I swear I’m going to be better going forward. I like to play with the guys, shoot hoops before the walkthrough and do all these things that we do as team-bonding but, at this point, we just need to focus on all the small things and all the details (and) how we cannot get exploited like that.
“That’s somewhere where I’m really looking at myself in the mirror and how can I get my unit better because I go as they go and they go as I go. It’s a collective thing. I’m proud to be a part of this unit and I just want us to play better in these last games, that’s all I want. I came a really long way to look negatively on the outcome of this season, so I just really want to enjoy it with the guys that’s here.”
As for the knee, there were no issues physically or mentally. Parsons played without a brace and got after the quarterback when there were opportunities.
Because of the Rams’ game plan on offense, Green Bay’s horrendous run defense and the lack of help provided by the Jordan Love-led offense, there just weren’t many opportunities for Parsons to do what he does best.
“I push it in practice,” he said. “I was about as dominant as I’ve been before in practice versus the game. I’m just sorry I couldn’t really show you guys really how good it can get because we just didn’t do a good enough job on first and second down. It’s something we need to fix and, hopefully, we can see it next game.
“But I’m not worried about the knee. I’ve prepared and prepared and prepared to get to this point and I think when you prepare like that, you don’t worry about things. You just stay into the process.”
