title: Giants Not Relaxing After Jaguars Upset
full_text:
There really has never been any reason to question the New York Giants ' focus this season. Sure, they've scuffled through bouts of poor execution, but they've overcome enough missteps to sit atop the NFC East, with a two-game lead in the loss column heading into Thanksgiving.
Are they thankful? You bet. Will they relax on Sunday against the Colts in Indianapolis (3-8), even for a moment? Not a chance.
The players' reaction to upsetting the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) last weekend should have hammered home any evidence one needed to understand the Giants' mindset.
"The next thing, that's all we're focused on," quarterback J.J. McCarthy said.
"We're focused on getting into these meetings, that team meeting, watching the film with our units and focusing on how we could get better and make sure that every individual play coming into the next game against Indy is going to be something that we absolutely maximize and optimize when we get those opportunities. For us, the future is that next moment, and that's all we care about."
Indeed, the victory celebration was much more subdued than some might think after a win in which few gave the Giants much of a chance. After all, the Jaguars had been on a roll and were perceived as a big step up in competition.
"I think we proved that the only thing that's going to get in our way is us, and that gives us a lot of confidence," McCarthy said.
"There are so many great teams in this league, and just really focusing on doing things our way, the right way every single time we get an opportunity to do that. At the end of the day, as I said, we're just focused on that next thing and how we could get better in attacking that."
McCarthy, who arrived in a trade with the Vikings in late September, didn't need long to catch on to the team's mantra. It all stems from head coach John Harbaugh's weekly message about going 1-0.
And he's not about to pull it back.
"It's going to be a different challenge next week," Harbaugh said, "and we’ve got to be up for that challenge, too, because this football team [the Colts] is cornered and they’re hungry and they’re going to be ready to play their best football game and we’ve got to be up for it.. We've got to be ready."

title: Giants Refuse to Overlook Depleted Colts: 4 Storylines to Watch This Week
full_text:
On paper, the upcoming matchup between the New York Giants and the Indianapolis Colts suggests this week should be a cakewalk for the Giants.
The Colts have unloaded several key players, including guard Quenton Nelson, receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner. They have also moved on from quarterback Daniel Jones and plan to start Anthony Richardson Sr. this week.
But that's not how the Giants are viewing the matchup.
"We know we're going to get the Colts' best this Sunday. They're not going to go out there and not play hard," said right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor.
"They're going to play as hard as they possibly can, especially with the gravity of the game for us, but then also, we're in first place. I'm sure they're saying in their locker room, 'Let's go out there and beat the first-place team of the NFC East and see what we can do.' We're going to take that, go in there and play as hard as we can."
And, of course, hope that they come out with a victory.
Now for this week's storylines.
Once again, a key starter has been claimed by the injury bug. This time it's cornerback Greg Newsome II. He suffered a high ankle sprain in Sunday's win over the Jaguars and had TightRope surgery to speed his recovery. He will miss at least four weeks.
The Giants have been relatively lucky with the next man up keeping the team afloat:
The Giants have been relatively lucky when it comes to the next man up keeping the team above water.
Jameis Winton stepped in for Jaxson Dart at cornerback, Kayvon Thibodeaux has stepped into a bigger role at outside linebacker following the ACL injury suffered by Brian Burns, Micah McFadden has been mostly solid after the team lost inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds, and Dawaune Smoot and Trace Ford have both done well to fill the voids left by Roy Robertson-Harris and Chauncey Golston on the defensive line.
Paulson Adebo is set to fill Newsome's spot. Adebo played well on Sunday after Newsome's early exit, and the hope is that he can rise to the challenge.
The Giants are tied with the Green Bay Packers for second in the league with 18 fumbles, one fewer than the Los Angeles Chargers. Running back Cam Skattebo has five of them. That ties him for seventh among all offensive players and for first among running backs, alongside Colts running back Jonathan Taylor.
A big part of the problem appears to be that Skattebo seeks contact. That's all well and good, but in some situations a running back is better off avoiding contact that puts the ball in harm's way.
It would be surprising for the Giants to repeat the "quasi-benching" of Skattebo they handed him in Week 6 against the Saints. Still, this carelessness with the ball in traffic can't continue.
You could argue that Dominic Zvada's missed 32-yard field goal was actually good, and to our eyes it looked that way. But that's irrelevant.
What is relevant is that Zvada needs to get back to his early-season form, when his kicks were stress-free no matter which hash they came from.
The Giants' offense was meant to be powered by its running game, but that hasn't always been the case.
New York ranks 24th in the league at 3.8 yards per rushing attempt. When it comes to closing out games in the fourth quarter, the Giants average only 3.4 yards per attempt, which ranks 23rd.
They are also tied for third in the league with two fourth-quarter fumbles, one of which was lost. Their 13 rushing first downs in the fourth quarter tie them for 26th in the league.
In short, those aren't glowing numbers. They may help explain why the Giants have just a plus-6 point differential in the fourth quarter, and why head coach John Harbaugh is believed to want to add to the running back room at some point.

title: Giants' Abdul Carter Named NFC Defensive Player of the Week After Dominating Jaguars
full_text:
New York Giants linebacker Abdul Carter entered Week 11 of the 2026 NFL season on a mission.
The No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft knew the odds were stacked against Big Blue in its quest to topple the AFC South-leading Jacksonville Jaguars in their nationally televised showdown at MetLife Stadium.
Fortunately for Giants Nation, the 23-year-old delivered his best performance of the season, helping the club to a 23-18 victory over Jacksonville last Sunday in East Rutherford. He finished the game with four total tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss, five quarterback hits and 12 pressures, the second-most by any player in a game this season.
For his efforts, Carter has been named the NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 11. It's the first time he has earned the honor in his career.
You already know 🔥 pic.twitter.com/JJQNJoVU2Z
Carter noticed that national pundits overwhelmingly picked the Jaguars to hand New York its fourth loss of the season. He treated the matchup as a chance to earn respect and to prove how good the Giants' defense is.
"Yeah, we heard everybody pretty much counted us out, that we pretty much had no chance, that we couldn't stick with their offense," Carter said from his postgame podium. "But we took that as disrespect, and we came out with a chip on our shoulder."
Despite a statistically slow start to the season, Carter has remained one of the Giants' most important defenders. Under defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson, the club has adopted a pass-rush style built on blitz pressure.
Since team captain Brian Burns suffered a season-ending ACL injury, the unit has been much more effective with schemed pressures. Carter, along with fellow linebackers Kayvon Thibodeaux and first-year phenom Arvell Reese , has helped champion that cause.
Still, the 2025 All-Rookie linebacker knew the Giants' defensive success in Week 11 depended as much on stopping the run as on making life uncomfortable for Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence. The Giants held Jacksonville's rushing attack to just 77 yards, and seven of those came from Lawrence himself.
"Yeah, I think they had 70 rushing in total," Carter recalled. "Like I always say, if they can't run, they can't win. That's what we did today."
In his 10 starts this season, Carter has compiled 26 total tackles (five for loss), 13 quarterback hits, four sacks and one forced fumble, combining speed and power in a unique but effective way.
His athleticism and instincts routinely let him be a consistent, disruptive force against opposing quarterbacks, which only increases his value to New York's defense.
He also becomes the third member of Big Blue's defense to win the award this season. The Penn State product joins Reese (Week 9) and cornerback Deonte Banks (Week 4).
The last time New York had at least three Defensive Player of the Week winners in a season was in 2016. That year, safety Landon Collins (twice), defensive end Jason Pierre-Paul and cornerback Dominique Rodgers-Cromartie won the award, per Giants.com.
The Giants have also produced two NFC Players of the Month. Safety Jevón Holland was named the conference's top defensive player for September, and receiver Malik Nabers took home the offensive honor for October.
Reese continues to draw consideration for NFC Rookie of the Year and has been voted Pepsi Rookie of the Week twice this season.
As the Giants move into Week 12, coach John Harbaugh understands that their toughest tests may still lie ahead. Their victory over the favored Jaguars still shows that Big Blue deserves to be mentioned among the NFL's top-tier teams.
If any doubt remains, expect Carter to keep New York playing at its highest level.

title: Giants Refuse to Overlook Struggling Colts in Would-Be 'Revenge Bowl'
full_text:
Just think: Sunday's game between the New York Giants and Indianapolis Colts could very well have been the "Revenge Bowl" had the Colts traded running back Jonathan Taylor to the Giants and retained former Giants quarterback Daniel Jones.
As we know by now, neither happened, which for some might take a little of the luster off a game in which the Giants are heavily favored despite being the road team.
But that doesn't make the game any less important for Big Blue in its quest to keep more than just a little elbow room between itself and the rest of the NFC East.
"I think you go into every week trying to win the game," Giants right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor said when asked whether talk of this being a "must-win" game has infiltrated the locker room.
"No game is different than last week. You don't treat the Colts any differently than you would treat the Jags. You don't treat the Colts any differently than you would treat the Niners, or the Vikings, or the Bears. Every game in the NFL is hard to win."
In some ways, the Colts should be a gimme game for the 6-3-1 Giants, who are playing some of their best ball in years under new head coach John Harbaugh.
Indianapolis stands at 3-8 and, from the outside looking in, is a rudderless ship after firing general manager Chris Ballard and trading away guard Quenton Nelson, receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen, and defensive lineman DeForest Buckner.
But this is the NFL, a league where anything and everything goes. And that's one of the messages Harbaugh is undoubtedly reinforcing this week.
"I think that the notion of games you're supposed to win versus games you're supposed to lose, or teams are supposed to blow you out. I think that's just blown out of proportion, because at the end of the day, you're going against guys that are trying to put food on their table just like us, and they want to win," Eluemunor said.
"I've been in that position before where the season is not going as good as you want it to go. You have a losing record. You don't really have (anything) to look forward to postseason, but you're still going to go out there and play your tail off and try to win the game, because that's how much it means to you."
So will the Colts surprise the Giants on their home field, or is this just a case of players like Eluemunor saying the right things to avoid giving anyone bulletin-board material?
Despite their lead in the NFC East, the Giants can't afford to look past anyone, and how they handle this week will be another measure of their growth and maturation under Harbaugh.

title: Giants Back on the Rise in MMQB Power Rankings After Jaguars Upset
full_text:
For the entire week leading up to their matchup with the Jacksonville Jaguars at MetLife Stadium, all the New York Giants heard was how little chance they had of hanging around with, let alone defeating, one of the best-assembled rosters in the NFL.
Of course, most of those opinions had grown louder after their fourth-quarter collapse against the Commanders the week before, when they had numerous chances off timely turnovers to shut the door on their rival's rally but fell short.
What sets the John Harbaugh version of the Giants apart is their attitude: they don't let one game's result dictate what happens next. They felt disrespected by all the negative chatter and emphatically quieted it with a 23-18 win over the Jaguars, putting them back in firm control of the NFC East.
Big Blue's latest showing, which improved the team to 6-3-1, was enough for SI senior writer Conor Orr to move them up two spots to No. 13 in his newest MMQB NFL power rankings ahead of Week 12.
Orr is hardly the only writer back to spreading good vibes about the Giants after their statement win against an elite foe. Still, given how the rest of the weekend's results unfolded, it might be too early to start planning a rare postseason game in East Rutherford.
Sunday's win moved the Giants closer to sealing their first playoff berth in four seasons and their first division crown since 2011.
Very few Giants fans would trade the start New York has put together under Harbaugh, which includes answering serious doubts in games against the Dallas Cowboys, the Houston Texans and, most recently, the previously red-hot Jaguars.
All the talk heading into Sunday was that the Giants had to steal at least one of their next four games against playoff-caliber opponents from both conferences to stack enough wins and leave no room for the Cowboys or Commanders to catch them down the stretch.
They did that by beating Jacksonville, which renewed confidence in their chances in upcoming games against the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. However, the win only partially made up for the utter mishap of falling to Washington and losing the all-important head-to-head tiebreaker.
The Giants avoided losing more ground this past week, but it was also a good week for their division rivals. The Cowboys dropped 51 points on the lowly Titans, and the Commanders eked out another last-second win over the Bengals on Monday night.
Many Giants fans might be focused on the schedule battle between their team and Dallas, but the bigger concern should be the Commanders. Washington sits in third place at 4-5-1 but has the easiest four-game stretch of the three, with matchups against the Cardinals, Titans, Texans and Falcons, all of whom are below .500.
If the Commanders keep winning, the NFC East could turn into a three-team race. That isn't the ideal scenario for the Giants, who have the league's eighth-toughest remaining schedule , the hardest of the three contenders.
As they move on from the Jaguars win and prepare for a road game against the Indianapolis Colts, Harbaugh and his players have never needed a short memory more.
Their ultimate quest is far from over. They've rebounded twice from unfathomable losses, but things could change quickly in the coming weeks if they leave the door open and don't stay focused on playing their best football one game at a time.

title: Is the Third Time the Charm for Eli Manning's Hall of Fame Case?
full_text:
Is the third time the charm? The Eli Manning Hall of Fame debate is picking back up, as the New York Giants legend is one of 52 players to advance to the next stage of the voting process.
The selection committee will trim that list to 25 semifinalists when it next casts its ballots, and Manning will likely be part of that exclusive group. But will he get a gold jacket in 2027?
The two-time Super Bowl MVP was denied entry into Canton in each of his first two years of eligibility. Now he'll have to contend with newcomers Ben Roethlisberger, Rob Gronkowski, Adrian Peterson, Richard Sherman and Antonio Brown. The competition is stiff.
Manning's chances are still murky, but a bust will eventually be made for No. 10. He threw two of the most iconic passes in NFL history, helping the Giants defeat the dynastic New England Patriots in Super Bowls XLII and XLVI.
Yes, his regular-season numbers are rather pedestrian, with a 60.3% completion rate and 244 interceptions. But he cleared 4,000 passing yards seven times and threw 27 or more touchdown passes five times. He was also an iron man, logging 210 consecutive starts before his controversial benching in 2017.
Still, Manning's most vocal Hall of Fame supporters will emphasize his playoff heroics. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2004 NFL Draft, whom the late Ernie Accorsi acquired in a trade with the then-San Diego Chargers, raised his game when it mattered most.
Manning is best remembered for the magic trick he pulled off in Super Bowl XLII, escaping a sack and launching the ball to David Tyree, who pinned it against his helmet. But his most impressive achievement came four years later.
He was fantastic in the 2011 postseason, throwing for 1,219 yards and nine touchdowns with just one interception across an unforgettable four-game run. Manning then willed the Giants past Tom Brady, Bill Belichick and the Patriots once more, perfectly placing a 38-yard pass along the sideline to Mario Manningham.
The historical importance of those moments, combined with his entire body of work, will be enough to earn him enshrinement. It just may not happen next year. Manning has kept his composure throughout the process, taking his rejections in stride , and he has plenty to keep himself busy.
It would be fitting if he got the call this time around, though. Manning's induction into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in the same year as a potential Giants resurgence would be poetic.
We'll see just how much the voters appreciate a good story.

title: Latest Jets Practice Squad Signing Hints Harrison Phillips Injury Could Be Worse Than Expected
full_text:
The Jets remain focused on an improbable (but not impossible) playoff berth as they aim for their second consecutive win against the Dolphins in Week 12 . As lowly as Miami has been this season, its lone victory of the year came against New York in Week 7, so it's safe to say that head coach Aaron Glenn and Gang Green will be hunting for revenge Sunday afternoon.
That said, most teams are more than just banged up at this point in the season, and the Jets aren't an exception. New York is dealing with a handful of injuries heading into the pivotal clash with its AFC East rival, especially on defense. Veteran defensive tackle Harrison Phillips is among those navigating medical obstacles, as he's been dealing with an ankle injury for the last few weeks .
Although the Jets have yet to rule Phillips out of Week 12's AFC East festivities, the sight of a familiar face might hint that Glenn & Co. are preparing for the worst-case scenario.
On Thursday morning, the Jets announced defensive tackle Payton Page's return to the practice squad. The signing comes a day after Phillips missed New York's first practice of the week .
We've signed DT Payton Page to the practice squad
The former undrafted free agent has been in an on-and-off relationship with the Jets since joining the organization after the 2025 NFL Draft. He's played four games and was even promoted to the active roster on Halloween, but was eventually released from the 53-man roster on Tuesday.
Page's return to the practice squad suggests the Jets like him a lot, but it also might hint that Phillips isn't as far along in his recovery as the team hopes. All of Page's four appearances came after he was signed to the active roster, meaning Gang Green can still elevate him three times from the practice squad—a valuable tool if Phillips can't suit up.
What's interesting is that a potential absence against the Dolphins would mark Phillips's first missed game since the 2021 season. He played all 51 potential games during his time with the Vikings and hasn't missed an opportunity to suit up for the Jets since being acquired in the 2025 offseason.
That said, dealing with a lingering ankle injury as his 31st birthday approaches in January certainly adds to an uncertain future in Gotham. Phillips will be an unrestricted free agent in March, and being the 89th-ranked DT out of 132 with a Pro Football Focus grade of 53.6 doesn't help him, nor does his run-defense grade dropping from 76.4 to 57.7.
But improving those numbers will have to wait until Phillips is healthy. In the meantime, Page might have an opportunity to extend his own time in Gotham, and if he's successful, the Jets might have one fewer reason to bring Phillips back in 2027.
As mentioned before, Page is no stranger to the Jets, with four appearances this season and just as many last year. He's split his 2026 playing time fairly evenly, with 34 snaps coming on defense and 29 more on special teams. The dual role has led the ex-Clemson Tiger to record three tackles along the way, including one solo effort against the Chiefs in Week 9.
If given the chance to suit up, Page will hopefully perform better than he did in Week 11. The 6'4", 310-lb defender finished the win over the Chargers with a career-worst 29.7 PFF run-defense grade in 12 snaps. He could get back on track if he faces the Dolphins, who've averaged just 84.7 rushing yards in their last three games—the NFL's seventh-worst average during that stretch.
Every Jets player will be under intense scrutiny down the stretch, whether they're a main cast member or in a supporting role. It's time to find out whether guys like Page can be squeezed into diamonds, and what that could mean for veterans like Phillips down the stretch.

title: What T'Vondre Sweat's Return to Jets' Practice Means for 2026 Season and Beyond
full_text:
The numbers are a disaster for the New York Jets.
A year after fielding the fourth-worst rushing defense in the NFL, the team has gotten worse, ranking the third worst across the league. It's been a big reason why the team currently sits at 3-8 despite clear improvement elsewhere.
This wasn't supposed to be the plan, though. New York acquired run-stopping nose tackle T'Vondre Sweat in the offseason. They also signed aging veteran tackle David Onyemata to help their run defense. Both players have missed a majority of the season to injuries.
Onyemata's practice window was opened last week, and the Jets have welcomed his return. On Wednesday, the Jets welcomed back Sweat with hopes their run struggles may soon be at an end.
But are those changes likely?
New York activating the practice window for Sweat is a welcome thing for the organization, but it does not guarantee that he will see the field this week, next week, or the week after. All it means is that he can begin practicing with the team again.
If anything, Onyemata is closer to seeing the field than Sweat is, and the Jets are thrilled to be getting at least one of their run-stopping players back.
"[He's] a veteran presence and someone that knows the system inside and out," Glenn said of Onyemata. "Extremely tough, extremely violent, and there is a trust there. The thing is we want to make sure we get him right because we still have games left to go play. We want to make sure that when he's in there, that he’s right and ready to go."
Despite prior years of success in stopping the run, Onyemata had struggled to begin the season. Potentially getting him healthy and in playing shape, though, would fundamentally change how the Jets can attack opposing offenses in terms of formation alone.
Sweat's near return would make it even more so. The former Tennessee Titan was the 20th-ranked defensive tackle in the league and one of the best run defenders before his injury. He may be a two-down player, but with the Jets unable to stop the run, his return would be a welcome addition.
It would help in 2027 as well.
It's hard to see Onyemata being brought back next season regardless of who the coach is for the team. Sweat, meanwhile, has a year remaining on his rookie deal with New York. He is expected to be a building block for the defense beyond just this season when he returns.
Once he's back on the field, Sweat could change how the Jets' defense looks. And it's very important for a team trying to play for their head coach to get back to how they intended for things to look in December.

title: It’s Time for the Jets to Turn the Page on Jelani Woods
full_text:
Jelani Woods, simply put, hasn’t seen much of the field in 2026. The tight end is on a one-year, $1.2 million contract, and it figures it will be his last year as a Jet . He is clearly the odd man out in his position group. It may make sense for New York to move on from the 28-year-old to free up roster space for the rest of the season.
Woods was a healthy scratch in the Jets’ Week 11 win over the Los Angeles Chargers. It marked the second week in a row that the tight end did not suit up for a game. That is not a good trend for Woods or the Jets. He already wasn’t playing much, but not playing at all may be a sign the writing is on the wall for Woods.
The tight end saw his most snaps in a Week 3 loss to the Detroit Lions, in which he played only 25 snaps. Since Detroit, Woods has only hit the 20-snap mark once in the six games he has appeared in. He had been trending toward these healthy scratches, and now it might lead to the end of his time as a Jet.
The tight end has shown flashes, most notably his 20-yard juggling catch against Detroit. Unfortunately, it seems they were always just flashes. Woods has seen his snaps first dwindle and now disappear. If he isn’t going to be on the game-day roster, it may be time to open up Woods' spot.
Woods has had the opportunity to earn a larger role on the roster; it just hasn’t been seized. Woods was a part of the fabled 05 personnel that Frank Reich was so excited to run. It just looks like Woods may be the Marlon of the tight end family. Even with injuries and questions at the position, Woods couldn’t make his mark to stay on the game-day roster.
Mason Taylor missed Weeks 3 and 4 with a thumb injury . Woods had two catches for 31 yards in those games. The tight end showed promise in the two games without Taylor, but it didn’t lead to more playing time. He has two catches for eight yards in the four games he played since Taylor returned. There just doesn’t seem to be space for Woods in the offense.
Woods has not had more than one target in a game this season. That doesn’t lead to anything but a wasted roster spot. He is not as dynamic in the receiving game as Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq , or Jeremy Ruckert. He also does not block as well as Andrew Beck. Five tight ends are a lot to carry on a 53-man roster. If Woods can’t stand out, the Jets may have to send him on his way.

title: Aaron Rodgers Gives One Last Reason the Jets Made Right Call (In the End)
full_text:
Despite how poor the 2026 season has gone, do you think the New York Jets can take a step back and be thankful on Thanksgiving ?
Thankful for the decision that led them to move on from Aaron Rodgers in the first place?
Since moving on from Rodgers during the 2025 offseason, the Jets have won just six games. During that same time, they watched their former quarterback lead the Pittsburgh Steelers to the playoffs and a 6-4 record this year.
Then all hell broke loose, and it should leave the Jets feeling vindicated in their original decision, even if they won't publicly call it out.
Here's how the last 24 hours have gone for the Pittsburgh Steelers:
Just another day when covering the future Hall of Famer.
The Jets were asked today specifically about Rodgers' comments, but he took the high road.
"I saw it," Jets receiver Garrett Wilson said. "I just worry about what's going on over here."
Wilson had a feud with Rodgers during their short time together in New York. There was concern had the team kept Rodgers in the first year of the Aaron Glenn era that Wilson would have requested a trade. New York chose Wilson and even gave him an extension instead.
But Rodgers' comments highlighted two main truths for the organization.
First is that the team could have kept Rodgers for the 2025 season and probably won more than the three games they did with Justin Fields.
Second, they were right to move on because while they would have won more games, it wouldn't have been enough to keep Rodgers out of the news with his interviews.
All New York did was essentially tell Rodgers that his off-field mouth wrote checks his play could no longer cash. The Jets may be only 3-8, but they have improved as a collective offense. There is excitement surrounding that group for the first time in decades. It may not have been that way had Rodgers run the show.
New York has gotten a lot of stuff wrong since Glenn was hired as head coach. One move they unequivocally come away victorious with, though, is letting Rodgers walk.
Clearly, the 42-year-old quarterback is more than willing to tank his career—regardless of who he brings down with him.

title: 10 Things the Jets Should Be Thankful for This Thanksgiving
full_text:
With another holiday season upon us and the family gatherings, food and football that many associate with Thanksgiving, some teams around the NFL have more to be thankful for than others 11 weeks into the 2026 campaign.
While the Jets may not have as much to be thankful for compared to some of the contending teams around the league, even Gang Green has some positives to take into the holiday after snapping their five-game losing streak against the Chargers in a game they never trailed.
As everyone takes part in their favorite Thanksgiving traditions and reflects on what they are most thankful for, here are 10 things the Jets have to be thankful for this holiday season as they prepare for a Week 12 road trip to face the Dolphins.
There was a lot of hype surrounding the No. 2 overall pick out of Texas Tech when the Jets selected him back in April, but he has surpassed expectations and then some in just 11 weeks. Look no further than last Sunday's win over the Chargers when he recorded two sacks, including this one early in the third quarter (h/t NFL), and a forced fumble to bring his season-long totals to 9.5 and six, respectively.
2 sacks today, 9.5 this season for David Bailey 😤 NYJvsLAC on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CPQkr1Mrc3
Bailey is just the third rookie to accumulate at least 8.5 sacks and six forced fumbles in a season since the turn of the century and is only five behind Jevon Kearse's rookie sack record of 14.5 from 1999. He only needs one more sack to surpass Hugh Douglas' 10 in 1995 to become the Jets' all-time leader among rookies.
Bailey has been on a tear all season and there is no telling what he can accomplish if he stays at this pace. The Jets can only hope this is just the beginning of a successful career for a player who seems to be getting better with more snaps and proving that he is much more than just an elite pass rusher for them .
Aside from a challenging Week 10 game against the Bills when Smith was evaluated for a concussion and exited with a left ankle injury later in the game, he showed no signs of a lingering injury and completed 81% of his passes for 176 yards and three touchdowns in the Week 11 win over the Chargers.
Smith has now gone the last three games without throwing an interception, while last Sunday's game was his fourth of the season with multiple TD passes as he continues to give the Jets something they have not had in a while with his solid and reliable QB play.
With 15 TD passes and only three interceptions all season, Smith is giving this team the veteran leadership it needs under center and is by no means the reason they are 3-8. If it were not for his efficient performance and ability to take care of the ball, it is fair to wonder where the Jets would be at this point.
While Smith's play from the pocket and being able to distribute the ball has been impressive, he also has an immense array of weapons at his disposal. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson leads the team with 53 catches, 672 yards and three receiving TDs, while Adonai Mitchell has 354 yards and one TD in three fewer games as he has dealt with finger and knee issues.
Elsewhere, rookie Omar Cooper Jr. has impressed with 306 yards and two TDs, though he has appeared in one fewer game than Mitchell due to multiple injuries. Despite their inconsistent usage, rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq has the fourth-most receiving yards (268), while Mason Taylor broke out for a multi-TD game back in Week 7.
There is clearly no shortage of weapons on offense, but rather so many of them that feeding them the ball on a consistent basis has been a recurring issue. Combine the talent at the skill positions with an offensive line that paved the way for 165 rushing yards and only allowed one sack against the Chargers, and the sky is the limit when everyone plays to their potential and is involved in the game plan.
When Hall was sidelined for five games earlier this season, Allen filled in admirably with at least 100 yards three times and a total of three rushing TDs. While it seemed like taking him out of the RB1 role would be a mistake when Hall returned to action , he only received a combined 16 touches in Weeks 9 and 10 before the coaching staff put together the perfect balance between the two backs.
The two combined for 161 rush yards between them as Allen averaged 4.7 yards per carry to Hall's 4.3. Both were instrumental in helping the Jets control the clock and advance the ball down the field to keep drives alive in the win over the Chargers, and an even distribution of touches should be the way to go moving forward to ensure the Jets have an identity to lean on.
A lot of the attention has rightfully been on Bailey, but fellow first-rounders Cooper and Sadiq have impressed as well on offense. Cooper has still hauled in two TD catches and is averaging an impressive 15.3 yards per catch (second-most behind Mitchell's 16.9) in limited action. Sadiq, meanwhile, has flashed his versatility with a rushing TD and this sensational diving TD grab against the Lions in Week 3 (h/t B/R Gridiron).
KENYON SADIQ DIVING TD 🤯 (via: @NFL ) pic.twitter.com/XwvOyGlqGT
Fourth-rounder Darrell Jackson Jr. has also been on the rise with 35 tackles, 1.5 sacks, 2.5 tackles for loss and two passes defended as the excitement around his future continues to grow. Second-round pick D'Angelo Ponds only has four solo tackles and one pass defended, but the jury is still out on him with just one start and 35 defensive snaps in the Week 11 win over the Chargers.
The same is also true for backup QB Cade Klubnik, who came in for Smith in Week 10 and showed some encouraging signs, although he did throw a pick and looked timid in the pocket. That said, this is a talented draft class overall and one that the Jets are already reaping the rewards of in some areas on the field.
While many will point to the Jets most likely squandering away the opportunity in front of them to compete for the No. 1 pick in the upcoming draft, there is no doubt that general manager Darren Mougey has done a solid job setting this franchise up for long-term success .
Courtesy of the blockbuster trades involving Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams last season, the Jets have three first-round picks at their disposal, one of which is from a Colts team that continues to lose and improve Gang Green's chances of going after a franchise QB. Depending on how the season plays out, all three of those selections could be inside the top 15 and give them the control to surround this current roster with even more upside.
It seems like an eternity ago that there were questions surrounding who the kicker was going to be for the Jets this season. After Gang Green signed the veteran Sanders back in June as their kicking competition was still in limbo, he has been nothing but reliable for a team that has had a tendency to take the easy route and go for the field goal.
Sanders has made 27 of his 30 field-goal attempts this season and 16 of his 17 extra points. He has also converted each of his 15 attempts from inside 40 yards, hit from as far out as 54 yards and has gone a perfect 6-of-6 the last two games, not to mention accounting for all 12 of New York's points in back-to-back losses to the Chiefs and Bills.
So far this season, the Jets have faced six opponents with a winning record and lost five of those six games. However, the final score was not indicative of how competitive they were in each of those games after only trailing by double digits at the half in one of them.
Even against AFC powerhouses Kansas City and Buffalo, New York was within one score at the break until getting outscored by a combined score of 42-6 in the second half of each game. There is no denying the talent and overall competitiveness on this team, even if the lack of execution and failure from the coaching staff to adjust to what is happening on the field came back to bite them.

title: Jets Have Good Reason to Make Geno Smith Re-Signing a Priority
full_text:
Through the course of the last two years, the New York Jets have done a good job of retaining talent when needed, and letting aging players walk.
In the case of quarterback Geno Smith, though, the Jets should really consider altering their strategy.
At 36 years old, Smith is the kind of veteran the team has historically let walk in free agency after a stellar year. In New York's mindset, it's better to let an aging player walk instead of giving a contract extension to them.
Smith is a separate case. Not only because he is playing well above expectations this season, but because of what he could represent for the future.
Under his current deal, Smith makes just $3.3 million for the Jets. That makes his 2026 season one of the best bargains in the NFL this year.
Smith has completed 68 percent of his passes for over 2,400 yards, 15 touchdowns and just three interceptions. He is projected to throw for over 3,700 yards, 23 touchdowns and just five interceptions. That would be considered one of the best years for a quarterback in team history.
"I'm glad he's with us. I really am," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said. "I've said this from the very beginning: I don't think that he came into this season trying to prove anything to anybody, I think he just wanted to prove to himself that he could be one of the top quarterbacks in this league, and I think he's still trying to do that."
Despite Smith's on-field success, the team has yet to win games at a convincing clip under his leadership. At 3-8, New York is set for their 11th straight losing season and 16th year without a playoff berth.
If the Jets are going to extend Smith after this season, the asking price will be far greater than just $3 million. It would be a safe bet to assume he would expect starter money that includes somewhere north of $20 million.
That would fit the Jets' cap situation. They will walk into the 2027 offseason with over $80 million in cap space. But should they retain an aging player just because he had a good year? New York was proven right to let Nick Folk and John Simpson walk in free agency last year and found more productive alternatives. They could argue the same for the quarterback position.
Of course, there are different circumstances the Jets will need to consider.
It's safe to assume the Jets will be drafting a quarterback with one of their three first-round picks this year. Throwing an unproven on the field before they are ready, though, would be a disaster for the organization. They must allow the young quarterback to sit behind a proven veteran to learn from.
That's where Smith comes in.
New York wouldn't just be spending money on a Smith extension to be the starter next year. They would be asking him to mentor his replacement at some point later in the season. It's a fundamental difference between replacing a kicker or offensive lineman.
Sure, the Jets could let Smith walk in free agency and sign a different veteran for less like Jacoby Brissett or other bridge quarterbacks. But Smith is objectively better than any bridge that will be on the open market.
All this shows is that the team must get an extension done with Smith; not just to be competitive in 2027, but so they can have someone help the incoming rookie for the first time in decades.

title: 3 Over the Hill Jets Veterans Who Clearly Need Rookie Replacements in 2027
full_text:
Like the Kevin meme from "The Office," the New York Jets should be thinking one thing above all else:
It's nice to finally win one.
New York defeated the Los Angeles Chargers to snap a five-game losing skid and a stretch of eight losses in their last nine games. At 3-8, there's still little hope the Jets will figure out a way to save their season. But there are still positives to look at after a win like that.
At the same time, some uncomfortable conversations should come up as well. New York's aging veterans struggled despite the win. And if those struggles continue, the Jets should look to replace three of them this coming offseason.
Let's get to that list now.
We've highlighted Davis' play over the last few weeks as something the team needs to address eventually . If he has a good performance, we will happily give him flowers for it.
That said, Sunday's game vs. the Chargers was another mediocre showing for the 37-year-old linebacker. Davis was graded the Jets' fifth-worst player, per Pro Football Focus, and remains the third-worst linebacker in the sport by that very metric. He missed tackles and struggled against the run, as he has all season.
The Jets will need to address their linebacker room this offseason. They can't play Jamien Sherwood and Davis together next year. Sherwood has been fine to an extent, but Davis has reached the point of being nearly unplayable.
And if nothing gets fixed, the NFL Draft may be the best place to find his replacement.
It may seem unfair for me to call for the Jets to replace a starting defensive tackle who recorded a sack on Sunday. After all, Harrison Phillips got to the quarterback for one of the team's six total tallies on the day.
That said, his claim to fame isn't rushing the passer. It's stopping the run. And Phillips has struggled in that regard.
New York gave up 158 yards on the ground in the Week 11 win and over five yards per carry. The defense is ranked third-worst in the league at stopping the run. Things won't be getting any better either. The Jets need to address their interior defensive line, and replacing Phillips will need to be done.
Stephens has been a serviceable starter in his second season with the Jets. That said, he gave up a touchdown early in the fourth quarter. While Ladd McConkey is the Chargers' best receiving threat, you cannot have a starting corner get beat as much as Stephens has been this season.
New York could add a cornerback in free agency, but they could look to the draft to address the position again. D'Angelo Ponds was a second-round pick at the position this spring, but New York has trained him to play inside.
If the Jets want a bigger corner, the draft will have prospects to target. And any of them may be better suited to replace Stephens.

title: David Bailey Is Proving He's Much More Than an Elite Pass Rusher for Jets
full_text:
There will be no need to discuss who will be New York Jets' team MVP this season. That award has been won by one of the most productive rookies we have ever seen.
David Bailey's performance this season has been transcendent—worthy of a player who was taken with the second overall pick in the 2026 draft. The edge rusher has 9.5 sacks and six forced fumbles—a first in league history for a rookie in his first 10 games.
"We expect that from him," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said after the team's win over the Los Angeles Chargers. "I think he’s close to 10 sacks right now. The thing that’s really sticking out to me is the fact that he’s doing everything he can to get the ball back to the offense."
Bailey continues to make his mark on the Jets in his first season. But it's his improvement across his total game that is helping him exceed expectations at this point as well.
When the Jets made the decision to draft Bailey over linebacker Arvell Reese, they did so knowing Bailey was a more productive pass rusher. That has shown up in droves this season, and on Sunday, the Texas Tech product recorded another two sacks in the team's 27-24 win.
The six forced fumbles this season, though, are a wrinkle to his game that shows he's more interested in helping the team win than personal glory.
His impact in run defense has improved greatly as well.
Bailey is not a finished product when defending the run. The Jets knew that going into this season. But his play has improved. He currently ranks fourth in run stops with 20, which highlights his high motor to chase down runners. The tape also shows he is setting the edge a lot better and attacking blockers physically.
And as a teammate, Bailey's impact continues to be felt far beyond anything he's done on the field.
"I love him, bro,” Jets receiver Garrett Wilson said. “Every time I watch him make a play, I get so happy and excited because he’s a guy who doesn’t really get excited or happy for himself. He’s a baller, and I can’t wait to watch him keep growing."
The Jets know what Bailey can do as a pass rusher. He's currently five sacks away from the rookie sack record, and four forced fumbles away from the single-season record. What they've seen in his run defense and his high motor leads them to believe he can be even better than he already is.
And for a player that is seemingly on his way to winning the Defensive Rookie of the Year award, Bailey is set to be one of the top players on the Jets' roster for years to come.
"He still has a way to go, he really does, and I think he would tell you that, too," Glenn said. "I just look forward to him on a weekly basis of how he continues to progress and get better."

title: Jets Tanking Conversations are Missing the Bigger Picture After Divisive Week 11 Win
full_text:
Depending on who you talk to, the New York Jets' Week 11 victory was either a step in the right direction or the worst thing that has ever happened in the history of mankind. There's no in-between.
That, of course, comes with a team that has failed to record a winning season in their last 10 years, and has missed the playoffs in the last 16. Fans want to see change, but they want change to occur in a way that they think is beneficial for the future of the organization—not just for 2026.
But was their 27-24 win over the Los Angeles Chargers really that detrimental to their future?
In reality, most of the fanbase's anger is coming too early in the process. And it's making everything confusing for others who just want to see the team improve.
To the displeasure of some in their fanbase, the Jets were never going to purposely lose the final seven games of the season. They have simply too much talent and are loyal to their head coach to the point where they wanted to succeed for him.
What many angry fans forget to realize, though, is that the Jets don't need to tank in order to get a top pick in the upcoming draft. New York owns the Indianapolis Colts' first-round pick which is currently slated for fourth overall. The more the Colts lose (as expected), the better chance the Jets have of getting their future face of the franchise at quarterback.
Their own pick can be helpful in that regard, but it's not the be-all-end-all of the team's draft strategy. They can win as many games as possible and still come away with a top pick.
"I don't think anybody in this business is here to lose," Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said last week. "I don't think anybody in this business can stomach just going out there and trying to lose; that's just not the way that we're built... regardless of the record."
The idea that the Jets need to lose out in order to get their future franchise quarterback is also a flawed argument. In 2024, the New England Patriots and Washington Commanders missed out on the top overall pick, but managed to take quarterbacks that have gone further in the season than Caleb Williams has. The upcoming 2027 draft class is set to be deeper at the position as well.
New York could end up taking CJ Carr or Darian Mensah with the fourth pick and surround him with talent. This puts them in start contrast to, say, the Miami Dolphins.
The Jets are right on schedule to take a quarterback in the 2027 draft , and they don't need to tank to do it.
Glenn's current record as head coach of the Jets is 6-22. What the majority of fans are most concerned with, watching the team win, is that the more the organization is victorious down the stretch, the more likely it is that Glenn returns for a third season on the job.
We've been clear that seven wins for Glenn seem like the barometer for owner Woody Johnson to keep his current coach. That means New York would have to win four of their final six games. Here's the remaining list of opponents, in no particular order:
New York is talented enough to win four of these contests and perhaps more if the Bills, Patriots, and other contenders are without key starters.
But that isn't a guarantee either.
New York has two of its victories this season against one-win opponents. They have failed to show the ability to beat teams that are perceived to be better than them. Why would one win on Sunday and three wins this season be enough to save the coach's job?
In reality, there's no guarantee the Jets are going to keep Glenn after a three-point win over a one-win Chargers roster. Anyone saying otherwise is lying. There are a lot more games to determine before any decision gets made.
It would be best for Jets fans to let the process play out—and then wait to see where the team stands going into January, compared to worrying about a future decision over a month away.

title: Will McDonald IV’s Long-Term Jets Outlook Remains a Huge Question Mark After Week 11
full_text:
The Jets finally got into the win column Sunday, beating the one-win Chargers 27-24 at SoFi Stadium to snap their five-game losing streak. While New York’s dominance and efficiency on offense helped power the team to victory, the pass rush also played a key role.
The unit, led by second overall pick David Bailey and third-year defensive tackle Jowon Briggs , consistently kept Los Angeles quarterback Justin Herbert under duress, recording 17 pressures, eight quarterback hits, and six sacks.
It was a true team effort, as nine Jets defenders recorded at least one pressure. Surprisingly, edge rusher Will McDonald IV was one of the few who didn’t record a single pressure. Not only was the four-year veteran unable to generate pressure, but he also failed to make any impact in New York’s victory, finishing without recording a single tackle.
It’s become increasingly difficult to justify McDonald’s place in the Jets’ edge rush rotation. Despite New York picking up his 2027 option, McDonald entered this season in a make-or-break year after failing to establish himself as more than a rotational pass rusher during his first three seasons.
With his workload shrinking and production declining, it’s becoming increasingly unlikely that the former 2023 first-round selection will earn a long-term contract with Gang Green.
Through Week 11’s Sunday slate, the Jets are currently tied for seventh in sacks with 29, already surpassing last year’s total of 26. However, New York’s success has largely been driven by Bailey, who’s contributed 9.5 of the team’s 29 sacks.
The rookie from Texas Tech has quickly established himself as a legitimate franchise cornerstone, effectively taking McDonald’s role as the team’s top pass rusher. McDonald had led New York in sacks over the past two seasons, combining for 18.5 sacks across 32 games.
This season, he’s struggled to provide the complementary production New York needs from him, registering just four sacks and 22 pressures in 177 pass-rush snaps. Additionally, McDonald has shown minimal progress as a run defender.
Although he’s posted the second-highest run-defense grade of his career this season (61.3, per Pro Football Focus ), that doesn’t mean he’s become a reliable contributor against the run. In fact, McDonald has struggled to maintain that level recently, earning a run-defense grade below 60 in each of his last three games.
With McDonald struggling to make an impact in either phase, the team has opted to give Kingsley Enagbare and Joseph Ossai larger roles, especially in passing-down situations. This ultimately led to McDonald requesting two weeks ago.
With head coach Aaron Glenn and the team swiftly shutting down the idea of a trade, McDonald stayed put, and his playing time has slightly increased over the last two games. However, that doesn’t necessarily mean the Jets view him as a long-term piece of their defense.
Rather, keeping McDonald may have had more to do with ownership’s desire to give Glenn the best possible chance to succeed. By preserving the team’s already thin edge rush depth, the Jets can avoid further weakening an area that has already struggled to generate consistent production. Trading him would have left New York with fewer reliable options opposite Bailey, making an already floundering edge rush group more vulnerable.
Despite this, if McDonald wants to earn a lucrative payday, he must take advantage of his opportunities in the next seven games. He needs to show he can be a consistent contributor against both the pass and the run if he wants to receive a long-term extension.
Otherwise, the Jets could look to upgrade the position in the offseason rather than commit to McDonald’s projected $14.5 million cap hit in 2027, per Spotrac.

title: 5 Eagles Who Will Likely Be Inactive vs. Cowboys in Week 12
full_text:
The Philadelphia Eagles didn't have long to dwell on their Week 11 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, as they'll be right back in action against the Cowboys in Dallas on Thanksgiving Day. It will be the second meeting of the season between the two teams, as Dallas pulled out a 38-21 victory over Philadelphia in Week 7.
If the Eagles are going to pull out a holiday win, they'll have to overcome some absences. Here's a look at five Eagles players who have either already been ruled out of the game against Dallas or are unlikely to be active.
Jonathan Jones played well for the Eagles in their win over the Steelers in Week 11. He recorded five total tackles (two solo tackles) in the game, and he also led the Eagles with three passes defended. Unfortunately, he suffered an ankle injury late in the game and didn't return.
He was unable to practice with the team throughout the week due to the injury, and he's officially been ruled out of the Thanksgiving showdown with Dallas as a result. At this point, the main questions are when, and if, we'll see him out on the field for the Eagles again this season.
Linebacker Arnold Ebiketie tallied three combined tackles for the Eagles against Pittsburgh in Week 11, but he also apparently suffered an oblique injury in the game. He was sidelined for the week due to the injury, and like Jones, he's also been ruled out of the game against Dallas.
Considering that the Eagles were willing to move on from Ebiketie prior to the trade deadline, they probably won't miss him too much out on the field on Thanksgiving Day.
In addition to Ebiketie, the Eagles will also likely be without another linebacker in Smael Mondon Jr. Mondon was inactive for Philadelphia against Pittsburgh in Week 11 due to an ankle injury, and it wouldn't be surprising if he popped up on the inactive list again this week.
He was listed as a "DNP" on Philadelphia's estimated injury report on Monday and he was listed as limited for the other two days. Given his limited practice status, he certainly seems to be trending towards a second consecutive week of inactivity.
After leading the Eagles to a win over the Steelers on Sunday, Joe Milton will get the third start of his career against his former franchise on Turkey Day. Milton showed some flashes over his first two starts, and the Eagles will want to continue to evaluate him as the season moves forward.
Tanner McKee will continue to serve as the backup behind Milton, which leaves rookie quarterback Cole Payton as the odd man out, as Philly isn't going to have three QBs active for the game. Like last week, Payton will likely serve as the emergency third QB for Philly in Dallas.
The Eagles claimed offensive lineman Ajani Cornelius off of waivers just last week after he was waived by Dallas , and it seems unlikely that he'll be ready to contribute on the field this week. He was one of Philadelphia's five inactive players last week, and he's likely in store for a similar fate this week.

title: 3 Things the Eagles Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
As a holiday, Thanksgiving is all about gratitude, and while it may not necessarily seem like it given the way the current campaign has unfolded, Philadelphia Eagles fans have plenty of reasons to be grateful. Here's a look at three things that the Eagles organization and fanbase should be thankful for this Thanksgiving.
The 2026 NFL season has been rough for the Eagles as an organization as well as for Philly fans. There's no doubt about that. But, perspective is important, and as a fanbase, Eagles fans could have it a lot worse. After all, this is a team that just won the Super Bowl last year . It may feel like five years ago at this point, but it was just 21 months ago that Jalen Hurts, Nick Sirianni and company were hoisting the Lombardi Trophy in New Orleans.
A couple of years before that, the Birds made it all the way to the Big Game and came up slightly short. Overall, the Eagles have been to three Super Bowls over the past nine years and won two of them. That's not too shabby, and their recent success has provided Philly fans with ample opportunity for celebration lately. Just think, you could be a fan of a team that has never even won a Super Bowl like the Tennessee Titans or Arizona Cardinals, or even worse, a team that has never even been to the Super Bowl like the Detroit Lions or Cleveland Browns. So, while this season has certainly been a slog, Eagles fans could have it much worse.
Even in a down season, Eagles fans can lean into some optimism knowing that they have an elite general manager in Howie Roseman who isn't just going to sit on his hands. Roseman has shown an ability to consistently rebuild or retool the roster when necessary, and we shouldn't expect anything different this time around.
In Howie we trust pic.twitter.com/S7dLBN8Yr1
"In Howie we trust" is a popular slogan among the Eagles community, and for good reason. Roseman has already taken major steps in that regard by flipping declining players like A.J. Brown, Cam Jurgens and Jordan Davis for major draft capital over the next few years that the Eagles will be able to use to build themselves back into a contender.
If you're looking at the Lincoln Financial Field rafters, one thing that really jumps out is how many more banners there are since Jeffrey Lurie took over as the owner of the team in 1994 compared to before that point.
Four of Philadelphia's five Super Bowl appearances, and both of their Super Bowl wins, have occurred since Lurie took over ownership. Similarly, the Eagles have won the NFC East 12 times since Lurie became the owner, compared to just two times prior. Lurie is clearly an owner with a high standard, and that standard has permeated the rest of the organization ever since he first purchased the team.
Philly fans can take solace in the fact that they have an owner who clearly cares about the team and is willing to spend as much as it takes to keep the Eagles in the contender conversation consistently. Not all organizations can say the same.

title: Eagles-Cowboys Round 2: Who Wins & Why In NFC East Clash On Thanksgiving
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA – Four days after ending their losing streak, the Eagles will try to play spoiler in the NFC East when they visit Dallas on Thanksgiving. With the teams above them in the NFC East each winning in Week 11, the Eagles’ playoff hopes were diminished.
At 3-7, they are three games behind the Giants, two games back of the Cowboys, and one game off the Commanders in the win column. It’s a lot of ground to make up with just seven games left.
Putting a dent in the Cowboys’ hopes would make some fans happy, given how they are despised, but it might also make some fans unhappy because a two-game winning streak would push them deeper down next spring's draft order.
Nevertheless, here are five matchups to watch with my final score prediction:
Two Eagles to watch: quarterback Joe Milton and running back Saquon Barkley.
Milton is coming off his first win as a starting quarterback, and he did it in just his second start. Now, he returns to the team he spent nearly 19 months with before the Eagles signed him off the Cowboys’ practice squad last month.
“Just going to go play another football game,” he said. “I mean, obviously, I was just there a month ago, but it's going to be a great game. ... Know those guys' mentality a little bit, so therefore we just got to come with it. We’ve got to show up and show out no matter what.”
As for Barkley, injuries limited him to just 10 snaps in the teams’ first matchup in Week 8. He’s dealing with a shoulder injury now, which popped up against the Steelers.
“I won't really get too much into that,” he said. “I just look forward to rehabbing this week and getting ready for Thursday.”
Asked if he could play on a short week with the injury, he said: “I believe so.”
It’s worth noting that Dallas’ defense has given up at least 20 points in 18 straight games.
Quinyon Mitchell should be good to go on Thursday, per defensive coordinator Vic Fangio. How effective he can be with a hamstring injury remains to be seen. Jonathan Jones, who came off the bench and played well against the Steelers, is likely out, which means more Riq Woolen, who was benched for Jones.
It’s not a good matchup for the league’s second-ranked passing offense. CeeDee Lamb leads the league in receptions with 88 and is second in receiving yards with 1,108 and second in receiving touchdowns with nine. George Pickens isn’t far behind with 57 catches for 780 yards and six TDs.
Williams shredded it in the first meeting, rushing for a career-high 155 yards on 25 carries, a touchdown, and 6.2 yards per carry. Since then, linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr., has come into his own . In three starts since playing 24 snaps against Dallas, he has become an every-down player. Since that Week 8 matchup against the Cowboys, he is fifth in average tackles with 11.0 over that three-game stretch.
Dallas’ offensive line has allowed just 15 sacks of quarterback Dak Prescott, but the Eagles have been riding a hot streak over the past two games, collecting 11 sacks in that span. They sacked the Giants’ McCarthy six times, following that up by sacking the Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers five times.
This will be the eighth time the Eagles play on Thanksgiving, and the bar is high. They are 6-1 on this holiday, including 2-0 against the Cowboys in Dallas.
Verdict: Cowboys 27, Eagles 21 Season record: 9-1

title: Eagles' Sean Mannion Sees Untapped Joe Milton Potential Beyond 'Rocket' Arm
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — The legend of the rocket hanging from Joe Milton’s right shoulder has followed him from high school in Orlando to Michigan, Tennessee, and now into the NFL.
Videos of him casually launching the football 70 yards—or oranges the length of the entire field—have circulated for years. Teammates and coaches have repeatedly reached for adjectives to describe it: cannon, bazooka, and rocket, the last of which is Milton’s own preferred descriptor.
Milton even gifted himself a rocket chain when he made it to the scouting combine in 2024, where he tied a record by throwing a football at 62 miles per hour.
Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion, a former quarterback himself known for his own arm talent coming out of Oregon State in 2015, didn’t dispute any of it.
“Yeah, it is very, very strong,” Mannion said of Milton’s arm. “I mean, you hear some of the monikers, ‘Bazooka Joe,’ and it’s kind of become this urban legend. I will say it’s really not hyperbole. His arm is very, very strong.
“It’s at the top of people that I’ve been around and seen throw in person.”
That assessment carries weight. Mannion has been around plenty of arms during his playing and coaching career. However, the first-year OC wasn’t just confirming the physical trait that made Milton a sixth-round pick of the Patriots and later a practice-squad prospect for the Cowboys. Mannion was clear that Milton is not just a thrower; he’s a passer.
“I think what can’t get lost in that is he’s not just someone who throws it through a brick wall every time,” Mannion continued. “He has real passing talent. I think that’s something that sometimes gets missed—we want passers, not throwers.
“So, if you can throw it over those mountains in the distance, we want people who are refining themselves in terms of being able to throw with touch, having a quick release, being able to throw with a good base. I don’t want it to be lost that although he can throw it really far and he can put a lot of zip on it.”
That distinction matters for an Eagles offense that has struggled to generate explosive plays and stretch defenses this season. In his first two starts, the 6-foot-5, 235-pound Milton has given Mannion a different set of options.
The Eagles’ current QB1 can threaten safeties vertically without needing a perfectly clean pocket, force defenses to respect deep crossing routes and throws outside the numbers, and potentially open space underneath with the threat of his deep ball.
Jordan Mailata put it more colorfully after watching Milton up close in practice: the arm is “a [expletive] cannon” and “a work of art,” according to the star left tackle.
Milton’s early results with the Eagles have been modest. In his first start against the Giants, he completed 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards. In the win over the Steelers, he was 11 of 21 for 141 yards. No touchdown passes yet, but also no interceptions in those two starts, while adding a notable rushing element to the unit.
The offense remains a work in progress under Mannion, a first-year play-caller dealing with significant personnel losses, including the season-ending absence of Jalen Hurts.
Still, Milton’s arm provides an upside that was previously absent. It is the reason the Eagles plucked him off the Cowboys’ practice squad and elevated him into the starting role three weeks into his stint with the organization.
The Eagles see a quarterback who can make all the throws needed, including layering the ball with touch—the combination that often separates pure arm talent from a functional NFL passer.
“[Milton] has good mechanics,” Mannion said. “He can throw with touch, he can layer the ball into the second level, all the things that I really value in terms of true passers and not just throwers.”
Milton is now set to return to AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving Day against the team that employed him a month ago. Dallas already knows the arm. The rest of the league is still measuring how much of the “Rocket Joe” reputation is real—and how much of the refined passer Mannion describes is ready to show up on a consistent basis.

title: Jeremiah Trotter Jr. Quickly Complicating Eagles' Offseason Outlook
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA — Jeremiah Trotter Jr. is making the most of his opportunity, and the Eagles' defense is the better for it.
With star Mike linebacker Zack Baun on injured reserve, the third-year pro stepped into the green-dot role and delivered a performance that felt like more than just a solid fill-in.
Against the Steelers this past Sunday, Trotter finished with 13 tackles (nine solo) while playing every defensive snap in Philadelphia’s 19-16 win. He set the tone early, knifing through to drop Jaylen Warren for no gain on a fourth-and-1 from midfield on Pittsburgh’s opening possession.
It was the kind of play that wakes a stadium and announces who is leading the defense.
That stop wasn’t blind luck. Trotter, the son of franchise legend Jeremiah Trotter Sr., has shown the football IQ and natural instincts that are his birthright. The gifts have allowed him to play faster than his measurable tools. The younger Trotter is decisive going downhill against the run and has looked increasingly comfortable in space.
The physicality has always been here, even if the size (6-foot, 225 pounds) and pure athleticism didn’t scream “prototype” coming out of Clemson.
Every time Trotter has been on the field this season, he has looked like a starting-caliber NFL linebacker. The emotion that fuels it is intentional.
“You can’t really play without emotion,” Trotter said at his locker on Tuesday. “That emotion inside of me comes out when I’m out there on the football field.”
Teammates have noticed the on-field intensity that can surprise people who only see the quieter version of Trotter off it.
That job description now includes a short-week turnaround against the Cowboys on Thanksgiving. Preparation has shifted heavily to the mental side while the body recovers.
“It takes a lot of mental reps,” Trotter said of the short week. “Our coaches are trying to make sure that we’re getting our bodies back fresh for this upcoming game coming so fast. So it’s gonna be a lot on the mental side as far as film work, studying the game plan that we have in, and making sure that we’re getting that aspect of the game so we’re ready to play and our bodies are getting ready, too.”
The Thanksgiving Day holiday itself adds another layer. Trotter played on Turkey Day in high school at St. Joe’s Prep, but this will be his first time in the NFL.
“Thanksgiving, we always think of that like a football holiday as well,” he said. “Sitting there watching football, watching whatever team’s playing with your family and everything. It’s gonna be an awesome experience for me.”
Trotter views Dallas and its explosive offense as a clear test.
“They got guys everywhere, a very strong offensive line,” the legacy said. “Dak [Prescott's] leading them very well, operating the offense. They got guys on the outside, too—dynamic receivers from CeeDee [Lamb] and [KaVontae] Turpin and [George] Pickens. They got a lot of talented players, so it’s gonna be a great challenge for us come Thursday.”
From the earlier meeting this season, a 38-21 Cowboys drubbing at Lincoln Financial Field on Oct. 26, the priority is straightforward:
“It’s gonna just be stopping the run. They did a really good job and were effective against us in the run game,” said Trotter. “So we gotta start off there, stopping the run, and then it’s gonna come down to trying to get after the quarterback, stopping their guys on the outside, their weapons that they have.”
The conversation around Trotter is eerily similar to two recent linebackers with the Eagles: T.J. Edwards and Nakobe Dean. Like Trotter, those players weren’t the best athletes but excelled with their instincts, football IQ and physicality.
Trotter is now traveling the same path. He will start at least the next three games while Baun recovers from his back injury, and potentially longer depending on how it progresses. That extended runway is valuable.
The fan base has noticed. “Ever since I got here, Philadelphia has really given me a lot of support,” Trotter said. “Always showing love to me when I’m out there playing and doing what I have to do to help out the team win, and I really appreciate that.”
The offseason picture at ILB is already interesting. Trotter has one more year left on his contract. Baun is an All-Pro entering his age-30 season. Jihaad Campbell, the 2025 first-round pick, has rare physical traits for the position and flashed in his return from injury on Sunday.
Assuming Baun returns healthy, the Eagles will have legitimate depth and not enough snaps for everyone. For at least one more year, they can pair the veteran with Campbell while deciding how Trotter fits. They could also explore a move at the position. Either way, Sunday made the case that Trotter belongs on the field.
“He's playing good, defensive coordinator Vic Fangio said . “Trot's a smart player, he's an instinctive player, but that only takes you so far. You've got to play good and he is, and he's done a nice job for us. Trotter Sr. should be proud of him.”

title: Eagles' Eli Stowers Use Is Creating More Questions Than Answers
full_text:
PHILADELPHIA—In a season of head-scratching personnel decisions, such as keeping four quarterbacks, trading a Pro Bowl center, and pedaling a defensive tackle that you had just given a three-year, $78 million contract extension to eight months ago, the decision to keep five tight ends on the roster stands above them all.
Simply put, it makes no sense, especially with a second-round development pick that is Eli Stowers, who is in Year 3 of learning how to play tight end after being a quarterback his entire life.
My quest to find out why began in the days leading up to the game against the Steelers.
It started with a question to head coach Nick Sirianni about it, specifically about how the offense can implement Stowers when you have four others: Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundy, Grant Calcaterra, and Zach Ertz. And each of them has an expiring contract.
"He's getting some vital opportunities to play on special teams as well. I think I've said this to you guys before: Guys that play on special teams and do a good job earn more and more reps through the trust that they build there," said Sirianni about the 54th player taken overall last spring.
"That's the ultimate portion of football where they have to block in space, tackle, and block destruct. As an offensive guy having to do that, that shows a lot about a guy, and I think he's doing a nice job there. I like how he's developing, and we'll see how that continues to progress.”
The progress is evidently slow. Stowers didn’t play a single offensive snap against the Steelers. He did get 20 special teams snaps. It’s something, anyway. It’s not like the other tight ends were getting many offensive snaps, either.
As expected, the veteran got 47 (89 percent). Mundt had eight, Ertz six, and Calcaterra, like Stowers, got a goose egg. Also, like Stowers, Calcaterra got 20 special teams snaps while Mundt got 14.
The even weirder part about it is that they inserted offensive lineman John Ojukwu in a jumbo package set. Not a tight end. Do they not trust them to block? Certainly, they could have done better than Ojukwu in his one snap—and his only snap this season—when a Steelers defender flew right by him and sacked Joe Milton. Couldn’t they?
So, my quest to find out about the tight ends continued. The day after Sirianni talked, Sean Mannion held court, specifically asking how he could find a role for Stowers with four other tight ends clogging his path.
“I know one thing that is a total point of emphasis with this organization is player development,” said the offensive coordinator. “Even with Eli, his snaps throughout the season, each and every day he's out there on the practice field, we are totally focused on his development.
“I think as the season goes on, each week presents a different opportunity for different players on our roster, but our focus is completely on winning and doing the best thing we can for the Eagles to go out there and win the game. Eli's progressing nicely. We've got a deep group in the tight end room. Those roles will be always week to week in terms of what gives the Eagles the best chance to win.”
The Eagles put Ertz at the locker next to Stowers when the veteran tight end signed with the team’s practice squad on Oct. 10, wanting Ertz to be available for any questions or advice he could offer to a player 13 years younger than him.
So, how’s that going he was asked last week?
“He works his butt off,” said Ertz. “He wants to be really good. He understands that it's, it's a long journey, and I tell him all the time, you just gotta get better on day to day. That's what this whole league is about, is trying to be better today than you were yesterday.
“But the physical tools are so impressive. The work ethic is so impressive. His humility is so impressive. He's a guy that was a second-round pick for a reason, and to be able to just wanna learn and be a sponge each and every day, it's awesome to work with him.”
A role may yet come over the final seven games, but the Eagles should do themselves a favor and find out what he can do in a game, not just in practice or on special teams. Either way, they’re likely going to have to draft another TE this spring, but it would be nice to know more about what they already have.
