title: Breaking Down Eagles' Injury Report Ahead of Cowboys Clash on Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Eagles will travel to AT&T Stadium to face off against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 12. It is the first time Philadelphia is playing on Thanksgiving Day since 2015. Overall, the Birds boast a 6-1 record on the holiday, including a pair of victories over the Cowboys (a 27-0 win in 1989 and 33-10 win in 2014).
Health remains crucial in the NFL. The Eagles will need to be in tip-top shape to keep up with Dallas' high-powered offense. Philadelphia utilized walkthroughs on Monday and Tuesday, so its injury report remains an estimate. Let's dive into who is banged up and who is ready to roll for Thursday's clash.
Tuesday’s Injury Report #PHIvsDAL pic.twitter.com/eGhrGMSYGj
Cornerback Jonathan Jones played well in an expanded role against the Steelers, tallying five tackles and three pass breakups in 35 defensive snaps. The veteran left late with a foot injury and was seen in a walking boot after the game. Back-to-back DNPs suggest Philly will be without Jones on Thursday.
Expect Riq Woolen to return to a starting role if Jones cannot suit up. Woolen was benched mid-game versus Pittsburgh due to a few frustrating missed tackles. The Eagles' secondary will have to be firing on all cylinders facing Dallas' elite wide receiver duo of CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens.
Arnold Ebiketie is nursing an oblique injury. The defensive end was not present for either Monday's or Tuesday's walkthrough. An upgrade to limited participation on Wednesday is vital for him to have any chance of playing. Expect A.J. Epenesa to join the pass-rushing rotation if Ebiketie is ruled out.
It's encouraging to see cornerback Quinyon Mitchell upgraded from DNP to LP on Tuesday. The All-Pro talent suffered a hamstring injury in Week 11, though he was seen on the stationary bike in the locker room after the win. Defensive coordinator Vic Fangio expressed optimism about Mitchell's status.
Eagles DC Vic Fangio on Quinyon Mitchell: “I think he’ll be fine.” After Nick Sirianni’s comments yesterday and now this, it looks like Mitchell will be good to go. pic.twitter.com/sOGqGIqVwn
Linebacker Smael Mondon's ankle injury kept him from playing against the Steelers. The good news is that an upgrade to limited participation means he is trending in the right direction. His status will be one to watch. The Eagles signed Chance Campbell to the active roster on Tuesday for depth at LB.
Will Shipley has been a limited participant on back-to-back days. The running back returned from a foot injury in Week 11, handling kick return duties and posting nine yards on four carries. That same injury, as well as an illness, continues to bother him. Wednesday's report will provide final clarity.
Philadelphia would turn to Jaydon Blue as Barkley's running mate if Shipley can't give it a go, as Tank Bigsby remains on injured reserve with a core muscle injury. Blue could use a bounce-back outing after he gifted Pittsburgh a possession by fumbling the opening kickoff of the second half.

Running back Saquon Barkley (neck/illness) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shin) were full participants on Tuesday. The duo accounted for 113 of Philly's 214 offensive yards in Week 11.

title: 3 Aging Eagles Veterans Who Clearly Need Rookie Replacements in 2027
full_text:
The Eagles boosted morale with a 19-16 win over the Steelers in Week 11. That said, it didn't change the fact that Philadelphia remains at the bottom of the NFC East. It's a disappointing result that should light a fire under general manager Howie Roseman as he tries to retool the roster for 2027.
Retooling covers several strategies, including cutting bait with aging players in hopes that youth can add a spark. Veterans bring important leadership and experience to the table, yet can also hold a team back from addressing clear needs. The last thing Philly wants is to be held back from improving.
Here are three aging Eagles veterans who need rookie replacements in 2027.
The nostalgia factor was turned up to the max when Philly signed tight end Zach Ertz in September. The three-time Pro Bowler has logged 582 catches as an Eagle, which trails only wide receiver Harold Carmichael for the most in franchise history (589). It's a record to monitor over the final seven games.
Nostalgia is unfortunately all Ertz has had going for him. The 36-year-old has failed to make an impact on offense, tallying 22 yards on three receptions (eight targets) in four games. Ertz was on the field for just six of the 53 offensive snaps in Week 11. It was his first game action since Week 5.
Not only is Ertz struggling as a receiver; he has whiffed on run blocks as well. The record should not be something that earns him snaps over rookie tight end Eli Stowers moving forward. Stowers is the sole Philly tight end under contract in 2027, so adding depth through the NFL draft will be crucial.
The Eagles have had to turn to veteran cornerback Jonathan Jones to play meaningful snaps on defense twice this season. Cornerback Quinyon Mitchell exited Philly's Week 4 contest early with a knee injury, and cornerback Riq Woolen was benched mid-game in Week 11 due to missed tackles.
The move paid off against the Steelers. Jones finished with the third-highest Pro Football Focus grade among defensive players (81.5). He gave up five receptions for 54 yards on 10 targets. Take note that Jones left late with a foot injury. It remains to be seen if he'll be healthy in time for Week 12's Thanksgiving showdown against the rival Cowboys.
Monday’s Injury Report #PHIvsDAL pic.twitter.com/TZVZ0UfQz3
Jones is 33 years old and is playing on a one-year deal. While he could be someone to lean on down the stretch, he should not be an option beyond 2026. Drafting Mitchell in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft transformed Philadelphia's secondary. Roseman has an opportunity to make a similar move in April.
Let's circle back to the tight end position. Johnny Mundt was signed last offseason to be a gritty veteran blocker on an offense that excels when the ground game is working. It hasn't gone to plan. The Eagles are a bottom-five offense in rushing yards per game (88.8) and yards per carry (3.7).
Of course, there's more blame to go around. Mundt sports the third-lowest PFF grade among 75 qualified NFL tight ends this campaign (49.6), though. That is not someone who should be averaging 23 snaps per game and out-snapping a developing pro like Stowers at this point in the year.
Mundt joins Ertz, Dallas Goedert, and Grant Calcaterra as Philly tight ends who will enter free agency next offseason. The position is in need of an overhaul. Receiving tight ends gain draft hype, meaning there are always blocking tight ends available in the later rounds.
Roseman has a chance to double dip.

title: 3 Eagles Who Helped Their Uncertain Futures in Week 11's Win vs. Steelers
full_text:
The Eagles snapped a seven-game losing streak with their win over the Steelers on Sunday. Several unheralded players stepped up for the Eagles in the way, and some may have helped themselves out in the process.
Here's a look at three Eagles who may have helped their uncertain futures with the franchise in the win over the Steelers.
Quarterback Joe Milton got his second career start against the Steelers on Sunday, and while he didn't blow anyone away with his play, he led the Eagles to a win and flashed some potential in the process. He made some nice throws down the field over the course of the contest, including a great throw down the sideline on the move in the first quarter.
Heck of a throw on the run from Joe Milton PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DWwabguGPB
He also iced the game for the Eagles with a clutch, tight-window throw to DeVonta Smith in the final minute(s) to snap Philly's seven-game losing streak.
On 3rd & 6, DeVonta Smith comes up clutch. PITvsPHI on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/kx0HtT2tQs
Plus, Milton showed off his cannon with a bomb to Smith that was a couple of feet away from being an epic highlight for both players.
Joe Milton just threw the most perfect incomplete pass pic.twitter.com/jmYlsnZFzc
After the game, Smith gave props to Milton's arm strength. "I didn’t think I could get overthrown," the veteran QB said. "And he did it."
Again, Milton was far from perfect in the game. He completed just 52% of his passes and didn't toss any touchdowns, but he provided enough intrigue for the Eagles to continue to evaluate him as a future backup option.
Safety Marcus Epps turned in his best performance of the season against the Steelers on Sunday. Watching the game, it felt like Epps was all over the field, and the stat sheet backs up the eye test in this scenario. He was second on the team in solo tackles with eight, including one tackle for a loss.
Marcus Epps having a nice game.
Epps will be a free agent over the offseason, and while the Eagles absolutely still need to address the safety spot via the draft and/or free agency, bringing back Epps for some relatively cheap depth at the position might be something that the team considers, especially if he can continue to play as he did against Pittsburgh for the rest of the season.
Epps wasn't the only veteran member of Philadelphia's secondary who had a productive performance against the Steelers. Cornerback Jonathan Jones did also. He tallied five total tackles (two solo tackles) in the game, and he also led the Eagles with three passes defended.
At 33, Jones clearly isn't a long-term answer or option for the Eagles at the cornerback position opposite Quinyon Mitchell, but like Epps, he could be a guy the Birds look to bring back in free agency over the offseason as an inexpensive depth piece.
Unfortunately, Jones suffered an apparent foot injury late in the game, and he was seen in a walking boot afterward. So his status for Philadelphia moving forward this season is in question.

title: Steelers President Art Rooney II Backs Mike McCarthy, Calls Out Aaron Rodgers
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers have the biggest spotlight in the NFL on them after Aaron Rodgers went on the Pat McAfee Show and called out his former head coach, Mike McCarthy, with multiple accusations, including sleeping during meetings and calling the team the Packers during halftime of a game.
Both of which McCarthy did not deny when asked about them.
But Rodgers is the only one who's gone. The Steelers benched and eventually released their former starting quarterback just days before his 43rd birthday, ending an almost two-year run together. Afterward, they shared their support for McCarthy, and now, Team President Art Rooney II is making that stance even stronger.
Speaking with Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, Rooney  shared his support for McCarthy while making it known that Rodgers was an issue within the organization.
"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney said. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."
The ultimatum Rooney is speaking of is Rodgers telling McCarthy that he believes he should be calling offensive plays instead of the head coach. McCarthy said no, and Rodgers reportedly told the team to release him then.
They benched him at first, but then released him after his tell-all interview on the Pat McAfee Show, where he claimed McCarthy was not watching film in a timely manner, falling asleep during quarterback meetings and said, "1, 2, 3 Packers" during hafltime of the Philadelphia Eagles game when he was breaking a huddle in the locker room.
Rooney sided with McCarthy despite the accusations and then made sure to share his thoughts about Rodgers' timing of things and how he put his teammates in a tough situation.
"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure.
"In general, I think, historically, what's in the locker room stays in the locker room. That's the way it's always been. That's the way it should be as far as I'm concerned."
He's not wrong about the timing. Pat Freiermuth, Drew Allar and others were asked about it just after Rodgers spoke on the McAfee Show and were having trouble finding the right words that would not get them in trouble.
At this point, the story is over between Rodgers and the Steelers, with Rooney putting a stamp on it. But how Pittsburgh performs the rest of the season may have more to say about the future of the franchise.

title: Aaron Rodgers' Ultimatum to Mike McCarthy Revealed, and It's Eye-Popping
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The breakup between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Aaron Rodgers was messy, public and brought up way more than anyone could have imagined. But how did it start? Where did it all suddenly come from?
Just over 24 hours before Rodgers was benched by the Steelers in a public statement made on their website and social media pages, head coach Mike McCarthy made it known that "Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback." It was shocking to see the news that he changed his mind, and the fallout that happened afterward felt so dramatic that it clearly meant something significant happened to cause it all.
McCarthy and Rodgers met multiple times throughout the day before his benching, discussing the future of the offense and how they can move forward. McCarthy acknowledged in his press conference after Rodgers' release that the quarterback gave him an ultimatum that was "above his pay grade," and that eventually led to him being benched and cut.
According to Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac, that ultimatum was for Rodgers to take over play-calling duties, removing McCarthy from the role.
SOURCES: In a Tuesday evening meeting, Aaron Rodgers gave Mike Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: I want to call all the plays or just release me. They called his bluff and released him.
Rodgers seemingly gave the reason for this, stating that McCarthy was falling asleep in offensive and quarterback meetings and was not watching film on opponents in a timely manner.
Rodgers claims he's worried about McCarthy's health and wanted him to lead team meetings and focus on a smaller role as a head coach, instead of play-calling duties. He also claims that he thought the two were on the same page prior to his benching.
The Steelers weren't budging, though. This team will move forward with a new quarterback, not play-caller. McCarthy remains the man in charge, and the organization shared their support of him publicly to make sure everyone was aware of the situation and which side they were choosing.
For now, the only change in Pittsburgh is the release of Rodgers. They sit 6-4 and McCarthy is leading the charge. He believes he's the right man for the job and will continue to be throughout the season - now with a new starting quarterback to work with.
"I know how to win, and that's the facts," McCarthy said when asked why he's the right man for the job moving forward. "This is my third program, and I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization. We've got started, and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier. So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of."
Pittsburgh's season may be rocky, but it's still alive. And McCarthy isn't changing how this operation will run for the remainder of the 2026 campaign.

title: Steelers' Mike McCarthy Situation Seemingly Ends One of Two Ways
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- The Pittsburgh Steelers are swirling. This team lived through possibly the craziest day in franchise history, and somehow woke up with their head coach still in place, a game in 24 hours and a 6-4 record that shows they're still right in the thick of it.
If you looked at them on paper, the Steelers are right on course. If you watched how things unfolded in real time, you'd be shocked that the building is still standing.
But here they are, preparing for the Denver Broncos in Week 12, with a locker room that just lost their starting quarterback and a public opinion that is anything but positive. Head coach Mike McCarthy has his sights on winning, but it doesn't seem like he has much of a grip on the locker room. Things may be falling apart for the Steelers, and that means it's all seemingly going to end in one of two ways.
For those who missed it, Aaron Rodgers unloaded on the Steelers' head coach, calling out instances of McCarthy sleeping in meetings or missing them altogether, for calling the Steelers the Packers during halftime of the Philadelphia Eagles game, and for not trying to connect with the defensive players at all.
It was jaw-dropping watching Rodgers l ambast his former head coach on the Pat McAfee Show, pulling back the curtain on a situation that was so much worse than a two-game losing streak and a benched quarterback could have ever portrayed.
Afterward, even more came out, with players trying to show their confidence in the head coach , but not displaying it with their body language. The locker room felt like someone had just lost their family pet and was not stuck with the evil stepmother to comfort them.
And that wasn't all. NFL insider Jordan Schultz made it known that players have had issues with McCarthy for some time, and that the locker room may be slipping on the head coach during his first season. Offensive players are disappointed in how things are happening, and players who worked with Mike Tomlin for years are struggling to connect with McCarthy.
Sources: The relationship between Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy has not been in a good place, and a path back together is considered “highly unlikely.” The frustration is not just with Rodgers. Multiple position groups have been upset, and I’m told McCarthy has not been what… https://t.co/1GHeWUIQOv pic.twitter.com/Kezunpjcmn
Here's the thing: the Steelers' front office and ownership will decide how this ends , because it appears to be headed in one of two directions.
Route one is that the Steelers move on from McCarthy either during or after the season. The head coach did not deny falling asleep in meetings and confirmed calling the team the Packers during halftime of a critical Week 11 loss. Former players like James Harrison, Rod Woodson and others have made it known how unacceptable it is and how surprised they are that McCarthy remains the team's leader.
This also isn't the first time I've heard that former players are upset with McCarthy and the way he's handling things. This goes back to training camp, when he first started interacting with the few alumni who showed up to practice.
Route two is that the team doesn't do anything. They let McCarthy remain the head coach and show support that this is "his team." Once that happens, everything changes.
Players like Cam Heyward, T.J. Watt and others may be on their way out. McCarthy begins to build what he believes is the right roster, which is probably a much younger group of players. And in a year, the locker room looks much, much different than it does today.
Roster turnover is needed for the Steelers, and has been for some time. How much is the question. If McCarthy is still here, it's probably a good idea to expect a lot.
But that's on Art Rooney II, Omar Khan and anyone else who's involved in the decision to keep McCarthy or let him go. They'll decide what the future of the Steelers looks like after, maybe, the craziest day in franchise history.

title: Inside the Steelers Facility as Aaron Rodgers Lambasted Mike McCarthy
full_text:
PITTSBURGH -- Aaron Rodgers didn't hold back on "The Pat McAfee Show". He didn't hide any of the stories he once felt he was covering up about his head coach. And as it was happening, the Pittsburgh Steelers were walking off the practice field, with Mike McCarthy making his way to the second floor of UPMC Rooney Sports Complex to prepare for the Denver Broncos, with Mason Rudolph as his starting quarterback.
To set the scene, reporters are required to wait in the lobby of the practice facility as the team comes off the practice field. This allows players to settle before the media rushes in for interviews. It also allows the coaching staff to make their way to their offices after talking post-practice.
On this particular day, the Steelers ended practice at 1:37 p.m. Coincidentally, their former starting quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, was speaking on "The Pat McAfee Show" at 1:40 p.m.
Usually, the McAfee Show is on the television in the lobby of the facility every weekday at noon until it ends. ESPN almost never gets turned off at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex. But just seconds before Rodgers was set to make his appearance, someone came in and changed the channel.
So, everyone turned to their phones. Crowds of reporters huddled around each other, listening to the words of Rodgers as he unleashed havoc on the Steelers and their head coach. And as he told stories of McCarthy "snoring" in meetings and chanting "1,2,3 Packers" to the team, the head coach himself came walking through the crowd.
"Excuse me," McCarthy said as he shuffled through the crowd and made his way onto the elevator, only to hear Rodgers say, "I'm concerned about his health" in the background.
BREAKING NEWS: @AaronRodgers12 addresses being benched by the Pittsburgh Steelers #PMSLive pic.twitter.com/6rggspWDGX
The moment was surreal. You knew that McCarthy knew, but it's hard to imagine he knew what was actually happening. That his once long-standing friendship evaporated as Rodgers let the entire world know that McCarthy is failing Pittsburgh as their lead man. That he would be the biggest topic of conversation across multiple platforms, radio shows, TV programs and Thanksgiving catch-ups, and not because he benched a future Hall of Famer, but because he's falling asleep in meetings.
With the release of Rodgers following his appearance on the show, the Steelers have made their stance clear. McCarthy isn't going anywhere, but it's hard to tell right now what that means for the future of the franchise.
"I love Aaron Rodgers and I love the Pittsburgh Steelers," Will Howard summed it up.
Truthfully, that's the line everyone is walking right now. This team was blindsided. Then, so was McCarthy. The mood of the locker room after the Rodgers interview was like everyone just found out they got coal for Christmas.
Fans, players and the organization need to pick a side. Some already have, and some are trying to let it cool before they do.
The Steelers are in a whirlwind, though. Most reporters in the room would tell you that they have never witnessed anything like this before, because there may have never been anything like this before.
To witness it in real time was jaw-dropping. This situation may be over, but the moment will last forever. And surreal may be underplaying how powerful it felt at UPMC Rooney Sports Complex.

title: Steelers Supporting Mike McCarthy Despite Aaron Rodgers Accusations
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are sticking by head coach Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers called him out for sleeping during meetings and chanting "1, 2, 3, Packers!" while breaking down a halftime meeting during the Steelers' Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, among other incidents, in an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show".
According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, McCarthy has the full support of the Steelers' organization, who don't plan on making any immediate changes as of right now after releasing Rodgers, who prior to being let go and going on "The Pat McAfee Show" had been benched in favor of Mason Rudolph leading into the team's Week 12 Black Friday matchup with the Denver Broncos.
#Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, the subject of Aaron Rodgers accusations today, has the full support of the organization, sources say. They are standing by him and not planning to make any immediate changes. pic.twitter.com/bRBqzmMlgc
Based on Rodgers' comments and his sudden benching , the relationship between the veteran quarterback and McCarthy had been crumbling for some time.
There was some hope coming into the season that Pittsburgh could find some magic by reuniting McCarthy, who replaced Mike Tomlin after he stepped down in January, and Rodgers considering the pair worked in tandem with the Green Bay Packers from 2006 to 2018 and won Super Bowl XLV over the Steelers in 2010.
Instead, Rodgers is walking out the door while McCarthy remains in place, at least for the time being.
During a press conference hours after Rodgers made his remarks, McCarthy told reporters that he met with the Steelers ' player leadership council and had a "very honest" meeting with the group.
"I thought that it was a meeting," McCarthy said. "Very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous, numerous of things that have been on their mind. Comments that brought discussion to the forefront. So, I'm proud of our leadership, I'll say that. And more importantly, I love the urgency that everybody had coming out of that meeting."
When asked why he feels like he's the right person to guide the organization forward, McCarthy simply answered "I know how to win. And that's the facts."
He also admitted to the "1, 2, 3, Packers!" chant at halftime of the Eagles game, which ended in a 19-16 defeat for Pittsburgh.
"The Philadelphia situation that, you know, halftime was very emotional and there was conversations prior to that," McCarthy said. "Embarrassing moment, but I just think, you know, we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments."

title: Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Mike McCarthy, Reveals Shocking Stories of HC
full_text:
Aaron Rodgers offered full insight into Mike McCarthy's tenure with the Pittsburgh Steelers after being benched ahead of the team's Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos.
During an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" , Rodgers stated that McCarthy came into a quarterbacks meeting late last Wednesday on November 18 before the Steelers' Week 11 game against the Philadelphia Eagles and then started snoring several minutes later.
Rodgers added that McCarthy missed multiple meetings and one of Pittsburgh's walkthroughs in the lead-up to the Eagles game, which the Steelers ultimately dropped by a score of 19-16 at Lincoln Financial Field.
The 42-year-old quarterback added that at halftime, McCarthy broke down the huddle with a "1,2,3, Packers!" chant.
“I think the nail of the coffin was at halftime, offense on one side defense on the other side," Rodgers said. "Without even a heads up, he says ‘1, 2, 3, Packers!’
Rodgers didn't hold anything back when talking about McCarthy and the general feel around the building since the latter has taken over as the Steelers' head coach after replacing Mike Tomlin in January.
It remains to be seen how the rest of this saga plays out, but Rodgers made his feelings and opinions crystal-clear.
Rodgers, of course, has a long history with McCarthy, as the quarterback and head coach were together from 2006 to 2018 with the Green Bay Packers.
While the pair did win Super Bowl LXV over the Steelers in 2010, their relationship wasn't exactly smooth despite Green Bay's success with the pair in place.
In fact, Rodgers stated that McCarthy believes he got him fired back in 2018 and told a staff member that he still doesn't forgive him for doing so. He also made it clear that the "ship has definitely sailed" in terms of returning to Pittsburgh at this point.
From stating that he learned that he would be inactive against the Broncos from Pat Freiermuth and not McCarthy to admitting that he has joked around with general manager Omar Khan about McCarthy falling asleep, Rodgers painted a picture of what feels like a broken operation.
Rodgers also insinuated that McCarthy didn't feel like he needed to get to know and talk to some of the Steelers' defensive players more than he already had, which is quite the departure from how Mike Tomlin approached the job and is overall an easy way to break apart a locker room.
There's multiple sides to every story, and McCarthy has yet to give his perspective, but things look pretty bleak as of right now all while Pittsburgh is still in an AFC Wild Card spot at 6-4.

title: Steelers Players Not Happy About Aaron Rodgers Benching
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench Aaron Rodgers and name Mason Rudolph their starting quarterback ahead of Week 12's showdown with the Denver Broncos came as a surprise to everyone.
It doesn't appear as though the Steelers' pivot from Rodgers to Rudolph was well-received within the locker room either. As reported by The Athletic's Mike DeFabo and confirmed by sources to Steelers On SI, head coach Mike McCarthy officially spoke with the team regarding their resolution on that front during a scheduled 8 a.m. team meeting on the morning of November 25.
It didn't seem to resonate well , with DeFabo noting that it sounds like it was "not a popular decision" in the locker room. Steelers on SI's Noah Strackbein reported that Rodgers was not at the facility for that meeting either.
Aaron Rodgers was not at the team facility this morning for the #Steelers 8am meeting, sources confirm
A spark is necessary for Pittsburgh's offense after posting a combined 477 yards of total offense in back-to-back losses to the Cincinnati Bengals and Philadelphia Eagles following its Week 9 bye.
With that being said, however, the timing and way in which the Steelers have gone about making the change to Rudolph and breaking the news that Rodgers was being benched almost seemed rushed, disjointed and like it came together quickly.
NFL Network's Mike Garafolo noted that the team went from "adamantly standing by Aaron Rodgers and tweaking the play-calling process in hope of providing a spark to turning to Mason Rudolph for said spark in a matter of hours," while the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette's Gerry Dulac reported that the situation had been "brewing for a while" before reaching a point of no return once he was benched.
Regardless, it still feels like there's more to the story behind the scenes that led to this decision being reached.
Rodgers was largely a shell of his former self for the Steelers this season, but that doesn't make the news any less jarring for both him and the rest of the team.
Given how well-liked he is in the locker room and the fact that he's an NFL legend, Pittsburgh turning its back on him is going to have reverberating effects.
Rudolph is an experienced veteran and should be able to steer the ship in Mike McCarthy 's offense, though it wouldn't come as a surprise if the coaching staff has a hard time getting the team to fully buy in over the final seven weeks of the regular season despite being 6-4 and in the final Wild Card spot in the AFC.

title: Could Drew Allar, Will Howard Start for Steelers This Season?
full_text:
The Pittsburgh Steelers' decision to bench Aaron Rodgers less than 72 hours before kicking off their Week 12 game against the Denver Broncos was nothing less than a total surprise.
Despite having a 60.9 percent completion rate that ranks as the 10th-worst among qualified passers to go with the third-worst EPA of any quarterback at -66.2 (per Next Gen Stats ), there was no real reason to believe the Steelers would move off of Rodgers as their starter and turn to Mason Rudolph.
The fallout from Pittsburgh's stunning resolution has yet to fully play out. With the 42-year-old in his final season, however, it feels like his relationship with the organization may now be completely severed, even if the team internally believes that it could still revisit their decision (as noted by NFL insider Jordan Schultz ).
If the Rudolph experiment doesn't work out for the Steelers and Rodgers is essentially out of the picture one way or another, is it possible either Will Howard or Drew Allar could supplant the former at some point this season?
If Rodgers sticks around on the Steelers' 53-man roster instead of leaving the team either by being released or retiring and thus is available to step back in for Rudolph if things go awry, neither Howard or Allar stands much of a chance to make their regular season debuts in 2026.
Should Rodgers and Pittsburgh part ways or the 42-year-old simply just be inactive for the remainder of the campaign, though, than a real conversation could be had about one of the franchise's young signal callers potentially earning a shot to prove themselves down the stretch.
At 6-4 and in possession of the final Wild Card spot in the AFC for the time being, head coach Mike McCarthy is likely going to stick with Rudolph for as long as he can.
The 31-year-old is a high-floor backup with 19 career starts under his belt who can manage a game and has seemingly impressed Pittsburgh's first-year coaching staff at every turn.
Rudolph is far more experienced and steady at this stage of his career than Howard and Allar are, and McCarthy probably believes he gives the Steelers their best shot at remaining competitive and in the playoff hunt moving forward.
At the same time, the decision to go with Rudolph might have to do with the fact that the team is in a short week before facing Denver and doesn't want to play Howard or Allar under those circumstances.
There's a very realistic scenario where Rudolph falters, though, as he's thrown just 56 passes since returning to Pittsburgh on a two-year deal worth $7.5 million ahead of the 2025 season and doesn't offer any real upside.
Should the wheels fall completely off over the next handful of weeks with Rudolph at the helm as the Steelers face the Broncos (Week 12), Houston Texans (Week 13), Jacksonville Jaguars (Week 14) and Baltimore Ravens (Week 15), that's when another quarterback change could come and either Howard or Allar are named the starter.
Allar is quite easily the higher-upside option between himself and Howard. The third-round rookie out of Penn State has a rocket of an arm and has made strides since entering the NFL, namely in terms of his footwork and throwing mechanics.
He showed off his potential during the preseason too, throwing for 351 yards and two touchdowns on  54 attempts, but 2026 was always supposed to be somewhat of a redshirt year for Allar.
He still has a ways to go in his development, and while he's more exciting of a player than Howard, the latter is the safer option at this juncture.
A 2025 sixth-round pick, Howard is simply further along than Allar in their respective progressions at the NFL level. He had a rougher go of it in the preseason, throwing three interceptions, though he's more polished mechanically and has picked up more experience dating back to college than Allar has.
Allar is a safer bet to be the Steelers' starter in 2027, but Howard is likely in better shape to do so in 2026.

title: Seahawks’ Front Office Suffers Rare Loss With Rookie Avery Smith
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks have one of the best front offices in the league thanks to a collective effort of ownership, general manager John Schneider, and the scouts. Schneider has created two Super Bowl-winning teams under two different rosters. Very rarely does the Seahawks make mistakes with their roster or any moves. There are players that don’t fit with the team’s long-term plans, but that isn’t a failure of the front office. On Wednesday, the Seahawks learned the hard way about the utilization of a rookie.
The Seahawks waived former undrafted rookie cornerback Avery Smith on Tuesday to make some room on the roster. On Wednesday, the Los Angeles Chargers claimed Smith on waivers. Smith re-joins the Chargers after the Seahawks traded for him following the end of training camp . This marks one of the conclusion of a gamble from Schneider that didn’t pay off.
The Seahawks traded a sixth-round pick to the Chargers for Smith. This came after the Seahawks looked to upgrade the defensive backs. Smith would be among the rookies that have played the most games for the Seahawks this season, but they have all been on special teams. Smith played six games for Seattle, which included 56 snaps on special teams and none on offense . Smith accounted for five total tackles, including two solo tackles.
With the Seahawks still making moves, they are constantly moving players around their active roster and the practice squad. After being partly on special teams, the Seahawks attempted to get Smith on the practice squad for a more impactful player, but this left the Chargers a chance to get their player back and still keep their sixth-round pick.
The Seahawks didn’t just lose a player; they lost an investment. Through the first ten weeks of the season, Smith had the third-most snaps by a rookie behind running back Jadarian Price and guard Beau Stephens. It was clear that Smith wasn’t going to be a key defensive contributor, but he was still an asset on special teams and still learning from leaders.
With the Chargers reclaiming their undrafted free agent, the Seahawks lose out on Smith becoming a key asset in the future. Schneider essentially traded a 2027 NFL Draft sixth-round pick for 56 special teams snaps. The Seahawks had 11 total picks for the 2027 Draft thanks to the compensatory picks , but one was lost with the Smith trade.
With the 2027 NFL Draft being a highly talented draft class, any picks to select a key asset or used to trade up for a higher draft pick would be beneficial. This is one of the rare times that Schneider failed to visualize the possibility of an outcome or where his gambles didn’t work.

title: Seahawks Mailbag: 3 Questions Leading Into The 49ers Game
full_text:
This week, the Seattle Seahawks have their last real chance of convincing the NFL world that they can still be real contenders this season, so all eyes are on Santa Clara. I asked my discord server what their biggest questions about the team are right now. Let’s take a look at what’s on the mind of the fans. The wording of the questions has been lightly edited for this article.
“What will it take for Sam Darnold to get benched?”
My theory is that they’re going to keep him out there until they feel like they’re certain that he’s not the guy. That might be frustrating for some fans, but it’s somewhat understandable. The Seattle Seahawks are a few months away from making a franchise-altering decision on extending Sam Darnold for massive money. They want more data.
That mentality might end up costing this team a postseason spot, but they might also believe that Drew Lock is capped and isn’t good enough to win in the playoffs. A year after winning the super bowl, the standard is higher than just making the dance. I understand it, although I’m not sure I agree with the assumption about Lock. I feel like Sam’s leash is still long.
“What do the Seahawks need to do for the offense to be more consistent with Sam?”
I think this one is pretty straightforward. Despite Sam’s tremendous amount of success on third down in the game against the Kansas City Chiefs, the Seahawks must stay out of third down and pass situations. That means being more successful on first and second down. I’m looking at Brian Fleury to call a better game, and the running game to grind out more yards.
Even with these adjustments in place, I don’t expect much. There’s reason to believe that Darnold was, to an extent, figured out last season at the halfway point . I don’t believe the early-season MVP-caliber Sam Darnold will ever come back. But he can be a good starter, good enough to have a lot of success on a team with a defense this elite.
“Is there any possibility for Anthony Bradford and Quenton Nelson to both start at guard when Nelson comes back?”
I have an appreciation for Anthony Bradford, and I do believe he has been over-hated in previous seasons, but I think it’s time to move on. His play since returning from his knee injury has been brutal, and I find it hard to believe the juice is worth the squeeze anymore. He’ll be gone in the offseason, we may as well play the players who are part of the future.
I don’t think there’s a good answer for Seattle’s offensive line problems this season. I do believe that Grey Zabel is destined to move to center next year , but he needs an offseason and training camp to learn how to consistently snap and call out blocking assignments. It’s just not reasonable for him to learn it on the fly. It’s suboptimal, but he’s right guard for now.

title: The Best, Worst and Likeliest Scenarios in Seahawks vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are facing off against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12, and the stakes could not be higher.
The Seahawks are 6-4 on the outside of the playoff picture in the NFC , but a win against the 49ers, whom they lost to in Week 5 at Lumen Field, will not only settle the score but help their chances of reaching the postseason. Here's a look at the best, worst, and likeliest outcomes from the game between the two NFC West rivals.
The last time the Seahawks were at Levi's Stadium, it was in Week 18 for the NFC West Championship. The winner got the No. 1 overall seed in the NFC, while the loser was forced to be the top wild card. The Seahawks managed to stifle the Niners with a 13-3 win, giving them the first-round bye, the division title, and the momentum they needed to win it all.
While the stakes aren't as high as that particular game, the Seahawks face a pretty close-to-must-win game for them, with the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams breathing down their necks and fighting for one final wild card spot. The Seahawks have to do everything they can to separate themselves from the pack. A win against the Niners would not only give them reason to believe they can beat any team in the NFL, but it would get them one step closer, mathematically, to the playoffs.
The Seahawks have the No. 1 defense in the league, so that should give them a chance to beat any team in the league, including the Niners, who have the league's top-scoring offense after dropping 35 points or more in each of the last three games.
As I previously mentioned, the Seahawks have the No. 1 offense in the league, and they made light work of the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday Night Football in Week 11. The Vikings have the second-best defense in the league, but the Niners were able to dismantle them.
The same could happen in San Francisco this time around, so the Seahawks need to make sure they have the proper game plan that can contain all of the weapons on the Niners' offense.
Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, Debo Samuel, Mike Evans and George Kittle form one of the toughest offensive attacks in the league. The Seahawks need to be ready for all the ways San Francisco can beat them.
Any game between two top teams is likely to come down to a couple of plays in the fourth quarter. Whichever team makes the most plays late should be able to come out on top in this one, just like things did in Week 5.
The Seahawks held a lead in the fourth quarter, but they were unable to hold it after an Evans touchdown with 11 minutes to go. The plays made down the stretch gave the Niners the win, which kept their record undefeated at the time.
Given that it is so hard to beat a divisional opponent twice in one season and Seattle's stronger need for desperation, I like the Seahawks' chances of evening the score with the Niners and pulling out a much-needed win.

title: 5 Things the Seahawks Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks are going into Thanksgiving Day with a lot on their plate and in their minds.
The team is 6-4, fresh off their bye week , and looking forward to competing in the final seven games of the season with the hope of returning to the playoffs and repeating as Super Bowl champions. Here's a look at five things the Seahawks should be thankful for during the holiday season.
The Seahawks are in the third year of the Mike Macdonald era, and it has proven to be a resounding success so far. Macdonald remains one of the youngest head coaches in the league at just 39 years old, setting himself up for a very long career in the Pacific Northwest.
Macdonald arrived in Seattle after being the defensive coordinator for the top defense in the NFL, and he has maintained that standard in Seattle. The dark-side defense was tops in the NFL last year, and it led to a Super Bowl title. This year, they are still on top of the leaderboard, and they have a chance to win every single football game because of them and the work Macdonald and his coaching staff put in.
The Seahawks have been very meticulous about their free agency and draft process, which could lead to them having an excess of picks when the draft comes about next April. The team currently has 11 picks to work with after acquiring multiple compensatory selections from great players like Kenneth Walker III, Coby Bryant, Riq Woolen and Boye Mafe leaving in free agency.
With 11 picks, the Seahawks can use them to move up and acquire players they really covet, or they can add a bunch of prospects that give them a better chance to churn out some strong contributors in 2027 and beyond. This gives them a chance to sustain their success and be one of the top teams in the league for many years to come.
In a season that could have gone totally awry after the first series, when Sam Darnold went down with an injury, backup quarterback Drew Lock has kept this team afloat. Lock has been the player under center for most of Seattle's wins this season, and he is playing near-flawless football.
While Lock had two fumbles in his most recent start against the Las Vegas Raiders, he has yet to throw an interception and has seven touchdowns so far this season. If the Seahawks make it to the playoffs, Lock's contributions should not go unnoticed, even if he doesn't play another down for the rest of the regular season.
As I alluded to earlier, the Seahawks have the best defense in the NFL, and it isn't particularly close. The Seahawks average 236.1 yards per game, which is 44 fewer than the next-highest team.
The Minnesota Vikings have the second-best defense in terms of yards and are ranked number one in terms of points allowed. The Seahawks are just behind the Vikings, with 175 points allowed, which means they've only allowed two more touchdowns than them over 10 games this season.
The Seahawks provide elite matchups on all three levels of the defense, forcing opponents to pick their poison, which usually doesn't go very well. The Seahawks have held their opponent to 10 points or fewer four times this season and are 4-0 in those games. It's a true testament to how strong the defense has been this year, and as more games go on, it is only going to become more crucial for the defense to step up.
In addition to having the league's best defense, the Seahawks also have the league's top wide receiver, who also isn't very close. Jaxon Smith-Njigba is one of two receivers this season to surpass the 1,000-yard mark. The only other player to do so is Dallas Cowboys star CeeDee Lamb, who has 1,108 yards in 11 games, compared to JSN's 10.
Smith-Njigba also is the only receiver this season to find the end zone 10 times, and he has two multi-touchdown games already this season. Smith-Njigba is trying to win his second consecutive Offensive Player of the Year award. If he can be the first wide receiver in league history to record 2,000 yards, he might as well have that award locked up.
He still has a long way to go to reach that goal, but if he continues to reach his season average of 120.7 yards per game, he should be able to make NFL history.

title: Seahawks Injury Report, Charles Cross, Sam Darnold, Much More
full_text:
Back to the grind for the Seattle Seahawks. The bye week is over, and it’s the Wednesday before a game, so we’ve got a new injury report. Brace yourself, it’s quite long, but applying context clues makes the situation a little bit more transparent. The San Francisco 49ers have their own concerns, by the way. So let’s get into it, starting with the Seahawks.
Two players were listed with injuries but got full participation today anyway. Pat O’Connell (toe) was one, which is of minimal impact, and Sam Darnold (quadricep) , which is of massive impact. Since Macdonald has indicated the plan is to start Darnold on Sunday if he gets through a full week of practice, and Darnold is already a full participant today, he’s the guy.
Limited players included Anthony Bradford (knee, illness), Charles Cross (ankle) , Ernest Jones (knee), Nick Kallerup (ankle), Drew Lock (right elbow), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (ankle), and Leonard Williams (stinger). There’s certainly nuance for each player, but I would expect all of these guys to be ready to roll on Sunday. And we’ll need most of them.
As for players who sat out entirely, we’ll separate them into three groups. First, we have the irrelevant one, Jalen Milroe (illness). Then, we have DeMarcus Lawrence (shoulder) and Jarran Reed (toe) , who are likely just being cautious due to their age and are probably playing on Sunday. We’ll see where it goes, but I’d expect both players to be available.
And then, Abraham Lucas (ankle) and Quenton Nelson (knee), who are already out of the picture this week. Macdonald made it clear that neither player is really on the table to be ready, although Nelson sounds like he might be back for the Cowboys game. This is the real issue for the Seahawks this week, as they’re down two starters on the offensive line.
For San Francisco, Romello Height (hand), Khalil Kareem (ankle), and Mykel Williams (hand), all edge rushers, were full participants today. Keenan Allen was limited, and Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams were out, but all three were just resting. Expect all six of these players to be available and healthy by Sunday. That’s not the big problem for the 49ers this time.
Dre Greenlaw (neck) led the limited participant group, which is worth watching since neck injuries are no joke. Deommodore Lenoir (foot), Austen Pleasants (knee), and Carver Willis (illness) were also limited. Same for Upton Stout (shoulder, neck). See the Greenlaw sentence above why that might be significant, despite being able to practice some.
Mike Evans (achilles) was held out today, but we all know he’s going to play through it. Siran Neal (knee, foot) and Jordan Watkins (groin) were also out, although that is of minimal impact. The big one, however, is Brock Purdy (ankle), who was already indicated to be in genuine danger of sitting out on Sunday by Kyle Shanahan. Stay tuned on this one.

title: Seahawks Land 'Legitimate Red-Zone Weapon' in New 2027 NFL Mock Draft
full_text:
As was the case in 2025, the Seattle Seahawks aerial attack is overly dependent on Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year is having a remarkable season with 79 receptions for 1,207 yards and 10 touchdowns. Those numbers would make for a great season, but JSN has seven games to add to those totals.
To highlight how much he’s leaned upon, the second-most receiving yards on the team belong to Cooper Kupp, who has just 272 yards. A.J. Barner follows with 229 yards, then it’s Rashid Shaheed who has 17 receptions for 171 yards and has yet to score a receiving touchdown.
It seems clear that the $51 million bet on Shaheed has not paid off, which is why NFL Draft On SI’s Justin Melo has the Seahawks looking for help at receiver in his latest 2027 NFL mock draft.
With their top selection in Melo’s mock, the Seahawks wind up with Indiana wide receiver Nick Marsh . Melo says Marsh is not only someone who can pick up yards after the catch, but he also called him a “legitimate red-zone weapon.”
"The Seattle Seahawks offense is made up of Jaxon Smith-Njigba and friends. Cooper Kupp is aging, and Rashid Shaheed is disappointing on his bloated contract. Nick Marsh is the best run-after-catch threat in this wide receiver class, and he's a legitimate red-zone weapon, too," Melo wrote.
Marsh began his career at Michigan State where he had 100 receptions for 1,311 yards and nine touchdowns in two years. He transferred to Indiana this offseason and has taken his game to a new level.
In 11 games, Marsh has 44 receptions for 791 yards and nine touchdowns. He’s proven to be a big-play wideout as well, averaging 18.0 yards per reception for the Hoosiers.
Adding Marsh would give Seattle an instant upgrade at the WR2 position. It would also bring up an interesting conversation regarding Shaheed.
While he signed a three-year extension this offseason, there is an out in his contract in 2027 ( according to Spotrac ). If Seattle exercised that, they would be left with $16 million in dead cap space, but they would avoid another $11.75 million in guaranteed money.
Unless they truly value Shaheed as a returner, that could be the path they choose to take.

title: How the Seahawks' Defense Plays Better vs. 49ers in Week 12
full_text:
From now until the end of the season, the Seattle Seahawks (6-4) can’t afford any more mistakes as they push for the playoffs. The Seahawks are coming out of the bye week and into their next toughest game of the season. Seattle is set to go on the road to take on their NFC Divisional rivals, the San Francisco 49ers (9-1).
The 49ers are coming off a 35-10  win over the Minnesota Vikings this past Sunday Night Football. It was a game where the Vikings showed their defense isn’t as dominant as many experts previously believed. The Seahawks’ Dark Side Defense could have an opportunity to take down the 49ers’ offense in Week 12 after learning from the Vikings’ mistakes.
​The Vikings' defense was only able to account for four quarterback hits and one sack against the 49ers' offensive line. These aren't great numbers considering the Vikings like to send constant blitzes. The Vikings are one of the most blitz-heavy teams in the league at 67.4%. The next closest team is the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at 37.2%.
Minnesota gave up certain coverages on the field in favor of a quick pressure, but quarterback Brock Purdy and the players watched a lot of film to understand what spots would be less covered.
​The Seahawks are just in the middle of the league in blitzing percentages at 26%. Seattle is just second in the league in pressure percentage (30.2%), just below Minnesota at 34.4%, but the Seahawks don’t have to send constant blitzes . Four players for Seattle have, at least, three sacks this season and three have more than 10 quarterback hits.
They possess solid pass rushers from the interior defensive line, the edge and from the linebacker/defensive back zone. The main goal is to pressure Purdy constantly, but ensure the defense doesn’t give up spacing and allow easy first downs.
​The 49ers have one of the most dynamic offenses in the league at the start of the season. They have since traded for veteran wide receiver Kennan Allen from the Indianapolis Colts during the NFL Trade Deadline. The Seahawks now have to prepare to cover Allen, wide receiver Mike Evans, wide receiver Deebo Samuel, tight end George Kittle and running back Christian McCaffrey. Evans caught seven receptions for 113 yards and a touchdown in Week 5 against the Seahawks.
​This is a game where the Dark Side Defense has to remain vigilant and play strong contested coverages. Second-year nickelback Nick Emmanwori could be the key asset for the Seahawks as they could switch coverage schemes on him to ultimately confuse the 49ers’ offense.
The Seahawks also possess reliable corners in Devon Witherspoon, Josh Jobe (who is looking to redeem himself from Week 5) and Nehemiah Pritchett. They possess a potential All-Pro in safety Julian Love and an underrated starter in Ty Okada.

title: 3 Seahawk Role Players Who Could Have Big Stretch Runs
full_text:
If the Seattle Seahawks are to make it to the dance this season , we’re going to need big-time production from our top players. I think we all understand that. But who are the lesser-known pieces who could tip the scales? Some players that didn’t do much over the first ten games that now need to put up something more? Let’s take a look at three candidates.
I don’t think this edge group is built to survive with only three useful players, even with the occasional help from Leonard Williams and Nick Emmanwori . DeMarcus Lawrence, and even Uchenna Nwosu, aren’t meant to play a ton of snaps at this point in their careers. In order to bridge the gap, Dante Fowler Jr must take the field and do something for this team.
Of course, it’s not necessarily up to him if he can take the field. Mike Macdonald hasn’t been giving him a lot of opportunities. I have to believe that, at some point, there will be a commitment to at least getting him 16-20 snaps a game, for the sake of our starters not getting overloaded. And he’ll need to do something with those snaps for this to work.
It’s a little questionable if AJ Barner qualifies as a role player given how much he plays. But despite his constant presence on the field, he’s currently on pace to have less than 400 receiving yards, and he’s got one receiving touchdown after ten games. He’s been a capable blocker, but the numbers suggest he’s far from any sort of star player.
We know he’s capable of much more than that. Last year, on a team with Jaxon Smith-Njigba that was near the bottom of the league in passing attempts, Barner had over 50 catches for 500 yards. Many thought he’d take a step forward in 2026. If he wants to take that step forward belatedly, it would go a long way in balancing out this offense a little bit.
I’m double-dipping on secondary pass catchers because it feels critical that we start getting a little more out of these receiving options. And in the case of Shaheed , who got his meaty contract extension in the offseason, it seems especially critical. The offense needs more big plays, and Shaheed is a big play threat. Find him and get it to him.
But there’s a layer beyond even that. Shaheed has yet to bust any big plays on kick or punt returns this year. To be clear, I don’t blame him at all for this. The fault clearly lies with the blocking team, who have been unable to set the table for Shaheed at all this season. But if and when things turn around, it’ll be Shaheed with the ball in his hands, getting the credit.

title: NFC Playoff Picture: Seahawks Face Huge Stakes in Week 12 vs. 49ers
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks still find themselves on the outside looking in on the NFC playoff picture after the bye week.
The team saw its chances of making it to the postseason dwindle to 44 percent, but they are still very much in control of their own destiny. A win against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 12 will increase their chances of making it to the postseason, but they still have a lot of work to do. Here's a look at how the playoff standings look going into Week 12.
1. San Francisco 49ers (9-1) — NFC West Leader 2. Detroit Lions (8-2) — NFC North Leader 3. New York Giants (6-3-1) — NFC East Leader 4. Carolina Panthers (5-5) — NFC South Leader 5. Chicago Bears (8-2) — Wild Card 1 6. Minnesota Vikings (7-3) — Wild Card 2 7. Green Bay Packers (6-4) — Wild Card 3 -------------------------------------------------- In the Hunt: 8. Seattle Seahawks (6-4) 9. Los Angeles Rams (6-4) 10. Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 11. Washington Commanders (4-5-1) 12. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 13. Atlanta Falcons (3-7) 14. New Orleans Saints (3-7) 15. Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 16. Arizona Cardinals (3-8)
There are several ways the NFC standings can change after the holiday week. In tonight's special Wednesday Night Football game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams, the tie between the two squads will be broken.
If the Packers lose, it opens the door for the Seahawks to climb back into that final wild card spot.
If they were to beat the San Francisco 49ers, who are in first place with a 9-1 record, and the Niners lose, it gives the Lions and Bears a chance to tie for first place depending on who wins the game between the two teams to start off Thanksgiving Day.
If the Seahawks were to lose to the 49ers while the Packers beat the Rams, it would put Seattle one game back of the final wild card spot.
Considering that they don't play the Packers at any point between now and the end of the season, it is actually in their best interest for the Rams to win . Seattle and Los Angeles will face off twice in the final three weeks of the season, including Christmas Day at Lumen Field.
No matter what happens, this week should be extremely transformative in how the rest of the season shakes out, so the Seahawks should do their best to be on the right side of this week's result.

title: Why the Seahawks Should Sign Brandon Aiyuk (And Why They Shouldn't)
full_text:
The Seattle Seahawks and the rest of the National Football League are reacting to the news of former first-round pick Brandon Aiyuk being released by the San Francisco 49ers.
Aiyuk was once a very talented receiver, notching over 1,000 yards and over 700 yards in each of his first four seasons, including 1,342 in 2023. Since then, his career has gone downhill. In 2024, he signed a 4-year, $120 million extension with the 49ers , but tore his ACL and MCL after just 7 games with the team.
In 2025, his relationship grew sour with the organization. Even though he was healthy from his knee injuries, the organization voided his guaranteed money for not showing up to the facility. The dilemma carried into the 2026 season, right up until earlier this month, when he was reinstated by the league. Two weeks later, the Niners opted to release him. Now he's a free agent and can sign anywhere, including the Seahawks.
The Seahawks have a need to add a wide receiver, especially considering the rumored trade interest for the position ahead of the deadline. Aiyuk is someone who won't cost the Seahawks much, and he also has a connection to Seattle's coaching staff.
"Despite Seattle's flip-flopping between quarterbacks Sam Darnold and Drew Lock because of injuries, Smith-Njigba leads the league with a whopping 1,207 receiving yards and 10 touchdowns. He's on pace to set a new single-season receiving record and has accounted for over half of the Seahawks' receiving yards this year," Bleacher Report contributor Kristopher Knox wrote.
"Unfortunately, the Seahawks lack reliable depth behind Smith-Njigba. Cooper Kupp is the team's No. 2 receiver with just 272 yards. It's worth seeing if Ayiuk can boost the overall group, as he'd be a natural fit for the offense. Coordinator Brian Fleury spent seven seasons on San Francisco's staff before joining Seattle in 2025."
There is also very little risk in signing Aiyuk to even just the practice squad. At worst, it doesn't work out, and the Seahawks can cut ties pretty quickly, considering they have been open to giving players a second chance after questionable pasts with cornerback Terrion Arnold signing with the team ahead of him being arrested for alleged battery and kidnapping charges.
Simply put, it's a move that won't hurt the Seahawks, so they might as well try.
Aiyuk is a walking red flag who hasn't played in an NFL game in over two years. His last NFL appearance came on October 20, 2024, when he had two catches for 23 yards against the Kansas City Chiefs. His last touchdown was during the NFC Championship against the Detroit Lions in January 2024.
The Seahawks don't need Aiyuk to be the player that he once was, but the possibility of that player coming in if they sign him is what is appealing. However, the Seahawks can't count on contributions from nearly three years ago as a reason to sign someone in 2026. Seattle has to focus on the future, and it doesn't seem likely that Aiyuk would be a major contributor during the 2026 season.
While the idea of signing Aiyuk is trendy and flashy, especially for the Seahawks as they play the Niners this week , it isn't a concept that makes much sense in theory.
The Seahawks can improve their wide receiver room from within and don't need someone like Aiyuk coming in to shake things up. The Seahawks have a strong locker room culture, and it's hard to see how Aiyuk fits in that. Ultimately, there are pros to signing Aiyuk, but the cons outweigh them. The Seahawks should not consider this idea until maybe the offseason, when circumstances may change.

title: Why the 49ers are Confident in Colton McKivitz's Replacement
full_text:
It was devastating to see San Francisco 49ers starting right tackle Colton McKivitz suffer a gruesome ankle fracture against the Minnesota Vikings .
The vibes were high in the Estadio Banorte up until that point. You could hear a pin drop from how silent the 10 minutes were during McKivitz’s placement on the cart to exit the game in the second quarter.
Losing him will be tough. McKivitz was playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level this season. Even Kyle Shanahan acknowledges that, and that his loss will sting the 49ers.
“I thought he was playing really well,” Shanahan said. “I was really hurt for him that he couldn’t finish this year because he's had a hell of a year.”
With McKivitz out for the year, Vederian Lowe will be the one who takes over. He was the player who filled in the rest of the game for McKivitz, and he actually did a pretty fine job.
“I thought he played real well. Coming in, especially going against that defense, just all the problems that they present, so I thought he came in and stepped it up really well,” said Shanahan. “That’s why we brought him here.”
“Anytime you have a swing tackle, that means you better be capable of starting. He’s started a lot of games in this league and has played like a starter and that’s why we targeted him as a swing tackle.”
Lowe could’ve easily been a liability on the offensive line against the Vikings. Their vaunted defense has made actual starters overwhelmed and confused, so imagine a backup who is cold.
But he held up nicely. If that’s how he’s going to play for the rest of the season, then the 49ers will be in pretty good shape. Now, you can expect there to be issues at times.
Defensive coordinators will certainly try to exploit any weaknesses Lowe has, despite how well he performed in Mexico City. This is part of the process of uncovering what player he is.
The 49ers will learn about him as well through those hard times. Should he begin to struggle, it will make it difficult for Shanahan and Brock Purdy to execute the offense.
Shanahan will need to allocate help for Lowe as well as carefully consider some of his play calls. Purdy will also need to be conscientious of pressure and get the ball out more quickly.
For now, the 49ers are confident in Lowe. And after the performance he had in Mexico City, it’s easy to see why.

title: Why Mike Evans Deserves 49ers’ Biggest Thanks on Thanksgiving
full_text:
There’s a lot for the San Francisco 49ers to be thankful for on Thanksgiving.
For starters, I’m sure they’re extremely happy they don’t have to play on the feasting holiday. They get to enjoy their evening as every normal person does. I’m sure they’re giving thanks for that.
But the very next thing they should be thankful for is star receiver Mike Evans. He deserves the 49ers’ biggest thanks on Thanksgiving. He’s been everything as advertised and more.
Evans is the reason the 49ers managed to beat the Seattle Seahawks in Week 5. He went ballistic in that game, tallying seven catches for 113 yards and one touchdown. All three stats are season highs for him.
Without Evans, the 49ers most likely lose. In his first press conference, Evans said he was the missing piece to their offense. He was right. Look at how they were able to get over the hump against Seattle.
The same can be said for this past week in Mexico City as well. The 49ers always struck out against the Minnesota Vikings because defensive coordinator Brian Flores had an impeccable scheme.
Turns out, all the 49ers needed was Evans to finally crack the code. Of course, the game plan implemented by Kyle Shanahan was amazing, and Brock Purdy was incredible as well. They’re all a perfect match.
Just imagine if Evans chose money as his priority in free agency. He never would’ve joined the 49ers. They didn’t have the means to sign him to a lucrative deal. He would’ve gone elsewhere had that been the case.
He prioritized winning, which led him to Santa Clara. Plus, if he didn’t believe the 49ers were the team that gave him the best chance of winning another Super Bowl, he would’ve gone to the Buffalo Bills, who made him an offer.
Evans would’ve gotten a better quarterback, but he wouldn’t have gotten a better team. Besides, Evans knew Purdy was already a good quarterback. If he teamed up with Purdy, he’d only improve him.
Sure enough, that’s been the case this season. Purdy has a 150.2 passer rating, five touchdown passes, and 0 interceptions when targeting Evans, the highest passer rating by any quarterback-receiver duo in a season in the last five seasons, per Next Gen Stats.
Thanks to Evans, Purdy is in the running for MVP again. He’s also the reason the 49ers can win the Super Bowl, which I believe they will if he stays healthy. What an addition he’s been.
No one else on the 49ers deserves a bigger thanks on Thanksgiving than Evans.

title: 5 Things the 49ers Should Be Thankful For This Thanksgiving
full_text:
As the San Francisco 49ers get ready for Thanksgiving, there are plenty of things for the fans to get excited about. What are some of the biggest reasons to be thankful for the 2026 49ers?
Sure, the 49ers have not been healthy this year. They have had plenty of issues. At the same time, it looked worse at this point last year. Nick Bosa and Fred Warner are back. They were unsure how healthy Brock Purdy was. George Kittle and Mykel Williams suffered season-ending injuries.
They got through a lot of injuries, and right now Colton McKivitz is the only impactful starter who will not be there for a playoff run.
The 49ers offseason was a hit. They added Mike Evans and Osa Odighizua. Both players have impacted both sides of the football. The draft found them role players, but Kaelon Black, Romello Height, Jaden Dugger, and James Thompson have carved out roles.
Then, the additions of DeForest Buckner and Keenan Allen have them trending up. This was a huge success.
49ers fans have to sit back and reflect and feel satisfied that Shanahan finally found his quarterback of the future. There were questions as recently as last year when he suffered his injury, and the team held firm with Mac Jones. However, at his best, Purdy is an MVP candidate, and that is showing this year. The 49ers have had a head coach and quarterback together for a long time. That is huge.
The 49ers lost Robert Saleh, who got promoted to being an NFL head coach. The defense did not take a hit and might even be better with Morris. Morris made the right moves, the right changes, and could be a head coach in a few years again after what he did.
The 49ers' start is hot, but the division rivals who were so tough last year do not look as daunting. Sam Darnold has seen the clock strike midnight, and the Los Angeles Rams do not appear healthy enough to make a serious postseason run. San Francisco has beaten both teams once already and will be favored against them both the second time around. Things are falling into place.

title: Brock Purdy Misses First Week 12 Practice With New Injury
full_text:
The San Francisco 49ers held out five players in their first Week 12 practice against the Seattle Seahawks, including Brock Purdy.
At his press conference today, Kyle Shanahan revealed that Purdy is nursing an ankle sprain. He suffered the injury in the second quarter against the Minnesota Vikings.
Shanahan was asked if he thinks Purdy can participate in practice later this week, to which he responded, "We'll see." He also said it's possible Purdy misses the game against Seattle.
The bright side is that Purdy is considered day-to-day. He's not dealing with a high ankle sprain, which is encouraging news. His absence on Wednesday is to keep him from aggravating it.
If Purdy can't go, Mac Jones will start in his place against Seattle. The 49ers were kept afloat last year thanks to Jones. He's a perfect fit in the 49ers' offense.
It's for times like this that justify why the 49ers didn't trade Jones, or why they held such a high price on him for anyone who wanted to acquire him.
The 49ers would've been forced to go with Kurtis Rourke. They stand no chance of beating the Seahawks, or any team, for that matter, with Rourke at the helm.
However, the Seahawks are an opponent the 49ers need Purdy to beat. Purdy's ability to keep plays alive, his in-rhythm passing, and his rapport with Mike Evans are crucial.
I wouldn't be confident the 49ers can beat the Seahawks, who are coming off a Bye Week, with Jones, as solid as he is. Purdy will need to be active for Friday's practice to keep his availability alive.
As for the other four 49ers that missed practice: Dre Greenlaw (neck), Siran Neal  (knee/foot), Evans (Achilles), and Jordan Watkins (groin).
Greenlaw was inactive against the Vikings with a neck injury despite getting in a limited practice before game day. He's in a volatile situation, but Shanahan said the 49ers aren't concerned about his longevity this season.
They will certainly want him back for Seattle, especially since he didn't finish the game in Week 5. His tone-setting physicality is needed for this matchup.
As for Evans, his absence is a moot point. This is part of the load management for him, and rightfully so. They need to keep his Achilles as fresh as can be for game days.
All eyes will be on Purdy throughout the week.

title: Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk Signs With a New Team
full_text:
After only a day as a free agent, former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has found a new home.
Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders to their practice squad, per ESPN's Adam Schefter . This was always bound to happen from the moment he cleared waivers on Tuesday.
He conducted himself on social media in the Summer as if he were already signed to them. Although there was a stretch when it seemed he would never join the Commanders.
Aiyuk and Jayden Daniels had gotten into a back-and-forth on social media, but they reportedly reconciled. The Commanders signing him proves that.
Otherwise, if there had still been a conflict, the Commanders would never have signed Aiyuk. Now, they are banking on the former All-Pro receiver to get up to speed and help their team make a playoff push.
Aside from the connection to Daniels, the Commanders needed a receiver. Terry McLaurin tore his patellar tendon against the 49ers on Monday Night Football in Week 6.
Stefon Diggs is their only viable receiver, with rookie Antonio Williams beginning to step it up. It made perfect sense for Aiyuk to join the Commanders.
It's better that he signs with them than with the Los Angeles Rams or the Seattle Seahawks. I had thought Aiyuk might've considered them for a petty incentive since they are the 49ers' divisional rival.
In any case, Aiyuk lands on a team, despite a bunch of 49ers fans believing he was never going to get picked up. The reality is, Aiyuk burning his bridge with the 49ers isn't that serious.
Yes, it's immature, weird, and annoying, but that's all social media. He wasn't toxic in the locker room or anything. It doesn't significantly detract from a team's interest in him.
So, of course, a team was going to give him a chance, especially a wide receiver-needy one like the Commanders. It's the NFL. If anyone has intriguing talent despite their baggage, they will be on a team.
He just couldn't be on the 49ers anymore. He took shots at them throughout the Summer. There's no coming back from that. In the end, the 49ers handled the Aiyuk situation perfectly.
This two and a half year weirdness is finally over. Both sides seem to be in a good spot. Although the 49ers are in a dramatically better spot with Mike Evans.

title: Why the 49ers Should Be Thankful Brock Purdy Is Their Franchise QB
full_text:
It's Thanksgiving for our American readers this week, so don't forget to be thankful that Brock Purdy is the franchise quarterback for the San Francisco 49ers.
There are many reasons for this. He's taken San Francisco to the NFC Championship Game, the Super Bowl and more recently the NFC Divisional Round. That's some effort.
But when looking beyond that, he's always played at a high level, and the level is even higher this year. The 49ers should be thankful that Purdy’s statistics reflect his effectiveness as a quarterback, as he's recorded 2,624 passing yards across 10 games, with a 71.0% completion rate and 23 touchdowns. His 118.2 passer rating speaks volumes.
But this points to a bigger reason to appreciate Purdy. Beyond his performances on game day, he embodies exactly what the 49ers, or any NFL franchise, would want in a quarterback.
His focus remains solely on football , with no distractions or unnecessary drama. Instead, he is constantly looking for ways to improve, whether through marginal adjustments or significant gains. This relentless desire to develop is undoubtedly one of his greatest qualities.
San Francisco lucked into a quarterback who was selected as the last pick of the draft and has established himself as an elite quarterback in the league. Yes, it helps that Kyle Shanahan of all people is his head coach, but all of Purdy's attitude and mentality towards the game is entirely down to him.
This mental aspect of the game is something that can't be taught, requiring natural composure, resilience and self-belief. His ability to handle pressure, learn, not be bothered by setbacks and maintain confidence separates him from many others.
The 49ers have their franchise quarterback for the years to come, and the Purdy era is well and truly underway. It's an exciting time to watch Purdy let it rip, whether he's connecting with future Hall of Famers like Mike Evans and Christian McCaffrey or making the most of opportunities with depth pieces such as Brandin Cooks and Jake Tonges.
But don't forget what he promised this offseason: he wants to win a Super Bowl for the city of San Francisco .
With the 49ers sitting at 9-1 and defeating opponents that mainstream media expected them to lose to, Purdy is certainly backing up those words. He's giving everything he has to deliver on that promise, and the city has every reason to believe in what he and this team are building.
